role: Declarative admin settings-form schema for Bokbasen credentials
description: Lists the dot-namespaced settings fields (api_base, oauth_token_url, client_id, client_secret, client_role) rendered by the admin Plugin Settings LiveView; must mirror exactly what Bokbasen.Settings.get_credentials/0 reads back.
whatBreaks: Admins could not configure or would misconfigure Bokbasen OAuth credentials, breaking all Bokbasen publish integration; a field-name mismatch silently desyncs settings storage from the runtime reader.

role: Route table for OnixEdit's four plugin-mounted endpoints
description: Declares the ping pilot route, Bokbasen ops console, staleness console, and the admin ONIX export controller, each with auth tiers (:admin/:ops/:api) mounted via the host router's plugin_routes macro; preserves legacy URLs.
whatBreaks: OnixEdit's admin consoles and ONIX export endpoint would 404 or be mounted with wrong auth, breaking Bokbasen operations and book export entirely.

role: OnixEdit sub-schema index/namespace module
description: Aggregates WI2 sub-schema modules (Contributor, TextContent, ThemaSubjectCategory) and exposes all() and codelist_refs() across them. Acts as the namespace boundary between WI1 (book schema) and WI2 nested shapes.
whatBreaks: Codelist ref aggregation and sub-schema discovery for OnixEdit WI2 fails, breaking schema splice and seeder manifest checks.

role: OnixEdit Contributor sub-schema module
description: Loads and parses the contributor.json sub-schema (ONIX book contributor fields), exposes definition_map() for splicing into the book schema, and declares codelist refs for lists 17, 74, 18, 44.
whatBreaks: Contributor field validation and codelist seeding for OnixEdit books fails; contributor data cannot be structured or validated against ONIX lists.

role: OnixEdit TextContent sub-schema module
description: Loads and parses text_content.json (collateralDetail.textContents array item schema), exposes definition_map() for splicing, and declares codelist refs for ONIX lists 153, 154, 34.
whatBreaks: Book blurb/text content fields in OnixEdit cannot be validated or structured; ONIX text type/format codelist refs are missing from seeder manifest.

role: Thema subject category field definition
description: Provides the static field definition map for the themaSubjectCategory ONIX codelist field (list 93). Used by the integration layer to splice the Thema subject field into the book document schema.
whatBreaks: The Thema subject category field is missing or malformed in the book schema, breaking ONIX subject classification metadata.

role: External-sync state metadata (labels/colors) for Bokbasen submission lifecycle
description: Maps the 'bokbasen' external_sync channel to a label and per-state badge (color/label) for states like pending/staged/accepted/rejected, rendered by Studio on book documents.
whatBreaks: Studio would show missing or mislabeled/miscolored Bokbasen submission status badges on book documents; no functional impact beyond display.

role: Bokbasen submission admin LiveView
description: Phoenix LiveView console for monitoring and managing Bokbasen ONIX publish submissions. Shows sortable/filterable submission list with real-time PubSub status updates, retry actions for terminal-error rows, and ops-tier authentication.
whatBreaks: Operators lose visibility into Bokbasen submission state and cannot retry failed submissions via the UI.

role: HTTP controller streaming a book document as ONIX 3.0 XML
description: Handles GET /v1/plugins/onixedit/export/:dataset/:id.onix, resolving draft-over-published precedence via the tenant-scoped Content.get_document, then delegates to Export.to_iodata and maps XSD/codelist errors to structured 500/422 responses. Explicitly notes a prior bug where an unscoped query let any admin token export another workspace's catalog.
whatBreaks: A regression could leak documents across workspace/tenant boundaries or break the ONIX export/Bokbasen publish flow entirely.

role: OnixEdit codelist staleness admin LiveView
description: A 314-line LiveView admin console at /admin/onixedit/staleness that lists all book documents, classifies their codelist refs against the current registry issue, and offers per-row re-validate and acknowledge actions for operators managing ONIX codelist drift.
whatBreaks: Operators lose visibility into ONIX codelist staleness across book documents and cannot acknowledge or revalidate stale refs from the admin UI.

role: Pulse plugin wiring — public anonymous event-channel routes, rate caps, TTL sweep
description: Thin plugin mount for the Shared Storm event substrate: registers public CORS-open POST/GET/OPTIONS routes for events/recent/stats plus an ops dashboard LiveView, wires the hourly SweepWorker cron and the live Metrics cost sampler, and documents its abuse-cap policy (per-IP token bucket, per-channel daily cap, byte ceiling). Off by default; registers zero schemas deliberately since events are ephemeral rows not documents.
whatBreaks: If routes/auth or rate caps are misconfigured, Pulse either exposes unthrottled public write endpoints (abuse/DoS risk) or breaks CORS preflight causing all browser writes to fail; missing SweepWorker crontab would leak ephemeral events forever.

role: Admin LiveView dashboard for Pulse channel live counters
description: Read-only Studio admin page at /admin/pulse showing durable per-channel strike totals, today/last-hour windows, live BEAM CPU/cost estimate, and storage stats; subscribes to each channel's PubSub topic for real-time updates plus periodic refresh/vitals ticks.
whatBreaks: Pulse admin dashboard shows wrong/stale counters or crashes the admin page, but has no effect on the live Pulse channels themselves since it is purely observational.

role: Plugin wiring module mounting the Hyperquiz live-quiz engine
description: Thin Barkpark.Plugin wrapper that registers the quiz Registry/DynamicSupervisor/Bridge workers, the public host/play LiveView routes, and the private 'quiz' schema, keeping core Quiz.* machinery decoupled from router.ex/application.ex per the plugins-off doctrine.
whatBreaks: Quiz rooms fail to start (missing Registry/Supervisor), /quiz/host and /quiz/play routes 404, or the quiz schema never registers so authors can't create quizzes in Studio.

role: Boot-time GenServer registry of all Barkpark.Plugin modules
description: Central facade for plugin discovery/lookup and every resolver-chain collector (action handlers, routes, desk items, checkers, settings schema, doc actions, edge extractors, CLI commands, etc.), backed by a persistent_term snapshot cache refreshed on every mutation. Delegates most logic to Discovery/ResolverChain/BootCollectors/PluginCallbacks submodules but owns the GenServer state and test-isolation reset/baseline machinery.

role: Boot/compile-time collectors for plugin workers, Oban crontab, routes
description: Pure functions run before the Registry GenServer exists (or at router compile time) that synchronously discover plugin modules and safely invoke register_workers/register_routes/oban_crontab, isolating per-plugin failures via try/rescue so one broken plugin never blocks boot or router compilation.
whatBreaks: A bug here can prevent the app from booting (missing supervision children), break router compilation (missing plugin routes), or silently drop Oban cron jobs for every plugin.

role: Disk-walk plugin discovery and manifest-to-module resolution
description: Walks priv/plugins and deps directories for plugin.json manifests, resolves each to an Elixir module, and registers it with Barkpark.Plugins.Registry, honoring the :barkpark, :plugins kill-switch/whitelist env config; discovery never raises, only logs and skips.
whatBreaks: Plugins silently fail to register at boot (kill-switch/whitelist logic broken) or a fresh install loads plugins it shouldn't (or none at all), breaking the plugin_free_boot_test invariant.

role: Runtime dispatch of per-plugin callbacks (content renderer, media hooks, seeders)
description: Facade module dispatching first-wins content_renderer/test_connection resolution and additive codelist-seeder/media-upload/media-delete hooks across registered plugins in load order, with defensive try/rescue/catch around every plugin call so one misbehaving plugin never crashes the host.
whatBreaks: Studio preview pane could render the wrong content or never render, codelist seeding could silently no-op, or media upload/delete lifecycle hooks could stop firing for all plugins.

role: Core additive resolver-chain driver for plugin desk-items/top-menu/etc
description: The central reduce_resolvers/3 engine that threads an accumulator through every plugin's resolver or additive callback (desk_items, top_menu_entries, doc_actions, checkers, etc.), applying per-workspace enablement filtering only to the three surfacing callbacks, plus duplicate-form warnings and the plugin load-order source of truth.
whatBreaks: Studio's desk tree, top nav menu, doc actions, or other plugin-contributed UI/behavior could disappear, duplicate, leak across workspaces, or deadlock the Registry GenServer (self-call) on boot with :barkpark,:plugins configured.

role: in-memory plugin run-status GenServer
description: A permanent GenServer tracking the last bootstrap and codelist-seed run result per plugin, powering the plugin admin LiveView at /studio/:dataset/_plugins. Exposes record/3, get/1, all/0 with defensive try/catch wrappers.
whatBreaks: Plugin admin UI shows no bootstrap/seed history; operators cannot see whether plugin setup succeeded or failed without checking logs manually.

role: CRUD API for encrypted per-plugin settings with audit logging
description: get/put/delete/reveal operations against SettingsRecord (Cloak-encrypted at rest), each atomically paired with a SettingsAudit row inside a DB transaction so a secret write/read is never left unaudited, plus telemetry emission. Used by Studio's settings LiveView for masked-field reveal flows.

role: Masks/unmasks secret values for Studio settings display and save round-trip
description: mask/1 recursively obscures string secrets (showing only last 4 chars) for display; restore/1 reconciles a submitted settings tree against stored values so a save that echoes back masked placeholders doesn't overwrite real secrets with the mask string itself.
whatBreaks: A bug in restore/1 could let a masked placeholder overwrite a real stored secret on save (destroying credentials), or leak unmasked secrets to the UI.

role: Ecto schema for plugin_settings_audit log rows
description: Simple schema/changeset for the audit trail of read/write/delete/reveal actions on plugin settings, validating the action vocabulary. Written exclusively by Barkpark.Plugins.Settings.
whatBreaks: Loosened validation could let malformed audit rows through, weakening the audit trail for secret access, but wouldn't affect core functionality.

role: Ecto schema for the encrypted plugin_settings table
description: Defines the persisted per-plugin settings row keyed by plugin_name, with `settings` stored via Barkpark.EncryptedMap (Cloak) and updated_by tracking. Backing store for Barkpark.Plugins.Settings.
whatBreaks: A schema/encryption misconfiguration could store plugin secrets unencrypted or make settings unreadable, affecting every plugin relying on stored credentials.

role: Plugin module wiring the Sheets (spreadsheet) document type and API
description: Declares the `sheet` schema, a strict before_save structural validation gate (cell A1 keys/grid bounds, merge area cap, conditional-formatting rule schema, tab color format), and registers the import/export/ops routes plus the public /sheets/:slug reader — with the actual grid/formula/session machinery kept in core modules so sheets keep working with this plugin off.

role: Pure conditional-formatting rule parser and evaluator for Sheets
description: Parses a tab's raw cond_formats into normalized rules and evaluates gt/lt/eq/between/contains conditions against raw cells to produce sanitized styles woven into the snapshot; also owns the single #rrggbb sanitizer regex shared by Core's manual style path and the plugin's write-gate.

role: A1 address helpers and dense snapshot synthesis for Sheets
description: Pure module converting a sheet tab's sparse cells map into the dense 'rows'/'head'/'merges'/'styles' snapshot embedded in the sheet portable-doc block (capped at 200k positions), plus the shared number/display-string formatting (number_to_display, display_value, sig15) used by every read surface (paper embeds, exports, TUI, Studio grid).

role: CSV/TSV codec (parse/import/export) for the Sheets plugin
description: RFC-4180-ish parser + encoder: strict quote-aware parsing, encoding normalization (UTF-16/CP1252→UTF-8), delimiter sniffing, type inference on import, and CSV-formula-injection guarding on export. Values-only, lossy by design (no styles/formulas/merges).
whatBreaks: CSV/TSV import or export of sheet documents corrupts data, silently mis-infers types, or reopens a formula-injection security hole in Excel/Sheets downloads.

role: The Sheets formula engine — full spreadsheet function library + recompute
description: Massive pure formula engine (100+ Excel-like functions, spill arrays, cycle detection, cross-tab dependency graph, error propagation) that recomputes cached 'v' values for every formula cell on each sheet save; the single source of truth for all sheet computation logic.

role: Sheet cell number-format vocabulary + xlsx numFmt mapping
description: Maps the sheet model's coarse 'fmt' semantic classes (fixed/percent/currency/thousands/date/datetime/checkbox) to/from xlsx numFmtId and canonical format strings, and renders display strings for every read surface (snapshot, Studio grid).

role: Sheet content → standalone HTML export renderer
description: Renders every tab of a sheet document as a self-contained HTML page reusing the PortableDoc article renderer and canonical paper stylesheet, so exports visually match the reader surface.
whatBreaks: The .html sheet export renders blank, unstyled, or diverges visually from the /papers reader.

role: Sheet content → GitHub-flavored Markdown table exporter
description: Renders each tab's dense snapshot as one Markdown table per tab (values only, lossy), synthesizing column-letter headers when no frozen row exists.
whatBreaks: The .md sheet export produces malformed or missing tables.

role: Per-sheet collaborative GenServer serializing ops, undo/redo, persistence
description: Lazily-started, registry-keyed GenServer owning one sheet's in-memory content, applying cell/structural/undo ops from the HTTP ops route with idempotent request_id replay, per-user undo/redo, coalesced recompute+delta broadcast, and debounced persistence through Content.upsert_document; core and plugin-independent.

role: Op-application engine for the Sheets collaborative session GenServer
description: Pure-map machinery (no GenServer state of its own) implementing every wire-shaped Sheets op — set_cell, structural row/col insert/delete, merges, sort, tab rename/add/delete/move/duplicate, conditional formatting, and per-user undo/redo (including per-gesture batch undo groups and multi-tab rename-restore inverses). This is the beating heart of realtime sheet editing; extremely dense, carries duplicated grid-bound constants deliberately kept in sync with Engine/Structure/the plugin gate.
whatBreaks: Any Sheets edit, undo/redo, or structural operation (row insert, merge, sort, tab rename) could corrupt or lose data across every collaborative sheet session.

role: Exactly-once replay cache (ETS-backed GenServer) for retried Sheets ops batches
description: Owns a named public ETS table (`:sheets_ops_replay`) that survives individual session GenServer restarts, so a retried POST /v1/plugins/sheets/:slug/ops with the same request_id replays its cached reply instead of double-applying non-idempotent ops. Bounded (32 entries/key, 1h TTL), node-local, fail-soft.
whatBreaks: A retried ops batch after a session crash could double-apply structural edits (e.g. duplicate row insert) instead of returning the idempotent cached reply.

role: Pure structural rewrite engine for Sheets tabs (row/col insert/delete, formula ref shifting)
description: Implements Excel-style shift/clip semantics for cells, merges, conditional formats, row/col sizes, frozen bands, plus cross-tab reference sweeps (rename/delete/shift), full-axis ranges (A:A, 3:3), and the sort_rows/permute_rows row-permutation machinery with its own formula scanner mirroring the Engine's lexer. No I/O, no Repo — called from Session/Ops after op validation.
whatBreaks: A wrong shift/clip formula rewrite would silently corrupt formula refs or produce wrong #REF!/range results across every sheet with row/col inserts, deletes, sorts, or cross-tab formulas.

role: HTTP controller for GET /v1/plugins/sheets/:slug/export.{xlsx,csv,tsv,md,html}
description: Ingest-token-gated export endpoint; flushes the live editing session first for read-your-writes, resolves draft/published document, and dispatches to Csv/Html/Markdown/XlsxExport converters with a uniform error envelope.
whatBreaks: All spreadsheet export downloads (xlsx/csv/tsv/md/html) fail or serve stale data, including a 503/retry contract other clients depend on.

role: HTTP controller for POST /v1/plugins/sheets/import (multipart upload)
description: Ingest-token-gated import endpoint: detects file kind, enforces byte/cell caps, converts via Csv/XlsxImport, resolves slug/title/dataset, and persists via Content.upsert_document.
whatBreaks: Uploading spreadsheets (xlsx/csv/tsv) to create/update sheet documents fails, or caps meant to prevent OOM/abuse are bypassed.

role: HTTP controller for POST /v1/plugins/sheets/:slug/ops (cell/structural wire ops)
description: Thin shim forwarding batched cell/structural ops (set_cell, insert_rows, merge_cells, undo/redo, etc.) to Sheets.Session.apply_ops, with idempotent request_id retry support and error mapping (404/422/503).
whatBreaks: Live spreadsheet editing (the Studio grid's real-time cell/structure mutation API) breaks or loses exactly-once retry safety.

role: Sheet content → xlsx binary encoder via elixlsx
description: Large, detailed exporter: maps tabs/cells/styles/formats/merges/frozen panes/tab colors to xlsx, translates engine-only formulas, and byte-surgically patches ZIP timestamps for deterministic output. Central round-trip half of XlsxImport.
whatBreaks: xlsx downloads are corrupted, non-deterministic, or lose formulas/styles/merges, breaking Excel interoperability and reproducible export tests.

role: xlsx binary → sheet-document content decoder
description: Combines XlsxReader (values/formulas) with a hand-rolled Saxy XML pass over styles/merges/widths/panes/tab-color; handles shared-formula rebasing, cell caps, and hostile-input guards (OOM bombs via col spans, ZIP64, grid bounds).
whatBreaks: Uploaded xlsx spreadsheets fail to import, lose formulas/formatting, or a hostile file can OOM/crash the import path.

role: Tasks plugin: schema, routes, CLI verbs, quality gate for type:task
description: Wires the task-document substrate as a plugin: registers the task schema, mounts /v1/tasks routes and Oban cron (TTL sweep, compaction), declares bp CLI verbs, enforces a before_save authoring quality gate (empty title halts, missing acceptance_criteria warns), and hydrates/extracts task_edges into the content graph.
whatBreaks: The entire bp task CLI / task board / dependency graph could break — routes vanish, malformed tasks get silently saved or valid ones rejected, or task dependency edges stop projecting into the content graph.

role: Studio LiveView kanban/deck board for the native Barkpark task system
description: Very large (3300+ lines) LiveView at /admin/projects rendering task cards with realtime PubSub updates, drag-to-restage through fenced Tasks primitives (claim/close/release), grouping/filtering via URL params, a task peek inspector panel with full family-tree/lineage/blockers/events, and a deck/gantt view. All writes funnel through Tasks.claim_by_id/close/release — never raw Content writes.
whatBreaks: The entire task board UI (kanban, deck, peek, drag actions) used to manage all bp task work in Studio would break or corrupt task state via bad optimistic writes.

role: Tickets plugin entrypoint: schema registration + full charter route table
description: Declares the private `ticket` document type/schema, the desk item, and the complete 4-bucket route table (submitter :ticket_key, operator :token_root, admin :api key-mint, Studio :admin LiveView) plus a merge-safe CLI delegate. Off by default; routes reference sibling-slice modules safely even before they exist.
whatBreaks: Wrong route/auth-bucket wiring here would expose ticket data to the wrong auth tier or break the entire Tickets feature (submission, triage, key mint) at once.

role: Security gate for ticket attachment uploads (magic-byte MIME sniffing + storage)
description: The mandatory hostile-upload trust boundary for outsider-submitted ticket attachments: derives MIME from magic bytes only (never client Content-Type/extension), enforces allowlist/size/count caps, then stores via the Media plugin and stamps the asset with owning ticket/key ids for scoped retrieval.
whatBreaks: A bypassed sniff/allow check would let an outside ticket-key holder upload disguised executables or leak another ticket's attachment via a scoping bug.

role: bp CLI manifest command definitions for ticket + ticket-key nouns
description: Returns static command maps (operator verbs inbox/show/answer/close, admin ticket-key mint/ls/rotate/pause/unpause/revoke) in the frozen cli_command() shape consumed by the /v1/capabilities manifest; deliberately omits submitter verbs since no bp credential can run them.
whatBreaks: A malformed command map would break `bp ticket`/`bp ticket-key` CLI generation or misrepresent auth tiers in the capabilities manifest.

role: Pure builder for the ticket key onboarding handoff card text
description: Given a host URL and freshly-minted raw ticket key, returns a fixed multi-line string (raw key + 3 curl examples + etiquette note) shown once on mint/rotate. Pure, no DB/config/clock, golden-tested.
whatBreaks: A broken handoff card would give a new ticket-key holder wrong/non-working curl commands, blocking their onboarding but nothing else in the system.

role: Studio operator LiveView for the Tickets inbox (triage/answer/close/key-mgmt)
description: Plugin-owned LiveView at /studio/tickets rendering three status partitions (needs answer/waiting on them/recently closed) via InboxPresenter, thread view, composer (answer/answer&close/close), and key management (mint/rotate/pause). All writes go through Thread.operator_answer/operator_close and Keys, wrapped in a safely/2 seam degrading DB blips to an error state.
whatBreaks: The entire Studio operator UI for managing support tickets (triage, answering, key minting) would break or crash the Studio session.

role: Pure render-model builder for the Tickets Studio inbox (partition/sort/format)
description: Takes ticket maps + now and returns the partitioned (needs_answer/waiting_on_them/recently_closed), sorted, humanized-age view rows including the submitter 'seen' delivery signal. No DB, dual string/atom key tolerance, exhaustively unit-testable in isolation.
whatBreaks: Wrong sort/partition logic would misorder or misclassify tickets in the operator's triage queue, e.g. burying an urgent open ticket behind answered ones.

role: Ticket-key auth tier: mint/verify/rotate/pause/revoke
description: Implements the low-trust TICKET-KEY credential tier riding the api_tokens table (kind=="ticket"), deliberately inert against normal token auth (Auth.verify_token filters kind=="api"). verify/1 is the sole resolver RequireTicketKey consumes; revocation/expiry/kind are enforced in the WHERE clause so a dead key is indistinguishable from missing.
whatBreaks: A bug here could let a ticket key escalate to normal-token privileges or leak whether a revoked/foreign key exists, breaking the whole Tickets low-trust security model.

role: Ticket conversation thread + lifecycle state machine
description: Owns the append-only ticket message thread and the pure open/answered/closed transition, plus CAS-append persistence through Barkpark.Content, fail-closed key-scoping, and the shared operator answer/close orchestration used by both HTTP and Studio's inbox so both emit identical mutation events.
whatBreaks: A scoping or CAS bug could leak one submitter's tickets to another, corrupt concurrent replies, or desync HTTP vs Studio event emission.

role: Pure sort/ordering logic for the operator ticket inbox
description: Stateless comparator ordering tickets open(oldest-waiting)→answered(newest)→closed(newest), plus waiting_age/2 for the 'how long has this waited' signal; shared by HTTP and the Studio LiveView so ordering never forks.
whatBreaks: A wrong sort key would misorder the operator inbox (e.g. hide the longest-waiting ticket), but no data corruption or security exposure.

role: Single deep-walk traversal over PortableDoc block trees
description: Unifies what used to be three parallel private tree walkers (wikilink/blockref targets, embed targets, ref/href harvest) into one pure collect/2 + collect_nodes/2 API; used by edge extraction (valueref/task-wikilink → content_edges) and other pre-resolve passes.
whatBreaks: A traversal bug would silently drop or duplicate wikilink/embed/valueref targets across every consumer that relies on it, corrupting link resolution and the content-edges graph.

role: Pure structural-declaration validator for PortableDoc block trees
description: Checks a block list against presence/cardinality/position declarations (index, not_index, top/bottom group, before/after relations) keyed by role/type string or composition tier atom; Content-free by design, consumed by Content.Papers.Template's enforcement layer plus slot/query-type gates.
whatBreaks: A validator bug would let malformed/out-of-order papers pass silently or falsely reject valid ones, breaking template structural guarantees across every paper doc type.

role: GFM markdown to PortableDoc block-list converter (Claude chat replies)
description: Converts assistant markdown replies into native PortableDoc blocks so chat renders through the same paper engine as every other surface; supports a ```mermaid fence (diagram block) and a ```portabledoc fence (raw JSON block splice, validated against an allowlist). Fail-soft throughout — degrades to a code block on any parse error.
whatBreaks: A parsing/escaping bug could corrupt chat message rendering or, worse, let disallowed block types slip through the portabledoc fence into the render pipeline.

role: Pure block-tree patch engine for PortableDoc (six ops)
description: Implements append/insert-after/patch/replace/remove/move ops over the PortableDoc block tree as pure, immutable functions with structured errors; also enforces template-lock placement and constraint-vocabulary cardinality/order rules. This is the cross-surface op contract every producer (CLI/SDK/Studio) and the Go pdrender twin build against, pinned by golden fixtures.
whatBreaks: Any editor op (Studio canvas, CLI, SDK) that patches a paper/document block tree could corrupt content, silently drop locked blocks, or break constraint enforcement across every PortableDoc-backed surface.

role: Bound/free block partition + project-on-write for PortableDoc
description: Sole writer of content[fieldName] and content["body"] derived from a document's block list, keeping the classic field index in sync with the block-based editor (Exp-P2); also derives content["preview"] when a resolver is supplied. Central no-drift guarantee for the block↔field-index relationship.

role: Facade: PortableDoc block/Pd-tree → inline-styled HTML renderer
description: Pure string-emission renderer (email + article palettes/themes) that composes blocks into a Pd-tree and walks it to HTML; delegates to Render.{Util,Palettes,Inline,Forms,Figures,Compose,Walk} submodules. Feeds body_html caches, PubSub deltas, and email export; version-stamps output for cache-staleness detection and mirrors the Go pdrender ANSI renderer via shared golden fixtures.

role: Email-safe inline-styled HTML emitters for cards/notes/pipeline blocks
description: Pure snapshot-driven leaf renderers producing inline style="" HTML (table-based layout) for cards, card, notes, note, pipeline, stage block types — the email-client-safe twin of the classed Render.Components emitters, sharing helpers so a stage and a pipeline node render byte-identical cells.
whatBreaks: Broken markup here would corrupt outgoing paper/email renders in mail clients (Outlook etc.) for any doc using these block types, though the article/Studio render path is unaffected.

role: Classed HTML emitters for task-tracking PortableDoc blocks (article style)
description: Pure snapshot-driven renderers for tasks, task-detail, cards, card, pipeline, stage, notes, status-legend, task-board, roadmap blocks, producing the classed bp-* markup styled by paper-surface.css; derives status glyph/colour from the shared StatusVocab manifest, no DB access.
whatBreaks: A rendering bug would break the visual task/board/roadmap UI on every paper and public reader page using these block types.

role: Core block-type dispatch: PortableDoc block map to Pd-tree node
description: The central compose_block/1,2,3 clause set — one match arm per block type (heading, paragraph, list, callout, section, image, sheet, field-*, terminal, columns, data-viz, task fleet, cards/notes/pipeline, etc.) mapping raw block JSON to intermediate PdNode trees consumed by the walker; theme/style-aware dispatch routes article vs email variants. This is the single largest and most load-bearing file in the PortableDoc render engine.
whatBreaks: Any regression here breaks rendering for one or more block types across every paper, email, Studio canvas, and public reader surface simultaneously — the highest-blast-radius file in the render pipeline.

role: Data-viz block emitters (stat/stats/heatmap/chart) — article + email HTML
description: Pure, snapshot-driven leaf emitters producing classed SVG/HTML (article) and inline-styled table/box fallbacks (email) for stat, stats/stat-grid, heatmap, and chart blocks; mirrors semantics of the Go pdrender TUI renderers (stat.go/heatmap.go/chart.go) for cross-surface parity.
whatBreaks: A bug would break chart/stat/heatmap visualization rendering across papers and their email variants, though scoped to those specific block types.

role: PortableDoc render: figure/code-block/divider/diagram/asciicast HTML emitters
description: Leaf HTML emitters for code blocks, section dividers, Mermaid diagrams, and asciinema recordings inside the PortableDoc render engine. Article mode emits the live-runtime mount points (pre.mermaid, bp-asciicast) that JS hooks upgrade; email mode intentionally omits them and degrades to plain code/links, so the runtime never mistakenly triggers in email.
whatBreaks: Wrong escaping or a leaked/missing mount-point marker would break Mermaid/asciicast rendering in Studio/papers or falsely trigger runtimes inside emails.

role: Email-safe inline-styled HTML emitters for task-fleet blocks (tasks/board/roadmap/detail)
description: Renders the same task/roadmap snapshots as the classed Studio components but with table scaffolding and inline styles only, since email clients ignore paper-surface.css. Draws colors from Palettes.email_skin and StatusVocab.tones so email never drifts from the reader's status vocabulary.
whatBreaks: Broken markup or wrong theme/tone mapping would corrupt task-fleet emails (e.g. Outlook rendering) or desync status colors from the live reader.

role: Render-only HTML emitter for PortableDoc form/questionnaire ("grill") blocks
description: Emits fieldset/legend/control markup per question type (yesno/single/multi/scale/text) with no script or submit wiring; caps scale ranges to prevent a render-time DoS from an attacker-supplied huge scale.max. Article and email modes differ only in inline style cues.
whatBreaks: A malformed control or missing scale cap could crash the renderer or allow a memory-exhaustion DoS on public /papers/:slug renders.

role: Inline node/mark composer folding ProseMirror-style inline JSON into Pd-tree nodes
description: Core inline-composition step of the PortableDoc render pipeline: turns text/strong/em/link/wikilink/blockref/tag/valueref nodes and mark lists into PdText/PdLink/PdWikilink/etc nodes for the Walk renderer to emit. Heavily fail-soft (never raises) on malformed/typeless/scalar inputs so a bad node degrades instead of 500ing saves, body_html, delta frames, and Studio view; has a Go pdrender parity twin.
whatBreaks: A regression here breaks inline text rendering (bold/italic/links/wikilinks/valuerefs) across every paper/document view, edit, and delta path, or reintroduces 500s on malformed inline JSON.

role: Per-render color/font/width palettes (email vs article) for PortableDoc rendering
description: Defines the runtime palette threaded through walk/3: email_palette/article_palette resolve theme-keyed skins from TokensGen (with CSS var() fallbacks for article mode so it flips with host theme), plus font/width constants. palette_for/2 is the dispatch point every renderer consumes.

role: Email-safe inline-styled HTML emitters for panel blocks (terminal/columns/status-legend)
description: Table-based, fully inline-styled twins of the classed article panel emitters, for stylesheet-less mail clients. Draws chrome colors from Palettes.email_skin and status colors from StatusVocab.tones; nested child blocks are pre-composed at evergreen theme only (documented tradeoff).
whatBreaks: Broken markup would corrupt terminal/columns/legend panels in emailed papers; wrong tone mapping desyncs legend colors from the reader.

role: Compile-time loader of the task status vocabulary from design/status-manifest.json
description: Single source of truth for status→role, role→glyph/spinner/label/meaning, read at compile time from the repo-root manifest via @external_resource; sibling surfaces (CSS tones, Go pdrender, web) derive from the same manifest via a check script. Marked @canonical capability:status-vocabulary.
whatBreaks: A drift or bug here would desync task status glyphs/colors/labels across email, article, and CSS surfaces, since this is the one Elixir-side source of truth.

role: Compile-time loader of the canonical paper-surface CSS for all render sinks
description: Reads api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css at compile time (via @external_resource) and exposes it as css/0, consumed by root.html.heex (Studio), bulldocs.html.heex (/papers reader), and the standalone sheet HTML export so View/Edit parity holds by construction instead of hand-mirrored CSS.
whatBreaks: A load failure or stale embed would break styling across Studio, the public papers reader, and standalone sheet exports simultaneously.

role: Generated design-token module (colors/fonts) for paper render surfaces, from design/tokens.json
description: Auto-generated by design/emit.mjs — DO NOT EDIT by hand. Provides theme-keyed (evergreen/ember/fjord) status tones, reading accent, reading font/weight/size, the full email skin per theme, and callout tone tints, consumed by Palettes, Util, Figures, FleetEmail, PanelsEmail.
whatBreaks: Any drift from design/tokens.json or a broken regeneration would desync colors/fonts across every render surface (email, article, callouts, status legends) that reads it.

role: Leaf HTML-escaping, URL-safety, and callout-tone helpers for PortableDoc render
description: Pure dependency-free helpers used across the whole render family: escape_html/escape_attr (fail-soft on non-binary), safe_url (scheme allowlist guarding against protocol-relative/javascript: URLs, with JS/Go parity twins), and tone_palette/1 wrapping TokensGen callout colors.

role: Pd-tree to inline-styled HTML recursive walker for PortableDoc render
description: Recursive `walk/3` plus one private renderer per PdNode kind (heading, paragraph, text, link, wikilink, sheet, table, valueref, task chip, etc.), emitting HTML for both `:email` (byte-frozen inline styles) and `:article` (bare semantic elements + `.bp-paper-surface` classes) palettes. Extracted verbatim from `Render` per the theme-vs-data contract; degrades unknown/malformed nodes instead of raising.
whatBreaks: Every paper/email render surface (reader, Studio View, TUI parity, exported HTML) would emit broken or unstyled markup, or crash on malformed Pd-trees.

role: PortableDoc widget slot vocabulary (callout/card/note/stage typed slots)
description: Pure, DB-free module defining slot declarations for widget block types, synthesizing legacy content into slot form for backward compatibility, and providing byte-identity accessors (callout_body_inline, card_title_text, etc.) plus the D1 tier-gate validator. Central to keeping legacy and slots-native encodings render-identical.
whatBreaks: Callout/card/note/stage widgets would render incorrectly or lose byte-parity between legacy and slots-materialized encodings across reader/Studio/TUI.

role: Lazy legacy-doc block synthesis + create-time scaffold for PortableDoc
description: Builds an in-memory block list for legacy documents lacking content["blocks"] (synthesize/3) and for brand-new Expectation-bearing docs (scaffold/4), plus a Classic-save bound-only patch helper to avoid data loss. Pure, no Repo access; the no-rewrite invariant (synthesize→project round-trips byte-equal) is load-bearing.
whatBreaks: A legacy document's first Beta-open in the block editor could lose or corrupt existing field values/body content, or a Classic form save could wipe free blocks/block order.

role: Resolves query-carrying task blocks into live task snapshots for papers
description: Pure block-tree traversal (`resolve/2`, `preview/2`, `apply_preview/2`) turning a paper's task-block `query` into fetched rows/aggregate tallies via injected fetcher functions, keeping Studio's diff baseline unresolved while enabling live rendering; also maps raw task docs into component snapshot rows (`row_from_task/1`).
whatBreaks: Live task lists/boards/roadmaps/dataviz blocks embedded in papers would show stale or missing data, or Studio's continuous-save diffing could persist stale snapshots into documents.

role: Canonical element/widget/section tier classifier for PortableDoc block types
description: Pure classification table mapping every renderable block `type` string to its composition-doctrine tier (`:element`/`:widget`/`:section`); a completeness test enforces it stays in sync with the render surface. Consumed by Slots.tier/1 for the D1 slot gate.
whatBreaks: Slot-nesting validation and future layout/parity gates would misclassify block types, silently allowing invalid nesting or breaking the completeness test that guards new block types.

role: Pure OpenGraph-style preview manifest projector for documents
description: Computes a document's shareable preview card (title/description/image/extensions) from content+blocks at write time, with a Repo-free `project/3` and an injectable `media_resolver` closure for rich images; per-doctype extension fallbacks (paper/task/sheet/ticket) with a truncation/fallback chain. Marked `@canonical capability:preview-manifest`.

role: Short-lived HS256 JWT signer/verifier for unpublished-draft preview access
description: Mints and verifies preview tokens with jti-based replay protection and DB-backed revocation (no Redis); verify_and_record combines signature/expiry/revocation checks with single-use enforcement, and sweep/1 reaps stale rows.
whatBreaks: Preview links could leak unpublished drafts to unauthorized parties, allow token replay, or reject legitimate preview requests across every surface offering draft previews.

role: Core Pulse public event-channel machinery (Shared Storm substrate)
description: Anonymous, rate-limited, schema-validated public event ingest/feed system: channel config lookup, payload validation/coercion, atomic event insert + durable counter increment, cursor-based feed reads, TTL sweep, and cost-meter accounting. Backs the `Barkpark.Plugins.Pulse` thin plugin wiring.

role: GenServer sampling live BEAM/CPU cost telemetry for Pulse channels
description: 2s-tick sampler computing real scheduler CPU utilization, memory, cursor/strike rates, and euro-cost estimates via `:persistent_term`/`:counters` for lock-free hot-path bumps; broadcasts a `vitals` event per channel topic and periodically flushes cost to the durable meter.
whatBreaks: The live cost/vitals dashboard on public Storm demos would show wrong or stale numbers, or (if crashing) stop broadcasting vitals; core ingest is unaffected since bumps degrade to no-ops.

role: Oban cron worker TTL-sweeping ephemeral pulse_events rows
description: Thin wrapper calling `Barkpark.Pulse.sweep/0` on a schedule; scheduled only when the pulse plugin is enabled, never raises on empty config.
whatBreaks: Pulse event rows would never be purged, causing unbounded table growth (or, if buggy, could wrongly delete durable counters if it drifted from sweep/0's contract).

role: Hyperquiz public context facade delegating to per-room GenServers
description: Thin pass-through API (`join/3`, `submit_answer/3`, `tally/1`, phase transitions, cursor/heat topics, PIN generation) to `Barkpark.Quiz.Room`; the entry point every Quiz channel/LiveView calls.

role: GenServer bridging Studio quiz edits to live running quiz rooms
description: Subscribes to per-dataset document-mutation PubSub topics; on a `quiz` document change, reloads and re-applies the question to every room bound to that quiz id (tracked per-pin per-dataset), enabling live-edit-to-running-game updates with no reconnect. Defers its own PubSub subscribe past boot-order races.
whatBreaks: Live edits to a quiz document in Studio would silently fail to propagate to running game rooms (stale questions shown to players), though initial room load/answering still works.

role: Bridges stored quiz Barkpark doc to Room's question shape
description: Defines the private schema-v2 'quiz' document type and parses stored doc content into the Room's in-memory question shape (id/prompt/choices/answer). Notable: schema is private-visibility so the answer key never leaks via public content API; load_question is the server-side-only path the Room uses.
whatBreaks: Wrong parsing would either leak correct answers to players or crash quiz question loading, falling back to the P1 hardcoded question.

role: Binary wire codec for batched quiz cursor positions
description: Quantizes normalized 0.0-1.0 cursor coords to 16-bit ints and encodes/decodes a delta frame (<<count, entries>>) broadcast at ~15Hz per room, keeping the wire O(N) instead of O(N^2). Pure functional codec, no state.
whatBreaks: Encode/decode mismatch would corrupt cursor positions or crash the client-side rendering of live cursors in the quiz room.

role: Fixed-size aggregate crowd-density encoder for large quiz rooms
description: Buckets quantized cursor positions into a 32x32 grid and encodes counts as a constant-size binary (O(1) regardless of player count), used above a player-count threshold instead of per-cursor frames to scale to 10k+ players.
whatBreaks: Large rooms above the heatmap threshold would send corrupted or oversized payloads, breaking the crowd-density visualization at scale.

role: Per-room GenServer owning live quiz state and realtime fan-out
description: Core stateful engine for the Hyperquiz feature: manages players, question phases, tallies, scoring, cursor/hover broadcasts, and idle/lifecycle timers via PubSub; lazily started, ephemeral, capped at 2000 players/room. Central to all realtime quiz behavior.
whatBreaks: A bug here breaks live quiz gameplay entirely — join/answer/score/reveal flow, cursor fan-out, or could leak the answer key or crash/zombie rooms.

role: Read-only observability helper for live quiz rooms
description: Exposes live_room_count/0 and room_stats/1 for ops/dashboard visibility into Registry-tracked quiz rooms; rooms also emit telemetry ticks independently.
whatBreaks: Only monitoring/dashboards would show wrong numbers; no impact on core quiz gameplay.

role: ETS-backed token-bucket rate limiter used by API plugs
description: Simple public ETS table implementing per-key (IP/token) token-bucket rate limiting with opportunistic pruning of stale buckets once the table exceeds a size bound, to prevent unbounded growth in the long-lived server.
whatBreaks: A broken limiter could either let abusive clients hammer the API unthrottled or wrongly block legitimate traffic API-wide, and unbounded pruning bugs could leak memory over time.

role: Shared secret-scrubbing engine for plugin error logs
description: Recursively redacts values under caller-supplied sensitive header/JSON keys from maps, lists, and JSON-looking strings so secrets never leak into inspect/Logger/test output; single-owner replacement for three duplicated per-plugin copies (Github, Indx, OnixEdit.Bokbasen). Marked @canonical capability:secret-redaction.
whatBreaks: Bearer tokens or OAuth secrets could leak into logs/error dumps across every plugin that relies on this module.

role: Production release task runner (migrations + seeds)
description: Provides mix-free `migrate/0` and `seed/0` tasks used in production deployments to run Ecto migrations and seed scripts without the Mix toolchain.
whatBreaks: Production migrations fail to run on deploy, leaving the database schema out of sync with the running BEAM code.

role: first-run crypto secret generator for local installs
description: Generates SECRET_KEY_BASE, PREVIEW_JWT_SECRET, and BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY and idempotently writes them to ~/.barkpark/.env for personal installs. Never touches the database; used only at setup time.
whatBreaks: Personal/local installs fail to bootstrap cryptographic secrets, preventing the server from starting in production mode.

role: Ecto.Repo — the single Postgres connection pool for the app
description: Standard Ecto.Repo definition plus a shared uuid_or_nil/1 guard (marked @canonical) that safely casts caller-supplied ids to binary_id UUIDs, used by every Repo.get/where on a binary_id primary key to avoid Ecto.CastError 500s.
whatBreaks: Every database read/write in the entire application depends on this module; a defect here (or in the uuid guard used app-wide) would break persistence globally or reintroduce 500s on malformed ids.

role: Boot-time GenServer that registers every plugin's schemas/checkers/seeders
description: One-shot supervised child (returns :ignore) positioned after Repo+Plugins.Registry and before Oban in the supervision tree, so plugin schemas/checkers/codelists are guaranteed registered before any Oban job dequeues; wraps the whole sequence in try/rescue so one broken plugin can't crash boot.
whatBreaks: Wrong supervision ordering or a raised error here could leave plugin schemas unregistered at boot, causing Oban workers or early requests to fail against nonexistent schemas application-wide.

role: SCIM 2.0 user/group provisioning and org-scoped directory sync
description: Implements IdP-facing provisioning/deprovisioning of users (with session/membership revocation on deprovision) and group-to-role mapping for org tenants, all audited and strictly org-isolated via workspace scoping.
whatBreaks: A bug could let a SCIM token leak/mutate another organization's users, fail to revoke access on deprovision, or silently break enterprise IdP-driven onboarding/offboarding.

role: Ecto schema for a SCIM group mapped to a Barkpark role
description: Standard Ecto schema/changeset for scim_groups table, scoping a display_name/role_name/external_id to an Organization with uniqueness on display_name per org.
whatBreaks: Invalid changeset validation could allow duplicate/unscoped groups or malformed role mappings, corrupting SCIM group provisioning.

role: Ecto schema for per-org SCIM bearer tokens
description: Stores only the SHA-256 hash of a SCIM token (never plaintext) scoped to one Organization, plus a hash_token/1 helper used for minting and lookup in Barkpark.Scim.
whatBreaks: A hashing or scoping bug could allow forged/cross-org SCIM authentication or make legitimate tokens unusable.

role: Ecto schema for search aggregate rows
description: Defines the Ecto schema mapping to the search_intel_crystals table — stores rolled-up search metrics (count, zero-hits, CTR, duration) per surface/scope/period bucket.
whatBreaks: Search analytics crystallization cannot read or write aggregate rows, breaking the search intelligence dashboard and synonym auto-generation.

role: Rolls raw search events into day/week/month analytics aggregates
description: Surface-agnostic crystallization job: aggregates search_intel_* events into query-performance crystals and click/merge-pattern transitions, with idempotent upserts and self-healing trailing-window backfill for missed cron runs or Oban failures.
whatBreaks: Search analytics dashboards/insights would show wrong or stale query performance and merge-pattern data, or backfill gaps would silently persist, but core search/read paths are unaffected.

role: Postgres full-text/trigram search Retriever implementation
description: The default (Postgres-backed) implementation of Barkpark.Search.Retriever: builds tsvector/trigram match queries, applies tenancy/owner/grant scoping, bounded ranking pools, facet counts, and perspective (published/drafts/raw) filtering for document search.
whatBreaks: A scoping or perspective-filter bug here could leak private/draft documents or another workspace's rows through the public search API — the primary defense-in-depth seam for search visibility.

role: Ecto schema for search analytics events
description: Defines the search_intel_events table schema with fields for surface, scope, query, result_count, zero_hits, actor_key, session_key, quality, and click-tracking (position, object_id). Used by Search.Intelligence to persist search telemetry.
whatBreaks: Search analytics fail to persist or query, breaking Intelligence suggestions and zero-hit reporting.

role: search quality golden-query evaluation harness
description: Loads JSONL fixture files of golden queries, runs them against live document/media search, and computes MRR, NDCG@10, and zero-hit-rate metrics. Also provides compare/2 to detect regressions against a baseline.
whatBreaks: Search quality regression detection is broken — developers cannot benchmark or catch MRR/NDCG regressions in search results.

role: Builds highlighted-snippet maps for search hits, redaction-aware
description: Wraps matched query terms in <mark> tags for document and media search results, HTML-escaping every segment (fixed a stored-XSS gap) and dropping content.* highlight fields the caller's schema doesn't permit via Envelope.field_readable?. Fails closed on missing schema/caller_context.
whatBreaks: A regression here either leaks redacted field content in search snippets or reintroduces stored XSS via unescaped highlight markup.

role: Search analytics engine — records events, suggestions, insights
description: Core module behind the search-intelligence feature: records search/interaction/correction events (never raising), computes autocomplete suggestions (recent/popular/nohits), aggregates period insights (quality, top queries, merge patterns, zero-hit/recovery rates) and auto-promotes synonyms after repeated corrections. Heavily relied on by any surface calling into Barkpark.Search.Intelligence.

role: Media DAM adapter translating media search params into search analytics context
description: Thin adapter over Barkpark.Search.Intelligence for the media surface — records searches/interactions, produces suggestions/insights, and normalizes WoodWing-style v1 media search params (offset/query/filters) into the shared analytics context shape. Meant to be the only entry point for Media Desk/picker/API instead of calling core Intelligence directly.
whatBreaks: Media search analytics (suggestions, insights, recorded searches) would be miscounted or malformed for the Media Desk and picker.

role: search intel merge pattern Ecto schema
description: Ecto schema for the search_intel_merge_patterns table, tracking transitions between search query fingerprints per surface/scope/period. A narrow analytics data model with no business logic.
whatBreaks: Search intelligence merge pattern recording breaks, losing analytics data about query refinement patterns.

role: Tokenizes raw search query strings into terms/phrases/excludes/prefixes
description: Small, pure parser: extracts quoted phrases, -excluded tokens, and trailing-* prefix terms from a query string; guards against non-binary input (e.g. array query params) by returning an empty parse instead of raising.
whatBreaks: Every document and media search query passes through this — a parsing bug changes what matches for effectively all search requests.

role: Unified search pipeline orchestrator: parse → expand → retrieve → recover → highlight
description: The single entry point (Barkpark.Search.QueryPipeline.search/4) that all search surfaces (documents, media) call: parses the raw query, expands synonyms, dispatches to the configured retriever engine (Postgres or Indx), runs zero-hit/thin-result recovery strategies, and assembles highlights.
whatBreaks: Since every document/media search request funnels through this module, a defect breaks search app-wide or reintroduces the tenant/grant leak this module's opts-threading was built to prevent.

role: search engine behaviour / seam contract
description: Defines the `@callback search/4` behaviour that all search engine implementations must satisfy. Plugins swap the engine by registering a module under a name; the dispatcher falls back to Postgres when the engine is unknown, so surfaces never go dark on misconfiguration.
whatBreaks: Custom search engines (e.g. Indx) cannot be plugged in correctly, or the seam contract drifts from implementations, breaking engine dispatch silently.

role: search engine retriever registry
description: Registry that maps engine names (e.g. 'postgres', 'indx') to their retriever module implementations. Plugins extend it via application config; unknown engines fall back to the Postgres default so surfaces stay live on misconfiguration.
whatBreaks: Plugin-registered search engines (e.g. Indx) silently fall back to Postgres, returning wrong results for surfaces configured with a custom engine.

role: Query quality gate — normalizes and rejects bad search query text
description: Shared normalize/reject logic used by all search surfaces: trims/collapses whitespace, enforces length bounds, rejects spam/profanity/control-char/punctuation-only queries, guards invalid UTF-8. Deliberately does not block SQL-keyword-shaped queries (relies on parameterized Ecto + ILIKE escaping instead).
whatBreaks: A bug could let junk/spam queries pollute analytics and synonym auto-promotion, or wrongly reject legitimate queries across every search surface.

role: Ecto schema/changeset for per-surface search tuning config
description: Defines the search_surface_config table (searchable_fields, typo_policy, zero_hit_strategy, highlight_fields) and a cast-based changeset that rejects wrong-typed caller PUT payloads with a 422 instead of crashing at dump time.
whatBreaks: A weakened changeset would let malformed config values crash the search-config update endpoint (500) instead of failing cleanly.

role: Cached loader/upsert API for per-surface search config, hot read path
description: Wraps SurfaceConfig with a bounded, TTL'd ETS cache (60s, max 512 entries, clear-on-full) keyed by {surface, scope}; provides defaults for documents/media surfaces, upsert with cache invalidation, and a seed_defaults! used at boot/seed time. Sits on the hot path for every document/media search request.

role: Ecto schema for search synonyms
description: Thin Ecto schema defining the search_synonyms table shape: surface, scope, from/to query, kind (one_way/bidirectional), source, enabled flag, and tenant foreign keys.
whatBreaks: Synonym query/insertion fails at the DB layer, disabling synonym-based search expansion.

role: Synonym CRUD + query-expansion and auto-promotion logic
description: Manages one_way/alt_correction synonym rows per (surface, scope): search_terms/correction_for expand queries during search, candidates/promote surface and auto-create synonyms from merge-pattern analytics, and create/delete/list back the admin synonym management UI. Dual-writes dataset_id alongside the legacy scope string.

role: Oban background job for search crystallization
description: Thin Oban worker that delegates to Crystallizer.crystallize_due/1 for a given date, scheduling search index crystallization as a background job.
whatBreaks: Search index crystallization stops running on schedule, causing stale or missing search results.

role: Oban background job for search index pruning
description: Thin Oban worker that calls Intelligence.prune/1 with a configurable retention period to delete stale search index entries.
whatBreaks: Search index grows unbounded without pruning old entries, causing storage and performance degradation over time.

role: Cloud run-secrets store facade — encrypted admin-managed secret KV
description: CRUD for encrypted-at-rest secrets (get/reveal/put/list/delete), atomic with an audit-log write for set/reveal/delete; get/1 is unaudited for cheap resolver polling. ingest_token/0 resolves the effective ingest shared-secret DB-first with config-env fallback, letting an admin rotate the token without redeploy.
whatBreaks: Broken secret storage/rotation could lock out ingest auth or leak/lose admin-managed secrets, and unaudited mutations would break the compliance trail.

role: Ecto schema for the secrets_audit table (set/reveal/delete log rows)
description: Simple schema + changeset enforcing the action vocabulary (set/reveal/delete) for audit rows written by Barkpark.Secrets. Mirrors Barkpark.Plugins.SettingsAudit.
whatBreaks: A malformed changeset here would silently corrupt or block secret-access audit logging.

role: Ecto schema for the secrets table (encrypted value keyed by name)
description: Persisted secret row with a Barkpark.EncryptedBinary-encrypted value column, string primary key `name`, and updated_by/updated_at tracking.
whatBreaks: Schema/encryption mismatch would corrupt stored secrets or break decryption for every reader of Barkpark.Secrets, including ingest_token/0.

role: Profile-switched DB seed dispatcher (demo vs clean)
description: Entry point invoked by priv/repo/seeds.exs / Barkpark.Release.seed/0: reads BARKPARK_SEED_PROFILE, delegates to Seeds.Demo or Seeds.Clean, then always runs the profile-independent tail (plugin schema bootstrap + search surface config defaults) so neither profile can forget them.
whatBreaks: A broken dispatcher would leave a fresh dev/prod database without demo content, plugin schemas, or search defaults, breaking `make seed`/`mix ecto.reset` and initial deploys.

role: clean-install seed profile
description: Seeds a minimal fresh install: creates the default welcome paper (idempotent, skips if already present) and bootstraps an admin token from env or generates one, printing it once. Used by bp setup.
whatBreaks: New installs via bp setup land without an admin token or with duplicate tokens, breaking initial access to the system.

role: Demo seed data — 8 schemas, ~27 documents, dev token, codelists
description: 668-line verbatim extraction of the original seeds.exs demo profile: defines schema_definitions (post, author, mediaAsset, etc. with field/layout/prefill config) and sample documents, then seeds the dev API token and EDItEUR/Thema codelists. Purely data-shaping, invoked only by Seeds.run(:demo).
whatBreaks: A malformed schema/document literal breaks local dev seeding and any demo-profile deploy, but does not affect production runtime logic once seeded.

role: Shared tenancy groundwork helper for every seed profile
description: Get-or-creates the Default Workspace/Project/dataset row and seeds the three global built-in roles (owner/admin/member), providing a stamp_schema_scope helper so every seeded schema/document lands under the Default tenant scope. Extracted verbatim from the old seeds.exs preamble; idempotent, safe to run repeatedly.
whatBreaks: A fresh mix ecto.reset would seed documents/schemas with missing or wrong tenancy scope, making them invisible to every scoped read on a new install.

role: Facade over the self-update Checker GenServer status API
description: Exposes enabled?/0, config/0, status/0, check_now/0 with a fail-closed contract (never raises; degrades to :disabled/:unknown when the Checker process is absent or dies). Owns base_status/1, the canonical status-map shape shared with the Checker.
whatBreaks: A crash here (violating the never-raise contract) could take down instance boot or the admin Studio self-update panel, though the feature is off by default.

role: GenServer polling upstream GitHub release info periodically
description: Timer-driven check comparing running release vs latest upstream release (integer 3-tuple compare), populating digest/notes/fork-advice fields in the status map; fully fail-closed (rescue+catch wraps run_check).
whatBreaks: Bugs would surface wrong/stuck update-availability status in the admin UI, but the fail-closed design limits blast radius to display-only wrongness.

role: Behaviour defining the self-update upstream client contract
description: Declares latest_release/1, digest/3, release_notes/2 callbacks that GitHub and Fake implementations must satisfy; the seam letting tests swap in Client.Fake.
whatBreaks: A contract drift would break either the real GitHub client or test fakes, but self-update is a dormant, non-critical feature.

role: Test double for the self-update Client behaviour
description: Reads scripted responses from Application env on every call so tests can re-prime per-check; supports per-repo scripting for fork-advice tests.
whatBreaks: Only self-update-related tests would break or give false confidence; no production impact.

role: Real self-update client hitting the GitHub REST API via Req
description: Lists tags to find latest vA.B.C release, fetches commit digest between tags, and fetches curated release notes; unauthenticated, fail-closed (never raises, wraps all failures as {:error, reason}).
whatBreaks: Wrong parsing/HTTP handling would misreport update availability or crash the check (mitigated by Checker's own rescue), affecting only the optional self-update feature.

role: GenServer executing the self-update apply command via OS Port
description: Single-flight trigger/0 runs a configured shell command (default scripts/self-update.sh) as a Port, streaming output into a bounded log; gated off by default and only enabled via BARKPARK_SELF_UPDATE_APPLY=1 in prod; never crashes on port failures.
whatBreaks: If enabled and buggy, could fail to apply updates cleanly or misreport run status, but the default-off gate and never-crash contract bound the risk to opted-in prod instances.

role: Context for item-level (P7) revocable share-link tokens
description: Mints, resolves, revokes, and lists opaque /s/<token> share links bound to a single document or media item; stores only the SHA256 of the raw token, caps TTL at 1 year, and treats revoked/expired/missing links identically to avoid existence leaks.
whatBreaks: Item share links could leak content past revocation/expiry, fail to distinguish access levels, or a bignum TTL could hang a request/produce an unrevocable link.

role: Ecto schema for share links
description: Defines the share_links table schema and changeset validation — kind (doc/media), access level (read/edit), token_hash uniqueness, revocation/expiry timestamps.
whatBreaks: Invalid share link rows reach the database or changeset validation rejects valid links, breaking the sharing feature.

role: Scoped-sharing registry — source of truth for LAN/network-exposed tenant scopes
description: Merges env-configured (BARKPARK_SHARES) and DB-persisted (StoredShare) grants into a live in-memory :shares list consulted by RequireShareScope; enforces default-off/default-deny invariants, provides parsing, add/remove, access_for, and share-link URL derivation (LAN IP or configured host).
whatBreaks: A default-deny/default-off regression here could either expose private papers/docs/media publicly or silently break legitimate sharing links across the network.

role: Ecto schema for persisted share grants
description: Defines the `shares` table schema and changeset for runtime-managed share grants (workspace/project/dataset scoped). Structural validation only; semantic re-validation happens on read via Sharing.parse/1.
whatBreaks: Share upserts fail or malformed rows bypass structural guards, though parse/1 on read is the second safety layer.

role: Shared SSO helpers — JIT provisioning, login audit, group-role resolution
description: Provides record_login, find_or_create_user, jit_provision (idempotent workspace membership grant on first SSO login), resolve_group_role (rank-based selection among admin-configured group→role mappings), and set_org_member_role (authoritative role sync mirroring SCIM). Shared by both the OIDC and SAML/social flows.
whatBreaks: SSO users could get wrong roles, no workspace access, or an escalation path from IdP-supplied group claims to unmapped roles.

role: Domain verification + SSO auto-routing (claim, verify, route email→org)
description: Lets an org claim a domain, verify ownership via DNS TXT token, and routes a login email's domain to the owning org's SSO — only verified domains route. Depends on the swappable Resolver behaviour.
whatBreaks: An unverified or wrongly-verified domain could route a login to the wrong org's SSO, or verified orgs could fail to auto-route to SSO at all.

role: DNS TXT lookup behaviour, swappable for tests (default :inet_res)
description: Small behaviour + default Inet implementation wrapping :inet_res.lookup for TXT records, with a rescue that swallows all resolution errors to an empty list. Config key :dns_resolver lets tests stand in a fake resolver.
whatBreaks: Domain verification would falsely succeed/fail depending on DNS lookup correctness; a broad rescue could mask legitimate resolver errors as 'no TXT records'.

role: OpenID Connect relying-party — authorize, token exchange, id_token verify
description: Implements the OIDC authorization-code + PKCE flow: builds authorize_url, exchanges the code via HTTP.post_form, verifies the id_token JWS (RS256-only against a JWKS key), validates iss/aud/exp/nonce, then find-or-creates the user and JIT-provisions/role-syncs via Barkpark.Sso. Also validates that OIDC group-role mapping targets are known roles before persisting a connection.
whatBreaks: A flawed signature/claim check could let a forged or replayed id_token authenticate as any user (full SSO auth bypass) for any org with an OIDC connection.

role: OIDC outbound HTTP behaviour (token POST + JWKS GET), swappable for tests
description: Callback behaviour with a Req-backed default client; config key :oidc_http lets tests mock the IdP's token and JWKS endpoints.
whatBreaks: OIDC token exchange or JWKS fetch could silently fail or be mocked incorrectly, breaking all live OIDC logins.

role: Ecto schema for a per-organization OIDC connection
description: Stores issuer/client_id/client_secret (encrypted via Cloak) and endpoints, plus groups_claim/group_role_mappings for era-w7 role sync; one connection per organization (unique constraint).
whatBreaks: Invalid validation could allow a broken or malicious OIDC config to persist, or leak client_secret if the encrypted-field type is misconfigured.

role: Ecto schema for an org's claimed/verified domain (SSO routing)
description: Stores domain, dns_token, and verified_at; domain is unique and lowercased on change. Used by Sso.Domains for claim/verify/route.
whatBreaks: Malformed verification state (e.g. verified_at set without real check) would misroute logins to the wrong org.

role: SAML 2.0 Service-Provider — authn request, ACS consume, Single Logout
description: Barkpark as SP delegates signature/condition verification to the esaml library (never hand-rolled XML-dsig); builds the SP-initiated redirect, consumes IdP assertions (SP- and IdP-initiated) to extract email/name_id/session_index, and implements both SP- and IdP-initiated Single Logout including cert-fingerprint pinning.
whatBreaks: A weakened trust-anchor or condition check could let a forged SAML assertion authenticate as any user, or let an unsigned LogoutRequest kill arbitrary sessions.

role: Ecto schema for a per-organization SAML SP connection
description: Stores idp_entity_id, idp_sso_url, optional idp_slo_url, and idp_cert_pem (the trust anchor); one connection per organization.
whatBreaks: A missing/wrong cert or endpoint would break SAML login for that org, or (if validation is too loose) allow an unsafe trust anchor to be saved.

role: Unified Google/GitHub/Microsoft social OAuth2 login flow
description: Single OAuth2+userinfo flow parameterized per provider (endpoints, scope, email/id keys); exchanges code for token, fetches userinfo, and find-or-links the Barkpark User by (provider, external_id), falling back to email match. Outbound calls go through Sso.Social.HTTP for test mocking.
whatBreaks: A flawed identity-linking check could let one email account be hijacked via a different provider's identity, or break login for all three social providers.

role: Swappable HTTP client behaviour for OAuth token/userinfo calls
description: Defines the `post_form`/`get_bearer` behaviour used by social-login OAuth flows (token exchange POST, userinfo GET), with a Req-backed default impl and config-swappable mock for tests.
whatBreaks: Google/GitHub/Microsoft social login would fail to exchange codes for tokens or fetch user profile data.

role: Ecto schema linking a User to a (provider, external_id) social account
description: Simple join schema for social login; enforces uniqueness on (provider, external_id) and requires an associated user.
whatBreaks: A broken constraint or cast could let duplicate social accounts link, or break social sign-in entirely.

role: Ecto schema for app-level OAuth client credentials per provider
description: Stores client_id/encrypted client_secret/enabled flag for google/github/microsoft; unique per provider, secret redacted in logs.
whatBreaks: Wrong validation or missing encryption could leak OAuth secrets or break social login configuration entirely for a provider.

role: Public status-page health + incident aggregation context
description: Probes DB/migrations/plugin-registry health, folds in open incidents to compute overall status, and provides incident CRUD + config-driven SLA data for the status page/API.
whatBreaks: The public status page/API would report wrong system health or fail to reflect real outages/incidents.

role: Ecto schema for a public status-page incident record
description: Standard incident lifecycle (investigating→identified→monitoring→resolved) with impact severity; validated inclusion lists back Status module's fold logic.
whatBreaks: Invalid impact/status values could corrupt the status page's incident history or crash incident creation.

role: Builds Studio's navigation/desk tree (Sanity deskStructure equivalent)
description: Composes the tiered desk (MAIN/Plugins/…Rest) from schema definitions and plugin desk contributions, honoring per-workspace plugin enablement/placement, scoping plugin nodes to the workspace's own types, and censusing every DB doc type so nothing is silently hidden; the Go TUI's structure.go and Studio LiveView both consume this shape.

role: Core context: Studio Claude chat sessions/messages, rail, approvals, titles
description: Very large (1600+ line) context module owning session/message CRUD, denormalized sidebar bumps, concurrent-append retry logic, the agents-rail state machine (background tasks, workflow phase-journey derivation), approval lifecycle, and title management for the /studio/chat feature (epic studio-claude-chat). Extensively charter-documented (D6-D62); pure helper functions shared with Recorder and ChatLive for consistent folding.
whatBreaks: Studio chat sessions could lose messages, mis-render the agents rail/mission-control view, double-count approvals, or corrupt sidebar state across the entire chat feature.

role: Ecto schema for one Studio chat message (display history)
description: Persists source_markdown + jsonb metadata per message with a UNIQUE (session_id, seq) constraint used as the concurrent-append race guard by StudioChat.append_message.
whatBreaks: A broken unique constraint or cast would let concurrent message appends silently drop or corrupt chat transcripts.

role: Projects an approved ExitPlanMode chat plan into a published Bulldocs Paper
description: Converts plan markdown to PortableDoc blocks and upserts a deterministically-slugged Paper (idempotent re-approve via sha256-derived slug), making the plan visible via the public /papers/:slug reader.
whatBreaks: Approved plans would fail to publish as Papers, or re-approving could create duplicate paper rows instead of updating.

role: GenServer: server-owned persistence/broadcast sink for one live chat session
description: Large stateful runtime process sitting between the ClaudeChat.Session subprocess and viewer LiveViews: persists every durable outcome (messages, tool results, approvals, agent-lifecycle frames, thinking pulses, rail snapshots) and rebroadcasts verbatim on PubSub so tabs are stateless viewers; self-reaps after idle timeout.
whatBreaks: Chat messages/tool results/approvals could be lost or duplicated on reconnect, agents rail could desync, or sessions could hang/never reap.

role: Ecto schema for a Studio chat session (sidebar index record)
description: Primary key is the minted Claude CLI session UUID (doubles as --resume key); holds denormalized sidebar fields (summary, counts, tokens, cost), mode/model/effort choices, draft, archive state, and the agents-rail jsonb snapshot; validates status/mode/title_source inclusion lists.
whatBreaks: Session resume could break, sidebar data (cost/tokens/status) could go stale or invalid, or an illegal mode could bypass permission-mode validation.

role: AI thread-title generator for Studio Claude chat sessions
description: Layered, fire-and-forget summarizer that turns the first chat message into a short title, trying the Anthropic Messages API, then a `claude` CLI one-shot, then a derived first-line fallback. Everything fails soft (never crashes/blocks the chat); pure builders are unit-tested directly and adapters/CLI/store are all injectable seams.
whatBreaks: Studio chat sessions get wrong/garbled titles or the fallback chain breaks and raises, but the chat itself keeps working since failures are swallowed.

role: Facade for the Barkpark-to-Barkpark pull/push sync subsystem
description: Entry point for the local-first sync feature: exposes enabled?/push_active?/config, builds Applier/Pusher contexts (resolving workspace slug to scope), and provides apply_frames/2 — the deterministic parse+apply+cursor drain seam used by both the live SSE Worker and tests. Config-gated and dormant unless BARKPARK_SYNC_* env vars are set; never touches content.ex/tasks.ex internals directly.
whatBreaks: When sync is enabled, a bug here can misresolve tenancy scope (risking NULL-scope writes) or mis-halt event draining, causing silent data loss or duplicate/incorrect local mutations; when disabled it is fully inert so blast radius is scoped to sync-enabled deployments.

role: Agent handoff doc for the local-first sync initiative
description: Non-code doc-tier:agent file tracking phase status (P0-P2 done, P3-P4 open), invariants, gotchas, and live-validation notes for the Barkpark.Sync subsystem; canonical design lives in a separate Barkpark paper.
whatBreaks: Nothing at runtime breaks; a stale/wrong handoff misleads the next agent working on sync into violating an invariant (e.g. editing content.ex or breaking cursor monotonicity).

role: Applies one parsed pull-sync SSE event into the local workspace
description: Routes a mutation envelope to createOrReplace/publish or delete via Content's public API only, with cursor-based echo-dedup and dead-letter quarantine after max_attempts; halts (does not advance cursor) on unresolved workspace scope or below-threshold errors to guarantee replay.
whatBreaks: A bug here can mis-route deletes as upserts (resurrecting deleted docs), advance the cursor past a real failure (silent data loss), or write into the wrong/NULL tenancy scope — but only affects deployments with sync enabled.

role: Ecto schema/store for the pull-sync per-source high-water-mark cursor
description: Persists the largest applied SSE event id per {source,dataset} in sync_cursors, used both as the Last-Event-ID resume point and the echo-dedup gate; put/3 is a monotonic upsert that never rewinds.
whatBreaks: A non-monotonic or wrong cursor causes duplicate re-application of already-applied events or skips real ones, breaking sync correctness for any workspace with pull-sync enabled.

role: Durable quarantine store for poison pull-sync events
description: Ecto-schema-backed table recording per-{source,dataset,event_id} failure attempts/envelope/status, so repeatedly-failing events are inspectable (list_dead/2) rather than silently dropped; envelope is write-once on insert.
whatBreaks: A poison event could be dropped without record (silent loss) or the cursor could advance incorrectly, but scope is limited to sync-enabled deployments and error-path events only.

role: Read-only query feeding the push-sync loop from local mutation_events
description: Fetches un-pushed, non-sync-originated (source != "sync") mutation_events rows in id order after a given cursor; the single enforcement point of push-side echo-suppression to prevent ping-ponging pulled events back to the remote.
whatBreaks: If the source exclusion filter is wrong, pulled events get pushed back to the remote causing an infinite pull/push ping-pong loop; affects only sync-enabled deployments with push active.

role: Durable quarantine store for rejected push-sync writes
description: Ecto schema recording per-{source,dataset,event_id} push conflicts (stale-base CAS rejection etc.), preserving the local loser document on insert-only so a remote write is never silently overwritten; queryable surface for the future Studio Conflicts pane.
whatBreaks: A conflicting local edit could silently overwrite a remote document instead of being quarantined, violating the fail-closed CAS invariant — limited to push-sync-enabled deployments.

role: Ecto schema/store for the push-sync high-water-mark cursor
description: Separate monotonic cursor from the pull Cursor, tracking the largest local mutation_events.id successfully pushed or durably conflict-recorded; includes bootstrap_if_absent/2 to seed the cursor to current head on first enable so pre-existing history isn't replayed to the remote.
whatBreaks: A wrong/rewound cursor could re-push already-sent events or, if bootstrap misfires, flood the remote with the entire pre-enable history on first activation; scoped to push-sync-enabled deployments.

role: Ecto schema/store for the remote-rev CAS ledger used by push-sync
