role: Ecto migration — creates content_edges table (content graph)
description: Creates the content_edges table (from_id, to_id, kind, weight, plugin_source, timestamps) with cascade FKs to documents, a unique (from_id,to_id,kind) index backing an upsert, plus forward/reverse scan indexes; underlies Content.add_edge/list_outbound_edges/list_inbound_edges for the content blast-radius/dependency graph and Studio Canvas2D force-sim.
whatBreaks: Content graph edges (backlinks, dependency/blast-radius queries, Canvas2D graph view) can't be stored or queried, breaking cross-document relationship features.

role: Guarded migration removing the dead legacy 'paperflow' dataset
description: Idempotent, reversible cleanup migration: deletes the vestigial `paperflow` dataset row (and its dead schema_definitions row) only if no documents/media_files still reference it, else no-ops with a log notice; down/0 re-seeds the row.
whatBreaks: If the safety guard were broken it could silently drop or orphan live content rows tied to the paperflow dataset; as written it's a safe no-op on any live content.

role: Migration creating sync_cursors table (PULL sync high-water mark)
description: Creates the `sync_cursors` table (source, dataset, event_id) backing `Barkpark.Sync.Cursor`, tracking the last applied remote event per source/dataset for resumable one-way PULL sync. Dormant until a sync source is configured.
whatBreaks: Wrong schema breaks PULL sync resume (Last-Event-ID tracking), causing full re-processing or missed dedup once any external sync source is enabled.

role: Migration creating sync_dead_letters quarantine table
description: Creates `sync_dead_letters` (source, dataset, event_id, attempts, status, envelope, last_error) so PULL-sync events that repeatedly fail to apply are durably quarantined before the cursor advances past them, rather than silently skipped.
whatBreaks: Missing/incorrect table would force sync to either silently drop poison events or halt entirely on any unapplyable event, losing the inspectable quarantine safety net.

role: Migration adding origin `source` column to mutation_events
description: Additive column (`source`, default "api") tagging every mutation event's origin so the PUSH sync outbox can exclude sync-applied writes and avoid echo/ping-pong; pre-existing rows default to "api".
whatBreaks: If wrong, PUSH sync could re-push events it just pulled from a remote, causing infinite sync ping-pong between two instances.

role: Migration creating sync_push_cursors table (PUSH high-water mark)
description: Creates `sync_push_cursors` (source, dataset, event_id) — a separate monotonic cursor in LOCAL mutation_events id-space, explicitly distinct from the pull cursor's remote id-space.
whatBreaks: Conflating this with the pull cursor's id-space (as the code comments warn against) would corrupt push resume logic and could re-send or skip local mutations to the remote.

role: Migration creating sync_push_doc_revs remote-rev ledger table
description: Creates `sync_push_doc_revs` (source, dataset, doc_id, remote_rev) tracking the remote's last-known revision per document, used as the CAS base (`ifRevisionID`) for push conflict detection.
whatBreaks: Without an accurate remote-rev ledger, push CAS checks would use the wrong base revision, causing spurious conflicts or silently overwriting remote changes.

role: Migration creating sync_push_conflicts quarantine table
description: Creates `sync_push_conflicts` capturing rejected pushes (stale-base CAS, fenced claim, resource conflict) with the full local document preserved before the push cursor advances past them, mirroring the pull dead-letter pattern.
whatBreaks: Missing this table means rejected/conflicting local pushes would be lost with no record, silently discarding a user's local edits during sync conflicts.

role: Migration adding PAT fields (name, last_used_at, created_by) to api_tokens
description: Additive-only columns extending api_tokens for a self-service Studio Personal Access Token pane, with parity to the cloud/ control-plane PAT; existing tokens keep working with new columns NULL, ownership tracked via `created_by` string since api/ has no users table.
whatBreaks: If wrong, Studio's token management UI (last-used tracking, audit breadcrumb) would break or existing tokens (dev token, share tokens) could be invalidated by a non-additive change.

role: Migration creating secrets and secrets_audit tables (encrypted KV store)
description: General-purpose encrypted-at-rest KV store keyed by `name` (value via Barkpark.EncryptedBinary), plus an append-only secrets_audit log; first consumer is the cloud run ingest_token, but the table is consumer-agnostic.
whatBreaks: A broken schema here would break encrypted secret storage (e.g. the ingest token), potentially exposing plaintext secrets or losing the audit trail of who changed them.

role: Migration: creates data_keys table for envelope-encryption DEKs
description: Creates the `data_keys` table storing per-scope Data Encryption Keys in wrapped (KEK-sealed) form only; plaintext DEKs never persist. Additive/no-op on existing data — nothing reads/writes it yet since no fields declare `encrypted: true`.
whatBreaks: If the schema or indexes are wrong, envelope-encryption key rotation and lookup (Barkpark.Crypto.KeyProvider/LocalKek) fail or silently allow multiple active DEKs per scope, corrupting encrypted-field rollout.

role: Migration: creates core users table for first-class login accounts
description: Adds the `users` table (email/citext, argon2id hashed_password, Cloak-encrypted TOTP secret, hashed recovery codes) — the first human-principal concept in Barkpark core, additive to the existing token-only auth model.
whatBreaks: Wrong column types/constraints (e.g. missing citext extension or unique email index) break user signup/login and every downstream auth feature (sessions, email tokens, ownership ACL) that FKs to users.id.

role: Migration: creates user_sessions table for browser login tokens
description: Adds `user_sessions` with hash-at-rest token_hash, revoked_at kill switch, expiry, and device metadata — backs browser session auth and 'sign out everywhere'. Additive, FKs to users with delete_all cascade.
whatBreaks: A broken unique index on token_hash or missing FK cascade would allow session collisions or orphaned sessions after user deletion, breaking login/logout correctness.

role: Migration: creates user_email_tokens table for verify/reset flows
description: Adds `user_email_tokens` (hashed, single-use, context-discriminated 'confirm'/'reset', pinned to sent_to address) backing email verification and password reset. Additive, FKs to users.
whatBreaks: Wrong hash/context/expiry handling could let stale or cross-address tokens confirm an email change or reset a password, a security correctness bug.

role: Migration: intentional no-op placeholder for field-visibility feature
description: Documents that per-field visibility attributes (private/visibility/readable_by) live inline in the existing `schema_definitions.fields` JSON, parsed with safe defaults — no DB column change needed. Kept only to preserve migration sequence numbering.
whatBreaks: Essentially nothing at the DB level; if removed or renumbered it could desync migration ordering causing an out-of-order Ecto migration error on deploy.

role: Migration: adds owner_id column to documents for row-level ACL
description: Adds nullable, FK-less `owner_id` to `documents` for the ownership ACL feature; deliberately no FK to users so ownership can outlive/predate a user row, and NULL means unowned (fails closed). Indexed for the owner_id-or-NULL read filter.
whatBreaks: Missing/incorrect index or column breaks the owner-scoped read-path filter in Barkpark.Content.Scope.scope_to_owner/2, potentially leaking or hiding documents across users.

role: Migration: adds owner_scoped boolean flag to schema_definitions
description: Adds a NOT NULL, default-false `owner_scoped` column marking whole schemas as row-ACL opt-in; existing schemas stay byte-identical (false) until explicitly toggled.
whatBreaks: Wrong default or nullability would silently opt existing schemas into (or out of) row-level ownership restrictions, exposing or hiding data incorrectly for non-admin users.

role: Migration: partial unique index enforcing one active DEK per scope
description: Adds a partial unique index (WHERE active) on data_keys.scope, moving the 'one active DEK per scope' invariant from app code into the DB to prevent DataKeys.active_dek/1's Repo.one! from crashing on duplicate active rows.
whatBreaks: If the partial index is missing or wrong, a concurrency bug or bad manual edit could create two active DEKs per scope, crashing every new encryption for that scope.

role: Migration: adds last_totp_at to users, fixes TOTP replay bug
description: Adds nullable `last_totp_at` to `users`, fed into NimbleTOTP's `:since` option to reject replay of an already-consumed 30-second TOTP code (RED-TEAM MEDIUM-6 fix).
whatBreaks: Without this column/check, a captured TOTP code remains valid for its whole 30s window and can be replayed, weakening MFA security guarantees.

role: Migration: adds actor_user_id to revisions for who-did-what trail
description: Adds a nullable, indexed string `actor_user_id` to the existing `revisions` (version-history) table, stamped atomically with each mutation transaction; deliberately no FK since actors are keyed by string id (user or api-token) with no single target table. Note: version deliberately renumbered above main's then-latest migration to avoid an out-of-order Ecto error.
whatBreaks: Missing index or wrong nullability breaks efficient 'everything user X edited' audit queries, and a mis-ordered migration timestamp can trigger Ecto's already-run migration error on deploy.

role: Ecto migration creating login_tickets table for Studio one-click entry
description: Creates the login_tickets table backing single-use, short-TTL login handoff tickets minted from a valid api_token; stores only the SHA-256 hash of the ticket and a Cloak-encrypted copy of the bound raw api_token, with a used_at race guard for single-use consumption.
whatBreaks: Studio one-click login handoff via GET /login/ticket/:ticket fails to provision or allows ticket replay/duplicate-consume races.

role: Migration adding jsonb_path_ops GIN index on documents.content
description: Adds a concurrent GIN index (jsonb_path_ops) on documents.content to serve the sheet write-through's JSONB containment (@>) probe used by Sheets embed-target lookups, replacing a full sequential scan on every debounced sheet flush; uses disable_ddl_transaction/disable_migration_lock for CONCURRENTLY safety.
whatBreaks: Sheet-to-paper embed refresh queries fall back to sequential scans over all documents, degrading write-through latency at scale, or a broken CONCURRENTLY migration could fail/lock the live documents table.

role: Migration adding last_latency_ms column to webhook_deliveries
description: Adds a nullable integer column recording the wall-clock latency of the most recent delivery attempt, surfaced in the webhook operator console.
whatBreaks: Operator console can't display per-delivery latency; harmless if missing beyond that UI gap.

role: Migration adding kind and paused_at columns to api_tokens
description: Adds the token-tier discriminator ("api" default vs "ticket") consumed by Auth.verify_token's fail-closed WHERE clause, and a paused_at column letting operators mute a Tickets ticket-key without revoking it.
whatBreaks: Auth token verification could misclassify tokens (letting ticket-tier keys act as full api tokens, a security regression) or ticket pause/mute controls silently fail to work.

role: Migration adding auto-disable columns to webhooks table
description: Adds consecutive_failures, auto_disabled_at, disable_reason to webhooks, backing automatic disabling of permanently dead webhook endpoints after repeated terminal delivery failures.
whatBreaks: Dead webhook endpoints never auto-disable (keep retrying forever) or get disabled incorrectly, disrupting webhook delivery for tenants.

role: Migration converging media webhooks onto shared durable retry machinery
description: Adds source_kind ("document"|"media") and payload_snapshot to webhook_deliveries and relaxes endpoint_id/event_id to nullable, letting media lifecycle webhooks reuse the document webhook retry/sweeper machinery instead of an in-task Process.sleep twin; down migration deletes media rows before restoring NOT NULL.
whatBreaks: Media webhook deliveries (e.g. media.deleted) lose their resumable retry state across crashes, or unified RetryWorker/StuckDeliverySweeper mis-branch on source_kind and corrupt/duplicate document webhook delivery behavior.

role: Migration closing a schema-name uniqueness race for NULL dataset_id rows
description: Adds a partial unique index on schema_definitions(name, dataset) WHERE dataset_id IS NULL to restore uniqueness protection lost when dataset_id became the uniqueness key, since Postgres treats NULLs as distinct; guards against concurrent upsert_schema races creating duplicate schemas in flat (non-tenanted) deployments.
whatBreaks: Flat/non-tenanted deployments (the common case with plugins off) could silently create duplicate schema_definitions rows for the same schema name under concurrent writes, corrupting the content model's schema registry.

role: Migration adding mfa_verified_at to user_sessions for step-up MFA
description: Adds a nullable timestamp of the most recent successful MFA factor presented on a session, read by require_recent_mfa to gate sensitive actions behind a freshness check.
whatBreaks: Step-up MFA gating for sensitive actions (e.g. token management, security settings) could be bypassed or incorrectly always-required, a security-relevant regression.

role: Migration creating webauthn_credentials table for passkey auth
description: Creates the table storing registered WebAuthn/passkey credentials per user (credential_id, COSE public key, sign_count for clone detection, nickname, last_used_at), unique-indexed on credential_id and indexed on user_id.
whatBreaks: Passkey/WebAuthn registration and login assertion verification fail entirely, or clone-detection via sign_count is unenforceable, weakening that auth factor's security guarantees.

role: Migration creating status_incidents table for the public status page
description: Creates the table backing public incident history (component, impact, lifecycle status, body, started_at/resolved_at) that drives the status page's overall degraded/operational state.
whatBreaks: The public status page can't record or display incidents, and overall status derivation (degraded when incidents are open) breaks.

role: Ecto migration creating the tenant-wide audit_events hash-chain table
description: Creates a single append-only audit_events table replacing two drifted narrow trails (plugin_settings_audit, secrets_audit); rows form a per-workspace sha256 hash chain, and a Postgres trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE to enforce immutability (TRUNCATE stays allowed for test sandbox resets).
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, the entire enterprise audit trail either fails to record events, loses tamper-evidence, or blocks legitimate inserts, undermining compliance guarantees across the whole system.

role: Ecto migration adding the Organization tier above Workspace
description: Creates the organizations table and adds a nullable organization_id FK to workspaces, back-filling all existing workspaces into a default organization; foundational for later SSO/SCIM waves and additive/non-breaking by design.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, every workspace could lose its organization linkage or the back-fill could fail, breaking org-scoped SSO/SCIM features and any code that assumes every workspace has an organization_id.

role: Ecto migration creating audit_export_sinks table for SIEM/webhook streaming
description: Creates configured export destinations that tail-ship audit_events via a cursor (last_exported_id) high-water mark, decoupling export from the emit path; supports global (nil workspace_id) or per-workspace sinks with auto-disable columns.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, SIEM/webhook audit export either fails to configure sinks or ships duplicate/missing events to customer security systems.

role: Ecto migration creating roles and role_permissions tables for custom RBAC
description: Creates data-driven roles (global built-in when workspace_id is NULL, custom when scoped to a workspace) and role_permissions granting actions; feeds the USER authorization path Tenancy.Auth.role_permits?, leaving the API-token permission model untouched.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, user role-based authorization could silently grant or deny incorrect permissions across every workspace, a severe security defect.

role: Ecto migration creating scim_tokens table for per-org SCIM bearer auth
description: Creates SCIM bearer tokens scoped to exactly one organization for /scim/v2/* IdP provisioning; stores only the SHA-256 hash, mirroring api_tokens' security pattern.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, SCIM provisioning could authenticate against the wrong organization or fail entirely, breaking automated user provisioning for enterprise customers.

role: Ecto migration creating scim_groups table mapping IdP groups to roles
description: Creates SCIM 2.0 Group records scoped to an organization; membership in an IdP group maps to a Barkpark role_name that grants/revokes access across the org's workspaces as users are added/removed.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, SCIM group-to-role sync could grant excessive access or fail to revoke access when users are removed from an IdP group.

role: Ecto migration creating oidc_connections table for per-org OIDC RP config
description: Creates a single OIDC relying-party connection per organization storing issuer/endpoints and an at-rest-encrypted client_secret (Cloak / Barkpark.EncryptedBinary); Barkpark acts as RP against the org's IdP.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, enterprise SSO login via OIDC could fail outright or leak client secrets if encryption is misconfigured.

role: Ecto migration creating social_providers and social_identities tables
description: Creates app-level OAuth client config per provider (Google/GitHub/Microsoft, secret encrypted) and per-user social_identities keyed by (provider, external_id) to prevent duplicate-account creation on re-login.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, social login could create duplicate user accounts or fail to authenticate returning users across every social provider.

role: Ecto migration creating org_domains table for verified-domain JIT SSO routing
description: Creates globally-unique verified email domains claimed by an organization via DNS TXT proof; once verified_at is set, logins on that domain auto-route to the org's SSO connection.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, domain-based SSO auto-routing could send users to the wrong organization's identity provider or fail to route them to SSO at all.

role: Ecto migration creating saml_connections table for per-org SAML SP config
description: Creates a single SAML 2.0 Service-Provider connection per organization storing the IdP's SSO URL and signing certificate (idp_cert_pem), the trust anchor used to verify assertion signatures.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong, SAML SSO login could fail to verify IdP assertion signatures, either locking out legitimate users or accepting forged assertions.

role: Ecto migration: SAML Single Logout columns
description: Adds idp_slo_url to saml_connections and saml_name_id/saml_session_index/saml_org_slug to user_sessions so SP- and IdP-initiated SAML logout can locate and revoke the right sessions; indexes saml_name_id. Nullable fields keep non-SAML sessions unaffected.
whatBreaks: SAML Single Logout (both SP- and IdP-initiated) would be unable to find or revoke the correct sessions, leaving stale authenticated sessions after logout.

role: Ecto migration: OIDC group-claim to role mapping columns
description: Adds groups_claim (default "groups") and group_role_mappings map to oidc_connections, enabling login-time role assignment from OIDC id_token group claims for orgs without SCIM; roles must come from the admin-configured map, never directly from the claim.
whatBreaks: OIDC logins for orgs relying on group-based role mapping would fail to assign correct roles, or (if the SELECT-only constraint were broken elsewhere) could let a claim asserting a role directly grant unintended privileges.

role: Ecto migration: audit-event webhook subscription columns
description: Adds audit_categories, audit_actions (array defaults []) and organization_id (FK, nullable=global) to webhooks so a webhook can subscribe to auth/membership/token audit events instead of content mutations, reusing the existing webhook delivery pipeline (HMAC, retries, dead-letter, SSRF guard).
whatBreaks: Audit-event webhook subscriptions (security/compliance alerting) would silently not fire or could misdeliver org-scoped audit events to the wrong subscribers.

role: Ecto migration: per-account login lockout columns
description: Adds failed_login_count (default 0) and locked_until to users, enabling account-level lockout independent of source IP, complementing the IP-keyed rate limiter.
whatBreaks: Brute-force login protection at the account level would be disabled or malfunction, either locking out legitimate users incorrectly or failing to stop credential-stuffing attacks.

role: Ecto migration: org-wide require-MFA flag
description: Adds require_mfa boolean (default false) to organizations, an opt-in overlay atop step-up MFA (#1140); with the flag unset, auth behavior is unchanged.
whatBreaks: Organizations that opted into mandatory MFA could have the requirement silently bypassed, weakening org-wide auth security policy.

role: Ecto migration: Pulse (Shared Storm) anonymous event tables
description: Creates pulse_events (ephemeral, TTL-swept feed rows with monotonic id cursor for polling) and pulse_counters (durable per-channel lifetime total), deliberately outside the Content document substrate for high-volume, race-free anonymous public ingest.
whatBreaks: The Shared Storm/Pulse public event feed and its durable counters would lose correct ordering/polling semantics or the atomic total, breaking the anonymous ingest feature end to end.

role: Ecto migration: user email on login tickets for cloud handoff
description: Adds nullable user_email to login_tickets so a USER-shaped ticket (cloud-identity-studio-handoff) can JIT-provision a user and mint a session instead of embedding an api_token; nil email preserves legacy token-shaped ticket behavior.
whatBreaks: Cloud-to-Studio login handoff would fail to provision/authenticate the right user, or could regress legacy token-ticket logins if the nullable fallback broke.

role: Ecto migration: GitHub bridge sync-conflict quarantine table
description: Creates github_sync_conflicts recording drift between the task ledger and mirrored GitHub Issues (out_of_band_edit, detached, dedup_refused) before/instead of silent overwrite; includes a partial unique index enforcing at most one open row per {repo, issue, kind} to prevent duplicate-conflict races under concurrent webhook redelivery.
whatBreaks: GitHub bridge drift (hand-edited issues, deleted/transferred issues, deduped intake) could be silently overwritten or duplicated instead of visibly quarantined, undermining the bridge's ledger-wins-but-never-silent guarantee.

role: Ecto migration: security backfill neutralizing stored-XSS media MIME types
description: One-way data migration (down/0 is a no-op) rewriting pre-existing media_files rows with browser-executable MIME types (image/svg+xml, text/html, JS types, etc.) to application/octet-stream, closing a stored-XSS hole (PR #1025) for uploads that predated the ingest changeset fix; matches MediaFile.dangerous_mime?/1 logic case-insensitively, ignoring charset params.
whatBreaks: Pre-existing uploaded files with dangerous MIME types would remain servable as browser-executable content, leaving a stored-XSS vector open despite the code-level fix.

role: Ecto migration: access_grants table for airdrop scoped-access links
description: Creates access_grants: time-boxed, scoped (workspace/project/dataset/type/doc_id ladder), account-bound capability grants identified by grantee_email until claimed; stores only a SHA-256 hash of the raw link token (never the token itself, unique index), with expires_at/claimed_at/revoked_at driving a derived (not stored) 'active' predicate.
whatBreaks: The airdrop grants feature (scoped access links for enterprise-ready auth) could leak raw tokens, grant unintended scope, or fail to correctly expire/revoke access, a direct auth-security regression.

role: Migration: adds nullable owner_user_id FK to api_tokens
description: Additive-only migration linking an api_token to an owning User (nilify on user delete). Token-lookup/auth path is untouched by design; only claim/mine surfaces read the new column, so un-owned tokens keep working identically.
whatBreaks: If the FK or nilify_all behavior is wrong, deleting a user could cascade-delete tokens or leave dangling references, breaking auth for unrelated tokens.

role: Migration: creates pulse_meters table for durable Shared Storm accumulators
description: Creates a simple keyed (name primary key) table storing bigint nanos, first used for cumulative compute cost tracking that must survive restarts/deploys.
whatBreaks: Wrong schema (e.g. non-atomic increments or wrong integer type) would let the storm's accrued cost drift or lose precision across restarts.

role: Migration: creates chat_sessions + chat_messages tables for Studio Claude chat
description: Foundational schema for the admin-only Studio chat feature: chat_sessions is a denormalized session index keyed by the Claude CLI session UUID (doubles as --resume key), chat_messages is display-only markdown history (never the real transcript) with a unique (session_id, seq) append-race guard. Deliberately not exposed as documents/HTTP routes to avoid leaking admin transcripts through the any-token query gate.
whatBreaks: Wrong PK/unique-index or FK design would break session resume identity, corrupt message ordering, or (if wrongly exposed via HTTP) leak private chat transcripts to any API token.

role: Migration: adds context-window snapshot columns to chat_sessions
description: Adds nullable last_context_tokens and context_window columns, set (not incremented) from the latest CLI result frame, driving the chat UI's context-fullness ring without a hardcoded model→window map.
whatBreaks: If these columns are misapplied as increments instead of snapshots, the context ring would show inflated/wrong fullness instead of the current turn's real headroom.

role: Migration: adds archived_at column + partial index to chat_sessions
description: Adds a nullable archived_at timestamp as an orthogonal lifecycle axis (separate from status) plus a partial index on last_active_at WHERE archived_at IS NULL to keep the sidebar's default (non-archived) listing query fast as archives grow.
whatBreaks: Missing/wrong partial index would slow the sidebar query as archived sessions accumulate; conflating archive with status would clobber the archive flag on every status transition.

role: Migration: adds pending_approvals denormalized counter to chat_sessions
description: Adds a not-null integer counter incremented/decremented alongside approval lifecycle events in chat_messages metadata, letting the sidebar show a 'needs you' pill without scanning messages.
whatBreaks: If the counter drifts from actual pending approvals (missed decrement/zero-on-teardown), the sidebar would show stale or incorrect 'needs you' badges.

role: Migration: adds model_choice string column to chat_sessions
description: Stores the user's picked model alias (haiku/sonnet/opus/fable) distinct from the observed `model` column (actual answering model), nil meaning CLI default.
whatBreaks: Confusing model_choice with observed model would misreport which model the user intended vs. which actually answered, breaking model-picker UI state.

role: Migration: adds jsonb settings bag to workspaces (theme system)
description: Adds a not-null default-{} map column to workspaces as the first durable per-workspace settings store, initially carrying theme identity so reader/Studio/email render the same theme server-side with no flash-of-wrong-theme.
whatBreaks: A missing default or nullable column would break theme resolution for existing workspaces, causing wrong or crashing theme lookups across every surface (Studio, reader, email).

role: Migration: adds nullable draft text column to chat_sessions
description: Stores the unsent composer text per session so switching away and reopening restores it verbatim; captured on switch-away, cleared on send.
whatBreaks: Wrong type or missing column would lose in-progress user composer text when navigating away and back.

role: Migration: adds rail_snapshot map column to chat_sessions
description: Persists the agents-rail mission-control snapshot keyed by sub-agent task_id (row/workflow/status/usage/seq), set wholesale in place so a reopened session replays the last-known agent rail; only structural changes write, not token ticks.
whatBreaks: If the column shape or in-place-set semantics are wrong, reopening a chat session would show a stale, incomplete, or crashing agents rail.

role: Ecto migration adding effort_choice column to chat_sessions
description: Adds a nullable `effort_choice` string column to `chat_sessions`, mirroring the existing `model_choice` column pattern — records the user's picked reasoning-effort tier (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) as intent-only (no paired observed-effort column, unlike model).

role: Studio image-field Web Component (upload/browse/remove)

role: systemd launch wrapper for the Phoenix prod process

role: Test: audit-trail coverage for access-grant mint/claim/revoke
description: Asserts that minting, claiming, and revoking an access grant lands a tamper-evident `access`/`grant.*` event on Barkpark.Audit with correct actor/subject/metadata, hash chain intact, and no raw token or link_token_hash leaked into audit fields.
whatBreaks: Regressions in grant audit logging or accidental leakage of secret material into the audit trail would go undetected, weakening security compliance evidence.

role: Test: airdrop-grants enforcement at auth + query-scoping layers
description: Proves non-vacuously that a grantee's active grants are folded into CallerContext and honored both by Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 (coarse) and Content.Query grant-scoped narrowing (fine), fail-closed in both cases — the core security invariant that grant access never exceeds capabilities ∩ scope.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions here could let a grantee read/write outside their granted scope or across tenants, a serious authorization bypass.

role: Test: access-grant lifecycle (mint/claim/expire/revoke) fail-closed paths
description: Covers that a grantor can only mint what it holds, expired/revoked grants are refused, out-of-scope/un-permitted actions are refused, claim binds exactly once, and UUID-guarded reads never crash — core Barkpark.Access module correctness.
whatBreaks: A broken or weakened test here risks shipping a grant-lifecycle bug (e.g. double-claim, unbounded permission escalation) undetected.

role: Test: GDPR-style subject export and erase for user accounts
description: Verifies Accounts.Privacy.export_subject/1 excludes secret material (hashed_password, token_hash) and erase_subject/1 scrubs PII while retaining the row, deletes sessions/memberships/email tokens, disables MFA, and emits a tamper-evident audit event.
whatBreaks: A privacy-erasure or export regression could leak credentials in an export or fail to fully scrub PII on a deletion request, a compliance/security risk.

role: Test: transactional email failure logging without PII leakage
description: Asserts that a failed Swoosh delivery (simulated via a DownRelayAdapter) logs a diagnostic line with email type/reason instead of vanishing silently, while never leaking the recipient's email address in logs, and preserves the fail-soft return contract used by anti-enumeration controllers.
whatBreaks: Silent email delivery failures would be undiagnosable in prod, or a regression could leak recipient PII into logs.

role: Test — per-account login lockout + HIBP breach-check
description: Covers failed-login lockout thresholds/reset/expiry, no-enumeration on unknown email, and the HIBP k-anonymity breached-password check (disabled-by-default, fail-open on HIBP outage, only 5-char SHA-1 prefix sent).
whatBreaks: Regressions here would let account lockout or breached-password rejection silently stop working, weakening brute-force and credential-stuffing defenses.

role: Test — passwordless magic-link login tokens
description: Verifies build/consume of single-use login tokens (hash-only storage, case-insensitive email match, expiry, and context isolation from password-reset tokens).
whatBreaks: A broken magic-link flow (e.g. token reuse or cross-context token acceptance) would let login tokens be replayed or misused as reset tokens.

role: Test — core Accounts context (auth, sessions, TOTP MFA)
description: Large suite covering registration/password hashing, login, session mint/verify/revoke (incl. throttled last_used_at), expiry predicates, password reset/email confirm, full TOTP MFA lifecycle (enable, recovery codes, replay protection, TOCTOU races), and workspace-scoped email-prefix search with LIKE-escaping.
whatBreaks: Auth, session validity, or MFA could silently break or leak across workspaces, undermining the whole authentication/authorization system.

role: Test — generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec vs live manifest
description: Asserts the OpenAPI document is well-formed, every route/manifest command has exactly one matching operation (parity gate against drift), security/scoping/error-schema shapes are correct — the SDK-generator contract guard.
whatBreaks: SDK generation or API docs would silently drift from the actual route surface, breaking client codegen and external API consumers.

role: unit tests for ApiTestRunner.Asserts evaluators
description: Tests all 8 built-in assertion evaluators in `Barkpark.ApiTestRunner.Asserts.evaluate/2` with passing and failing cases, nil body, malformed JSON, and unknown tag edge cases.
whatBreaks: Regressions in assertion evaluators go undetected, causing the API test runner to silently mis-report pass/fail results.

role: integration tests for ApiTestRunner round-trip
description: Tests `ApiTestRunner.run/2` and `run_one/3` end-to-end using Req.Test HTTP stubs, covering happy path, failing assert, connection error, and cleanup-always semantics.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the runner's HTTP dispatch, error handling, or cleanup logic go undetected.

role: Parity test for ApiTester Endpoints facade vs pre-split baseline
description: Asserts the decomposed Endpoints facade (per-category modules under endpoints/) produces the exact same ordered static catalog as a compiled baseline fixture, normalizing the dynamic mutate-create _id; plugin-* entries excluded from comparison.
whatBreaks: A refactor of the API Tester endpoint catalog could silently drop/reorder/alter example endpoints without detection.

role: unit tests for ApiTester.Runner request builder
description: Tests `Runner.build_request/3` for path interpolation, query param encoding/omission, Authorization header attachment, and Content-Type for create endpoints.
whatBreaks: Request construction bugs (wrong URL, missing auth headers, leaked empty params) go undetected in the Studio API tester.

role: Test — audit log SIEM export sink (tail-shipping webhooks)
description: Covers cursor-based tail shipping to external sinks, workspace-scoped vs global sinks, HMAC signing, and auto-disable after repeated failures.
whatBreaks: A broken export sink could double-ship, drop, or fail to auto-disable audit events sent to external SIEM systems.

role: Test — tamper-evident audit event hash-chain
description: Verifies append + hash-chaining per workspace, DB-level append-only enforcement (UPDATE/DELETE rejected by trigger), chain tamper detection, and that content mutations emit audit events end-to-end.
whatBreaks: A broken hash chain or append-only guard would let audit history be tampered with undetected, defeating the compliance/security audit trail.

role: Test — API token hashing + changeset validation
description: Small unit test for deterministic SHA-256 token hashing and the ApiToken changeset (required token_hash, permissions casting).
whatBreaks: A broken hash or changeset could allow malformed/duplicate tokens or break token verification for API auth.

role: tests for share-edit token minting and revocation
description: Tests `Auth.create_share_token/5` and `revoke_share_tokens/3`, verifying that edit tokens are only minted for live-shared scopes, carry opaque share permissions, correct expiry, and are revoked correctly.
whatBreaks: Auth bugs in share tokens could allow unauthorized edit access or fail to revoke tokens on share removal.

role: Unit tests for Barkpark.Auth token verification
description: Covers verify_token/1 behavior (active, revoked, expired tokens) against Auth.ApiToken records scoped to a workspace/dataset.
whatBreaks: Regressions in API token auth (e.g. expired/revoked tokens still verifying) would go undetected, risking unauthorized access.

role: Test — compile-time build/version identity (BuildInfo)
description: Pins the A.B.C.D version format derived from git describe, release truncation, and the info/0 map shape used by self-update tooling; pure, no DB.
whatBreaks: Version reporting used by instance self-update and diagnostics could go stale or show 'unknown', confusing deploy/version tracking.

role: test for EDItEUR XML codelist parser
description: Tests Barkpark.Codelists.EDItEUR XML parsing against a synthetic fixture, covering parse_xml/2 for codelist values and translations.
whatBreaks: ONIX codelist parsing regressions go undetected, silently corrupting book metadata exports.

role: Test — id-less PortableDoc block backfill + ingest chokepoint
description: Extensive coverage of BlockOps.ensure_block_ids/normalize_list_items collision-safe minting, the BackfillBlockIds migration task (dry-run/apply/idempotent/tenancy-complete), and that every document/paper write path (create, upsert, block-ops, scaffold) guarantees unique non-blank block ids.
whatBreaks: Duplicate or missing block ids would corrupt PortableDoc rendering/editing and block-op addressing across Papers and documents.

role: Test — Content.Broadcast topic naming + deferred-broadcast queue
description: Covers workspace-scoped doc/paper PubSub topic string formatting and the process-dictionary deferred-broadcast/webhook queue clear/flush helpers.
whatBreaks: Wrong topic strings would break realtime SSE/PubSub subscriptions for documents and papers across workspaces.

role: Unit tests for CallerContext.from_conn resolution order
description: Verifies caller_context/api_token/anonymous resolution precedence in Barkpark.Content.CallerContext, including admin-token detection. Fast ExUnit case, no DB.
whatBreaks: Regressions in caller-context resolution (e.g. anonymous getting admin rights) would go undetected, risking authz bypass.

role: Changeset tests for the Codelist schema (ONIX codelists)

role: Changeset tests for Codelists.Value (codelist entries)
description: Checks required codelist_id/code and optional position/metadata/parent_id fields on Barkpark.Content.Codelists.Value changesets.

role: Unit tests for Content.Codelists register/lookup
description: Tests round-tripping flat ONIX-style codelists and multi-language label fallback via Codelists.register/3 and lookup/3.
whatBreaks: ONIX/onixedit codelist registration or lookup (e.g. contributor roles, languages) could regress silently.

role: test for cross-field document validator
description: Tests cross-field validation logic in Barkpark.Content, ensuring documents satisfy multi-field constraints before persistence.
whatBreaks: Cross-field validation bugs that corrupt or accept invalid documents go undetected.

role: Changeset + DB unique-constraint tests for core Document schema
description: Covers required doc_id/type, defaults (dataset, status, content), status inclusion validation, optional scalar/tenancy field casting, update-path nil clearing, and a Repo-level unique_constraint test on (doc_id,type,dataset_id).
whatBreaks: Document is the core content record; broken changeset rules or a missed unique-constraint mapping could let duplicate/invalid documents be written or corrupt writes API-wide.

role: Unit tests for DraftId prefix helpers
description: Verifies drafts_prefix/0, draft_id/1 and published_id/1 idempotency and draft?/1 detection — the Sanity-style 'drafts.' convention used throughout publish/unpublish.
whatBreaks: A bug in draft/published id conversion would break publish/unpublish and draft-vs-published perspective filtering across the whole content system.

role: Verification test for reference-field edge extraction (Phase 2)
description: ExUnit test suite for Phase 2 edge extraction from reference fields. Covers five key scenarios: typed scalar refs (with refType), untyped scalar refs, arrayOf-of-reference, draft-only targets under the published lens, and draft-source coalescence. Tests the full round-trip from extract → store in content_edges → read back. The gap-#1 and gap-#2 regression locks are embedded here.
whatBreaks: Edge extraction regressions aren't caught before release. Untyped refs falsely flag dangling, typed/untyped disagreement goes unnoticed (gap #2), dangling edges escape into the table (violating FK constraint), and arrayOf refs fail to round-trip correctly. The slug-to-UUID resolution bug (gap #1) resurfaces.

role: DB-backed tests for Content.Edges reference-graph queries

role: Test suite for Barkpark.Content.Graph BFS traversal engine
description: Covers clamp_depth, traverse (truncation reasons, dedup via visited set), rank_dependents ordering, reverse_referencers, and orphans detection over materialised content_edges.
whatBreaks: Regressions could cause the blast-radius/backlink graph to silently miss edges, mis-rank dependents, or loop/crash on cyclic references.

role: Unit tests for Content.Labels codelist/style/render-opts helpers
description: Covers Barkpark.Content.Labels: codelist_label/3 nil/blank guards and DB-backed codelist resolution, paper_style/2 precedence rules, and render_opts/paper_render_opts option-map shaping used by paper rendering.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let ONIX/codelist label lookups or paper style resolution silently misbehave without test coverage catching it.

role: Regression test for rev-fenced concurrent-write protection on lifecycle verbs
description: Drives a concurrent-write race (via a before_* lifecycle hook that bumps a row's rev between read and delete) against publish/unpublish/delete to prove the rev fence returns {:error, {:rev_mismatch, _}} instead of silently destroying newer edits; also covers happy paths and already-gone-row semantics.
whatBreaks: Losing this test's guarantee reopens a data-loss class bug where a concurrent edit during publish/unpublish/delete could be silently discarded.

role: Core behaviour tests for Content.Lifecycle publish/unpublish/discard/delete
description: Verifies happy-path row transitions (draft<->published) for the four lifecycle verbs and that a row already consumed by a concurrent writer surfaces as {:error, :not_found} rather than an uncaught Ecto.StaleEntryError.
whatBreaks: Broken lifecycle semantics could cause 500s or phantom/partial document states across the entire publish/unpublish/delete flow, which every content type depends on.

role: Test suite for LocalizedText fallback-chain resolver
description: Verifies resolve/2's language fallback ordering (primary -> secondary -> first-non-empty -> :no_value), including empty-string and whitespace-only treated as missing.
whatBreaks: Broken localized-field fallback logic (v2 schema type) could surface blank or wrong-language text without any test catching it.

role: Security regression test for private-field redaction in mutation echo
description: Tests that apply_mutations echoes the mutated document back through real caller redaction (not the :internal no-redaction sentinel), so non-admin/anonymous callers never see private fields in a create/patch echo response.
whatBreaks: Reverting this fix leaks private schema fields (e.g. salary) in write-response payloads to non-admin callers, a real security regression.

role: Row/ownership ACL test suite for owner_scoped document types
description: Large suite (319 lines) proving user A can never read user B's documents on an owner_scoped:true type via any read path (get, list, search, tag, alias, batch), while admins/api-tokens see everything and non-owner_scoped types are unaffected.
whatBreaks: A failure here means cross-user data leakage on owner-scoped types — one user reading another's private documents.

role: Unit test for Content.search_papers/3 title-substring typeahead
description: Verifies case-insensitive substring matching, title ordering, blank-query short circuit, and the 20-item result cap used by the `[[` autocomplete/quick-switcher.
whatBreaks: Paper linking/autocomplete in the editor could return wrong, unordered, or unbounded results.

role: Coverage for the doctrine-template corpus backfill (plan/1, run/1)
description: Large (515-line) test of DoctrineBackfill's pure classifier (title synthesis heuristics, featured-image promotion rules, conformer detection, idempotence, unfixable classes) and its DB-scan/apply writer, including a byte-identical no-op guarantee for already-conforming papers.
whatBreaks: A broken backfill could corrupt legacy papers' content/title/body_html when migrating them to the content-first template doctrine, or silently mutate already-conforming papers.

role: Tests for the Papers content-first template enforcement (Template module)
description: Locks seeding of new blank papers (locked title + body), title derivation from the locked title block, template shape validation, and op backstops preventing removal/move/unlock of locked blocks.
whatBreaks: Loss of this guarantee could let clients delete or reorder the locked title/structure of a Paper, breaking the content-first doctrine invariant relied on across Bulldocs.

role: Unit tests for Barkpark.Content.Query read surface
description: Covers pure guard clauses (nil doc_id/type/dataset, empty id list, blank search query) and list_documents/search_documents_by_title behavior including limit/offset clamping (1..1000) and result capping.
whatBreaks: Query is the extracted heavy read path used across the API; a regression could cause crashes on nil input or unbounded/incorrect query results.

role: Test for actor_user_id threading into the revisions audit trail
description: Verifies that opts[:user_id] passed to writes/publish/delete is stamped onto the resulting revision row (actor_user_id), with nil back-compat when no user_id is supplied, powering the who-edited-what activity log.
whatBreaks: Without this, the activity/audit log would lose attribution of who made a given edit, publish, or delete.

role: Unit tests for Content.Revision changeset
description: Tests required fields (doc_id/type/action), the dataset default of 'production', and casting of optional fields (title, status, dataset, content, workspace_id, project_id) plus that unknown fields are ignored.
whatBreaks: A regression in Revision.changeset validation could let malformed revision rows be written (or reject valid ones), silently corrupting the audit/provenance trail.

role: Test suite for SchemaDefinition v2 schema parser
description: Exercises parse/2 for v2 field types: nested composite, arrayOf (ordered/unordered), and likely codelist/localizedText per file size (687 lines). Guards the schema-v2 field-type contract used across editor/validation/rendering.
whatBreaks: A broken v2 schema parser would let malformed schemas through or reject valid ones, cascading into validation, editor, and rendering failures for every v2-typed field.

role: Regression test for NULL-dataset_id schema uniqueness race
description: Pins the partial unique index (name, dataset) WHERE dataset_id IS NULL that backstops flat (no-project) schema deployments where Postgres NULL != NULL would otherwise allow duplicate schema rows; also asserts distinct dataset strings still coexist.
whatBreaks: Without this guard/coverage, concurrent flat-deployment schema upserts could silently create duplicate SchemaDefinition rows, corrupting schema lookups repo-wide.

role: Runtime guard test for per-field 'surface' metadata round trip
description: Verifies the paper.json schema's 'surface' field stamps survive SchemaDefinition.parse -> Content.upsert_schema -> serialize_schema_for_sdk, and that every demo-seeded schema field re-parses with a valid surface (nil/body/sidebar) — protects unconsumed metadata from silently being dropped before a future feature reads it.
whatBreaks: A dropped or corrupted 'surface' stamp would go unnoticed until a future sidebar-v2 feature consumes it, at which point fields would render in the wrong UI location with no test signal today.

role: Unit tests for the Content.Scope tenant-boundary query helper
description: Directly inspects the Ecto.Query AST produced by scope_to_workspace/2-3, scope_to_workspace_global/1, and scope_to_workspace_or_global/3 — covers fail-closed on nil workspace_id (where: false), workspace-only vs workspace+project WHERE clauses, and composability with pre-existing wheres.
whatBreaks: Scope is the hard multi-tenant boundary used across Content queries; a regression here (e.g. fail-open instead of fail-closed on nil workspace_id) would be a cross-tenant data leak.

role: test for search intelligence module
description: Minimal test (25 LOC) for search intelligence helpers, likely covering query expansion or relevance scoring utilities.
whatBreaks: Search quality regressions go undetected, degrading full-text search results.

role: Regression test for drafts.-prefix vs status-column coherence invariant
description: Covers (a) create_document/upsert_document/apply_mutations coercing a caller-supplied status=published into a drafts.-prefixed draft row, (b) the published_only read-side prefix conjunct hiding an incoherent raw-inserted row, and (c) patch dropping the server-owned status field.
whatBreaks: If this invariant regresses, a draft-prefixed row could read as 'published' and leak unpublished content to anonymous/public surfaces (or vice versa hide published content).

role: Unit tests for Content.papers_with_tag/3 JSONB tag-index read
description: Covers exact-match (no case-fold), title-ordering, and blank/no-match returning [] for the #tag Obsidian-parity index over content['tags'].
whatBreaks: Tag-filtered paper listings (e.g. Bulldocs #tag views) could return wrong, missing, or wrongly-ordered results.

role: Unit tests for Content.search_tags/3 tag typeahead
description: Covers DISTINCT case-insensitive substring matching, capping at 20 results, blank-query top-distinct-tags fallback, and per-dataset scoping (no cross-dataset tag leak) for the #tag typeahead candidate list.
whatBreaks: The #tag typeahead in the paper editor could suggest duplicate, unbounded, or cross-tenant tag names.

role: test for schema validation evaluator
description: Tests the validation evaluator that applies schema field rules to documents, covering required fields, type checks, and constraint evaluation (203 LOC).
whatBreaks: Validation evaluator bugs allow malformed documents to persist, corrupting content integrity across the CMS.

role: test for validation ops evaluator
description: Tests Barkpark.Content.Validation.Ops — the expression evaluator for schema validation rules (:eq, :in, :gt, etc.). Covers scalar, map, and list comparisons.
whatBreaks: Incorrect validation operator logic goes undetected, allowing documents to bypass schema constraints.

role: test for validation path parser
description: Tests Barkpark.Content.Validation.Path — parses JSON-pointer-style path strings used to address fields in schema validation rules.
whatBreaks: Broken path parsing causes validation rules targeting nested fields to silently mismatch or crash.

role: Test suite for the Phase-0 recursive field validator + flat_mode parity
description: Confirms every legacy v1 seed schema round-trips unchanged through Validation.validate/3, and that v2 recursive validation (composite/arrayOf/codelist/localizedText) produces JSON-Pointer-ish error paths; notes the top-level validations rule slot is intentionally inert in this phase.
whatBreaks: Validator regressions could silently accept invalid documents or reject legitimate legacy schemas, breaking save/edit parity across the whole content system.

role: Tests for Content.Papers.ValueWriteback edit-through gate
description: Large, detailed test suite covering the 3 acceptance criteria for valueref edit-through: authorization is checked against the TARGET doc's scope (not the hosting paper's), impact preview via reverse_referencers fails closed (out-of-scope referencers vanish with no leak count), and the guarded write goes through Content.apply_mutations with rev-CAS, draft-divergence blocking, and provenance revisions.
whatBreaks: A regression could let a caller write to a canonical value doc outside their tenant scope, leak cross-tenant referencer titles/counts, or silently clobber someone's unpublished draft edit.

role: Tests for valueref drift/dangling detection and accept-baseline
description: Covers the pre-resolve pass's drift vs resolved vs dangling states rendered as data-valueref-state, the protective rule that public drift compares only against the published value (a diverged draft can't leak), and Content.accept_valueref_baseline/6's precise re-pinning of matching nodes, CAS-guarded writes, and provenance revisions.
whatBreaks: Wrong drift/dangling classification could mis-flag stale content as fresh (or vice versa) in Papers, and a broken accept-baseline could corrupt sibling blocks or silently overwrite content on a stale rev.

role: Tests for Content.resolve_values_in_blocks/3 valueref pre-resolve pass
description: Covers the batched valueref resolution pass: published-row preference over a diverged draft twin, published_only gating for anonymous surfaces, render-then-read redaction of private fields (never a caller-less bypass), tenant scoping, and the scalar-only rule (maps/lists/empty/dot-paths never resolve).
whatBreaks: A regression here could leak private-field values or draft-only/cross-tenant content to anonymous readers of Papers embedding valuerefs, or silently break value resolution across the app.

role: Test suite for Content.resolve_wikilink/3 title/alias resolution
description: Covers case-insensitive title match, exact alias containment, title-over-alias precedence on collision, blank/miss nil handling, and the deep-collecting resolve_wikilinks_in_blocks/3 across nested blocks including blockref targets.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions would let wikilinks resolve to the wrong document or silently degrade, corrupting navigable links across Papers.

role: Test suite for type-dispatched wikilink resolver powering the live task chip
description: Verifies resolve_wikilink falls through paper→task, builds the chip hit shape (kind/status/priority/criteria), enforces paper precedence on title collisions, tolerates garbage acceptance_criteria, and enforces published_only fail-closed gating for anonymous surfaces on both papers and tasks.
whatBreaks: A broken published_only gate would leak draft task titles/state to anonymous readers, or task chips would render with wrong status/criteria counts.

role: Unit tests for pure/DB-free helpers of Content.WriteScope
description: Tests build_ctx/1 defaults, inherit_scope_attrs/2 (copies workspace/project/dataset scope fields, skips nils), fire_after/3 error pass-through, and resolve_read_dataset_id/2 non-binary handling — no Repo involved.
whatBreaks: Scope-inheritance bugs could cause new documents to lose or wrongly inherit tenancy scope, risking cross-tenant data leaks.

role: Protective tests for optimistic-concurrency fencing in Content.Writer
description: Drives a concurrent-rev race via a before_save hook to prove ifMatch/ifRevisionID patch and replace paths reject stale writes (rev_mismatch) instead of last-write-wins, and asserts generate_id/1 entropy prevents id-collision overwrites on id-less creates; async:false because it mutates global plugin env.
whatBreaks: A regression here reintroduces the lost-update race, letting concurrent writers silently clobber each other's data despite optimistic-lock preconditions.

role: Unit tests for Content.Writer pure helpers (deep_merge, dynamics, envelope coercion)
description: Covers deep_merge/2 (nested map merge, list replace-not-merge), resolve_dynamics/1 ($today tokens in strings/maps/lists), from_envelope/1 (flat Sanity-style envelope coercion into content, reserved-key exclusion, default draft status), and a trivial validate_task_kind/2 passthrough.
whatBreaks: Envelope coercion bugs would leak reserved keys into content or misroute flat-style writes, corrupting document shape on ingest.

role: DB test guarding Classic-save block/data-loss invariant
description: Proves creating an Expectation-bearing document (e.g. post) instantiates bound layout blocks + free body blocks correctly, and that a Classic-mode save updates the bound field/block without dropping or reordering any free block — the '#1 invariant' for the block-editor/Classic-form dual-write path.
whatBreaks: A regression could cause Classic-form saves to silently drop or reorder a document's free content blocks, a severe data-loss bug across every PortableDoc-backed document type.

role: test for dataset CORS origin resolution
description: Tests Content.allowed_origins_for_dataset/1 — verifies that CORS origins are unioned and deduplicated across schemas in a dataset.
whatBreaks: Incorrect CORS origin merging allows unauthorized origins or breaks legitimate cross-origin access.

role: test for cross-project dataset isolation
description: Proves that dataset name strings are project-scoped — reading 'production' for project A must not bleed rows from project B's 'production' dataset. Covers stats, export, revisions, and schema functions.
whatBreaks: Dataset scope regression causes one project's data to leak into another project's reads, a serious multi-tenancy bug.

role: test for dataset_id as authoritative scoping key
description: Proves the W2 invariant: dataset_id (not the dataset string) is the unique scoping key, allowing two projects to each own a document with the same doc_id + type without collision. Also verifies read-scope and string-mirror consistency.
whatBreaks: Regression on dataset_id uniqueness causes cross-workspace document collisions or data loss.

role: test for dataset listing
description: Tests Content.list_datasets/0 — verifies that distinct dataset name strings are returned sorted from both schema_definitions and documents.
whatBreaks: Broken dataset listing causes the Studio dataset picker to show wrong or duplicate entries.

role: test for drafts list pagination
description: Tests pagination of draft documents in the Content module, using pinned deterministic timestamps to avoid CI flakes from wall-clock ordering races.
whatBreaks: Drafts pagination regressions (wrong order, off-by-one page boundaries) go undetected.

role: test for envelope id handling on document create
description: Pins the fix for a mixed-shape footgun where supplying a top-level _id alongside a legacy content map silently dropped the id. Ensures supplied ids are honoured across all input shapes.
whatBreaks: Regression causes created documents to receive generated ids instead of caller-supplied ones, breaking all downstream references.

role: test for Expectation read API
description: Tests Content.resolve_expectation/1 — verifies that a schema's layout/prefill Expectation resolves correctly from explicit stored columns or falls back to field-order defaults.
whatBreaks: Wrong Expectation resolution causes block scaffolding on new documents to use incorrect field order or prefill values.

role: test for Expectation-aware slash menu field availability
description: Tests Content.available_expected_fields/2,3 and expected_field_blocked?/3 — pure functions that enforce max-cardinality caps on expected fields for the slash insert menu.
whatBreaks: Cardinality enforcement bugs allow inserting duplicate singleton fields or incorrectly hide still-available ones in the editor.

role: Test suite for Content.list_documents filter operators
description: Verifies filter_map operators (eq and others) against seeded published documents, checking query-layer filtering correctness for the /v1/data/query surface.
whatBreaks: Broken filter operators would return wrong document sets from the query API, affecting every consumer that filters content (web, SDK, CLI).

role: test for find_referencing_docs and disconnect_references
description: Behaviour-lock tests for `find_referencing_docs/3` and `disconnect_references/3`, pinning that the SQL-pushed eq filter returns only referencing rows and leaves non-referencing docs untouched.
whatBreaks: Reference-disconnect bugs (orphaned or wrongly-severed references) go undetected on schema deletions or document moves.

role: test for flat envelope round-trip
description: Single test confirming flat (non-nested) document creation and Envelope.render round-trip preserves scalar and array fields.
whatBreaks: Flat document field corruption on create/render goes undetected.

role: test for schema initial_values pre-fill
description: Tests that schema-declared `initial_values` (including `$today` variable expansion and nested defaults) are pre-filled when new documents are created.
whatBreaks: New documents silently missing default field values, breaking Studio UX that relies on schema-driven defaults.

role: Negative test guarding cross-workspace tenancy isolation on mutate paths
description: Proves a workspace-B caller cannot publish/unpublish/delete/reference-resolve/media-delete a same-id artifact owned by workspace A, closing a fail-open scope_to_workspace bug (barkpark-s6t1/af50). Uses identical dataset+doc_id across two workspaces to force isolation to come from workspace_id alone.
whatBreaks: A regression here reopens a critical cross-tenant data leak/mutation vulnerability, letting one workspace's users mutate or delete another workspace's documents.

role: Test suite for optimistic-concurrency (:if_rev) guard on paper batch ops
description: Confirms Content.apply_paper_block_ops/4 rejects a batch with {:error, :precondition_failed} and leaves the paper untouched when if_rev mismatches current rev, and applies + bumps rev when it matches.
whatBreaks: Losing this optimistic-concurrency guard could let concurrent Papers editors silently clobber each other's block edits.

role: DB test for project-on-write PortableDoc paper path
description: Confirms editing a bound title block updates content["title"] visible via the Classic Envelope query, doc.body resolves from free blocks, and lazy synthesis of legacy docs (no content["blocks"]) is byte-equal without rewriting the stored row on read.
whatBreaks: A regression could break the Classic/block-editor projection parity, causing legacy documents to be silently mutated on read or bound fields to desync from block content.

role: test for PubSub workspace/project context
description: Verifies that realtime PubSub broadcasts are additive — the existing `documents:<dataset>` topic fires AND the message carries `workspace_id`/`project_id`, and a new workspace-scoped topic is emitted without breaking the original.
whatBreaks: Workspace-scoped realtime subscribers miss updates or receive updates from wrong workspaces.

role: PubSub cross-workspace leak regression test
description: Proves that paper and document PubSub topics are workspace-scoped, so writes in workspace B produce no events on workspace A's subscriptions even when slug/type/pubid collide.
whatBreaks: Real-time leakage of private document deltas across tenant workspace boundaries.

role: test for reference_title resolver
description: Unit tests for `Content.reference_title/3`, verifying it never raises on non-unique doc-ids and returns a single title preferring the published row over draft twins.
whatBreaks: Reference title resolution crashes or returns wrong titles in Studio reference fields.

role: test for per-request dataset-id memoization
description: Tests that resolve_read_dataset_id is memoized per HTTP request process but NOT for LiveView or Oban worker pids, preventing stale dataset references after workspace cascade-delete.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the memoization opt-in gate go undetected, risking reads pinned to deleted dataset ids in long-lived processes.

role: test for document revision stamping
description: Two minimal tests verifying that create_document stamps a binary rev field and that upsert_document produces a new rev distinct from the prior one.
whatBreaks: Silent regression in rev generation goes undetected, breaking revision history and conflict detection.

role: Negative test guarding revision-history IDOR + cross-dataset restore
description: Proves HistoryController.show/restore correctly scope by dataset (not just workspace/project), closing an intra-workspace IDOR read and a cross-dataset write bug (barkpark-vdmk) where a revision from dataset A could be restored into dataset B.
whatBreaks: Regression reopens an IDOR vulnerability letting any token in a workspace read/restore another dataset's revision by UUID, and could corrupt documents via cross-dataset restore.

role: test for cross-workspace schema isolation
description: Proves that schema definitions (field shapes, visibility flags) are strictly scoped per workspace — workspace A's schemas are invisible to workspace B reads and vice versa.
whatBreaks: Cross-tenant schema leakage goes undetected, exposing one tenant's content model to another workspace.

role: Integration test lock for sheet-embed write-through + hydration + formula recompute
description: Exercises Barkpark.Content's sheet CRUD, write-through refresh of embedding papers' block snapshots on sheet mutation/publish, backfill via the RehydrateEmbeds mix task, formula recompute (M3) including #CYCLE! handling, PubSub broadcast ordering, and the draft-content boundary (a draft sheet edit must never leak into a published paper's cached snapshot).
whatBreaks: if this test regressed silently, sheet embeds in papers could go stale or leak unpublished draft cell values to public /papers readers

role: unit tests for Studio LiveView helper functions
description: Tests fetch_doc_with_draft/3, doc_to_form/2, and build_content/2 — pure helper functions extracted from StudioLive for the document editor form lifecycle.
whatBreaks: Bugs in Studio document form helpers (draft fetching, form building) go undetected.

role: test for write-scoping fix in upsert prev-doc lookup
description: Regression test for barkpark-0mw9: verifies that upsert_document's prev-doc lookup is scoped to the writer's workspace/project, preventing cross-workspace document clobber when two workspaces share doc_id+type.
whatBreaks: Regression restores the cross-workspace write bug allowing an upsert in workspace B to overwrite workspace A's document.

role: test for workspace-scoped content read isolation
description: Proves the hard tenant boundary on the read path: documents from workspace A do not appear in workspace B's scoped reads, while the Default scope remains backward-compatible.
whatBreaks: Cross-tenant document leakage on read paths goes undetected.

role: test for workspace-scoped write stamping
description: Proves the write-side tenant boundary: apply_mutations stamps the correct workspace_id on new documents and those documents are invisible to reads scoped to a different workspace.
whatBreaks: Write-side tenant isolation regression goes undetected, allowing documents to be created without proper workspace scoping.

role: Test suite for the envelope-DEK crypto stack (KEK/DataKeys/FieldCipher)
description: Exercises LocalKek wrap/unwrap round-trip and tamper-fails-closed, DataKeys per-scope DEK lifecycle (create-on-demand, rotation, one-active-DEK DB constraint), FieldCipher envelope encryption round-trip/AAD-scoping/tamper-detection/idempotency, malformed-envelope fail-closed cases, and full KEK-rotation-with-previous-key-fallback rewrap_all flow.
whatBreaks: Undetected crypto regressions could leak plaintext secrets, corrupt encrypted fields irrecoverably, or break KEK rotation, compromising all encrypted-at-rest data.

role: Test suite for the bounded in-process unwrapped-DEK ETS cache
description: Verifies the DEK cache clears-on-full at its 10,000-entry cap (rather than growing unbounded) and that puts/gets still work correctly under and after the cap trip.
whatBreaks: An unbounded cache would leak memory holding decrypted keys indefinitely under high scope cardinality, a security and stability risk.

role: Test suite for the DataCase sandbox-drain fix guarding fire-and-forget DB tasks
description: Directly pins the behavior of Barkpark.DataCase.drain_owned_tasks/2: awaits $callers-chained fire-and-forget tasks (including transitive task-of-task spawns like webhook fan-out) before the sandbox owner stops, while never blocking on another test's unrelated tasks (raw spawn breaks the $callers chain).
whatBreaks: Regressing the drain reintroduces flaky test-suite failures from killed Postgrex connections under concurrent test runs (a known flake cluster across multiple content-write-path tests), undermining CI trust.

role: Security regression test: fail-closed edge resolution across colliding-slug tenants
description: Proves Content.add_edge/add_edges and Projector.rebuild_scope/upsert_record refuse to resolve or delete edges across workspaces when a workspace_id is nil, guarding against a cross-tenant content_edges leak/deletion when two tenants share a dataset string and colliding slug.
whatBreaks: a regression here means content_edges rows (and thus Graph.traverse results) can silently span two tenants, leaking or destroying another workspace's data

role: Test suite for the paper body-walk edge extractor + reprojection wiring + backfill
description: Covers Bulldocs.extract_edges/2 (valueref/wikilink/ref/href → content_edges, dedup, self-edge rejection, drafts.-prefix coalescing), that all three paper writers enqueue debounced ProjectorWorker rebuilds, the full loop from a block-op edit through a performed job to a real stored edge row (including a mixed-type Oban uniqueness-key regression guard), and EdgeProjector.Backfill's dry-run vs apply idempotent behavior over pre-existing corpus content.
whatBreaks: A regression here would silently stop paper wikilinks/valuerefs from projecting into the content_edges graph, breaking backlinks, live-value chips, and the Truth Fabric edge graph across the corpus.

role: Unit/integration test for Barkpark.EdgeProjector.Projector + ProjectorWorker
description: Verifies project/3 unions core reference-field edges with plugin-projected edges (deduped), fresh-install-with-no-plugins yields only core edges, delete_record removes both edge directions, upsert_record replaces changed edges and prunes stale ones, and the Oban ProjectorWorker routes rebuild/delete ops correctly.
whatBreaks: the content graph (used for reference navigation/backlinks) could show stale, duplicated, or missing edges after doc publish/delete

role: Test suite for ProjectorWorker's Oban enqueue/2, enqueue_upsert/3, enqueue_delete/3
description: Asserts job args shape (op, scope, types normalized sorted+deduped, perspective default, nil-opt dropping) and specifically guards the lvw-t11-followup-dedup fix: mixed-type rebuilds (e.g. task vs paper) in the same debounce window must NOT collide/drop under Oban's uniqueness key, while same-type bursts still collapse into one job.
whatBreaks: A regression reopens the mixed-type dedup drop, silently discarding one type's edge-rebuild job whenever two different doc types are edited within the debounce window, leaving the edge graph stale with no retry.

role: Unit tests for ProjectorWorker.perform/1 cancel/error paths
description: Covers Oban job cancellation reasons (:missing_id, :no_type_for_upsert, :doc_gone) and success path via injected content/projector test-seam module overrides, complementing ProjectorTest's happy-path DB coverage.
whatBreaks: Regressions in edge-projector cancellation/error routing (e.g. jobs retrying forever on missing docs) would go undetected.

role: test for Tasks plugin edge extraction
description: Verifies that the Tasks plugin's extract_edges/2 reads from the authoritative task_edges table (not the dead content.dependencies key) and maps both 'blocks' and 'discovered-from' kinds correctly through to graph edges.
whatBreaks: Task dependency graph edges may silently project from wrong data sources or drop edge kinds, breaking the task graph view.

role: Unit tests for the EncryptedMap Ecto custom type
description: Verifies cast/dump/load/equal?/embed_as behavior including encrypt-decrypt round-trip via Cloak, ensuring encrypted map fields behave correctly as an Ecto type.
whatBreaks: Silent corruption or plaintext leakage of encrypted map-typed fields could go unnoticed, risking data loss or security regressions.

role: test for Idempotency key hashing
description: Tests that Idempotency.hash_key/4 is deterministic for the same inputs and produces distinct hashes when any of the four inputs (key, token, method, path) differ.
whatBreaks: Bugs in idempotency key hashing go undetected, risking duplicate mutations or collisions on write endpoints.

role: Unit tests for Media.Storage.Access permission/visibility logic
description: Pure-logic tests (no DB) covering visibility resolution, watermark profile, allowed?/4 for view/preview/original/edit_metadata, permissions/3 listing, and checkout/actor_label edge cases including empty-string and admin overrides.
whatBreaks: Broken access checks could leak private/checked-out media metadata or wrongly deny/allow edit and delivery permissions across the media API.

role: P0 security regression test for cross-workspace media metadata leak
description: Verifies Media.asset_docs_for_files and the search LEFT JOIN never surface one workspace's mediaAsset title/tags for another workspace's blob sharing the same dataset string, while legacy NULL-workspace asset docs remain visible in their own tenant (never-worse guarantee).
whatBreaks: a regression re-opens a real P0 leak where one tenant's media titles/tags/rights metadata become visible to another tenant

role: Regression test for redaction of embedded mediaAsset in asset responses
description: Ensures AssetResponse.render routes the embedded document through the Envelope redaction boundary so anonymous/conn-less callers get private fields dropped while admin callers see raw content; guards a prior security bug (WS-B HIGH-2).
whatBreaks: Private/encrypted fields on media assets could leak to unauthenticated API callers, a real security regression.

role: Unit test for the Media CDN URL-rewriting/invalidation module
description: Covers Cdn.public_url prefixing behavior and Cdn.invalidate_paths posting purge requests to a configured HTTP adapter (via Bypass), toggling the global :media_cdn Application env (hence async: false).
whatBreaks: CDN URL rewriting or cache purge could silently fail, serving stale media or broken asset URLs

role: Unit tests for Media.Delivery.Retriever text-filter query building

role: Integration test for media webhook delivery/retry via Barkpark.Media.Delivery.Events

role: Integration tests for the Vix (libvips) image rendering backend

role: Unit/integration test for MediaFile changeset
description: Covers Barkpark.Media.Storage.MediaFile.changeset/2: required fields, dataset default, FK casting, and the dangerous-MIME neutralization (svg/html/xml/js → application/octet-stream, stored-XSS hardening), plus the (path, dataset_id) unique-constraint DB behavior.

role: Unit test for Barkpark.Media.Probe image dimension/EXIF parsing

role: P0 security regression test for cross-workspace media relations-graph leak

role: Test for image rendition generation gating and preset specs

role: P0 security regression test for cross-workspace media share-link write leak

role: Unit test for Barkpark.Media.Storage.SignedUrl HMAC signing/verification
description: Round-trips sign/verify for media file URLs, and asserts expired signatures and tampered paths are rejected.

role: Context-boundary test suite for Barkpark.Media
description: Exercises upload_dir/0, file_path/1, get_file/get_file_by_path/list_files/query_files/search_files, delete_file (including race/stale-entry safety), and upload/3 fault paths: storage failure, config-gated MIME/extension allowlist, size cap, and that the server-derived MIME (not client-supplied) governs acceptance.

role: Test: workspace tenancy isolation for Media file reads
description: Proves the WHERE workspace_id filter on the Media context (list_files/query_files/search_files/get_file) prevents cross-workspace leaks, and that unscoped/Default-scope reads still work for back-compat. Mirrors ContentWorkspaceScopeTest.

role: SSRF-guard test for Barkpark.Net.SafeOutbound
description: Tests IP classification (rejects loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/unspecified for both IPv4 and IPv6, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 unwrapping), URL shape validation (host/userinfo/scheme), the allow_private_outbound escape hatch, and post/2 refusing blocked URLs without making a network call.

role: Test for Papers body_html cache-version stamping

role: Test: workspace tenancy isolation for Bulldocs paper_events

role: Test: Barkpark.Papers.TextDiff pure LCS line-differ

role: Test: Barkpark.Plugin top_menu_entries/0 callback contract

role: Test: Barkpark.Plugins.Bootstrap auto-install of plugin schemas

whatBreaks: The goal-path rail (gitGraph-style event timeline) could show duplicate, missing, or wrongly-scoped events, or intents could be double-processed/never surfaced.

role: Test for ContentProbe.content_get/2 safe nested-map reader

role: Unit tests for GitHub sync conflict quarantine recorder

Also proves recording never emits mutation_events (no loop surface).

role: Unit tests for GitHub outbound mirror high-water-mark cursor
