role: Deterministic GenServer tests for the outbound mirror drain-tick loop
description: Fully-injected-seam tests (no Oban/network/sleep) for DrainWorker: backoff schedule, bootstrap-on-boot, per-event enqueue with halt-not-skip on failure, idle gate when Settings.active? is false, dark-to-active transition, active? memoize TTL, and a capstone loop-immunity test proving a source="github" stamped write is never re-enqueued.
whatBreaks: A regression could let the drain loop enqueue events out of order, fail to halt on an enqueue error (skipping events silently), or reintroduce an outbound/inbound echo loop that spams GitHub with duplicate issue mirrors.

role: Property-style tests enumerating the GitHub field-ownership matrix
description: Pure ExUnit tests (no DB) asserting Fields.all/0 entries each have exactly one direction (outbound_only/inbound_intake_only/never), that the three buckets partition all fields, that every outbound field maps to one issue_attr owned by barkpark/derived, and that claim/epoch/fence/rail_rev are permanently :never with no reverse writer function existing.
whatBreaks: If the field matrix accidentally became bidirectional or a ledger-only primitive (claim/epoch) leaked outbound, GitHub could overwrite or race Barkpark's own task-claim state, corrupting the task ledger.

role: Tests for the local-read GitHub sync-health snapshot aggregate
description: DB-only tests for Health.snapshot/1: totality/zero-shape when dark and DB empty, active/repo header resolution (incl. fail-closed on half-provisioned creds), conflict bucketing/capping at 50, per-dataset cursor/head/lag/pending (incl. 500-row pending cap), and Oban github_mirror queue depth counting by live state.
whatBreaks: A broken snapshot would make the Studio/console health view (or an API caller) show false-healthy status or raise, hiding real drain lag, queue backlog, or unresolved conflicts from operators.

role: Tests for inbound GitHub webhook detach/close-event handling
description: Tests Barkpark.Plugins.Github.InboundEvents.handle/2: deleted/transferred issues detach an existing intake task (state flip + detached conflict row), closed-by-human detaches while bot-sender or already-adopted closes are ignored/dropped, bot-drop runs before every action, every detach mutation_event is stamped source="github" (outbox-excluded), and the conflict_fun seam is best-effort (raises are swallowed).

role: Tests for inbound GitHub issue-to-task intake birth flow
description: Tests Barkpark.Plugins.Github.Intake.ingest/2: only issues.opened is processed, bot-sender drop before any Content write, deterministic gh-<num> task birth with correct labels/lifecycle, mutation_events stamped source="github" for outbox exclusion, idempotent re-delivery (no clobber of post-birth edits), dedup-refusal path (comment + dead-letter conflict row, never silent), and best-effort backlink comment posting that never fails intake even on raise.
whatBreaks: If broken, outsider GitHub issues could either fail to birth tasks, double-birth on redelivery, silently drop look-alike duplicates without notifying the reporter, or leak inbound writes back out through the outbound mirror loop.

role: Tests for the content.github bookkeeping Link helper
description: Tests Barkpark.Plugins.Github.Link get/put/synced?: round-trips content.github, stamps mutation_events source="github", patch-merges rather than clobbering, collapses a draft twin into an already-published task without leaving a permanent draft, proves loop immunity (Outbox never drains the stamp), and synced?/1 correctness keyed on synced_rev == doc rev.
whatBreaks: A bug here could create permanent duplicate draft/published task pairs, break the sync-status computation used to short-circuit MirrorJob (causing redundant PATCHes or missed syncs), or leak the bookkeeping write back into the outbound drain loop.

role: Large integration test suite for the outbound MirrorJob.reconcile Oban worker
description: Extensive Bypass-mocked-GitHub tests for MirrorJob.reconcile/2,3: create/update/close issue mirroring, tenant-scope threading, full HTTP error classification (422 cancel, 429 snooze, 5xx retry, 404 detach), out-of-band drift conflict quarantine with fingerprinting, short-circuits (intake gate, already-synced, detached, repo_unconfigured), Oban args wiring incl. drafts.-id normalization, and Projects/Relations projection wiring with failure isolation (swallowed errors/raises, rate-limit snooze, sub-issue rejection recording, relink debounce/cap).

role: regression test for GitHub label-length clamp on task mirror close
description: End-to-end red-before/green-after test proving MirrorJob.reconcile/2 clamps a long `worker:` label to GitHub's 50-char limit so the close PATCH succeeds instead of 422'ing (the live defect that silently broke auto-close-mirror for long worker ids).
whatBreaks: a regression where worker-label projection exceeds 50 chars again would silently break auto-closing of mirrored GitHub issues (422 client error) and this test would no longer catch it if itself broken/removed.

role: Tests for the outbound mutation_events outbox reader (loop-cut #2)
description: Tests Outbox.fetch/3: excludes source="github" rows (loop guard) and non-task types, includes default/unset source rows, and returns ordered/paginated results respecting after_id cursor and limit for causal replay.

role: Unit tests for the Github plugin's manifest/routes/settings contract
description: Verifies Barkpark.Plugins.Github's manifest, register_routes/oban_crontab/register_workers gating (drain worker toggle), settings_schema masking, fail-closed validate_settings/1, and desk_items. Locks the plugin's public wiring contract.

role: Unit tests for the pure task→GitHub-issue Projection module

description: Covers Barkpark.PortableDoc.FromMarkdown's GFM block mapping (headings, inline marks, lists, code, tables, hr), the mermaid-fence-to-diagram and portabledoc-fence-to-native-blocks upgrades, and fail-soft degradation (malformed JSON, disallowed types, HTML never reaching output unescaped).
whatBreaks: A regression could let unescaped/malicious HTML from an LLM chat response reach rendered output (XSS), or corrupt tables/diagrams generated from chat into papers.

role: Test suite for PortableDoc.Patch.apply_patches/2 batch semantics
description: Pure, DB-free tests of the all-or-nothing batch fold over apply_patch/2, including the ordering of append/patch/remove ops and the idempotent-no-op handling of a stale remove-block targeting an already-absent id (protects concurrent-edit batches from being discarded).
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a batched canvas edit either apply ops out of order or abort an entire user edit because of a harmless stale delete, corrupting or discarding real content changes.

role: Conformance test suite for the PortableDoc.Patch block-op engine
description: Generates one test per golden fixture under test/support/fixtures/doc-patch-op/*.json, asserting apply_patch(before, op) == after for all five ops (append/insert-after/patch/remove/replace-block); also checks input immutability and bare-block-list operation.
whatBreaks: A regression here would silently break the canonical block-patch semantics that every PortableDoc editor and canvas relies on, corrupting document edits across Papers/Bulldocs.

role: Test suite for PortableDoc.Projection bound/free block projection
description: Pure tests for the Exp-P2 bound-block model: partition/2 splits bound field-blocks from free blocks, and project/3 is the sole writer of content[fieldName] plus content['body'] (JSON + rendered HTML), preserving unrelated content keys.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let field-bound blocks (title, slug, featured image) fail to project into document content, or let free-block body content get lost/duplicated on every PortableDoc save.

role: Tripwire test: every emitted CSS class resolves to a real rule
description: Scans the :article render of the shared ParityFixture for every class= token and asserts each either has a matching selector in the canonical paper-surface stylesheet or sits on a justified @layout_hooks allowlist, catching typo'd/orphaned classes that would render as unstyled text.
whatBreaks: A walk.ex change adding a themed class without its stylesheet rule would silently ship unstyled paper content to readers, undetected by any other test.

role: Shrink-only ratchet test pinning allowed inline style= properties on :article
description: Asserts exact-set equality between CSS property names actually emitted inline in :article render output and a documented @allowlist (author-DATA only); a new structural property fails, and a stale allowlist entry (theme property migrated to a class) must be deleted in the same diff, enforcing the View/Edit-parity migration doctrine.
whatBreaks: A reintroduced structural inline style would break the 'View and Edit render identical selectors by construction' contract, reopening View/Edit visual drift the migration was meant to close.

role: CI gate enforcing canvas-editor/reader render byte-parity (pd-doctrine rule 3)
description: Large, heavily-documented gate proving every non-prose fleet block (tasks, cards, pipeline, roadmap, form, diagram, sheet, embed, etc.) is painted in the canvas via exactly one reader emitter (Render.render_block) or carried verbatim, that the editor JS bundle contains zero hand-mirrored reader markup, and includes injected-drift mutation proofs (§5) plus cross-checks into the paper-editor JS/mjs test chain.
whatBreaks: Losing this gate would let the canvas editor and the public paper reader silently diverge in appearance (a second HTML producer forking from the reader), corrupting the 'what you see is what ships' guarantee across the entire Papers/Bulldocs feature.

role: Test suite for the card WIDGET reader (Model B slot-based card)
description: Covers Components.card_html's arbitrary-slot recursion (media/title/body/action via the shared compose/walk bridge), tone accent classes, empty-slot omission, HTML-escaping, and freezes the legacy `cards` fleet grid emitter byte-for-byte as a separate, untouched producer.
whatBreaks: A regression could break card widget rendering (wrong slot order, XSS via unescaped title/body, or accidental corruption of the legacy cards fleet grid used elsewhere in papers).

role: Test suite for email-safe (inline-styled, table-based) fleet block rendering
description: Covers Barkpark.PortableDoc.Render.CardsEmail's cards/card/notes/note/pipeline/stage HTML-email variants: table layout, tone-colored borders sourced from the StatusVocab manifest, byte-identical stage/pipeline-node twinning, theme-aware /3 seam, and author-string escaping — proving the email palette never leaks bp-* classes or SVG (email clients can't handle them).
whatBreaks: Emails generated from papers could render broken (unsupported CSS classes/SVG stripped by mail clients) or leak unescaped author content as an XSS/HTML-injection vector in transactional email.

role: cross-surface golden-parity test for paper component renderer
description: Freshness + realization suite proving the Elixir Render.Components emitter, web fixtures, and Go pdrender fixtures stay term-identical and that real emitter HTML realizes the shared structural projection per block type. Fixture-driven loops over GenGoldenParity.types(); regenerate via mix barkpark.paper_components.gen_golden_parity.
whatBreaks: if this drifts silent, api/web/TUI paper-component surfaces can diverge without any gate catching it

role: unit tests for Render.Components HTML emitters (tasks, board, etc.)
description: Async, pure snapshot tests asserting status-vocab glyph/role mapping, phase grouping/rollups, momentum header math, and nested task depth rendering for the shared paper components library.
whatBreaks: regressions in task/board component rendering (glyphs, counts, nesting) ship undetected into Papers

role: unit tests for Render.Compose block-to-semantic-kind mapping
description: Verifies compose_block/1-2 converts raw PortableDoc blocks (heading, divider, action, image, etc.) into semantic Pd* kinds correctly for both email and article render styles, including default/edge-case handling.
whatBreaks: wrong semantic kind mapping corrupts rendering across every PortableDoc surface (email + article)

role: unit tests for DataViz block emitters (stat, stats, heatmap)
description: Pure in-process tests asserting stat/sparkline/bullet-bar rendering, empty-state handling, and heatmap intensity normalization/clamping in the paper data-visualization components.
whatBreaks: data-viz blocks (stats/heatmaps) in Papers render incorrect values or malformed HTML unnoticed

role: committed golden HTML fixture for the :email render byte-lock
description: A large, generated-and-committed single-line HTML blob exercising every PortableDoc block kind under the :email inline-style palette; used as an exact byte-identity oracle by email_golden_test.exs. Regenerated only deliberately, never hand-edited.
whatBreaks: an accidental email-palette regression (which breaks real email clients that strip stylesheets) goes undetected

role: byte-lock test guarding the :email render palette against drift
description: Asserts Render.render_html/2 under :email opts is byte-identical to the committed email_golden.html and that the golden covers every rendered block kind; documents that :article Stage-2 rewrites must never leak into the :email inline-style path.
whatBreaks: email HTML output (which real mail clients depend on staying inline-styled) silently regresses when article-mode refactors leak across the palette seam

role: unit tests for Render.Figures leaf emitters (mermaid, captions, code block)
description: Tests HTML-escaping and formatting behavior of encode_mermaid, figcaption_inner, code_block_html, section_divider_html, and diagram_html, including a token-bound CSS accent-color assertion for code blocks.
whatBreaks: diagram/code-block/caption rendering in Papers mis-escapes content or drops styling, including XSS-relevant escaping

role: unit tests for FleetEmail component emitters (tasks/board/roadmap in email mode)
description: Mirrors data_viz_test pattern: asserts real <table>-based markup (no bp- classes/svg) and status-color hex values sourced from StatusVocab.tones() for the email-safe fleet component renderers.
whatBreaks: task/board/roadmap blocks embedded in outbound emails render broken or with wrong status colors in real mail clients

role: server-side edit-island repaint test for fleet blocks (cards/pipeline/notes)
description: Proves Patch.apply_patch's patch-block op shallow-merges edited content (immutable id/type) and that re-rendering via Components.*_html reflects new content — i.e. server is the sole producer of fleet HTML for the in-canvas editor loop.
whatBreaks: in-canvas edits to cards/pipeline/notes blocks either fail to persist correctly or the preview drifts from actual saved content

role: unit tests for Render.Forms question/section HTML emitter
description: Asserts form_html/2 wraps questions in correct section/fieldset markup by kind (grill/questionnaire) and renders text/yesno/single/multi question types with proper input elements across article/email styles.
whatBreaks: form blocks in Papers render malformed or wrong input types, breaking questionnaires/grills

role: Unit tests for PortableDoc inline node composer (Render.Inline)
description: Pure, in-process tests covering compose_inline_children/1 and compose_inline/2 — text nodes, scalar tolerance, and inline formatting composition for the block-render engine.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let broken inline text/formatting rendering ship silently into every paper/email/article surface.

role: Unit tests for Render.Palettes (fonts/colors/width constants)
description: Pure tests asserting the constant accessors (font_body, font_mono, brand hex, default_width) and the email_palette/0 struct shape used to theme the email rendering path.
whatBreaks: Undetected drift in palette constants would silently change brand color/typography across every rendered email.

role: Unit tests for email-safe panel block emitters (terminal/columns/status-legend)
description: Pure tests on Render.PanelsEmail verifying table-based, class-free HTML output (email clients strip <style>/classes) including the hard-coded traffic-dot hex colors and live-flag behavior tied to StatusVocab tones.
whatBreaks: A broken panel emitter could produce email HTML with unsupported CSS classes, causing panels to render blank or unstyled in real email clients.

role: Guard test: dark-theme CSS token parity between edit surface and /papers reader
description: Cross-checks paper-surface.css's html[data-theme=dark] tokens against bulldocs.html.heex's prefers-color-scheme dark block, ensuring every edit-dark token is re-skinned for the OS-dark reader; regression tripwire for bug #1217 (light callout boxes on dark article).
whatBreaks: A newly added dark token skipped in the reader's prefers-color-scheme block would silently reintroduce mismatched light-on-dark styling for anonymous OS-dark readers.

role: Byte-freeze tests for Render's document wrapper (email vs article envelopes)
description: Pins the exact HTML envelope bytes produced by Render.render_html/2 with doctype:true for both :email (inline-only, byte-frozen forever since email clients strip <style>) and :article (embeds canonical paper-surface stylesheet) document kinds.
whatBreaks: A silent envelope change could break email client rendering (adding disallowed <style>/classes) or break the article export's self-containment guarantee.

role: Fuzz/tolerance guard: render_blocks/2 must never raise on malformed nodes
description: Feeds 7 known-malformed-but-plausible block/inline shapes (nil, boolean, numeric-as-string, non-list items, etc.) into Render.render_blocks/2 to prove it degrades gracefully instead of raising, since schemaless Papers data can be mutated into invalid shapes by any raw API/SDK/CLI call.
whatBreaks: A poisoned block/inline node could crash the Papers save, body_html cache refresh, delta frames, Studio view, and public reader with a 500 error simultaneously.

role: Tests for section grid-layout engine (stack vs grid emission) in Render
description: Verifies byte-identity between no-layout and explicit {mode:stack} sections (legacy-corpus tripwire) and correct .bp-section__grid/.bp-section__cell emission with --bp-tracks CSS var when layout.mode=grid.
whatBreaks: A layout-engine regression could silently reflow every legacy paper's section HTML or break the newer grid-section feature.

role: Unit tests locking the design/status-manifest.json → StatusVocab contract
description: Asserts exact role/glyph/spinner/tone mappings derived from the status manifest that every surface (CSS/Go/web) is expected to match; a companion shell script (status-manifest-check.sh) checks cross-surface drift.
whatBreaks: A manifest edit that changes status→role/glyph/tone mapping without updating this test would desync task-status visuals across Elixir, CSS, Go, and web surfaces.

role: Guard test for the single-source paper-surface CSS embedding contract
description: Confirms Render.Stylesheet.css/0 returns the on-disk paper-surface.css byte-identically, contains sentinel tokens (--bp-h1-size, --paper-ink), is embedded in both root.html.heex (Studio) and bulldocs.html.heex (/papers reader), and that root.html.heex no longer locally redefines --bp-* tokens.
whatBreaks: Divergence between the CSS source and its two sinks would cause Studio and the public reader to render papers with mismatched typography/theming.

role: Tests proving the theme-injection thread is live end-to-end through Render
description: Two-part guard: byte-lock proof that the :evergreen default theme renders identically to a theme-less call, and a liveness proof that a fully-overridden theme map propagates through every relocated color (buttons, data-viz, field-color swatches).
whatBreaks: A broken theme-resolution thread could silently fall back to hard-coded evergreen colors for every custom-themed paper/workspace.

role: Unit tests for PortableDoc render HTML-escape helpers
description: Pure ExUnit tests for `Barkpark.PortableDoc.Render.Util` — escape_html/1 and escape_attr/1, covering double-escape avoidance and fail-soft nil handling.
whatBreaks: If wrong, XSS-escaping regressions in every rendered PortableDoc block (paper/email/article) would ship undetected.

role: Fixture-driven tests for the inline live-value (valueref) render node
description: Tests the PURE render side of the inline valueref node against a shared golden fixture set also consumed by the Go TUI and web renderers, covering resolved/unresolved/missing-resolver fallback paths and injection safety.
whatBreaks: A break here means live-value substitution (e.g. task/sheet values inline in prose) could silently render wrong data or leak unescaped HTML across all three renderer surfaces.

role: Drift tripwire asserting View and Edit paper typography stay byte-identical
description: Parses the real `Render.Stylesheet` CSS and `root.html.heex` Edit-surface CSS and asserts every shared (element, property) pair matches, guarding pd-doctrine rule 3 (prose typography leg; sibling test covers the non-prose fleet leg).
whatBreaks: If this guard is broken/weakened, the Studio editor and the public paper reader could silently diverge visually (double-spacing, font drift) without any test catching it.

role: Core unit tests for the PortableDoc block-tree HTML walker
description: Large (771-line) pure test suite for `Render.Walk.render_body/3` covering per-block-type HTML emission (hr, and presumably many more blocks) across email vs article palettes, including inline-escaping/injection safety.
whatBreaks: Regressions here mean the core block-to-HTML renderer used by papers, emails, and articles could emit malformed or unsafe markup across the whole PortableDoc surface.

role: Test suite for the PortableDoc Render 'sheet' embed block
description: Covers Render.compose_block/2 for type 'sheet', verifying snapshot data (head/rows/col_widths) composes to a PdSheet render node correctly, including empty-snapshot and partial-snapshot cases and style-invariance.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let embedded sheet snapshots inside Papers render with missing headers, wrong rows, or crash on partial snapshot data.

role: Large conformance test suite for the PortableDoc static HTML render walker
description: Extensive (1500+ line) pure test file covering Render.render_html/walk for essentially every PdNode kind (PdContainer, PdBox, PdHr, etc.), doctype wrapping, and the body_html_render_version cache-cutover stamp used by mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html to detect stale cached HTML.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let the static HTML render pipeline for every Paper/document body silently produce wrong markup or fail to bump the cache-version stamp, leaving stale HTML served indefinitely.

role: Tests proving legacy-content vs slot-model callout encodings render byte-identically
description: Large suite covering `Barkpark.PortableDoc.{Constraints,Slots}` and `Render.Compose`, proving the additive slots encoding and legacy inline `content` encoding of the same callout body compose to identical Pd trees.
whatBreaks: A regression could make legacy-format callouts render differently from new slot-format callouts, causing visual/byte drift across reader/TUI/email outputs.

role: Unit tests for schema-field-to-block synthesis logic
description: Pure tests for `Barkpark.PortableDoc.Synthesis` — field_block_type/1 (v1/v2 schema field type mapping), synthesize/3, scaffold/4, and patch_bound_values/2.
whatBreaks: Wrong field-type mapping breaks auto-generation of paper blocks from schema fields, e.g. schema-bound editors rendering the wrong widget.

role: test for v2 field block config preservation
description: Pins that PaperFieldBlock.build_field/1 correctly carries structural config ('of'/'fields'/'codelistId'/'languages') on synthesized v2 blocks, guarding against a past Studio LiveView crash on arrayOf-of-composite fields.
whatBreaks: Missing config on synthesized blocks silently degrades arrayOf composite rendering and can crash Studio LiveView on document open.

role: Unit tests for PortableDoc task-block query-to-snapshot resolution
description: Tests `Barkpark.PortableDoc.TaskResolver.resolve/2` traversal logic that replaces task-list/task-detail block queries with fetched snapshot rows, using a stub fetcher to isolate traversal from DB.
whatBreaks: If broken, task-list/task-detail blocks embedded in papers could render stale queries instead of resolved task data, or crash on empty results.

role: Unit tests classifying PortableDoc block types into the Element/Widget/Section tier ladder
description: Tests `Barkpark.PortableDoc.Tiers.tier_of/1` against representative block type names, verifying the composition-doctrine tier ladder (element/widget/section) stays correctly classified as new block types are added.
whatBreaks: Misclassifying a block's tier could break composition/layout rules that depend on the Element·Widget·Section·Layout·Document ladder.

role: Cross-surface preview-manifest parity lock test (Elixir leg)
description: ConnCase test asserting one shared Preview.project/3 fixture stays byte-identical across three mirrors and renders correctly through the papers reader (ShareMeta), the v1 query envelope wire hoist, and the Studio PaneBuilder row meta; siblings exist in web (TS) and Go TUI.
whatBreaks: A break here means OpenGraph preview cards could silently diverge or fail across the public reader, API response, and Studio, without any surface's own tests catching it.

role: Unit tests for the pure OpenGraph preview-manifest builder
description: Tests `Barkpark.Preview.project/3` (pure, no DB) covering image/title/description fallback chains, the injected media-resolver seam, per-doctype extensions, and the degradation invariant producing a valid card even with no preview options.
whatBreaks: Bugs here directly break how link previews (social cards) are computed for every document type across all consuming surfaces.

role: Unit tests for signed/JWT-style preview-link token lifecycle
description: Covers Barkpark.PreviewToken sign/verify round-trip, tamper detection, expiry, jti replay/revocation, verify_and_record atomicity, and the sweep/1 grace-period cleanup. Exercises the security-sensitive one-time-use preview link mechanism.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a leaked or replayed preview token stay valid, or a legitimate preview link fail, without being caught before merge.

role: Test suite for the Pulse live cost/vitals metrics sampler
description: Exercises the supervised Barkpark.Pulse.Metrics GenServer: per-interval rate bumps/decay, CPU/mem vitals sanity, PubSub 'vitals' broadcast on the pulse channel, and the durable cost-nanos meter accrual/read-back. Uses shared-mode Sandbox so the globally supervised process can share the test DB connection.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let the live cost/CPU dashboard silently show wrong or non-decaying numbers, or let cost accrual drift, without any test catching it.

role: Test for quiz-edit-to-live-room bridge (Studio publish syncs running quiz)
description: Covers Barkpark.Quiz.Bridge: binding a room to a published quiz doc, a live edit+publish pushing the new question into an already-running room via the document_changed PubSub broadcast, dataset isolation (same quiz_id in two datasets must not cross-inject content), and ignoring unrelated document changes.
whatBreaks: A broken bridge would mean quiz edits in Studio never reach live rooms (or worse, leak staging content into production rooms) with no test to catch it.

role: Test for the quiz content schema and doc→question parsing/loading
description: Covers Barkpark.Quiz.Content: to_question/2 parsing (including graceful defaults and title fallback), the private 'quiz' schema definition (answer key must not be public-readable), plugin schema registration/authoring flow, and loader fallback to Room.default_question when a quiz doc is missing.
whatBreaks: Wrong parsing or a flipped visibility flag could either crash quiz loads or leak answer keys through the public content API.

role: Unit test for the binary cursor-frame codec (quantize/encode/delta)
description: Tests Barkpark.Quiz.CursorFrame's quantize/dequantize clamping and round-trip precision, binary encode/decode round-trip, fixed frame-size formula (2+6n bytes), and delta computation that keeps only changed/new cursor entries.
whatBreaks: A codec bug would corrupt or misplace live cursor positions broadcast to all quiz participants, or bloat/break the wire frame size.

role: Load/perf test proving O(1) heatmap frame size at 10k cursors
description: Encodes 10,000 synthetic cursors through Barkpark.Quiz.Heatmap and asserts the output stays a fixed 2048-byte frame, encodes in under 1s, and preserves the total cursor count; also checks frame size is identical at 100 vs 10k cursors.
whatBreaks: If the heatmap encoder stopped being O(1)/fixed-size, large quiz rooms could blow up broadcast payload size or CPU cost with no guard rail.

role: Unit test for the fixed-size occupancy-grid heatmap encoder
description: Tests Barkpark.Quiz.Heatmap: fixed frame size regardless of cursor count, count-sum correctness after decode, all-zero empty case, correct corner-cell placement, and co-located cursors stacking into one cell.
whatBreaks: A broken grid mapping would render an inaccurate or corrupted crowd heatmap to viewers in large quiz rooms.

role: Test for cursor-frame vs aggregate-heatmap crossover threshold logic
description: Verifies the room's cursor tick emits individual per-player cursor frames at/below a configurable heatmap threshold, and switches to emitting a single fixed-size aggregate heatmap frame (and stops individual frames) once player count exceeds it.
whatBreaks: Wrong crossover behavior would send excessive per-cursor traffic in large rooms (defeating the O(1) heatmap optimization) or silently drop cursor visuals in small rooms.

role: Test for quiz room's ~15Hz batched cursor delta broadcast
description: Covers Barkpark.Quiz.Room cursor handling: per-player slot assignment, move+tick producing a delta cursor frame decodable back to the correct quantized position, no re-broadcast when cursor is still, and no-ops for non-joined players or missing rooms (and that a missing room is never auto-started by move).
whatBreaks: Broken slot assignment or tick batching would misroute or spam cursor updates, or accidentally spin up ghost rooms on stray move calls.

role: Test for the quiz room game-phase state machine
description: Covers Barkpark.Quiz.Room phase transitions (question→reveal→leaderboard→ended, plus to_lobby), each broadcasting a {:phase, _, payload} message, answers being gated to the :question phase, and start_question resetting the answer tally.
whatBreaks: A broken FSM could let players submit answers in the wrong phase or desync the game state seen by all clients in a live quiz.

role: Test for per-choice hover-intent counts in quiz rooms
description: Covers Barkpark.Quiz.Room hover handling: per-choice hover counts updating and broadcasting, moving hover between choices, clearing on nil/leave, ignoring invalid choices or non-joined players, and suppressing redundant broadcasts to avoid O(N) amplification.
whatBreaks: A regression could cause incorrect 'N hovering' counts shown live, or reintroduce an O(N) broadcast storm under many players.

role: Load/scale test for the Quiz Room GenServer's cursor broadcast path
description: Simulates ~200 players joining one quiz room and streaming cursor moves, asserting broadcast frames are correctly sized (2 + 6·N bytes) and the union of delta frames covers all players; also checks hover aggregation at scale. Targets the individual-cursor path (heatmap/10k+ path is a separate P5 concern).
whatBreaks: A regression here would let the Quiz room's cursor-frame encoding silently corrupt or drop players under realistic load without any test catching it.

role: Unit tests for Quiz Room scoring/streak/leaderboard logic
description: Verifies correct-vs-wrong answer scoring, streak increment/reset behavior, leaderboard sort order, and that reveal broadcasts scores over PubSub.
whatBreaks: Scoring/streak/leaderboard bugs in the Quiz plugin could ship undetected, producing wrong player rankings or scores live.

role: Security-hardening tests for Quiz Room answer-leak and crash resistance
description: Asserts the correct answer never reaches players before :reveal (snapshot and question-phase broadcast both omit it), that it IS disclosed at reveal, and that a malformed live-edited question is rejected without crashing the room process.
whatBreaks: Losing this coverage risks players seeing quiz answers early (cheating) or a malformed question payload crashing the live room GenServer for all connected players.

role: Core walking-skeleton test suite for the Quiz Room GenServer
description: Covers lazy room lifecycle, join/leave, answer tallying (last-write-wins), validation of invalid choices/non-joined players, PubSub fan-out (join/tally/leave events), idempotent re-join, cursor slot recycling, and that read-only calls never resurrect a stopped room.
whatBreaks: Core Quiz room state-machine invariants (join, tally, leave, room lifecycle) could regress with no coverage, breaking the live quiz feature end-to-end.

role: Tests for Quiz Room's server-authoritative countdown/reveal timer
description: Verifies auto-reveal on countdown expiry, that a manual reveal cancels an armed timer (generation-tokened, preventing double reveal), and correctness of the exposed seconds_remaining field.
whatBreaks: A broken timer could cause double-reveal race conditions or a quiz round that never auto-advances for all players in a room.

role: Tests for server-side fairness of Quiz Room speed-based scoring
description: Confirms an earlier answer scores at least as high as a later one using server-recorded timestamps (not client-trusted), and that scoring uses the armed round duration rather than the question's nominal time_limit.
whatBreaks: Losing this guard could let scoring become client-timing-exploitable or use the wrong denominator, unfairly rewarding/punishing players.

role: Tests for Quiz live observability/telemetry (Barkpark.Quiz.Stats)
description: Checks live_room_count and room_stats reflect actual joined rooms/players/phase, and that room activity emits a [:barkpark, :quiz, :tick] telemetry event.
whatBreaks: Quiz observability metrics/telemetry could silently drift from reality, breaking dashboards or alerting built on these counters.

role: Unit tests for the ETS token-bucket rate limiter
description: Verifies Barkpark.RateLimiter burst capacity, per-key independence (token/IP/method-class/dataset scoping), time-based refill, and the stale-bucket pruning/bound-enforcement path on the shared ETS table.
whatBreaks: An undetected bug could let rate limiting silently fail open (DoS exposure) or fail closed (locking out legitimate API traffic), or let the ETS table grow unbounded.

role: Tests for the shared Barkpark.Redaction engine and per-plugin error redactors
description: Guards the extracted Redaction engine plus the Github/Indx/Bokbasen plugin Errors modules that delegate to it; the load-bearing invariant is that each plugin's allowlist stays DISTINCT (never unioned), so a key from one plugin's secrets never gets redacted—or left exposed—by a sibling plugin's redactor.
whatBreaks: If allowlists were ever unioned or broken, secrets (tokens, passwords, client_secret) could leak in logs/error payloads across multiple plugins simultaneously — a security regression this test is specifically designed to catch.

role: test for release secrets generator
description: Verifies Barkpark.Release.Secrets.generate/0 produces exactly the three required crypto keys (SECRET_KEY_BASE, BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY, PREVIEW_JWT_SECRET) with correct entropy.
whatBreaks: A broken secrets generator would produce weak or missing keys, silently compromising production security.

role: migration correctness test for content cascade on scope delete
description: Guards migration 20260527160000 which changed documents/revisions/media_files/schema_definitions FK actions from nilify_all to cascade, preventing orphan content rows after workspace deletion.
whatBreaks: Cascade failure leaves orphaned content rows with NULL scope columns that resurface under the Default dataset.

role: migration regression test for jsonb[] codelist fields
description: Reproduces a production failure mode where multi-element jsonb[] arrays with nested composites were mishandled by the add_codelist_issue_version migration; tagged :flaky and excluded from default test run.
whatBreaks: Silent regression in codelist migration corrupts schema_definitions.fields for multi-element jsonb arrays.

role: migration correctness test for peripheral table cascade
description: Guards migration 20260527170000 which extended CASCADE to seven peripheral tables (webhooks, mutation_events, search_intel_*, search_synonyms, paper_events), closing the same orphan-resurfaces-under-Default leak for those tables.
whatBreaks: Orphan rows in webhook/search/paper_events tables resurface under Default dataset after workspace deletion.

role: migration test for bp_export_status promotion
description: Verifies the bp_export_status promotion migration is idempotent, reversible, and correctly default-fills missing composite fields on existing document rows.
whatBreaks: Broken migration leaves documents with invalid or missing bp_export_status composite fields, causing export failures.

role: migration correctness test for paper_events dataset rescoping
description: Guards corrective migration 20260527143000 which fixes a Wave-2 backfill that stamped all paper_events with the Default project's dataset_id, creating structurally-impossible scope tuples for non-Default papers.
whatBreaks: Mismatched dataset_id/project_id on paper_event rows causes scope-filtered queries to miss or misroute events.

role: migration regression test
description: Regression test for the NULL-dataset_id dedup restore migration (20260527150000). Seeds datasets rows and stamps dataset_id on legacy NULL search rows to restore uniqueness constraints after a schema flip.
whatBreaks: The dedup migration's correctness goes unverified, potentially allowing duplicate search rows when the migration is re-run or rolled back.

role: Unit test for Barkpark.Repo.uuid_or_nil/1 UUID-cast guard
description: Pure, DB-free test confirming uuid_or_nil casts valid UUIDs (including case-normalization) and returns nil for garbage/non-binary input, guarding against CastError crashes on Repo.get with :binary_id.
whatBreaks: Without this guard behaving correctly, malformed IDs passed to Repo lookups across the whole app could raise uncaught Ecto.CastError 500s instead of returning nil/404.

role: migration gate test for schema dedup
description: Wave-2 gate test asserting the duplicate-collapse migration (20260527133000) leaves no (name, dataset_id) duplicates in schema_definitions, while preserving same-name schemas across distinct datasets.
whatBreaks: Schema uniqueness migration goes unvalidated, risking silent collisions when the uniqueness index flip runs on prod.

role: Test that SCIM token minting emits an audit trail event
description: Asserts Scim.mint_token/2 writes a token/scim_token_minted Audit.Event with correct category/subject/metadata and that the audit hash-chain still verifies, ensuring the audit trail fires regardless of caller (portal vs API).
whatBreaks: A regression here means SCIM token minting could go unaudited, breaking compliance/traceability for provisioning admin-level tokens.

role: Tests for search-event aggregation into periodic 'crystal' rollups
description: Verifies Barkpark.Search.Crystallizer.crystallize_period/4 correctly aggregates raw Event rows into Crystal rows (per query/filter fingerprint) and MergePattern rows, including quality/rejected-event bucketing.
whatBreaks: Broken aggregation would corrupt search analytics/suggestions data that downstream Intelligence.suggestions relies on after raw events are pruned.

role: Test: DocumentsRetriever bounded-ranking-pool behavior
description: Verifies the search ranking pool bound (ranking_pool_size) limits expensive ts_rank/similarity scoring to the N newest candidate rows while count/total still reflects the full match set; also checks browse mode is unbounded and EXPLAIN uses the GIN index.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let search cost/perf regressions (unbounded ranking scans) or incorrect result counts ship undetected.

role: Test: DocumentsRetriever perspective (draft/published) filter
description: Pure DB-free test asserting perspective_filter/2 fails closed to :published for unknown/string/nil perspective values, guarding against accidental draft-content exposure.
whatBreaks: A broken fail-closed guard could leak unpublished drafts through search results to unauthorized callers.

role: test for multi-tenant search scope isolation
description: Proves that DocumentsRetriever resolves dataset string to dataset_id before filtering, preventing cross-project result leakage when two projects share the same dataset name string.
whatBreaks: Multi-tenant search isolation bug goes undetected, allowing one project's search to surface another project's documents.

role: Test: DocumentsRetriever.search/4 core behaviors
description: Covers browse mode (empty query returns all published docs), type filtering, perspective, types allowlist, and a regression guard that negative limit/offset are floored instead of producing a Postgres error/500.
whatBreaks: Search API could 500 on malformed pagination params or return wrong document sets for browse/type-filtered queries.

role: search quality golden evaluation test
description: Runs golden-set search eval scenarios against the GoldenEval module, seeding default surface configs and schemas to verify search ranking quality does not regress.
whatBreaks: Search relevance regressions against known-good queries go undetected.

role: Test: Search result highlighter field-visibility redaction
description: Verifies Highlighter.highlight_documents/4 drops content.* highlight fields for non-admin callers (per schema field visibility) while preserving them for admins and for the caller's own public fields, closing a prior over/under-redaction bug (WS-B LOW-11).
whatBreaks: Search highlights could leak private/schema-restricted field content to unauthorized callers via the highlight snippet.

role: P0 tenant-isolation regression guard for the Indx search engine seam
description: Proves that Indx.Retriever.load_document/3 always re-scopes hits through Postgres by workspace/project even when the injected Indx client returns cross-tenant documentKeys, and that an unscoped indx request falls back to the scoped Postgres DocumentsRetriever inside QueryPipeline. Uses a fake client injected via opts since no live Indx engine runs in test.
whatBreaks: If this guard regresses (or the underlying scope-forwarding it protects breaks), one workspace's private documents could leak into another workspace's search results via the Indx relevance index — a cross-tenant data leak.

role: test for Indx title-affinity reranking
description: Unit tests the pure rerank_by_title/2 function that gives title matches priority over BM25F order from the Indx engine, running async with no DB or live engine.
whatBreaks: Title-affinity reranking regressions silently degrade Indx search result ordering.

role: Test: Intelligence.escape_like_prefix/1 ILIKE escaping
description: Small pure test confirming ILIKE metacharacters (%, _, backslash) are escaped correctly with backslash escaped first.
whatBreaks: A wrong escape order could allow prefix-search wildcard injection or broken exact-match search behavior.

role: Tests for search event retention pruning and suggestions
description: Covers Barkpark.Search.Intelligence.prune/1 (retention-window deletion of raw Event rows) and that popular-query suggestions still work by reading day crystals after raw events are pruned.
whatBreaks: A pruning bug could delete live search events prematurely or leave suggestions broken once raw events age out, degrading the search UX silently.

role: Tests linking click/select interactions to prior search events
description: Verifies Barkpark.Search.Intelligence.record_interaction/4 correctly links a click event to its originating search Event and that crystallization rolls click_count/CTR into query crystals.
whatBreaks: Broken interaction linking would corrupt CTR-based ranking/analytics used to improve search relevance over time.

role: Test: cross-module ILIKE pattern-escaping consistency
description: Pure string tests checking DocumentsRetriever.like_pattern/1, Media.Delivery.Retriever.like_pattern/1, and Media.Delivery.Search.escape_like/1 all escape backslash-then-wildcards identically, keeping the three independent LIKE-escaping implementations in lockstep.
whatBreaks: Divergent escaping across the three search/media modules could allow wildcard/LIKE injection or search-term mismatches in one surface but not another.

role: Test: media search tenant-scoping and empty-query regression guards
description: Regression tests for two prior bugs: a 500 crash on relevance sort with a zero-term (prefix-only) query, and a tag-facet SQL query that leaked counts across workspaces sharing a dataset string by not scoping to workspace_id.
whatBreaks: Media search could 500 on prefix-only relevance queries or leak tag facet counts across tenant/workspace boundaries.

role: Test: MergePattern Ecto schema struct/persistence
description: Checks default field values, schema field presence, and round-trip insert/read of the MergePattern schema used for search facet-transition/merge analytics.
whatBreaks: Schema drift in MergePattern could silently corrupt or drop search-pattern analytics records.

role: Unit tests for the search query string tokenizer
description: Small, focused tests for Barkpark.Search.QueryParser.parse/1 — terms, quoted phrases, exclude tokens (-word), prefix wildcards (word*), edge cases like bare hyphens/stars, and malformed (non-binary) input.
whatBreaks: A parser regression would misinterpret search queries (wrong terms/excludes/prefixes) across every surface that uses the search engine.

role: test for search query pipeline
description: Integration tests for the search QueryPipeline module, seeding schemas/documents and asserting ranked search results across types.
whatBreaks: Search pipeline regressions go undetected.

role: Test: Retrievers engine-to-module registry resolver
description: Pure unit tests for Retrievers.resolve/1 and registry/0, confirming the postgres engine maps to DocumentsRetriever and unknown/nil engines fall back to it rather than failing.
whatBreaks: An unhandled search engine value could route to a missing retriever module and crash search instead of falling back safely.

role: Unit tests for search query sanitization/spam-rejection
description: Verifies Barkpark.Search.Sanitizer normalizes valid queries and rejects empty/short/profane/spammy/invalid-UTF-8/excluded-pattern input, while allowing legitimate English phrases containing SQL keywords and non-Latin scripts.
whatBreaks: A sanitizer bug could let profanity/spam pollute search analytics, or wrongly reject legitimate queries (including non-Latin-script ones), degrading search quality.

role: Test: SurfaceConfig schema defaults and changeset validation
description: Verifies SurfaceConfig struct defaults, Ecto schema field types/table name, and that changeset/2 (using cast, not raw change) rejects type-mismatched typo_policy values with a validation error instead of raising Ecto.ChangeError at dump time (regression guard for a 500 on PUT search settings).
whatBreaks: Malformed search-surface-config updates could 500 instead of returning a clean 422, or silently store wrongly-typed config.

role: test for search surface isolation
description: Tests that media and documents search crystals are kept isolated per surface/scope during crystallization.
whatBreaks: Cross-surface search result contamination goes undetected.

role: Unit test for Search.Synonyms non-UUID id guard
description: Exercises Barkpark.Search.Synonyms.delete/3 with malformed/non-UUID ids, asserting a fast {:error, :not_found} short-circuit without hitting the DB. No DataCase needed.
whatBreaks: A regression here means malformed synonym-delete ids could crash with a cast error or reach Repo unnecessarily, instead of failing gracefully.

role: test for search synonyms expansion
description: Tests synonym creation and expansion (one-way and alt_correction) in the Synonyms module used by the search pipeline.
whatBreaks: Synonym expansion regressions silently degrade search relevance.

role: Test suite for Barkpark.Secrets encrypted-at-rest store
description: Covers put/get/reveal round-trip, rotation, encryption-at-rest (raw column never contains plaintext), audit logging (set/reveal/delete rows, get writes none), masked list/0, delete, and ingest_token DB-override-of-config fallback.
whatBreaks: If these tests are wrong/missing, a regression could leak plaintext secrets at rest, silently break audit trails, or expose the wrong ingest token, without any test catching it.

role: test for clean seed profile
description: Tests the clean seed profile (bp setup fresh install): verifies no demo rows, admin token creation with correct permissions, welcome paper idempotence.
whatBreaks: Fresh installs via bp setup may produce broken or missing seed state without detection.

role: GenServer test for SelfUpdate.Checker status/version logic
description: Tests the self-update Checker's state machine (disabled/current/behind/unknown), digest and release-notes tolerance of upstream errors, and fork-vs-canonical divergence advice, all via a Fake client seam.
whatBreaks: A broken Checker could report the wrong update status to admins (e.g. hide an available update or crash the status endpoint) with no test to catch it.

role: Pure unit test for GitHub tag-parsing/version-max logic
description: Tests GitHub.max_release_tag/1's numeric (not lexicographic) version comparison and filtering of non-release tags (cli-v*, rc, junk); no network involved.
whatBreaks: Wrong tag parsing could make self-update pick a lower/wrong release as 'latest', misleading version-behind detection.

role: Test for Sharing.Links TTL clamping (security guard)
description: Verifies Links.create/1 clamps an attacker-supplied bignum ttl at one year (mirroring Auth's max TTL) to prevent runaway date math or never-expiring share links; also covers normal ttl and nil ttl (no expiry).
whatBreaks: Without this clamp guard, a malicious huge ttl could hang the server on bignum date math or mint an effectively permanent share link, a real security/DoS exposure.

role: Changeset test for Sharing.StoredShare struct
description: Pure changeset validation tests for StoredShare (required fields, non-empty surfaces list); documents that surface/access token semantic validity is deferred to read-time revalidation, not enforced here.
whatBreaks: A broken changeset could let malformed stored-share rows (missing slugs, empty surfaces) persist, causing failures later at read time.

role: test for persistent share registry
description: Tests the persistent share store (shares table): add/remove/list/refresh operations and the env+DB merge feeding the live :shares config.
whatBreaks: Sharing persistence bugs (stale or lost share config) go undetected.

role: test for scoped-sharing registry
description: Tests Barkpark.Sharing parse/1, shared?/access_for/active? checks, and env mutation with async:false to avoid races on the global :shares application env.
whatBreaks: Sharing access control regressions (wrong grants or denials) go undetected.

role: Performance regression guard for Sheets Engine recompute
description: Builds a near-cap (~47k cell) sheet with chains, per-row SUMs, and cross-tab refs, then asserts Engine.recompute/1 stays within a 10s wall-clock bound and scales roughly linearly (not quadratically) with row count — a value-correctness-blind O(n^2) regression tripwire.
whatBreaks: A silent regression from O(cells+edges) to O(n^2) recompute would make large sheets time out or hang in production while all functional tests stay green.

role: Large unit-test suite for the Sheets formula engine (recompute)
description: 5000+ line pure-function test suite for Barkpark.Plugins.Sheets.Engine.recompute/1 — covers totality guarantees, formula evaluation, dependency handling (including eager-IF cycles → #CYCLE!), and written-back cell descriptor shape. No DB involved; doctest-backed.
whatBreaks: A regression in the formula engine would silently miscompute spreadsheet cell values or fail to detect circular dependencies across every Sheets document, corrupting user data displayed in Studio/reader surfaces.

role: Hardening tests for the per-sheet Sheets.Session GenServer
description: Covers three deferred-but-verified failure modes: flush/2 surfacing a failed persist as {:error, reason} rather than silently serving stale data, call_session/4 retrying a dead session exactly once before returning :session_unavailable, and apply_ops/3 rejecting oversized batches before reaching a session. Uses an injected before_save hook to force a genuine persist failure.
whatBreaks: Without these guards, a sheet write failure could be masked as success (stale reads served as fresh) or a crashed session could hang/crash callers instead of degrading gracefully.

role: Exactly-once retry semantics test for Sheets Session ops
description: Verifies the request_id replay ring (ETS-backed, restart-surviving) prevents double-application of non-idempotent batch ops (e.g. insert_rows) under 503-retry scenarios, including session-crash survival, while confirming no-request_id and different-request_id batches still both apply.
whatBreaks: Without correct idempotency, a client retry after a transient 503 could double-apply structural edits (e.g. inserting rows twice), silently corrupting a user's sheet.

role: Test for Sheets set_cell_meta op (format/style, non-mutating)
description: Locks the display-only set_cell_meta op: stamps fmt/s without touching v/f, validates fmt vocabulary and strict style grammar, refuses empty/merged cells, and confirms undo/redo round-trips restore prior cell state exactly.
whatBreaks: A regression could let formatting silently mutate stored values (e.g. re-parsing a string as a number) or corrupt undo history in the Studio sheet editor.

role: Test for sort_range PubSub broadcast metadata (rect+perm)
description: Verifies forward/undo/redo sort_range ops each broadcast the correct rect and permutation (forward perm, then its inverse on undo, then original again on redo) so remote collaborators can remap selections/open editors correctly after a sort.
whatBreaks: Wrong rect/perm in the broadcast would cause remote collaborators' cursors or open cell editors to point at stale/wrong coordinates after any sort action.

role: Test suite for the Sheets collaborative Session GenServer
description: M1 locks for Barkpark.Plugins.Sheets.Session: lazy lifecycle, mailbox-serialized LWW ops, per-op recompute deltas, debounced/idle persistence, and external-write conflict warnings. async: false because sessions are globally registered processes sharing the SQL sandbox.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in Sheets realtime collab (lost writes, stale persistence, missed deltas) would ship silently.

role: Test suite for per-user undo/redo in the Sheets Session GenServer
description: M4 locks covering own-op-only undo, inverse correctness per op type (cell, insert/delete, col/row resize, tab rename/add/delete), redo-cleared-on-new-op semantics, 100-depth stacks, and cross-user overwrite races. async: false, same session-registry constraints as session_test.exs.
whatBreaks: Broken undo/redo semantics (wrong inverses, cross-user leakage) in the Sheets editor would go undetected.

role: Regression test: spilled array cells project across all Sheets export surfaces
description: Seeds a materialized SPILL cell shape into a doc and asserts snapshot/CSV/Markdown/HTML/paper-embed/TUI projection and conditional-formatting all render the engine-written spilled values byte-identically to plain cells. Does not exercise the spill-writing engine itself (that's a separate, not-yet-landed slice).
whatBreaks: A regression here means spilled formula results silently vanish or corrupt on one of five Sheets export surfaces without any test catching it.

role: Pure-function test suite for Sheets formula ref-shift/structure edits
description: Locks Barkpark.Plugins.Sheets.Structure's Excel-style rewrite_formula/3 (row/col insert/delete ref shifting, ranges, quoted-string literal protection, $A$1 absolute refs) plus tab-level rewrites of cell keys, merges, row_heights/col_widths, frozen bands, and grid-bounds insert cap. async: true, no DB.
whatBreaks: Formula corruption on row/column insert or delete (wrong cell refs, broken ranges) would silently ship in the Sheets engine.

role: HTTP-driven end-to-end proof of the Sheets M0 embed contract
description: Independent proof (no direct Content calls) that sheets embedded in Papers hydrate snapshots on ingest, stay frozen on the published paper across draft edits, and refresh via write-through only on publish; also checks malformed-sheet write rejection. Deliberately overlaps zero fixtures with builder tests.
whatBreaks: A break in the sheet-embed write-through or draft/publish isolation contract for Papers would go undetected at the wire level.

role: HTTP-driven end-to-end proof of Sheets M1 realtime/collab contract
description: Two simulated colleagues edit a shared sheet concurrently while a PubSub watcher observes the op-delta stream (not the SSE listen endpoint); asserts monotonic revs, LWW on shared cells, formula recompute in deltas, eventual persisted-state equality, and sub-500ms op latency.
whatBreaks: Realtime collaboration guarantees (delta ordering, LWW conflict resolution, persistence convergence) for Sheets could regress unnoticed.

role: HTTP-driven end-to-end proof of Sheets formula engine + xlsx import/export
description: Imports a deliberately-wrong-cached-value .xlsx workbook via elixlsx, asserts the engine recomputes on import, verifies paper-embed write-through, and round-trips export.xlsx/csv/md including hostile inputs (cell cap, garbage bytes, oversized merges, out-of-range refs).
whatBreaks: xlsx import/export or formula recompute-on-import could silently corrupt data or accept malformed workbooks.

role: HTTP-driven end-to-end proof of Sheets M3 formula engine contract
description: Proves formulas (SUM, division, date math, div/0) compute inline on mutate, render correctly through paper embeds, and stay frozen on the published paper until re-publish after a draft cell edit.
whatBreaks: Formula computation-on-write or draft/publish freeze semantics for sheet formulas could regress unnoticed.

role: Pure-function test suite for Sheets merged-cell/style rendering fidelity
description: Verifies snapshot_for/2 encodes merges as 0-based [row,col,rowspan,colspan] and that Render.render_block honors merges (colspan/rowspan, no <td> for covered cells) and cell styles in HTML, while the dense value grid used by the TUI stays unchanged. Pure, no DB.
whatBreaks: Merged cells or styled cells could render incorrectly (wrong colspan, missing style) in Paper embeds without detection.

role: Cross-surface parity test for Sheets rendering (editor/reader/paper/export)
description: Renders one canonical sheet through Studio grid editor, Studio read-only view, public /sheets/:slug reader, paper embed, and html/markdown export, then diffs extracted semantic content (values, spans, widths, styles) to assert they agree, with documented deliberate losses (row heights, frozen panes, markdown values-only). async: false due to global session registry.
whatBreaks: Sheets could silently drift out of visual/semantic sync across editor, reader, paper embed, and export surfaces.

role: Unit test suite for Sheets Core A1-ref helpers and snapshot synthesis
description: Pure-function tests (plus doctest) for Barkpark.Plugins.Sheets.Core's parse_ref/1 (A1-notation parsing incl. bijective base-26 multi-letter columns and malformed-input rejection) and snapshot synthesis. No DB.
whatBreaks: A1-reference parsing bugs would corrupt cell addressing throughout the Sheets plugin.

role: Test: SSO domain DNS-TXT verification, email routing, JIT membership provisioning
description: Covers Barkpark.Sso.Domains — DNS TXT token verification via a mocked resolver, that only verified domains route emails to their org, and that jit_provision idempotently grants workspace memberships on first SSO login.
whatBreaks: An unverified domain could hijack SSO login routing, or JIT provisioning could duplicate/omit workspace memberships, without detection.

role: Test: OIDC relying-party flow, token verification, group-to-role mapping
description: Exercises Barkpark.Sso.Oidc against a mocked IdP (signed id_token via JOSE, mocked token/JWKS endpoints) — happy path user find-or-create, rejection of issuer/audience/expiry/nonce/signature mismatches, PKCE authorize_url shape, and IdP group-claim to workspace-role mapping including downgrade/unmapped-group/unknown-role cases.
whatBreaks: A broken signature/issuer/audience check could let a forged id_token authenticate as any user, or group mapping could silently over-grant admin roles.

role: Test: SAML SP assertion consumption and Single Logout signature validation
description: Plays a self-signed test IdP (X509 + xmerl_dsig) to verify Barkpark.Sso.Saml accepts validly signed (including unsolicited/IdP-initiated) assertions and LogoutRequests, and rejects assertions signed by an untrusted key, wrong audience, or unsigned/foreign-signed logout requests.
whatBreaks: A signature-validation regression could let a forged SAML assertion or unauthenticated LogoutRequest authenticate/kill sessions for arbitrary users.

role: Test: social OAuth login (Google/GitHub/Microsoft) find-or-create + linking
description: Mocks provider HTTP (token exchange + userinfo) to verify Barkpark.Sso.Social finds-or-creates users, links social identities to existing email accounts without duplication, and is idempotent on repeat login by the same external id.
whatBreaks: A regression could duplicate user accounts per login or fail to link an existing email account, fragmenting identity across the same person.

role: Test: every SSO/social login emits an sso_login audit event
description: Verifies Sso.record_login writes distinct audited events (with provider metadata) for OIDC, social, and SAML logins, and that the audit hash chain stays valid afterward.
whatBreaks: A gap here means SSO logins could go unaudited or corrupt the tamper-evident audit hash chain undetected.

role: Test: Status.get_incident safely handles non-UUID input
description: Small regression guard pinning that get_incident/1 (after de-duplication onto Repo.uuid_or_nil/1) resolves real incidents and returns nil (not an Ecto.CastError 500) for malformed or absent UUIDs.
whatBreaks: A malformed status-page incident id could 500 the status endpoint instead of returning a clean not-found.

role: Test: Studio desk render safety net for a clean bp-setup install
description: Verifies a fresh install (only paper + mediaAsset/mediaCollection schemas, no post/page/project) still builds a valid Studio desk tree via Structure/PaneBuilder — Papers list present, Media out of the tree (top_menu placement), no Settings node, zero-schema-safe.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a fresh clean-profile install crash or mis-render the Studio desk without any test catching it.

role: Test: Media plugin's placement in the tiered Studio desk tree
description: Asserts the media plugin's structure_placement :top_menu keeps the Media group out of the main desk tree by default (reachable via top-menu instead), its doc types aren't leaked into the …Rest bucket, and a per-workspace override can promote it back into 'main'.
whatBreaks: Media types could leak into …Rest or fail to appear/disappear correctly per workspace override, breaking the tiered-desk contract from studio-structure-polish.

role: Test: Structure.build gates plugin-returned %Node{} structs by workspace scope
description: Regression test pinning that a plugin's resolve_desk_items/2 override returning a full %Structure.Node{} (not a map) still goes through workspace-scoped gating instead of leaking into every workspace's desk, and that the built desk tree is deterministic across rebuilds (stable divider ids for LiveView keyed diffs).
whatBreaks: A plugin desk node could leak into workspaces that never registered its schema, exposing content types across tenant boundaries in the Studio desk.

role: test for tasks plugin desk entry
description: Pins that the Tasks plugin contributes a Tasks desk entry through the plugin highway, gated on the task schema existing in the dataset, with no host special-casing.
whatBreaks: Tasks desk entry regression goes undetected — Studio shows Tasks section without schema or hides it incorrectly.

role: Test: core Barkpark.Structure desk-tree builder (main/plugins/…Rest tiers)
description: Large (631-line) suite covering Structure.build/1 across legacy schemas, type census counts (draft+published), plugin grouping, and the …Rest catch-all bucket — the backbone test for how the Studio (and TUI) navigation tree is derived from registered schemas.
whatBreaks: The Studio/TUI desk navigation could mis-group or hide document types across the whole app, since Structure.build is the shared tree-construction entry point.

role: Test: Structure.build scopes the Studio desk tree to the requesting workspace
description: Verifies host schema groups and plugin desk nodes (including requires_schema-tagged nodes like OnixEdit's Bokbasen) are filtered to the workspace's own registered schemas, and that an unscoped build preserves legacy unfiltered behavior — regression guard for a prior workspace-desk-leak bug.
whatBreaks: Without this scoping, one workspace's Studio desk could show another workspace's content types and plugin nodes — a tenancy leak in the UI.

role: Test: approved Studio-chat plans publish as real Bulldocs Papers
description: Verifies PlanPapers.publish/3 writes a published article-style paper at a deterministic slug (pure function of session_id+request_id), that re-approving the same plan upserts one row (idempotent update, never a duplicate), and that plan markdown lands as rendered blocks in the paper body.
whatBreaks: A broken slug/idempotency guarantee could duplicate papers on every plan re-approval or silently fail to update the published plan content.

role: Test suite for the Studio Chat server-owned Recorder GenServer
description: Proves the Recorder is the chat Session's permanent sink — writes land even with no LiveView viewer attached, and every frame rebroadcasts to PubSub subscribers. Large (1237-line) suite covering ensure/idempotency, assistant/tool frame persistence, and the 'close the tab, turn still lands' guarantee.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let Studio chat messages silently vanish when the browser tab is closed mid-turn.

role: Unit tests for AI-generated chat session titles (Barkpark.StudioChat.Titles)
description: Uses fake HTTP/CLI adapters and a fake store to test the haiku-model title request shape, timeout/kill path, and the human-rename clobber guard (AI never overwrites a human-set title).
whatBreaks: Broken title logic could overwrite a user's manually renamed chat session with an AI-generated one, or hang on a slow CLI call.

role: Test suite for the Studio Chat session-store spine (StudioChat context)
description: Large (1591-line) DataCase suite proving UUID-as-PK semantics, per-session monotonic seq, denormalized sidebar field updates on append, the rename/AI-title race guard, and cost/metric accumulation across turns for the Studio Claude chat feature.
whatBreaks: Corruption here risks duplicate/out-of-order chat message ordering or silent loss of session sidebar state across the Studio chat UI.

role: End-to-end test of the Sync pull pipeline (parse + apply + echo-dedup + cursor)
description: Manufactures a real mutation event locally then runs it through SSE.parse_frames and Applier.apply into a separate workspace, proving cross-instance content sync applies correctly and that re-applying the same event is a no-op (echo-dedup) via the cursor.
whatBreaks: A broken Applier could duplicate documents or infinite-loop re-syncing the same mutation between two Barkpark instances.

role: Unit tests for the Sync push outbox reader (Barkpark.Sync.Outbox)
description: Verifies source:"sync" rows are excluded from the outbox (echo-suppression on the push side) and that fetch respects id-ascending order, after_id cursoring, and limit for causal replay.
whatBreaks: A bug would cause pulled mutations to be pushed back to their origin, creating sync echo loops.

role: Unit tests for the Sync push high-water-mark cursor (PushCursor)
description: Focuses on bootstrap_if_absent: seeding the cursor to current dataset head on first enable (skipping pre-enable history), idempotency/never-rewinding, and per-dataset scoping.
whatBreaks: A cursor bug could replay a dataset's entire pre-existing history to a remote on first push-enable, or leak cursor state across datasets.

role: Deterministic tests for the Sync push drain-tick GenServer (PushWorker)
description: Asserts the default-off gate (push must be explicitly enabled even with full pull creds) and drives one injected :drain_tick to prove pending events push in id order and the cursor reaches max id.
whatBreaks: If the default-off gate regresses, a fresh install could start pushing local mutations to a remote without explicit opt-in.

role: Core tests for the Sync push seam (Pusher.drain/3) with injected transport
description: Covers URL scoping (regression-guarded), happy-path cursor/doc-rev advance, CAS conflict preservation without overwriting remote state, transient-halt non-advance, phantom double-push reconciliation, and task reconcile via claim/epoch (not content merge).
whatBreaks: A regression could silently overwrite remote documents on a CAS conflict or corrupt cross-instance task claim state.

role: Pure unit tests for the Sync SSE wire-frame parser (Barkpark.Sync.SSE)
description: No DB/network — tests frame decoding, welcome/keepalive skipping, cross-chunk buffering, multi-line data: joining, and multi-frame batches with a carried trailing partial.
whatBreaks: A parser bug would corrupt or drop live mutation events streamed over SSE between Barkpark instances, breaking sync entirely.

role: Deterministic GenServer tests for the Sync listen Worker
description: Drives the real Worker process via injected stream_fun/backoff_fun seams; tests URL scoping/trailing-slash trim, Accept header correctness (regression: */* not text/event-stream, which 406s), Last-Event-ID resume, and reconnect-with-fresh-ref behavior.
whatBreaks: A regression here (e.g. wrong Accept header or URL) would silently break the SSE listen connection that drives all pull-side sync.

role: DB test for task aggregate-count resolver + TaskResolver dataviz arm
description: Exercises Barkpark.Tasks.Query.agg_for_query/2 and the PortableDoc.TaskResolver aggregate branch, proving cross-workspace count isolation (scope leakage would let workspace A's count include workspace B's rows). Uses TenancyFixtures to build two full workspace/project scopes with registered task schemas.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a scope leak in aggregate task counts ship silently to production charts/stat blocks.

role: Cross-surface glyph-parity gate between GUI task board and Go TUI
description: Pure string/regex test (no DB) that parses the Go TUI's generated tokens_gen.go lifecycle-glyph table and asserts codepoint equality against Barkpark.Tasks.Board.glyphs/0 for shared lifecycle keys, guarding against silent visual drift between surfaces; embeds Board.glyphs() at compile time to avoid an atom-interning race under async tests.
whatBreaks: The GUI and TUI task boards could silently diverge on status icons without any test catching it, breaking the 'same icons as TUI precisely' contract.

role: DB test for Barkpark.Tasks.Claim (claim/claim_by_id) task-queue logic
description: Covers atomic next-ready claim, empty-queue behavior, claim-by-doc_id including drafts.-prefixed fallback, not_ready on already-claimed tasks, and resource-conflict refusal — core of the task claim-queue concurrency contract.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions could let two workers claim the same task or corrupt the claim-queue semantics that bp task next relies on.

role: DB test for Barkpark.Tasks.Close (task completion/fencing logic)
description: Large (688-line) suite covering invalid lifecycle guard, not-found, close of never-claimed task, cancelled as valid terminal state, close_reason persistence, and the stale_claim guard against re-closing a terminal task; includes a foreign_patch_content! helper to simulate concurrent content edits racing a close (CAS/rev fencing).
whatBreaks: A broken Close implementation could let tasks close with a stale claim epoch or lose the fencing guarantee bp task close depends on, corrupting task state.

role: test for task document compactor
description: Comprehensive tests for the Compactor module: selection analysis, happy-path compaction of large event histories, idempotence, restore reversibility, advisory-lock concurrency, cap enforcement, and no-op on empty set.
whatBreaks: Compactor bugs (data loss, non-idempotence, concurrency races) go undetected — task history can be silently destroyed.

role: Pure unit test for acceptance-criteria met/total progress counting
description: DB-free tests of Barkpark.Tasks.Criteria.progress/1 verifying only met===true entries count, %Document{} input works, absent/garbage criteria yields nil (never 0/0), matching the wire contract in portabledoc-inline-liveref-taskchip-wire.
whatBreaks: Task progress chips/counters (e.g. '2/3 criteria met') could render wrong counts or fabricate 0/0 for tasks with no criteria.

role: DB test for the task find-or-create duplicate-detection gate
description: Exercises the real Content.create_document/4 write path end-to-end to prove near-duplicate cross-epic tasks are refused with a similar-tasks payload, guarding the task-obsession dedup layer.
whatBreaks: Duplicate task creation could silently succeed, defeating the dedup gate the task-obsession initiative relies on to keep the ledger clean.

role: Pure changeset test for Barkpark.Tasks.Edge (blocks/discovered-from links)
description: DB-free tests validating Edge.kinds/0 returns exactly the two documented kinds and that Edge.changeset/2 validates required fields and UUID pairs for blocks/discovered-from task-relationship edges.
whatBreaks: Invalid task-edge kinds or malformed edges could pass validation, corrupting the task dependency graph.

role: DB test for the expectation reverse-view (paper→task driven-by linkage)
description: Full-loop test proving a published task citing a paper in design_doc produces a real content_edges row via the projector, driven_tasks/2 lists it unsatisfied, and closing with met=true+evidence flips it to satisfied without republish; also covers publish gating and criteria-less/unresolvable-paper edge cases.
whatBreaks: The Papers-to-tasks 'expectations' reverse view could show tasks as perpetually unsatisfied or leak drafts into the published corpus.

role: DB test for allow-and-fence claim epoch bumping + same-worker renewal
description: Covers the canonical fencing scenario (holder's claim epoch bumped by a concurrent blocker/reparent mutation, stale-epoch close fenced_off, same-worker renewal recovers), edge-add on unclaimed tasks not bumping anything, renewal refreshing ts_iso but not work_digest, and cross-worker claim rejection.
whatBreaks: Broken fencing could let concurrent claim holders silently overwrite each other's task state or block legitimate lease renewal.

role: Pure unit test for Barkpark.Tasks.Internal helper functions
description: DB-free tests of generate_rev/0 (32-char hex uniqueness), current_epoch/1 (extraction + 0 fallback), and task_broadcast/4 map assembly from Document + MutationEvent.
whatBreaks: Broken rev generation or epoch extraction would ripple into claim/close fencing and PubSub broadcast payloads across the task subsystem.

role: Unit tests for the tier-2 LLM duplicate-judge (mocked HTTP)
description: Tests Barkpark.Tasks.Judge — configured?/0 key detection, parsing structured JSON verdicts (duplicate/distinct), and error handling for non-200/transport/unparseable responses via a FakeAdapter (no real network).
whatBreaks: A regression here means the tier-2 LLM-judge duplicate-detection fallback used by task creation could silently misclassify or crash without being caught.

role: DB-backed tests for Barkpark.Tasks.Move (task reparenting)
description: Covers move_by_id/2: parent_id updates + task.reparented events, move-to-root removing the key, cycle guards (self/descendant), no-op idempotence, and not_found handling.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions could let task moves create cycles, silently fail to persist, or stop emitting task.reparented events that other systems (rail digests) depend on.

role: DB-backed tests for Tasks.Query.rows_for_query and Papers task-list resolution
description: Verifies the live-plan fetcher derives correct status rows (ready/backlog/blocked/in_progress/done) from real substrate data including dependency-blocker gating and label filtering, plus that PortableDoc task-list blocks resolve live snapshots via Papers.resolve_tasks_in_blocks/2.
whatBreaks: A broken query/resolver would show wrong task statuses in Papers task-list blocks and epic dashboards, misleading agents about what's actually ready to claim.

role: Focused tests for Barkpark.Tasks.Queue (ready_query/ready)
description: Tests the composable Ecto query builder used by Claim.claim/2: dataset isolation, limit option, fail-closed with no workspace scope, draft/published twin collapse, drafts.-prefix normalization for phase/dependency matching, and dependency-based readiness gating (including dangling deps failing closed).
whatBreaks: A bug in the ready queue could let workers claim wrong-dataset/blocked/duplicate-twin tasks or fail to surface truly ready work, corrupting the whole task-claiming pipeline.

role: Digest tests for Barkpark.Tasks.Rail (rail_rev ETag)
description: Proves the rail_rev digest is sensitive to child create/close/reparent/priority/blocks-edge changes but stable under edits to non-child tasks; also covers unsatisfied_blockers/1.
whatBreaks: A wrong digest could cause stale rail views to look fresh (clients miss updates) or thrash unnecessarily on unrelated changes.

role: Unit tests for Barkpark.Tasks.Release (voluntary task unclaim)
description: Covers the happy path (lifecycle reset, epoch bump, assignee cleared, task.released event), holder-only enforcement, epoch fencing, in-progress-only guard, not_found, and epoch monotonicity across release-then-reclaim.
whatBreaks: Broken release logic could let non-holders steal/release tasks or leave stale claims blocking rework, corrupting the claim/epoch fencing invariant.
