description: Models a Team-owned Site (framework, domains array with GIN index for on-demand TLS lookup, encrypted env, scale mode, GitHub repo/branch/webhook-secret for CI deploys, gh-6 previews_enabled kill switch); domain/slug validation and (team_id, slug) uniqueness gate site creation.
whatBreaks: A bad domain validator could register an unroutable or hostile domain into the TLS allowlist, or break GitHub push-to-deploy webhook matching.

role: AES-256-GCM encrypt-at-rest primitive for all Cloud registry secrets
description: Single-key authenticated encryption (fresh IV per call, fail-closed decrypt) used as the shared seam by Provider.encrypted_token, Site.env_encrypted, and EnvVar.value_encrypted; explicitly no rotation/KMS/versioning yet, just the swap-later seam.
whatBreaks: A crypto bug here (e.g. reused IV, broken tag check) would compromise or corrupt every stored cloud credential and secret across the whole Cloud control plane.

role: Ecto schema for the warm-pool pre-baked host claim store
description: Atomic claim store (via Postgres FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) for pre-booted Hetzner boxes enabling ≤15s go-live; flat ready/claimed/retiring/refreshing lifecycle with reaper-driven stale-claim recovery, replacing a prior fixed-name 'warm-1' collision bug.
whatBreaks: A race in claim semantics could double-assign a warm box to two go-lives simultaneously, corrupting a customer's new instance.

role: Ecto release-migration task run by the Cloud container's boot CMD
description: Standard Mix-release migrate/rollback helper invoked via `bin/barkpark_cloud eval` since Mix isn't present at runtime; the Dockerfile CMD runs migrate/0 before the app starts serving requests.
whatBreaks: If migrate/0 fails silently or targets the wrong repo, the Cloud container boots against a stale schema and every DB-backed request errors.

role: Ecto.Repo for the control-plane Postgres DB
description: Standard Ecto.Repo definition plus `uuid_or_nil/1` and `get_by_uuid/2` helpers that guard :binary_id primary-key lookups against Ecto.Query.CastError on malformed path params, converting them to a clean nil/404 instead of a 500.
whatBreaks: Every DB-backed query in the cloud control plane fails or a malformed id causes 500s instead of clean 404s.

role: Normalizer turning raw agent health payloads into a stable envelope
description: Pure, total `normalize/1` converts the on-box agent's jsonb health report (disk/cpu/mem/load/backup/checks) into a fixed-shape map the dashboard's Timeline/Overview panels consume, defaulting missing fields to nil/zero rather than raising or inventing values.
whatBreaks: Dashboard health/telemetry panels crash or show wrong/fabricated values for every managed instance.

role: Public display-metadata catalog for the template picker
description: In-memory catalog (title, description, what-you-get bullets, env keys, repo/docs links) driving the `/new?template=` launch flow; mirrors (and is lock-tested against) the Go provisioner's authoritative template manifests since the Elixir app can't reach repo-root JSON at compile time.
whatBreaks: Template picker shows wrong/missing descriptions or drifts from the actual deployable templates, though the lock test would catch slug mismatches.

role: Renders vendored Next.js template files for the 'Create GitHub repo' flow
description: Reads vendored app-file trees under cloud/priv/templates/<slug>, reproduces the create-barkpark-app CLI's scaffold transform (rename _gitignore/_npmrc, strip .tmpl, substitute {{ }} placeholders) and returns a file batch pushed to a new GitHub repo; guarded by a drift test against the JS starter source of truth.
whatBreaks: The 'Create GitHub repo' deploy button produces broken or stale repos, or silently pushes wrong content for a template slug.

role: Composes the console's usage/meter envelope (documents, telemetry, seats, fleet)
description: Large (884-line) module with a pure, total `compose/1` shaping every usage meter (documents/datasets/webhooks/db_size/disk/cpu/ram/req_per_s/p95_ms/seats/instances/api_requests/bandwidth) into one honest fixed-shape envelope (never fake zeros), plus IO gather/record/summary functions for the instance-inventory fan-out and cached fleet samples feeding it.
whatBreaks: The console's Usage tab and fleet Overview strip show wrong, fabricated, or missing meter values across all managed instances.

role: Ecto schema for cached per-instance usage snapshots
description: Stores the full Usage.compose/1 envelope as jsonb per instance per ~15min tick, letting GET /v1/usage/summary answer from the latest row with zero live instance HTTP; retained 14 days and cascade-deleted with its instance.
whatBreaks: Fleet usage summary reads fail or serve stale/missing data instead of the cached fast path.

role: Context for the zero-paste 'Deploy to Vercel' claim-code handoff
description: Orchestrates deploying a template to Vercel with env vars pre-installed and minting a 24h claim/transfer code so users receive an already-configured project via a claim link; defaults to the Fake client when no platform token is configured, fails closed (503) rather than half-broken.
whatBreaks: The Vercel deploy-and-claim flow fails to deploy, leaks secrets, or gives users dead/stale claim links.

role: Behaviour seam defining the Vercel API client contract
description: Declares deploy_project/3 and create_transfer_code/1 callbacks implemented by Vercel.Fake (dev/test) and Vercel.Real (prod), decoupling the Vercel context from any concrete HTTP implementation.
whatBreaks: Fake and Real Vercel clients diverge in contract, breaking either tests or the real deploy path depending on which drifts.

role: In-memory deterministic double of the Vercel client for dev/test
description: Implements Vercel.Client with process-dictionary-recorded deploys/codes and deterministic SHA-based ids/urls, plus 'fail-' prefixed and invalid_project_id sentinels for exercising every error branch without network or cost.
whatBreaks: Tests and dev environments can't exercise the Vercel deploy flow, or false-pass tests hide real integration bugs.

role: Real Vercel platform API client (project create, file upload, deploy, transfer)
description: Builds and sends the actual Vercel REST calls (create project with encrypted env vars, content-addressed file upload, production deployment, transfer-request) over an injectable HTTP transport that fails closed with no client configured; pure request builders are directly testable without network access.
whatBreaks: Real production deploys to Vercel fail, silently misconfigure env vars, or never reach api.vercel.com correctly once the platform token is wired.

role: On-demand golden-path health-check suite for a live Barkpark instance
description: Runs a 3-probe suite (API auth, login sentinel, Studio render via manual redirect-following) against a customer instance to prove the golden path works, not just that TCP answers. Shares a probe-vocabulary fixture with the Go provisioner's birth-gate to prevent drift, never raises, and scrubs the admin token from all evidence/output (SSRF-hardened redirect following, restricted to same-origin).
whatBreaks: A broken probe could either mask a dead-on-arrival instance (false positive rollout confidence) or leak the admin bearer token into stored evidence/logs.

role: Bearer-token auth plugs for the control-plane HTTP API
description: Resolves three distinct principals (user session, on-box agent, shared worker secret) from one Authorization header into separate conn assigns, plus role/ability gates (team admin/owner, PAT abilities, per-route team-role checks). Fails closed when the worker token is unconfigured; uses constant-time compare and non-existence-leaking 404s for team membership checks.
whatBreaks: A bug here could let an unauthenticated caller reach any control-plane route, or let one team's user access another team's Barkpark/billing data — a full authz bypass across the whole cloud control plane.

role: Plug.Parsers body reader that preserves raw bytes for webhook HMAC verification
description: Drop-in replacement for Plug.Conn.read_body/2 that stashes each raw chunk into conn.assigns[:raw_body] as it's consumed, since Plug.Parsers normally discards the exact bytes needed to verify GitHub's HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature.
whatBreaks: GitHub webhook signature verification would fail (bytes mismatch) or silently accept forged webhook payloads if raw bytes aren't captured exactly as sent.

role: The entire control-plane HTTP API router (Plug.Router, 8000+ lines)
description: Defines essentially every /v1/* route for the Barkpark Cloud control plane — auth, device-login, barkpark lifecycle, billing, webhooks, GitHub integration, Hetzner/provider catalogs, env vars, notifications, and more — in inline Plug.Router style. This is the single largest, most central wire-seam file in the cloud app; skimmed only (too large to read in full).
whatBreaks: A routing/handler bug here can take down or misroute any control-plane API endpoint used by the CLI, dashboard, and off-box provisioner — effectively the whole cloud product surface.

role: Daily Oban job pruning agent_events/agent_tokens/usage_samples tables
description: Deletes rows past defined retention windows (14d events, 30d-past-terminal tokens, 14d usage samples) to keep three append-only tables bounded; idempotent, max_attempts 1, never touches a still-live token.
whatBreaks: A wrong cutoff could delete a still-live agent token (breaking that box's auth) or let tables grow unbounded, degrading DB performance over time.

role: Serial fleet-wide autoupdate rollout Oban worker
description: Each tick settles in-flight instances against their live self-update status (clearing or pausing on timeout) then advances exactly one new 'behind' instance to trigger, enforcing a strictly serial one-at-a-time canary rollout across the managed fleet.
whatBreaks: A bug could either stall the entire fleet's autoupdates indefinitely or fire updates to many instances in parallel, losing the health-gated canary safety property.

role: Oban worker delivering one chat notification to one channel with retry/backoff
description: Wraps Notifications.deliver_chat/4 with Oban's native retry (4 attempts, fixed 1s/5s/30s backoff), treating 4xx/bad-creds as terminal cancels and 5xx/transport errors as retryable — decrypts channel creds in-process per delivery, never persisting plaintext.
whatBreaks: Chat notifications (Slack/Discord etc.) could silently fail to deliver or retry-storm on permanently bad credentials.

role: Oban worker: daily fleet-update digest email
description: Once a day, reads the whole fleet from Registry.all_barkparks/0 and hands it to Notifications.deliver_fleet_digest/1 to email platform admins the current/behind/paused rollup. Unique per 86400s and max_attempts:1 so it never double-sends or retry-storms; a crash is caught and logged as a no-op.
whatBreaks: Platform admins silently stop receiving the daily fleet health digest, or (if the rescue/unique guards are wrong) the queue could wedge or double-send digests.

role: Per-minute Oban worker that deletes expired device-authorization requests
description: Pure hygiene sweep — expiry is already enforced in-band by query filters, so this only deletes tombstoned rows to keep device_auth_requests from accumulating; correctness never depends on it, dedup-unique per 60s window.
whatBreaks: Worst case is unbounded table growth in device_auth_requests; login/device-auth flow correctness is unaffected.

role: Per-minute Oban worker recovering stuck/crashed deployment claims
description: Sweeps stale 'building'/'pushing'/'queued' deployment rows to re-claimable or terminal states via Registry.reap_stale_deployments/0, since crashed builders/agents otherwise wedge a site's deploy pipeline forever with no other recovery path.
whatBreaks: A crashed builder or on-box agent would leave a customer's deployment stuck in an eternal 'deploying' spinner with no automatic recovery.

role: Per-minute Oban worker recovering wedged instance-provisioning jobs
description: Proactively sweeps stale 'claimed' provisioning jobs to re-claimable or failed state via Registry.reap_stale_provision_jobs/0, using the same staleness threshold and attempt budget as the lazy in-request recovery path so the two never disagree; idempotent, per-row CAS avoids races.
whatBreaks: A crashed provisioning worker would leave a customer's new Barkpark stuck 'provisioning' forever with no automatic recovery.

role: Oban worker: hourly free-trial notice + expiry teardown sweep
description: Scans live `trial` subscriptions, sends T-3/T-1 advance-notice emails exactly once via atomic claim UPDATEs, and enqueues deprovision jobs through the existing Registry teardown path for trials whose window closed without converting. Idempotent and crash-safe; only ever sees plan=="trial" rows so it cannot touch a paid team's box.
whatBreaks: A bug here could either silently never tear down expired trial boxes (cost leak) or, worse, wrongly deprovision a converted paying team's instance.

role: Oban worker: hourly self-update status sweep for fleet dashboard
description: Asks each instance for its own update verdict via Registry.refresh_update_status/1 and mirrors it onto the row the fleet dashboard reads; per-instance rescue prevents one bad box from sinking the sweep.
whatBreaks: Fleet dashboard would show stale or wrong self-update availability, or one crashing instance could abort the whole sweep without the rescue guard.

role: Oban worker: ~15-minute cached usage sample writer for fleet meters
description: Walks checkable instances and writes one Usage.Sample row per instance so GET /v1/usage/summary can answer the Overview meter strip without live per-instance HTTP fan-out; degrades gracefully for down boxes.
whatBreaks: Fleet usage overview would go stale or show fake data, and one instance failure without the rescue guard could break sampling for the whole fleet.

role: Mix task: bootstrap the first control-plane admin user/team
description: One-shot operator command creating a User + Team + owner membership directly via Accounts context in one transaction, with idempotent email-taken handling and slug dedup mirroring the HTTP path's slugify.
whatBreaks: A fresh control-plane deploy could not be bootstrapped with a working admin account, or could crash/duplicate on a mismatched slug/email race.

role: Mix task: grant a team the admin-only permanent 'forever' billing comp
description: Resolves a team by id/slug/owner-email and calls Billing.grant_forever/1 to write or convert a subscription into an active 'forever' plan bypassing Stripe; idempotent no-op if already forever.
whatBreaks: An operator could accidentally grant permanent free entitlement to the wrong team, or fail to comp a team correctly, causing billing/access mismatches.

role: Mix project/build manifest for the barkpark_cloud control-plane app
description: Declares deps (ecto_sql, bcrypt_elixir, nimble_totp, plug/bandit for the HTTP API, oban, swoosh/gen_smtp for mail), release config, and elixirc_paths; heavily annotated with rationale for each dependency choice.
whatBreaks: Wrong deps or release/application config would break compilation, the OTP release build, or runtime boot of the entire cloud control plane.

role: Dockerfile for the self-hosted Postfix+OpenDKIM outbound mail relay sidecar
description: Builds a Debian-based container with postfix/opendkim/sasl2 packages, volumes for DKIM keys/mail queue/TLS certs, entrypoint script; deliberately hand-rolled (no third-party image) since it holds DKIM private keys and SMTP secrets.
whatBreaks: Transactional email (password resets, invites) delivery would fail to build or run, or could leak DKIM/SMTP secrets if the image were misconfigured.

role: Human runbook for the self-hosted mail relay setup and rollout
description: Documents DNS/SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, PTR setup, Hetzner port-25 unblock, TLS cert automation, and deliverability rollout plan for the postfix sidecar; canonical-for self-hosted-mail-relay.
whatBreaks: An operator following stale instructions could misconfigure DNS/DKIM and break email deliverability or leave the relay unreachable.

role: Container entrypoint: configures Postfix+OpenDKIM+SASL at boot
description: Idempotently generates DKIM keypair/self-signed TLS fallback if absent, writes OpenDKIM and Postfix main.cf/master.cf config (SASL auth, TLS, milter, disables chroot for DNS resolution), then execs postfix in foreground.
whatBreaks: Misconfiguration here would break DKIM signing (mail flagged as spam/rejected), break SASL auth (control plane can't send mail), or fail outbound delivery entirely.

role: Ecto migration: baseline control_plane_meta table
description: Creates the minimal control_plane_meta key/value table (schema version stamping etc.) as the first migration in the cloud app's history; other core tables (identity, registry, teams) come in later migrations.
whatBreaks: Since it's the baseline migration, a broken version would prevent the cloud database from being created/migrated at all on a fresh setup.

role: Ecto migration creating the control-plane `users` table
description: Creates the citext-backed users table (case-insensitive email uniqueness) plus hashed_password — the cloud control plane's login identity, distinct from api/'s token-based principals. Enables the citext Postgres extension.
whatBreaks: If this migration is wrong or missing, no user can register/log into the control plane at all — every downstream table (teams, memberships, tokens) FKs into users.

role: Ecto migration creating the control-plane `teams` table
description: Creates the teams table (name + globally-unique slug) — the control-plane analogue of api/'s Workspace, the boundary for members and owned Barkpark instances.
whatBreaks: A broken teams table breaks team creation and every FK'd resource (barkparks, providers, subscriptions, memberships) since they all scope to team_id.

role: Ecto migration creating the `team_memberships` join table
description: Binds users to teams with a role (owner/admin/member); enforces a user belongs to a given team at most once via a composite unique index. Control-plane mirror of api/'s Tenancy.Membership.
whatBreaks: Wrong constraints here would allow duplicate memberships or break authorization checks that gate a user's access to a team's Barkparks.

role: Ecto migration creating the `barkparks` registry table
description: Creates the central registry row for each managed Barkpark instance a team owns (slug, host, health/agent status, version) — the row the warm-pool provisioner writes when handing a fresh server to a team. slug is unique per team.
whatBreaks: This table is the hub of the cloud control plane; a broken schema here breaks instance registration, dashboards, health tracking, and every table that FKs to barkpark_id (agent_events, agent_tokens, provision_jobs).

role: Ecto migration creating the `providers` table (linked cloud accounts)
description: Creates the providers table storing per-team connected cloud accounts (e.g. Hetzner) with an AES-256-GCM-encrypted token column; plaintext tokens never touch the DB.
whatBreaks: A wrong schema breaks provisioning into a team's linked cloud account, or worse could expose plaintext credentials if the encrypted_token contract is violated.

role: Ecto migration creating the append-only `agent_events` table
description: Creates the event stream table (jsonb payload, no updated_at) that on-box agents write to for health beats/status flips/backups; indexed by (barkpark_id, inserted_at) to serve recent-events queries.
whatBreaks: Breaks agent telemetry ingestion and any recent-activity views in the cloud dashboard, though it's a leaf/append-only concern with limited blast radius.

role: Ecto migration creating the `agent_tokens` table (agent auth)
description: Creates revocable bearer tokens (SHA-256 hash only, never plaintext) that on-box agents use to authenticate reports to the control plane; mirrors api/'s api_tokens pattern.
whatBreaks: Wrong constraints break agent authentication (agents can't report health/status) or could weaken the security model if plaintext leaked into storage.

role: Ecto migration creating the `subscriptions` (billing) table
description: Creates per-team billing subscription rows (plan/status + gateway customer/subscription ids) with a partial unique index enforcing at most one active subscription per team; backs the StubGateway/Stripe billing integration.
whatBreaks: Breaks billing state tracking and could allow multiple simultaneous active subscriptions per team, corrupting plan/quota enforcement.

role: Ecto migration creating the `user_tokens` table (session auth)
description: Creates session bearer tokens for logged-in users (SHA-256 hash only, expires_at, context defaulting to "session") used by POST /v1/auth/login and subsequent authenticated control-plane API calls.
whatBreaks: Breaks user session authentication for the entire control-plane HTTP API — logged-in users would be unable to make authenticated requests.

role: Ecto migration creating the `provision_jobs` queue table
description: Creates the plain-table job queue (pending→claimed→succeeded|failed, CAS claim via claim_token) bridging the Elixir control plane and the off-box Go warm-pool provisioner (cmd/barkpark-provisioner); indexed on status for cheap claim scans.
whatBreaks: Breaks the provisioning pipeline entirely — new Barkpark instances would never get claimed/provisioned by the Go worker, stalling all go-live purchases.

role: Ecto migration: global unique index on barkparks.url
description: Adds a partial unique index on barkparks.url (where not null) as a DB-level backstop against cross-tenant subdomain collisions, since barkparks.slug was only unique per-team. Defense-in-depth for Barkpark.provisioning_subdomain/1's globally-unique FQDN construction.
whatBreaks: Two teams could provision boxes that overwrite the same customer-facing FQDN, a cross-tenant DNS/security bug, if this constraint is missing or malformed.

role: Ecto migration: adds attempts counter to provision_jobs
description: Adds an attempts integer column to provision_jobs, enabling stale-claim recovery (reaping jobs stuck in 'claimed' state) with a bounded retry count so permanently failing provisioning jobs stop looping.
whatBreaks: Without this column the stale-claim reaper can't bound retries, so a crashed worker's job either wedges forever or retries infinitely, leaving customer instances stuck provisioning.

role: Ecto migration: creates the sites table (hosted Next.js apps)
description: Creates sites, the table backing hosted Next.js/nixpacks websites co-located with a Barkpark instance; includes team/barkpark FKs, unique (team_id, slug), a GIN index on the domains array for TLS ask-gate lookups, and encrypted env storage.
whatBreaks: The entire hosted-site feature (Vercel-style site hosting on Barkpark Cloud) has no schema to persist against — site creation, domain routing, and deployments all fail.

role: Ecto migration: creates the deployments table (build/release jobs)
description: Creates deployments, one row per build-and-release of a Site; carries the claim/fencing fields (claim_worker, claimed_at, claim_epoch) used by the off-box builder to atomically claim queued jobs, plus status/history indexes.
whatBreaks: Off-box builders have no queue to claim work from and no deployment history is recorded, breaking the entire build pipeline for hosted sites.

role: Ecto migration: adds GitHub repo/branch/webhook columns to sites
description: Adds nullable github_repo, github_branch, and github_webhook_secret_encrypted columns to sites for the P7 github-webhook auto-deploy-on-push feature; unconfigured sites are unaffected since the webhook route 404s when the secret is null.
whatBreaks: GitHub push-to-deploy integration for hosted sites can't store or verify webhook secrets, breaking automatic deployments triggered by git pushes.

role: Ecto migration: adds kind discriminator to provision_jobs
description: Adds a kind column ('provision' | 'deprovision') to provision_jobs so the deprovision flow reuses the same claim/attempts queue machinery instead of a parallel table, plus an index so each kind's claim query scans only its own rows.
whatBreaks: Deprovision jobs could be claimed by the provision worker (or vice versa), causing wrong-path handling of teardown vs go-live requests.

role: Ecto migration: installs Oban's job-queue schema
description: Calls Oban.Migrations.up()/down() to create the standalone oban_jobs table, oban_job_state enum, oban_peers table, and insert-notify trigger, mirroring api/'s identical Oban migration. Intentionally has no FKs to app tables.
whatBreaks: Any background job scheduled via Oban in cloud/ (notifications, async work) fails outright since its backing schema doesn't exist.

role: Ecto migration: combined session-lifecycle + PAT columns on user_tokens
description: Alters user_tokens with session lifecycle/device metadata (revoked_at, ip_address, user_agent, last_used_at) and personal-access-token columns (name, abilities, team_id), deduping two originally-separate migrations into one superset alteration of the dual-purpose token table.
whatBreaks: Session revocation (logout/sign-out-everywhere), active-session listing, and personal access token creation/listing all depend on these columns and indexes existing correctly.

role: Ecto migration: creates per-team email_notification_settings table
description: Creates email_notification_settings, one row per team holding notification transport config (instance/smtp/api) and per-event alert toggles, mirroring Coolify's notification settings; all secret columns store ciphertext only via Vault encryption.
whatBreaks: Teams cannot configure or persist their notification preferences/SMTP credentials, and the notification dispatcher has no settings row to read from.

role: Ecto migration: creates notification_deliveries send-log table
description: Creates notification_deliveries, a durable per-recipient send record (status/attempts/last_error) for every notification the dispatcher emits, modeled on api/'s webhook_deliveries; team-scoped with indexes for listing and future retry logic.
whatBreaks: Notification sends have no audit trail or retry seam, making failed alert/transactional emails silently unrecoverable and undebuggable.

role: Ecto migration creating team_invitations table
description: Creates the pending-invitation table (email+role, SHA-256 token_hash, expiry) for inviting users to a Cloud team, with a partial unique index enforcing one live invite per email per team. Cascades on team delete, nilifies inviter on user delete.
whatBreaks: Team invitation flow (invite creation, accept, and uniqueness guarantees) breaks or the schema drifts from the Invitations context code.

role: Ecto migration adding billing lifecycle columns to subscriptions
description: Adds past_due/cancel_at_period_end/current_period_end/canceled_at/refunded_at to subscriptions and relaxes the one-active-per-team unique index to one-live (active OR past_due) per team, keyed for Stripe-style lifecycle webhooks.
whatBreaks: Billing state machine (dunning, cancellation, one-live-subscription-per-team invariant) and gateway webhook lookups could double-charge or mis-suspend teams.

role: Ecto migration adding billing-suspension flags to barkparks
description: Adds suspended/suspended_reason/suspended_at columns to barkparks as a billing-verdict axis distinct from health/agent status, used to bulk-suspend a team's managed instances on subscription lapse.
whatBreaks: Billing enforcement (suspending/restoring instances on payment lapse or recovery) fails, letting non-paying teams keep access or wrongly suspending paying ones.

role: Ecto migration adding encrypted admin_token column to barkparks
description: Adds a nullable admin_token_encrypted text column storing an AES-256-GCM-encrypted per-instance admin bearer token, so owners can retrieve instance admin access from the product instead of SSH.
whatBreaks: Owners lose the in-product path to instance admin credentials, or (if encryption misapplied) plaintext tokens could leak into the DB.

role: Ecto migration creating external_identities table for OAuth/SSO
description: Creates the external_identities table keyed by (provider, provider_uid) rather than email, deliberately avoiding the email-linking footgun Coolify has; cascades on user delete and enforces one identity per provider subject.
whatBreaks: OAuth/SSO login could misattribute accounts across users (an account-takeover class bug) or fail to link/verify identities at all.

role: Ecto migration creating oauth_states single-use CSRF table
description: Creates a nonce-keyed table making signed OAuth state tokens single-use via delete-to-consume semantics, with a TTL sweep index to reap unredeemed states, closing a replay window in the OAuth CSRF-state design.
whatBreaks: OAuth callback URLs become replayable within their TTL, a CSRF/session-fixation-adjacent security gap in the SSO login flow.

role: Ecto migration adding TOTP 2FA columns to users
description: Adds encrypted TOTP secret, encrypted recovery-code hashes, confirmed_at, and last-accepted-step columns to users implementing opt-in two-factor auth with OTP replay protection, mirroring Coolify's design.
whatBreaks: Two-factor login (enrollment, verification, recovery codes, replay-guard) breaks, either locking users out or allowing OTP replay/bypass.

role: Ecto migration adding onboarding-state columns to teams
description: Adds a resumable jsonb onboarding_state blob and onboarding_completed_at timestamp to teams, defaulting fresh teams into an onboarding state for first-run checklist UX and activation-time analytics.
whatBreaks: New-team onboarding checklist loses its resumable state or activation-time metrics become wrong, but core product function is unaffected.

role: Ecto migration creating env_vars table for team/instance secrets
description: Creates the encrypted env-vars table scoped to team or barkpark (instance), with per-scope partial-unique key indexes and a check constraint tying the scope discriminator to barkpark_id presence; injected into provisioned instances.
whatBreaks: User-managed secrets/env vars for instances could collide across scopes, fail to inject correctly, or violate the scope/FK invariant the app code relies on.

role: Ecto migration adding email-confirm and change-email columns
description: Adds confirmed_at and citext pending_email to users, plus sent_to and failed_attempts (brute-force lockout counter) to user_tokens, supporting the account-confirmation and verified email-change flows atop the existing token lifecycle.
whatBreaks: Email confirmation and email-change flows break, or the brute-force lockout on change-email codes stops enforcing, weakening account security.

role: Ecto migration creating the append-only audit_events table
description: Creates a team-scoped, append-only audit_events table (actor/action/target/metadata) with FKs cascading from teams and nilifying on user delete, plus a DB-level trigger that raises on any UPDATE/DELETE to enforce immutability at the storage layer, not just in Ecto.
whatBreaks: If the trigger or FK semantics are wrong, audit trail integrity is lost (mutable/erasable logs) or a hard team-delete path could deadlock against the append-only trigger.

role: Ecto migration adding staleness-detection columns to barkparks
description: Adds unreachable_count and unreachable_notification_sent to barkparks plus a partial index on last_seen_at for online instances, backing the StalenessWorker's debounce+alert-latch for detecting silently-wedged agents (port of Coolify's pattern).
whatBreaks: Wrong columns/index break offline detection, causing false-online status or spammy/duplicate outage notifications, and a full-table scan instead of an indexed one as the fleet grows.

role: Ecto migration adding chat-channel jsonb columns to notification settings
description: Adds `channels` (array of Vault-encrypted ChannelConfig embeds) and `event_routes` (event→channel-type map) jsonb columns to email_notification_settings, plus http_status to notification_deliveries, folding Discord/Slack/Telegram/Pushover/webhook egress into the existing notification system instead of a new table.
whatBreaks: Wrong jsonb defaults or missing columns break chat notification delivery or leak credentials if the encrypted-blob convention is violated.

role: Ecto migration adding the durable one-trial-ever ledger to teams
description: Adds trial_started_at/trial_ends_at/notice-sent timestamps to teams as the durable ledger enforcing 'one trial per team ever' (guarded by an atomic UPDATE...WHERE trial_started_at IS NULL), and backfills existing active trial subscriptions into the new columns.
whatBreaks: A bug here lets a team re-claim a free trial repeatedly (revenue leak) or incorrectly marks paying teams as trial-locked, and the backfill UPDATE could corrupt ledger dates for existing customers.

role: Ecto migration adding content-template bootstrap columns to barkparks
description: Adds the chosen deploy template slug and bootstrap outputs (workspace/project/dataset slugs, Vault-encrypted read token, Vault-encrypted app env blob) to barkparks so the dashboard can retrieve go-live bootstrap results without SSH.
whatBreaks: If the encrypted columns are misconfigured or accidentally serialized, secrets (read tokens, app env) could leak in barkpark_json output; missing columns break the deploy/dashboard bootstrap display.

role: Ecto migration creating the warm-server pool claim table
description: Creates warm_servers (pre-baked Hetzner boxes) as a race-safe FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim store, enabling near-instant go-lives by assigning an already-booted box instead of cold-provisioning; unique index on name, plain index on status for the claim scan.
whatBreaks: Missing unique/status indexes or wrong claim semantics let two workers double-claim the same warm box, causing provisioning collisions or lost fast-launch performance.

role: Ecto migration adding a DB-enforced one-active-job-per-barkpark guard
description: Adds a partial unique index on provision_jobs(barkpark_id, kind) scoped to pending/claimed status, closing a check-then-insert race (especially on the retry endpoint) that could otherwise double-provision and double-bill a customer for one intent.
whatBreaks: Without this constraint, rapid retries or concurrent deletes can enqueue duplicate provision/deprovision jobs, causing double-billing or orphaned infrastructure — a direct money-path bug.

role: Ecto migration widening provision_jobs.error from varchar to text
description: Fixes a real production incident: the worker's compound fallback-ladder error message exceeded varchar(255), causing the /fail report itself to 500 and jobs to stall forever in 'claimed' instead of failing cleanly for retry.
whatBreaks: If reverted or not applied, long error messages truncate/crash the fail-report endpoint, leaving provision jobs stuck unrecoverably instead of retriable.

role: Ecto migration adding a jsonb[] steps array to provision_jobs for progress narration
description: Adds a `steps` array column that the Go worker appends step transitions to (create/secure/configure/content/ready x started|done|failed) so a refreshed /new page can render mid-provision progress without relying solely on the SSE stream.
whatBreaks: Missing or malformed column breaks progress UI on page refresh during provisioning, degrading UX but not causing data loss or billing issues.

role: Ecto migration adding a jsonb[] console log array to provision_jobs
description: Adds a `console` array column that the Go worker tees redacted create-to-live narration into (server-side capped ~300 lines) so the /new progress screen shows a live, refresh-resilient provisioning console.
whatBreaks: Missing or malformed column breaks the live provisioning console UI on refresh, a UX regression rather than a data-integrity or billing issue.

role: Ecto migration creating github_installations table for GitHub App links
description: Creates the github_installations table storing one encrypted GitHub App installation per team (unique index on team_id), with plaintext account_login for display. FK cascades delete on team removal; the installation handle ciphertext lives only in installation_id_encrypted.
whatBreaks: GitHub App connection (installs, repo-linked deploys) fails to persist or leaks/loses the installation handle.

role: Migration adding append-only build console array to deployments
description: Adds a jsonb array `console` column to deployments so the off-box builder can stream/persist build log lines for the live deploy console UI, surviving page refresh independent of SSE ticks.
whatBreaks: Live build console UI shows no log lines or crashes deploy JSON serialization.

role: Migration adding delivery_id + DB-level dedup indexes for deployments
description: Adds delivery_id column plus two partial unique indexes (per delivery_id, and per active site+git_ref) as a DB backstop against duplicate deployments from GitHub webhook redeliveries; also collapses pre-existing duplicate active rows before index creation.
whatBreaks: Concurrent GitHub push redeliveries could create duplicate/racing deployments for the same commit.

role: Migration adding branch-preview environment fields/indexes to deployments and sites
description: Adds environment/branch/preview_slug/preview_host to deployments and previews_enabled to sites, re-scopes the prior active-deployment uniqueness index to production only, and adds preview-specific uniqueness and lookup indexes — implements Vercel-style non-production branch previews.
whatBreaks: Branch preview deploys could collide with production deploys, fail to dedupe per branch, or the on-demand TLS host lookup for previews would break.

role: Migration adding self-update status cache fields to barkparks (instances)
description: Adds update_state/update_running_release/update_latest_release/update_checked_at to barkparks, caching each instance's self-reported update check so the fleet dashboard can render update availability without a live fan-out.
whatBreaks: Fleet dashboard's 'update available' status becomes stale or unrenderable.

role: Migration adding single latest-wins detail caption column to deployments
description: Adds a text `detail` column to deployments for a live plain-language sub-caption shown under the deploy status pill; best-effort telemetry, missing value is harmless.
whatBreaks: Deploy status UI loses its sub-caption text; no functional deploy impact.

role: Migration adding Postgres trigger enforcing cross-site domain uniqueness
description: Creates a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger function that rejects adding a domain to a site's text[] domains array if another site already owns it, as a DB-level backstop against domain takeover/collision; only guards newly-added domains, does not heal pre-existing duplicates.
whatBreaks: A malicious or buggy write could let two sites claim the same custom domain (domain takeover), or conversely legitimate domain adds could be wrongly rejected.

role: Migration relaxing notification_deliveries.team_id to nullable
description: Allows team_id to be null on notification_deliveries so user-scoped transactional emails (password reset, verify, email-change) without a team context can still write an observable Delivery row; purely additive, no backfill needed.
whatBreaks: Transactional emails without a team in context would fail to insert their Delivery row (breaking send or observability).

role: Migration adding Vercel zero-paste claim fields to barkparks
description: Adds vercel_project_id, vercel_deploy_url, and an encrypted vercel_claim_encrypted (plus mint timestamp) to barkparks, backing the platform-deployed instance's Vercel ownership-claim handoff flow.
whatBreaks: Vercel-deployed instance claim flow (vercel.com/claim-deployment) cannot store or redeem the claim code.

role: Migration adding custom_host field + uniqueness index to barkparks
description: Adds a nullable custom_host string to barkparks for team-attached platform-zone hostnames, with a partial unique index preventing two instances from sharing the same custom host.
whatBreaks: Two instances could be attached to the same custom domain, causing routing collisions.

role: Ecto migration adding refreshed_at tracking to warm_servers table
description: Adds a nullable refreshed_at timestamp and a composite index on {status, refreshed_at} to warm_servers so the pool self-refresh loop can claim the stalest box first (nulls-first ordering). One-time schema change, additive and backward compatible.
whatBreaks: The stalest-box claim query in the warm-pool refresh worker would mis-order or fail if this column/index is missing or misnamed.

role: Ecto migration adding fleet autoupdate policy columns to barkparks table
description: Adds autoupdate_enabled (opt-out default true), autoupdate_paused, pinned_release, and autoupdate_triggered_at columns plus a partial index used by the AutoupdateRolloutWorker's hot query to find eligible instances cheaply as the fleet grows.
whatBreaks: The autoupdate rollout worker's eligibility filter and staged-rollout health gating would break or silently update/skip instances incorrectly.

role: Ecto migration adding provider/region/server_type columns to barkparks
description: Introduces provider-neutral hosting fields (defaulting provider to "hetzner" for backward compatibility) so provision jobs can thread {kind, region, server_type} to the Go worker instead of hard-coding Hetzner defaults; region/server_type are nullable with control-plane fallback.
whatBreaks: Multi-provider instance provisioning (charter Decision 9) would break, or legacy rows could get mis-tagged with the wrong provider/region, misrouting provision jobs.

role: Ecto migration adding bundle_ref column to provision_jobs for resurrect jobs
description: Adds a nullable bundle_ref string used only by resurrect-kind provision jobs to name the object-storage archive to restore from; relies on an existing partial unique index for one-active-job-per-kind semantics.
whatBreaks: Portable-archive instance resurrection (azh-w6) would be unable to reference which backup bundle to restore, breaking that recovery path.

role: Ecto migration creating device_auth_requests table for CLI device-code login
description: Creates the RFC-8628-style device-authorization ledger backing `bp login`: stores only SHA-256 hashes of device_code and user_code (never plaintext), status lifecycle pending→approved→consumed-by-delete, TTL expiry with a sweep index, and FK to users with delete_all.
whatBreaks: The entire `bp login` device-authorization flow (CLI polling, browser approval, session minting) would fail or leak credentials if hashing/uniqueness/expiry semantics are wrong.

role: Ecto migration creating usage_samples table for cached fleet usage snapshots
description: Creates a table storing one JSONB usage envelope row per instance per ~15min sample (written by a usage-sampler worker), backing GET /v1/usage/summary's fast DB-only read for the fleet overview meter strip; index backs both latest-per-instance lookup and retention pruning.
whatBreaks: The Cloud Console's fleet usage overview would be unable to show usage meters, or would show stale/wrong data if the barkpark_id+measured_at index or delete_all cascade is wrong.

role: Migration adding barkparks.channel + fleet_settings table
description: Adds a NOT NULL 'channel' column (prod/staging) to barkparks for canary-gated rollout, with an index, and creates a single-row fleet_settings table holding the fleet-wide autoupdate_halted kill switch.
whatBreaks: Canary rollout logic (staging vs prod gating) and the fleet-wide autoupdate halt switch would have no backing schema, breaking the isu-w5.2 rollout worker or corrupting existing rows if the default/null constraints are wrong.

role: Node-vm unit test harness for the Cloud Console dashboard SPA (app.js)
description: 5000+ line, 370+ test pure-Node harness that evaluates the shipped app.js verbatim inside a node:vm sandbox (browser stubs, side-effect-free since document.readyState stays "loading") and exercises pure helpers exposed via a guarded __bpTestHook — focused on route/decode/escape helpers where a malformed deep link once white-screened the dashboard. Rendering/fetch/SSE are deliberately out of scope (exercised live instead).
whatBreaks: A regression in app.js's routing/decoding/escaping helpers (e.g. a deep-link URIError) would ship undetected and could white-screen the Cloud Console dashboard for users.

role: Zero-dependency static design-contract linter for the Cloud Console SPA CSS/HTML/JS
description: Node script enforcing 8 hard error classes (undefined CSS var consumption, orphan classes, unvetted dynamic class composition, unparseable class tokens, WCAG contrast failures for both themes, raw color literals outside token blocks, external resource loads for offline-only rendering, scoped dark-theme alias leaks) plus 3 report-only classes; run as a CI/build gate per the epic charter's design-system enforcement decision.
whatBreaks: A real CSS/HTML/JS contract violation (e.g. broken dark-mode contrast, dead class, external resource dependency) would ship to the Cloud Console SPA without being caught if this checker regresses or its allowlists go stale/wrong.

role: Test fixture defining instance-state ranking/bucket/tone metadata for fleet UI
description: Static JSON listing each instance lifecycle state (removal_failed, failed, suspended, degraded, behind, removing, provisioning, ok) with its display rank, bucket (attention/in-flight/healthy), tone, glyph, and label — used by tests validating the fleet attention-sort ordering in the Cloud Console.
whatBreaks: Tests asserting the fleet dashboard sorts/labels instance states correctly would give false confidence or fail incorrectly if this fixture drifts from the real ordering logic.

role: Test fixture with sample domain-verification API responses for Cloud Console tests
description: Static JSON with three canned domain-status scenarios (all_serving, mid_issuance TLS pending, serving_failed 502) mirroring the shape of the domain-verification endpoint's DNS/TLS/serving stage checks, used to test the Console's domain-status rendering.
whatBreaks: Tests covering the Cloud Console's domain verification status UI (DNS/TLS/serving stages) would lose coverage of edge cases like pending TLS issuance or 502 serving failures if this fixture is wrong or removed.

role: Fixture list of Cloud audit/event category names
description: Flat JSON array of event-type/category slugs (audit, deployments, fleet, github, members, notifications, onboarding, sites, subscription, barkpark.restored/suspended) used by the Cloud SPA preview harness to populate filter UI or fixture data. Static, hand-maintained fixture, not generated.
whatBreaks: Preview/demo event-type filter dropdown shows wrong or missing categories, but production behavior is unaffected.

role: Fixture snapshot of a Hetzner provider resource overview
description: Static JSON mocking the response shape for a Hetzner Cloud fleet overview (counts + resources: backups, dns_zones, firewalls, etc.) consumed by the Cloud SPA preview/mock harness to render provider-detail screens without a live backend.
whatBreaks: Preview screens for the Hetzner provider dashboard render incorrect or empty data in demo mode only.

role: Fixture catalog of cloud provider regions/server types
description: Static JSON listing region and server-type/pricing catalogs for hetzner and azure, used by the preview harness to mock the provider catalog API for instance-provisioning UI screens.
whatBreaks: Provisioning wizard preview shows wrong region/server-type options or prices in demo mode; no production impact.

role: Fixture matrix of per-provider feature capabilities
description: Static JSON mapping each provider (hetzner, fake, azure) to boolean capability flags (core, catalog, archive, resurrect, decommission, adopt, audit, pause, labels) mirroring the real provider-capabilities contract, used to drive preview UI gating.
whatBreaks: Preview harness enables/disables the wrong provider actions in the UI (e.g. shows Pause for hetzner); production capability checks unaffected since real API is separate.

role: Fixture list of billing/usage meter names and labels
description: Static JSON array of usage-meter definitions (documents, datasets, webhooks, db_size, disk, seats, api_requests, bandwidth, instances, cpu, ram, req_per_s, p95_ms) with display labels, used by the Cloud SPA preview to mock usage/billing panels.
whatBreaks: Preview usage/billing dashboard mislabels or omits meters; no production billing impact.

role: Fixture definitions of health-check verify probes
description: Static JSON list of named verification probes (verify.api, verify.login, verify.studio) each with a label and pass_rule expression, used by the preview harness to mock the post-deploy verification/smoke-check UI.
whatBreaks: Preview verify/smoke-check panel shows wrong probe names or rules; does not affect real deploy verification logic which lives elsewhere.

role: Standalone static harness proving cross-surface design-token coherence
description: Self-contained HTML page (Unified Aesthetic sign-off instrument) that composes Studio/web, paper, and TUI vocabulary on one page with a single light/dark toggle cascading to every pane, reading tokens live from app.css and embedding paper-surface.html as an iframe plus committed Go TUI golden fixtures — used to visually verify no surface hand-copies a hex value.
whatBreaks: Loses the one cross-surface visual proof that Studio/web/paper/TUI tokens stay in sync; a real token drift could go undetected, but nothing in production runtime depends on this file.

role: Browser-side fetch/EventSource stub for the Cloud SPA preview harness
description: Classic script injected before app.js by serve.mjs that stubs window.fetch and window.EventSource so the SPA renders committed scenarios with zero backend, dynamically importing scenarios.mjs as the single source of truth shared with smoke.mjs; scenario/theme chosen via URL params.
whatBreaks: Cloud SPA preview/demo mode fails to render fixture data or crashes (no live backend to fall back on), breaking the design-review/smoke-test workflow, but production app.js and real backend are unaffected.

role: Standalone live preview of paper-surface design tokens
description: Self-contained HTML page linking the real api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css stylesheet to render swatches for --paper-*, --bp-tone-* and type-scale tokens with a light/dark toggle; also reused verbatim as an iframe inside coherence.html.
whatBreaks: Design-token preview/sign-off page shows stale or broken swatches, or the coherence.html iframe breaks since it embeds this file verbatim; no production runtime impact.

role: Single source of truth for Cloud SPA preview fixture scenarios
description: Large (1135-line) ES module of committed fixture scenarios (barkpark list envelopes, provision_steps, etc.) mirroring real server serializer shapes (router.ex barkpark_json/3), imported both by mock.js in-browser and by smoke.mjs under Node to boot app.js against fixtures without a backend.
whatBreaks: Every preview scenario and the Node smoke test (smoke.mjs) that boots the real app.js against fixtures breaks or shows wrong states, undermining the primary demo/QA harness for the Cloud SPA; no production backend impact.

role: Zero-dep static server for the Cloud SPA preview harness
description: Node http server that serves cloud/priv/static/ verbatim but injects a mock.js script before app.js when serving index.html, letting the SPA render any scripted scenario (?scen=) with no backend. Backs `make cloud-preview`.
whatBreaks: Developers/agents lose the ability to visually preview or screenshot Cloud dashboard states without a live backend.

role: Headless-Chrome screenshot driver for every Cloud SPA scenario
description: Bash script that boots serve.mjs, then drives Chrome/Chromium headless to screenshot each scenario x theme x width combo into a gitignored output dir; backs `make cloud-shots`.
whatBreaks: Visual QA / screenshot review of the Cloud console across scenarios and themes silently fails or produces wrong/missing PNGs.

role: node:vm smoke test that boots real app.js against scenario fixtures
description: Standalone test runner loading the shipped app.js verbatim into a sandboxed DOM shim, running init() with stubbed fetch/EventSource per scenario, and asserting structural markup (element/class presence, row counts) per an EXPECTATIONS table.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the Cloud SPA's real render→route→load path (onboarding/timeline/fleet views) go undetected since this is the only harness exercising app.js end-to-end without a backend.

role: All CSS for the Barkpark Cloud dashboard (tokens + components)
description: Single stylesheet, no framework, with design tokens auto-generated from design/tokens.json (regenerate via node design/emit.mjs --write) plus hand-authored component styles; supports light/dark via [data-theme] and self-hosts Inter.
whatBreaks: The entire Cloud console visually breaks or mis-themes (light/dark, tokens) across every screen — it is the sole stylesheet.

role: Entire Barkpark Cloud SPA application logic, vanilla JS no build
description: 10k+ line hand-written (not bundled/generated) single-file SPA: auth, hash-based routing, fleet/instance views, onboarding, toasts/modals, theme switching, all fetch calls with Bearer auth and 401 logout. This is the whole Cloud dashboard's client-side brain.
whatBreaks: The entire Barkpark Cloud control-plane UI (fleet management, billing, provisioning, auth) stops working or renders incorrectly for all users.

role: "Deploy with Barkpark" badge SVG asset
description: Static SVG badge image (214x36) used presumably as a deploy-button graphic embedded in READMEs/templates for the Deploy-with-Barkpark flow.
whatBreaks: A deploy badge image renders incorrectly or missing; purely cosmetic.

role: SIL Open Font License text for the bundled Inter font
description: Legal license text accompanying the self-hosted Inter-var.woff2 font file referenced by app.css; required for license compliance, not executable.
whatBreaks: No functional impact; only a license-compliance/documentation concern if missing.

role: SPA shell / entry HTML for the Barkpark Cloud dashboard
description: The single HTML document loaded by all Cloud console routes: sets pre-paint theme via inline script (reading localStorage bpcloud.theme / bp_theme), defines auth screen and app chrome markup, and loads app.css/app.js.
whatBreaks: The Cloud dashboard fails to boot or theme correctly for every visitor — this is the sole HTML entry point for the SPA.

role: Living style guide / design-token demo page for Cloud console
description: Standalone HTML page that renders tokens, scales, and shared components from app.css side by side in both themes, for visual QA of the design system; page-local chrome only, no app.js dependency.
whatBreaks: Design review/QA of the Cloud design system tokens becomes harder or shows stale/incorrect examples; no runtime impact on the app itself.

role: Doc: marks starter templates as a synced mirror
description: Explains that cloud/priv/templates/{blog-starter,website-starter} are a byte-for-byte mirror of js/packages/create-barkpark-app/templates, with the sync script and diff verification command.
whatBreaks: A developer could hand-edit the mirrored templates directly, causing silent drift from the canonical create-barkpark-app source until the next sync overwrites their changes.

role: Example env file for the blog-starter Next.js template
description: Documents required env vars (BARKPARK_API_URL, tokens, workspace/project slugs, Postgres, Phoenix secret) for developers scaffolding a project from the blog-starter template.
whatBreaks: New projects created from the blog-starter template get missing/wrong env var guidance, causing setup confusion but not affecting running systems.

role: Setup/reference doc for the blog-starter Next.js template
description: Documents the scaffolded Next.js 15 blog starter shipped by Barkpark Cloud's project templater — quick start, auth token rotation, draft-mode preview, webhook revalidation tag format, and deploy env vars. Templated with {{projectName}}/{{pmCommand}} placeholders substituted at project-creation time.
whatBreaks: New Cloud users following stale/wrong instructions get a broken local setup or leak the default dev token into production

role: gitignore template for scaffolded blog-starter projects
description: Named `_gitignore` (not `.gitignore`) so it ships inside the npm/priv template tree without being ignored itself; renamed to `.gitignore` when a new project is generated from this template.
whatBreaks: Scaffolded projects would commit node_modules/.env/.next artifacts

role: Next.js route wiring Barkpark's revalidation webhook handler
description: Thin glue that wires `createWebhookHandler` (HMAC-verified) from `@barkpark/nextjs/webhook` to `revalidateBarkpark`, so Studio mutation events trigger Next.js cache revalidation in the scaffolded template app.
whatBreaks: Template's realtime revalidation stops working; scaffolded blog would show stale content after edits in Studio

role: Route disabling Next.js draft mode for the blog template
description: GET/POST handler that disables `draftMode()` and redirects to a same-origin-only path (guards against `//`/`/\\` open-redirect tricks).
whatBreaks: Draft preview mode couldn't be exited, or an open-redirect vulnerability if the path guard were wrong

role: Route enabling Next.js draft mode for the blog template
description: Enables `draftMode()` guarded by `BARKPARK_PREVIEW_SECRET` (fail-closed in production if unset), with same-origin-only redirect target; simple template example rather than the production-grade `createDraftModeRoutes` signed-URL flow.
whatBreaks: Draft/unpublished content could be exposed to anonymous visitors on a deployed site, or preview would be entirely broken

role: Author profile page for the blog-starter template
description: Server component fetching one author by id and filtering all posts client-side by `author._ref`; example usage of the template's `getDocById`/`getDocs` fetchers and Next.js metadata API.
whatBreaks: Scaffolded blog's author pages would 404 or show wrong/missing posts

role: Pagination UI component for the blog-starter template
description: Reusable client-safe pagination nav (prev/next + page numbers) driven by `currentPage`/`totalPages`/`basePath` props with query-string page links.
whatBreaks: Paginated post feed in the scaffolded blog would render broken/missing page navigation

role: App Router error boundary for the blog-starter template
description: Client-component error boundary shown on render/runtime errors within its route segment, with a 'Try again' button calling Next's `reset()`.
whatBreaks: Scaffolded blog would show Next.js's default unstyled error page instead of the branded one

role: Global Tailwind stylesheet for the blog-starter template
description: Tailwind base/components/utilities imports plus a couple of small overrides (color-scheme, body colors, prose link color) for the scaffolded app.
whatBreaks: Scaffolded blog loses base styling/dark-mode support

role: Root layout for the blog-starter Next.js template
description: Defines `metadataBase` (from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`), site chrome (header/nav linking to Studio, skip-link for a11y, footer), wraps every page in the scaffolded app.
whatBreaks: Every page of the scaffolded blog loses its shell/nav or gets wrong canonical/OpenGraph URLs (falls back to localhost)

role: Next.js loading skeleton for blog-starter template
description: Renders an animated skeleton placeholder while a route segment's async data resolves. Cosmetic UX-only component with no logic.
whatBreaks: Users would see a blank screen instead of a skeleton during data fetch, but no functionality breaks.

role: Next.js branded 404 page for blog-starter template
description: Replaces Next's default unstyled 404 with a branded page shown when notFound() is called or a route doesn't match. Static, no data dependency.
whatBreaks: Unknown post/tag slugs would show Next's generic 404 instead of the branded one; purely cosmetic.

role: Home page listing paginated blog posts for blog-starter template
description: Server component that fetches posts via getDocs('post', ...) with offset-based pagination and renders a post grid with links to detail pages.
whatBreaks: The template's homepage would fail to list posts or paginate incorrectly, breaking the primary landing experience of every project scaffolded from this template.

role: Client component for optimistic draft-mode post preview
description: Renders a post in Next.js draft mode with an optimistic-update hook (useOptimisticDocument) and an exit-preview action; commitOptimistic is a stub meant to be wired to a server action for persistence.
whatBreaks: Draft-mode preview editing (optimistic title edits, exit-preview flow) would break or fail to render for editors previewing unpublished content.

role: Blog post detail page with SEO metadata and draft mode
description: Fetches a post by slug (published or draft based on draftMode()), resolves author/tags, generates OG metadata via barkparkMetadata, and renders either the DraftModePreview or the public article view.
whatBreaks: Post detail pages would 404 incorrectly, leak draft content to the public, or produce broken SEO metadata/crawler previews.

role: Next.js robots.txt generator for blog-starter template
description: Emits a permissive robots.txt pointing crawlers to the sitemap, using NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL with a localhost fallback.
whatBreaks: Search engine crawling directives or sitemap discovery could be misconfigured for sites built on this template.

role: Next.js sitemap.xml generator for blog-starter template
description: Builds the sitemap from all posts, authors, and tags fetched via getDocs, using their slugs/ids and _updatedAt for lastModified.
whatBreaks: SEO sitemap would omit or mis-link content, or throw if getDocs shape changes, degrading search indexing for sites on this template.

role: Tag detail page listing posts for that tag
description: Fetches a tag by slug, filters all posts by tag reference, and renders tag metadata plus a list of tagged posts; generates SEO metadata via barkparkMetadata.
whatBreaks: Tag archive pages would 404 or fail to list correct posts, breaking taxonomy navigation on the template site.

role: Template-file scaffolding the Barkpark client config for blog-starter
description: A .tmpl file (rendered at project generation time, {{projectName}} placeholder) creating the shared barkparkClient and projectConfig used throughout the template's data-fetching lib. Documents the flat vs workspace-scoped API path tradeoff.
whatBreaks: Every generated blog-starter project would fail to connect to the Barkpark API (wrong URL/dataset) since all pages depend on this client instance.

role: Manifest declaring the blog-starter template's schemas, seed, and env vars
description: Machine-readable manifest (validated against templates/barkpark.template.schema.json) listing content schemas, seed script, dataset, and required env vars (API URL, dataset, workspace/project, tokens, preview secret) consumed by the cloud template-provisioning system.
whatBreaks: Bootstrapping a new project from this template via cloud provisioning would fail to wire schemas, seed data, or required env/secrets, breaking the entire template's onboarding flow.

role: Example override for building API image from local checkout
description: Sample docker-compose override that switches the `api` service from the published ghcr image to a local build context pointed at `../../../../../api`. Copied by scaffolded users, not used directly.
whatBreaks: Wrong build context path just breaks a manual opt-in local-dev override, no runtime impact.

role: Docker Compose stack for the blog-starter template's self-hosted deploy
description: Defines postgres + barkpark api services (env-driven DB creds, healthcheck, ports 5432/4000) shipped as part of the blog-starter scaffold template so generated projects can self-host the API stack.
whatBreaks: Every project scaffolded from blog-starter would fail to bring up its local/self-hosted API+DB stack via `docker compose up`.

role: Template's server-side data-fetch layer wrapping the Barkpark Next.js SDK
description: Instantiates `createBarkparkServer` and exposes typed helpers (getDocs, countDocs, getDocById, getDocBySlug) that all pages in the scaffolded blog use; comments flag the cache-tag/draft-mode contract as load-bearing (must route all fetches through barkparkFetch or revalidation silently no-ops).
whatBreaks: Every generated blog-starter project's pages (post lists, post detail, tags, authors) fail to fetch data or ISR/webhook cache revalidation silently stops working.

role: Template's informational GROQ-like query string constants
description: Named query strings (allPosts, postBySlug, etc.) and POSTS_PER_PAGE constant; explicitly documented as not-yet-wired (future codegen migration) — pages currently use the typed helpers in barkpark.ts instead.
whatBreaks: Currently inert/documentation-only in the template; no runtime behavior depends on it yet.

role: Next.js config for the blog-starter scaffold template
description: Sets server-action body size limit and allowed remote image hostnames (localhost, barkpark.dev) for scaffolded projects.
whatBreaks: Generated blog-starter projects could reject large form submissions or fail to render remote cover/avatar images.

role: package.json template (with {{packageName}} placeholder) for blog-starter scaffold
description: Declares scripts (dev/build/codegen/seed) and dependencies (@barkpark/core, nextjs, react SDKs, Next 15, React 19, Tailwind) rendered into generated projects by the scaffolder.
whatBreaks: Every project scaffolded from blog-starter gets wrong/missing deps or scripts, breaking install/build/dev for the generated app.

role: PostCSS config enabling Tailwind+autoprefixer for the template
description: Minimal PostCSS plugin list (tailwindcss, autoprefixer) copied into scaffolded blog-starter projects.
whatBreaks: Tailwind classes wouldn't compile in generated projects, breaking all styling.

role: Barkpark content-model schema for 'author' document type in blog-starter
description: Declares the author document's fields (name, slug, bio, avatar, twitter) as public-visibility schema, seeded into every project scaffolded from this template.
whatBreaks: Generated blog projects' author content type/admin UI and any queries filtering on author fields would be wrong or fail.

role: Barkpark content-model schema for 'post' document type in blog-starter
description: Declares the core blog post schema (title, slug, excerpt, richText content, author reference, coverImage, publishedAt, tags array) that drives the template's entire content model.
whatBreaks: The scaffold's primary content type breaks — post creation, listing, and rendering all fail in every generated blog-starter project.

role: Barkpark content-model schema for 'tag' document type in blog-starter
description: Declares the tag document's fields (title, slug, description) used by post.tags references in the scaffold.
whatBreaks: Tag-based filtering/listing pages in generated blog-starter projects would break.

role: Seed script for the blog-starter template's demo content
description: Populates a fresh Barkpark dataset with 2 authors, 3 tags, and 7 posts (6 published, 1 draft) via the /v1/data/mutate API, using workspace/project scoping if set. Run via `pnpm seed` in generated blog-starter projects; requires the local docker-compose stack to be up.
whatBreaks: New blog-starter projects would fail `pnpm seed` or show broken/missing demo content, undermining the template's first-run experience.

role: Tailwind config for the blog-starter Next.js template
description: Defines content globs, a brand color, and typography plugin defaults for generated blog-starter projects. Plain scaffolding config, not shared code.
whatBreaks: Generated blog-starter sites would lose brand styling or Tailwind wouldn't scan the right files, causing missing/unstyled classes.

role: TypeScript compiler config for the blog-starter template
description: Standard Next.js 15 App Router tsconfig (ES2022, bundler resolution, strict mode, `@/*` path alias). Copied verbatim into generated projects.
whatBreaks: Generated blog-starter projects would fail to typecheck/build or lose path-alias resolution.

role: Env var template for the website-starter Next.js scaffold
description: Documents required env vars (API URL, dataset, workspace/project, dev + server tokens, Postgres, Phoenix secret/host) for a generated website-starter project; copied to `.env.local` by users.
whatBreaks: Users following the README quick-start would be missing required config or use insecure default secrets, breaking auth/deploy for generated sites.

role: README shipped inside generated website-starter projects
description: Onboarding doc for the website-starter template covering quick start, dev-token rotation, webhook/revalidation contract, and deploy notes; uses `{{projectName}}`/`{{pmCommand}}` template placeholders filled at generation time.
whatBreaks: New website-starter users get wrong setup/auth/deploy instructions, causing broken first-run or leaked default tokens.

role: gitignore template for generated website-starter projects (renamed to .gitignore)
description: Standard Next.js ignore list plus Barkpark-specific entries (.barkpark, .barkpark-codegen); stored as `_gitignore` in the template source to avoid interfering with the barkpark repo's own git tooling, renamed on scaffold.
whatBreaks: Generated projects could commit node_modules/.env/build artifacts or codegen caches.

role: Example About page for the website-starter template
description: Server component fetching a 'page' doc by id 'about' from Barkpark and rendering title/subtitle/PortableText body, with generateMetadata via barkparkMetadata; demonstrates the fetch pattern for generated sites.
whatBreaks: Generated site's About page would fail to render or show incorrect SEO metadata; low blast radius since it's example/scaffold code.

role: Revalidation webhook route example for website-starter template
description: Wires @barkpark/nextjs's createWebhookHandler to revalidateBarkpark, forced dynamic/nodejs runtime; the template's reference implementation of the Studio→Next.js cache-revalidation contract (HMAC-signed).
whatBreaks: Generated sites wouldn't receive real-time cache invalidation from Barkpark Studio mutations, serving stale content.

role: Server Action for the website-starter contact form example
description: Validates and submits a contact form via @barkpark/nextjs's defineActions().createDoc, creating a 'contact' document; example of the typed server-action mutation pattern.
whatBreaks: Generated site's contact form would silently fail to save submissions or show wrong validation/error messages.

role: Client component rendering the website-starter contact form
description: Uses useActionState with submitContact to build an accessible contact form (name/email/message) with a persistent aria-live status region for submit feedback.
whatBreaks: Generated site's contact form UI would be broken or inaccessible to screen-reader users on submit.

role: Next.js App Router error boundary for the website-starter template
description: Client component that catches render/runtime errors in this route segment and offers a 'Try again' retry button calling reset(). Part of the scaffolded starter site shipped to new Barkpark Cloud projects, not the running Barkpark app itself.
whatBreaks: Scaffolded sites generated from this template would show an unstyled/broken error screen or crash instead of a graceful retry UI on render errors.

role: Global Tailwind stylesheet for the website-starter template
description: Loads Tailwind base/components/utilities layers and sets a few global rules (color-scheme, body background/text with dark mode, prose link styling). Applies to every page in generated starter sites.
whatBreaks: Generated starter sites would lose Tailwind styling entirely or have broken dark-mode/prose link colors.

role: Conditional banner shown only on the barkpark.dev hosted demo
description: Renders an amber notice ('Connected to the Barkpark hosted demo...') only when BARKPARK_API_URL starts with https://barkpark.dev, otherwise returns null; invisible on self-hosted/local installs.
whatBreaks: The hosted demo could either wrongly show/hide the disclaimer banner, mildly confusing users about whether their data persists.

role: Root layout for the website-starter Next.js template
description: Defines the HTML shell (skip link, header/nav, footer), site-wide metadata (metadataBase from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL), and mounts HostedDemoBanner; wraps every page in generated starter sites.
whatBreaks: Every page of a generated starter site would lose its nav/footer/metadata or break entirely (Next.js requires a root layout to render anything).

role: Route-level loading skeleton for the website-starter template
description: Simple animated pulse skeleton Next.js streams in while an async route segment resolves data, replacing a blank screen during navigation.
whatBreaks: Generated sites would show a blank white screen during data fetches instead of a loading skeleton; purely cosmetic.

role: Branded 404 page for the website-starter template
description: Rendered when a route calls notFound() (e.g. unknown post slug) or no route matches; replaces Next's default 404 with a styled page and a 'Back home' link.
whatBreaks: Generated sites would fall back to Next.js's unstyled default 404 page instead of a branded one.

role: Home page of the website-starter Next.js template
description: Server component that fetches the 'home' page doc and 'post' list docs via lib/barkpark's getDoc/getDocs, rendering a hero and a 'Latest posts' list linking to /posts/[slug]; the main landing page consumers see in generated starter sites.
whatBreaks: The homepage of any Barkpark-generated starter site would fail to build/render or show no content/posts list.

role: Dynamic blog post page for the website-starter template
description: Server component fetching a 'post' doc by slug via lib/barkpark's getDocBySlug, rendering title/date/excerpt and PortableText body content; also implements generateMetadata via @barkpark/nextjs's barkparkMetadata, calls notFound() on missing posts.
whatBreaks: Blog post pages in generated sites would 404 incorrectly, fail to render content, or produce wrong SEO metadata.

role: Static pricing page for the website-starter template
description: Server component fetching a 'page' doc keyed 'pricing' via lib/barkpark's getDoc, rendering title/subtitle/PortableText body; falls back to a 'run pnpm seed' message if no doc exists. Also sets metadata via barkparkMetadata.
whatBreaks: Generated sites' /pricing route would fail to render or show wrong content/metadata.

role: robots.txt generator for the website-starter template
description: Next.js MetadataRoute.Robots convention file allowing all crawlers and pointing to the sitemap, using NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL (defaults to localhost).
whatBreaks: Generated sites would serve an incorrect or missing robots.txt/sitemap reference, affecting SEO crawling only.

role: Next.js sitemap.xml generator for website-starter template
description: Uses Next.js's file-convention sitemap() export to build a MetadataRoute.Sitemap from static routes plus published `post` documents fetched via lib/barkpark's getDocs. Relies on NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL for absolute URLs in prod.
whatBreaks: Generated sites ship a broken or empty sitemap.xml, hurting SEO indexing for the deployed content site.

role: Template file that becomes the Barkpark SDK client config in generated sites
description: Instantiates createClient from @barkpark/core with projectUrl/dataset env vars and documents the optional multi-workspace scoping (BARKPARK_WORKSPACE/PROJECT) seam; `{{projectName}}` is a scaffolder placeholder substituted at project-generation time.
whatBreaks: Every generated website-starter project fails to reach the Barkpark API or scopes requests incorrectly (wrong workspace/project), breaking all content fetches for that site.

role: Template manifest declaring schemas, seed, and required env vars for website-starter
description: Consumed by the cloud provisioner/scaffolder to know which schemas to register, whether to seed demo content, and which env vars (with roles/sources) to inject when instantiating this template for a new project.
whatBreaks: Provisioning a new website-starter project mis-wires env vars or skips schema/seed setup, leaving the generated app unable to fetch or missing demo content.

role: Example override for building the API from a local barkpark checkout
description: Documented example (copy to docker-compose.override.yml) that swaps the published ghcr.io image for a local build context at ../../../../../api; purely a local-dev convenience file for template consumers.
whatBreaks: Only affects developers trying to build the API locally alongside a scaffolded site; no runtime impact since it's an .example file not used directly.

role: Local dev compose stack (Postgres + Barkpark API) for website-starter template
description: Spins up postgres:16 and the published ghcr.io/barkpark/api image with health-checked dependency ordering, giving scaffolded projects a one-command local backend.
whatBreaks: Developers using a generated website-starter project can't `docker compose up` a working local API+DB backend.

role: Server-only data-fetch helpers wrapping the Barkpark Next.js SDK for this template
description: Builds one shared barkparkFetch via createBarkparkServer, and exposes getDocs/getDoc/getDocBySlug typed helpers used by pages; comment flags a real gotcha — hand-rolling fetch instead of using barkparkFetch desyncs the cache tags used for webhook revalidation, causing silent permanent staleness.
whatBreaks: All content-rendering pages in generated sites fail to fetch data, or webhook-driven revalidation silently stops working, leaving stale content indefinitely.

role: Next.js config for the website-starter template
description: Sets serverActions body size limit and whitelists remote image hostnames (localhost, barkpark.dev) for next/image.
whatBreaks: Generated sites reject larger server action payloads (e.g. contact form uploads) or fail to render remote images outside the whitelisted hosts.

role: package.json template for scaffolded website-starter projects
description: Declares Next.js 15/React 19 deps, @barkpark/* SDK packages, and scripts (dev/build/codegen/seed); `{{packageName}}` placeholder is filled in by the scaffolder.
whatBreaks: Wrong or missing dependency versions/scripts break install, build, or the codegen/seed workflow for every project generated from this template.

role: PostCSS config enabling Tailwind + autoprefixer for the template
description: Minimal plugin list wiring tailwindcss and autoprefixer into the build pipeline for generated sites.
whatBreaks: Tailwind utility classes stop being processed and vendor prefixes are missing, breaking styling in generated sites.

role: Barkpark schema definition for the 'author' content type in this template
