description: Declares a public document schema (name/slug/bio/avatar fields) registered via barkpark.template.json's schemas list; drives the content model, Studio UI, and generated TS types for author documents.
whatBreaks: Author content can't be created/queried correctly, or codegen'd types drift from the actual schema, breaking author bylines/pages in generated sites.

role: Scaffold schema for a marketing page in the website-starter template
description: Defines a plain-object 'page' document schema (title/slug/heroImage/subtitle/body richText) that ships as boilerplate content when a user provisions a new Barkpark Cloud site from the website-starter template.
whatBreaks: New sites scaffolded from this template would get a broken or missing page content type until the user edits it themselves.

role: Scaffold schema for a blog post in the website-starter template
description: Defines the 'post' document schema (title/slug/excerpt/content/author reference/coverImage/publishedAt/tags) used as starter content for new website-starter projects; consumed by seed.ts's mutate calls.
whatBreaks: Seed script and generated site would reference fields/types that don't match, breaking the starter blog demo for new users.

role: Node script seeding demo content into a fresh Barkpark instance via mutate API
description: Standalone script (run with `pnpm seed`) that POSTs createOrReplace/publish mutations to `/v1/data/mutate/:dataset` (optionally workspace/project-scoped) to populate 2 authors, 3 pages, 3 posts as demo content for the website-starter template; reads BARKPARK_API_URL/DATASET/TOKEN/WORKSPACE/PROJECT env vars.
whatBreaks: New users following the starter-template quickstart get an empty or erroring demo site instead of seeded example content; low blast radius since it's opt-in tooling, not runtime code.

role: Tailwind CSS config for the website-starter Next.js template
description: Minimal Tailwind config scoped to app/ and components/, adding a 'brand' color extension; boilerplate shipped to users who scaffold a site from this template.
whatBreaks: Only affects styling/build of newly generated starter sites, not the Barkpark platform itself.

role: TypeScript compiler config for the website-starter Next.js template
description: Standard Next.js App Router tsconfig (strict, bundler resolution, @/* path alias) shipped as part of the scaffolded starter project, not used to build barkpark itself.
whatBreaks: Only breaks TS compilation/IDE support inside a freshly generated starter site, isolated from the main repo.

role: Unit tests for the team RBAC policy module Accounts.Authz
description: Exercises role/2, team_admin?/owner?, the total authorize/3 action table (read/launch/billing/delete_team across owner/admin/member), rank/1, and the anti-escalation can_grant?/3 plus the Accounts.add_member_as/4 context wrapper — the core permission gate for all team-scoped cloud operations.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in RBAC/anti-escalation logic could let a lower-rank member perform billing, delete-team, or role-escalation actions they shouldn't be able to.

role: Tests for the append-only team audit-trail context (record_audit/audit/list_audit_events)
description: Covers record_audit/1 validation, the atomic audit/3 wrapper (mutation+event committed or rolled back together), keyset-paginated/team-scoped list_audit_events/2 with actor preload, and DB-trigger-enforced immutability (raw UPDATE/DELETE against audit_events must be rejected).
whatBreaks: A broken atomicity or trigger guard could let audit records be silently missing, forged, or tampered with, undermining compliance/security review of team actions.

role: Test that verified email change fails-soft on billing gateway sync errors
description: Verifies that when a user's verified email change succeeds but the Stripe/billing gateway's update_customer call fails, the email swap still commits (only logged, not rolled back); uses a custom FailingUpdateGateway stub and swaps global billing config (async: false).
whatBreaks: A regression could either roll back a valid email change on transient billing-gateway errors, or silently drop the fail-soft log, both degrading account/billing consistency.

role: Security tests for confirm/change-email token flows in Accounts context
description: Covers confirmation token single-use/replay/expiry/cross-context isolation, the 6-digit change-email code with brute-force lockout, code-to-target binding, and enumeration/takeover safety when staging an already-registered email — each asserting a concrete security guard.
whatBreaks: Regressions here could allow token replay, session hijack via non-session tokens, brute-forcing the email-change code, or account-enumeration/takeover — direct account-security exposure.

role: Context tests for team invitations, membership management, and role gating
description: Covers invite_member/4 (token hashing, role ceiling on invites, duplicate/expired handling), get_live_invitation/1, accept_invitation/2, remove_member/2 (with session eviction), update_member_role/3, and the anti-escalation *_as/4 variants (admin cannot promote/demote past their rank, last-owner guards).
whatBreaks: Bugs here could let admins escalate roles to owner, remove/demote peers or owners they shouldn't be able to, or leave a team without an owner — a core multi-tenant security surface.

role: Test suite for forgot-password Accounts context flow
description: Covers request_password_reset/1 (enumeration-safe mint) and reset_password_by_token/2 (single-use consume + sign-out-everywhere), including supersede, expiry, weak-password, and malformed-token cases.
whatBreaks: A silent regression in password-reset security (token reuse, enumeration leak, or failure to revoke sessions) would ship undetected.

role: Core test suite for BarkparkCloud.Accounts (users, teams, sessions, PATs, onboarding)
description: Large, wide-ranging test file covering registration, auth, team membership, session tokens, personal access tokens (incl. ability escalation guards), onboarding status derivation, and a concurrency regression guard for email-change code brute-force lockout (FOR UPDATE row lock).
whatBreaks: Auth, team-scoping, PAT privilege escalation, or the concurrent-brute-force lockout could regress silently, exposing account-takeover or privilege-escalation vectors.

role: Test suite for ArchiveStore SigV4 S3 reader and GET /v1/archives route
description: Proves SigV4 signing against AWS known-answer vectors, XML/manifest parsing, team-scoped bucket prefixing (no cross-tenant leak), pagination via continuation tokens, and fail-closed behavior on misconfiguration/unreachable store.
whatBreaks: A broken SigV4 signer or a prefix-scoping regression could either break archive listing entirely or leak one team's server archives to another team.

role: Test suite for AutoupdateRolloutWorker Oban job (isu-w4)
description: Verifies the rollout tick: settles in-flight instances via a fake HTTP client, gates further advancement while a wave is unsettled, advances one eligible instance at a time, and contains/pauses instances that fail to settle or return 503.
whatBreaks: A broken gate could cause the autoupdate rollout to advance multiple instances simultaneously (fleet-wide bad-update blast radius) or get stuck advancing nothing.

role: Test suite for AzureCatalog normalizer (raw ARM data to neutral shape)
description: Pure fixture-fed tests proving Azure locations/VM sizes normalize into the same provider-neutral {regions, server_types} shape as HetznerCatalog, with MB→GiB conversion, price threading, and dropping of half-formed rows.
whatBreaks: Azure server-catalog listings could show wrong prices/specs or crash on malformed ARM rows, breaking the provisioning wizard's Azure catalog view.

role: Test suite for Azure FakeClient/RealClient credential verification seam
description: Covers FakeClient's dev/test verify+list_catalog behavior, and RealClient's pure request builders (OAuth2 token exchange, ARM resource/locations/SKU URLs) asserted without ever calling the network; confirms fail-closed when no http_client is configured.
whatBreaks: Malformed Azure API request shapes (wrong URL/headers/api-version) would only surface once a human points RealClient at a real tenant, risking a broken or leaking integration.

role: Test suite for Azure Retail Prices client (credential-free pricing, S7a)
description: Verifies pagination via NextPageLink, cheapest-price reduction across regions, exclusion of Spot/Low-Priority/Windows decoy SKUs, ~24h cache with serve-stale + coalesced background refresh, fail-closed degrade to cache/{} on transport errors, and price enrichment into the Azure catalog without breaking a 200 response during a pricing outage.
whatBreaks: Users could see wrong (e.g. Spot/Windows-inflated) VM prices, or a pricing-service outage could incorrectly 502 the whole provider catalog instead of degrading gracefully.

role: Test suite for Billing.HttpClient :httpc transport adapter
description: Pure-mapping tests for to_httpc/1 (charlist encoding, Content-Type extraction, TLS verify_peer + timeouts) plus injected-stub tests proving StripeGateway routes 2xx/error responses correctly; never touches the real Stripe API.
whatBreaks: A broken httpc request mapping (e.g. TLS verification disabled, wrong Content-Type handling) could break all real Stripe calls or silently weaken transport security.

role: Test suite for Billing subscription lifecycle past 'active' state
description: Covers dunning (past_due grace/lapse), cancellation (immediate/grace), recovery, webhook idempotency/signature safety, re-activation during dunning, entitlement gating, self-serve portal/cancel, and Registry suspend/resume primitives — all via StubGateway, no live Stripe.
whatBreaks: Billing state machine bugs could wrongly suspend paying customers' instances, fail to suspend non-paying ones, or double-charge/duplicate subscription rows on webhook replay.

role: Test suite for per-plan managed-instance quota enforcement + downgrade reconciler
description: Security-focused tests for barkpark_limit/1 and barkpark_limit_reached?/1 against config plan limits, un-bypassable quota backstops on all create paths (register_barkpark, register_managed_barkpark, upsert), and reconcile_plan_limit/1's reversible newest-first suspend/restore that must never cross-talk with billing-lapsed suspension.
whatBreaks: A quota bypass would let teams exceed paid instance limits for free, or a reconciler bug could wrongly restore billing-suspended instances or fail to restore paid-for capacity on upgrade.

role: Test suite for the Billing context and Stripe/Stub gateways
description: Covers gateway selection, StubGateway determinism, subscribe/checkout/webhook activation, StripeGateway request-builder shapes and real HMAC signature verification, and the admin grant_forever comp tier. Encodes the money-flow contract in detail (idempotency, one-live-sub-per-team, fail-closed webhook signature checks).
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in billing subscribe/webhook activation could silently double-charge, fail to activate paid plans, or accept forged Stripe webhooks.

role: Test suite for the free-trial-to-paid billing lifecycle
description: Verifies grant_trial/start_trial entitlement semantics, the one-trial-per-team durable ledger, trial-to-paid upgrade converting the same row (no gateway create call), and adversarial forged-webhook resistance. Uses a raising fake gateway to catch a specific regression (BILL-3) where activation would wrongly call create_subscription.
whatBreaks: A regression here could let teams re-claim trials indefinitely or let a forged webhook extend/convert a trial, undermining the billing funnel's trust boundary.

role: Test suite for content-template launch bootstrap + credential retrieval
description: Covers POST /v1/launch template validation against a known catalog, the Go worker's succeed report storing Vault-encrypted bootstrap outputs, and the owner-only GET /v1/barkparks/:id/bootstrap reveal endpoint (auth/team-scoping/404 no-leak). Also cross-checks the template catalog against the Go worker's embedded list.
whatBreaks: A broken template validation or encryption path could launch broken sites, leak plaintext secrets, or let non-owners read another team's bootstrap credentials.

role: Test: PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS prod runtime config parsing
description: Evaluates the real config/runtime.exs prod block via Config.Reader to prove PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS is comma-split/trimmed/blank-rejected, and that an unset var yields an honest empty list rather than a broken allowlist.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a release ship with a permanently-empty admin allowlist, silently disabling the daily fleet digest with no signal to operators.

role: Test suite for the CLI device-authorization login flow
description: Covers DeviceAuth start/inspect/approve/deny/poll lifecycle (single-use CAS, expiry, replay-safety), the rate limiter, the reaper's expired-row sweep, and full HTTP handshake including host-based verification_uri boxing and auth gating/429s. This is the core of bp login's two-secret device flow.
whatBreaks: A defect could let a device code be replayed to mint extra sessions, let an unauthenticated caller approve a login, or break the bp CLI login flow entirely.

role: Test suite for the per-domain DNS/TLS/serving status executor and its route
description: Exercises DomainStatus.check/2 offline via injected DNS/TLS/HTTP fakes: stage ordering/skipping, TLS certificate attribution (self-signed/expired/valid), IPv6 canonicalization, a real loopback TLS handshake test, and a drift-gated cross-surface JSON fixture shared with the Go CLI and SPA. Also covers the authenticated, team-scoped HTTP route.
whatBreaks: Wrong stage semantics could show a broken domain as healthy (or vice versa) across dashboard, CLI, and SPA, and fixture drift would silently desync three consumers of the same contract.

role: Contract test enforcing SSE event-type registry consistency
description: Asserts Events.types/0 matches a shared JSON fixture also read by the dashboard's JS harness, and source-scans lib/ to ensure every broadcast call site passes a literal registered event type (catching typos at test time instead of runtime).
whatBreaks: An unregistered or mistyped event type could crash a live broadcast at runtime or silently desync the dashboard's SSE dispatch table from the server's emitted types.

role: Test suite for the team-scoped pub/sub layer backing dashboard SSE
description: Exercises Events.subscribe/broadcast over OTP :pg directly: delivery shape, default payload, cross-team isolation, nil/blank team no-op, and auto-unsubscribe on subscriber process death (polled via an eventually/2 retry helper).
whatBreaks: A broken isolation or auto-unsubscribe guarantee could leak one team's live events to another or leave dead subscriber entries accumulating in the pg group.

role: Test suite for FailureCopy.humanize/1 error-message translation
description: Pure unit tests asserting reaper/provision jargon and Hetzner/Azure provider-error classes map to specific human-readable copy, idempotency under double-humanization, unknown-reason passthrough, and remediation/capability-gap-reason helper coverage.
whatBreaks: Wrong or non-idempotent error copy would surface confusing raw provider jargon to end users across the dashboard and CLI.

role: Test suite for the real GitHub App API client (JWT + REST builders)
description: Verifies RS256 App-JWT construction/signature, pure REST request builders (repo create, content push, webhook register), and compose paths (token exchange, installation lookup, webhook registration) driven against a transport fake — no network call ever made; also asserts fail-closed behavior with no client/credentials configured.
whatBreaks: A malformed JWT or request shape would break the GitHub App integration (repo creation, push, webhook registration) once credentials are live, likely undetected until production use.

role: Test suite for the GitHub context and its in-memory Fake client
description: Covers record_installation/connection_state/disconnect, installation id encryption at rest via Vault, cross-team isolation, the deterministic Fake client's side effects (create_repo, push_files, register_webhook idempotency), and list_repos_for/register_site_webhook higher-level flows used by gh-4 auto-registration.
whatBreaks: A regression could leak a GitHub installation across teams, store plaintext installation ids, or register duplicate/incorrect webhooks for site auto-deploy.

role: Test suite for the Oban staleness sweep worker (offline detection)
description: Drives StalenessWorker.perform/1 directly to prove the debounce gate, offline flip + single alert, idempotent backoff, subscription gating, latch re-arm on recovery, and best-effort-mail invariants (delivery failure doesn't roll back the flip; no-recipient teams flip silently). async: false because one test swaps the Mailer adapter globally.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let the health-status flip/alert pipeline silently double-alert, never alert, or roll back status on mail failure without any test catching it.

role: Test suite for the Hetzner proxy action allowlist catalog
description: Pure, DB-free tests asserting the Hetzner catalog's structural integrity: well-formed entries, unique (resource, verb) pairs, tier/method semantics, the nine read-only overview kinds served this wave, and that every :destroy entry requires the typed-name confirm echo. Also proves fetch/2 is exact-match only.
whatBreaks: Undetected drift in the allowlist catalog (e.g. a destroy entry missing its confirm guard, or a duplicate resource/verb pair) could open an unsafe or ambiguous Hetzner proxy action.

role: Test suite for the instance-API (webhook) proxy allowlist catalog
description: Pure tests verifying the instance-API catalog's two-tier (:read/:mutate, no :destroy) grammar per charter D46, uniqueness of capability ids, the eight frozen webhook capability templates, and render_path/2's placeholder substitution including SSRF/path-injection guards (traversal, query, fragment, percent-encoding, whitespace).
whatBreaks: A hole in render_path validation or a malformed catalog entry could let a crafted dataset/id value inject a path-traversal or query-string attack into the proxied webhook API call.

role: Test suite for Metrics.build/3, the health-beat time-series builder
description: Exercises the pure, total fold of health beats into the chart envelope: series mapping honesty (the -1 sentinel and absent fields become null, not zero), oldest-to-newest ordering regardless of input order, beat status thresholds, service_health roll-up from the newest beat, and totality guarantees against garbage/nil input.
whatBreaks: A charting bug (e.g. treating -1 sentinel as a real 0, or reversing series order) would silently corrupt every instance's CPU/mem/disk/load dashboards.

role: Test suite for the chat-channel half of the Notifications context
description: Covers channel credential sealing (Vault encryption), the save-time SSRF guard blocking private/metadata webhook URLs, channels_for_event/2 selection (default-on/off, explicit routing, disabled channels), the redacted settings view, and dispatch_event/3 fan-out enqueuing one Oban ChatNotificationWorker job per routed channel.
whatBreaks: A regression could leak plaintext webhook credentials, allow an SSRF-vulnerable webhook URL to be saved, or misroute/duplicate chat alert delivery.

role: Test suite for SafeUrl, the SSRF-blocking URL validator
description: Unit tests for check/1 and private_address?/1 covering literal internal hostnames, private/loopback/link-local IPv4 and IPv6 (including IPv4-mapped IPv6), non-http schemes, and that legitimate public provider URLs pass.
whatBreaks: A gap in IP-range classification (e.g. missing an IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback case) would let a webhook/notification target reach internal infrastructure or the cloud metadata endpoint — an SSRF vulnerability.

role: Test suite for the email half of the Notifications context
description: Covers EmailSettings changeset validation, event_enabled?/2 defaults, lazy auto-create idempotency, the SMTP secret encryption/masking boundary, dispatch_event/3 alert fan-out (toggle, always-send, team-members-only), transactional email always riding the platform transport regardless of per-team SMTP config, and the 10s test-send rate limit.
whatBreaks: A regression could leak SMTP secrets unmasked, mis-route transactional mail through a misconfigured team SMTP relay, or break the alert dispatch toggle so users stop receiving (or start over-receiving) email alerts.

role: Test suite for Delivery-row observability on transactional emails
description: Verifies every identity/transactional email type (invite, password-reset, verify, email-change-code) writes exactly one Delivery row with correct kind/scope (user vs team), and that a mail relay failure lands a 'failed' row with the error captured. async: false due to a global Mailer adapter swap.
whatBreaks: Silent loss of delivery observability would make it impossible to diagnose why a user never received a password-reset or invite email.

role: Test suite for the OAuth/SSO context and account-linking logic
description: Covers signed-state CSRF protection (single-use, provider-bound, tampered/expired/forged rejection), authorize-URL building for GitHub/Google, stubbed token-exchange/userinfo fetch, and the safe identity-linking precedence in Accounts.get_or_create_user_from_oauth/1 — converging same-email logins across providers/password without ever forking or taking over an account.
whatBreaks: A linking-logic bug could let an attacker take over an existing account via OAuth, fork duplicate accounts for the same person, or allow CSRF/replay of an OAuth state token.

role: Cross-surface drift gate: CP fixture vs canonical Go providers-capabilities fixture
description: Pure test asserting cloud/priv/static/__fixtures__/providers_capabilities.json is byte-identical to internal/cli/cloud/providers_capabilities.json (the Go-owned canonical contract), plus structural sanity on the parsed capability map. Prevents the SPA and bp CLI from silently diverging on which provider capabilities are claimed.
whatBreaks: If the CP copy drifts from the Go fixture, the web SPA and bp CLI would disagree on which provider capabilities exist, showing wrong gap/availability UI without any build failure.

role: Test suite for the provision-jobs queue bridging control plane to Go provisioner
description: 2023-line test covering Registry enqueue/claim/succeed/fail provision-job flows and the /v1/internal/provision-jobs/* HTTP endpoints gated by a shared WORKER token, including claim-fence staleness races.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let stale or double-claimed provision jobs slip through, silently breaking off-box Barkpark provisioning correctness.

role: Pure unit test for Deployment status transition graph legality
description: Small, no-DB ExUnit test asserting legal_transition?/2 accepts every declared edge, same-status writes, and rejects illegal/resurrecting/terminal-status transitions.
whatBreaks: An unguarded illegal transition (e.g. failed→live) could let a Deployment resurrect or skip states without this test catching it.

role: Pure unit test for preview subdomain slug/host derivation
description: Tests preview_slug_for/2 and preview_host_for/2 for DNS-safety (63-char limit, lowercase, hyphen-only), determinism, and sanitization of special characters used to build Caddy preview hosts.
whatBreaks: An invalid or non-deterministic slug could produce a broken DNS label, causing preview deploys to fail to route via Caddy.

role: Pure unit test for connected-provider (hetzner/azure) credential changeset
description: Validates Provider.changeset/2 kind grammar and per-kind credential shape gates (hetzner token vs azure 4-field JSON blob), and confirms errors attach to the virtual credential field, never the stored ciphertext.
whatBreaks: A loosened credential validation could let malformed or incomplete cloud credentials persist, breaking downstream provisioning against Hetzner/Azure.

role: Pure unit test for ProvisionJob schema kinds and resurrect bundle_ref gate
description: Asserts the 4 canonical job kinds (including resurrect), the unchanged 7-step vocabulary, and that resurrect jobs require bundle_ref while other kinds don't.
whatBreaks: Loss of the bundle_ref requirement could let a resurrect job enqueue with nothing to restore from, causing a no-op or crashing provisioner run.

role: Test suite for custom-domain attach flow (set_custom_host + attach_domain job queue)
description: 274-line DataCase test covering set_custom_host/2 normalization and cross-surface uniqueness (Site domains, other barkparks' custom_host, provisioning FQDN ghosts), the attach_domain job queue idempotency/fencing, and the TLS ask-gate domain_registered?/1.
whatBreaks: A broken uniqueness or normalization check could let two barkparks claim the same custom domain or block legitimate TLS issuance.

role: Test suite for fleet-autoupdate eligibility policy and in-flight state
description: Covers next_autoupdate_candidate/0 gating logic (behind/live/not suspended/enabled/not paused) plus in-flight query markers and the narrow policy setter used by AutoupdateRolloutWorker.
whatBreaks: A broken eligibility gate could trigger autoupdates on suspended, pinned, or already-in-flight instances, causing unwanted fleet-wide rollouts.

role: Test suite for claim-time Azure service-principal credential decryption
description: Tests resolved_azure_credentials_for_barkpark/1, mirroring the env-var resolver: newest connected provider wins, fails closed to nil when nothing connected or ciphertext undecodable.
whatBreaks: A decryption/resolution bug could hand a provisioner stale or wrong Azure credentials, or silently fail closed and block legitimate Azure provisioning.

role: Test suite for the stale-deployment-claim sweep worker and its epoch fence
description: 265-line test proving reap_stale_deployments/0 and StaleDeploymentReaper requeue stale 'building' rows under budget, fail them at budget, release stale 'pushing' claims, and never yank fresh claims — with real epoch-fenced re-claim races.
whatBreaks: A broken reaper could leave crashed deploys stuck forever or double-execute a deploy via a race between two workers on the same row.

role: Test suite for the team/barkpark-scoped encrypted secrets (env var) context
description: 342-line test covering put/list/reveal/delete env vars, partial-unique NULL≠NULL scoping, write-once refusal, most-specific-wins resolution, cross-team isolation, fail-open-on-bad-row behavior, and FK cascade on delete.
whatBreaks: A resolution or isolation bug could leak one team's secret into another team's deployment or resolve the wrong-scoped value into a live Barkpark's environment.

role: Tests for Registry staleness/health-status detection (offline flip, recovery)
description: Exercises Registry.stale_online_barkparks/1, bump_unreachable/1, mark_offline/1, record_agent_report/2 and recent_events_for_team/3 — the heartbeat/staleness state machine backing BarkparkCloud.Health.StalenessWorker. Verifies subscription-gating, offline backoff, and cross-team isolation.
whatBreaks: Instance offline detection or the recovery/latch flag could silently mis-fire, causing false outage alerts or missed real outages in the control plane.

role: Large test suite for the Registry context (core cloud control-plane model)
description: Covers Barkpark registration/upsert, provisioning subdomain/FQDN uniqueness, encrypted provider tokens, agent token mint/verify/revoke, provision/deprovision job lifecycle, deployment console/detail append, and site domain collision guards. This is the widest and most load-bearing test file in the batch, directly exercising the cloud control plane's core multi-tenant invariants.
whatBreaks: Regressions here would mean undetected breakage in tenant isolation, DNS subdomain collisions, token security, or provisioning job correctness across the whole cloud control plane.

role: Tests Registry.refresh_update_status/1 self-update check mirroring
description: Verifies that the control plane calls an instance's own /v1/admin/self-update endpoint with a decrypted admin bearer token and persists (or safely degrades) the update-state verdict, including no-admin-token and 404 pre-feature-instance paths.
whatBreaks: Update-availability status shown in the console could go stale or lie (e.g. showing an old 'behind' state after a failed check) instead of failing closed to 'unknown'.

role: Tests for Telemetry.normalize/1, the pure health-payload normalizer
description: Verifies normalize/1 maps full/partial/garbage agent health payloads into a stable envelope without ever raising, including health_checks roll-up logic and reported_at stamping from AgentEvent. Pure/no-DB, high signal-to-noise for a widely-consumed function.
whatBreaks: Malformed or partial agent telemetry could crash the console dashboard or misreport pass/fail health-check counts instead of degrading gracefully.

role: Drift tripwire test between vendored cloud templates and create-barkpark-app source
description: Asserts byte-identical equality (both directions) between cloud/priv/templates/<slug>/ and js/packages/create-barkpark-app/templates/<slug>/, ensuring the deploy-button repo output matches the local scaffold tool exactly. Points to `make cloud-templates-sync` on failure.
whatBreaks: The 'Deploy with Barkpark' button could silently push a stale/divergent app tree that no longer matches what create-barkpark-app scaffolds locally.

role: Tests for BarkparkCloud.Templates.AppFiles catalog + render transform
description: Verifies app_slugs/app_template? catalog membership and render/2's scaffold transform (stripping .tmpl, renaming _gitignore, filling {{packageName}} placeholders, slugifying names) for the deployable starter templates.
whatBreaks: A pushed repo from the deploy button could contain unfilled template placeholders or leftover .tmpl/.gitkeep artifacts, producing a broken initial app.

role: Tests for the 2FA login challenge fixed-window rate limiter
description: Verifies TwoFactorRateLimiter.check/2 allows exactly 5 attempts per 60s window, rolls over cleanly to a fresh window, isolates counters per user, and resets deterministically via an injected now_ms (no wall-clock sleeps).
whatBreaks: A broken rate limiter could allow unlimited 2FA brute-force attempts or lock out legitimate users across window boundaries.

role: Context-level tests for TOTP two-factor auth enrollment/verify/replay-guard
description: Covers enroll→confirm→verify→consume-recovery→disable/regenerate flows, encrypted-at-rest secrets, redacted inspect output, the two-phase login pending token, and the TOTP single-use replay guard (including stale-struct and ±1-tolerance-window edge cases) — a security-critical auth surface.
whatBreaks: A regressed replay guard would let an attacker reuse a captured OTP or recovery code to authenticate repeatedly, defeating two-factor auth.

role: Cross-runtime meter-vocabulary drift tripwire test (Elixir leg)
description: Pins the shared priv/static/__fixtures__/usage_meters.json meter-name set to Usage.compose/1's keys, ensuring the SPA Usage tab, `bp cloud usage` CLI, and this composer never drift apart on which meters exist.
whatBreaks: A meter added/renamed in one of the three usage-metering surfaces without the others would silently desync the CLI, SPA, and control-plane usage displays.

role: Tests for Usage.compose/1, the pure usage-envelope shaper for the console
description: Extensive coverage of the 13-meter usage envelope: fixed vocabulary, uniform shape, honest 'unmetered' degradation (never a fake zero) for flow/inventory/telemetry/seats/instances meters, ceiling/threshold rules per meter class, and total-input-never-raises behavior.
whatBreaks: The billing/usage dashboard could show fabricated zero values instead of honest 'unmetered' states, or apply wrong quota/warning thresholds, misleading customers about their plan usage.

role: Test suite for the Vercel zero-paste deploy handoff
description: Covers BarkparkCloud.Vercel's client selection/Fake context (deploy, claim code encryption, idempotent re-deploy), the Real client's pure HTTP request builders, and the router's gate ladder for POST /v1/barkparks/:id/vercel-deploy (503/404/409/422/201).
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a broken Vercel deploy flow (leaked claim codes, wrong gate ordering, or duplicate deploys) ship unnoticed.

role: Test suite for the on-demand golden-path instance VERIFY executor/route
description: Exercises BarkparkCloud.Verify's three probes (api/login/studio) via a fake HTTP transport, asserting pass/fail rules, SSRF redirect guard, total failure handling, token custody, the Go-shared probe vocabulary fixture, and the POST /v1/barkparks/:id/verify route's auth/team-scope/error states.
whatBreaks: Loosened assertions could let a probe regression (e.g. token leak, SSRF bypass, or false-green verify) reach prod undetected.

role: Test suite for the warm-pool pre-baked instance claim store
description: Covers Registry's warm-server register/claim/claim-for-retire/claim-for-refresh/reap-stale/delete logic (including race-safety and claim-fencing bp-c55), plus the /v1/internal/warm-servers/* HTTP endpoints gated by the worker token.
whatBreaks: A hole here could let the warm-pool double-assign a box or leak claims across workers, causing go-live failures or box loss.

role: Test suite for the team/barkpark-scoped env-vars HTTP surface
description: Drives GET/POST/DELETE /v1/env-vars and the provision-job claim injection seam, asserting value masking, owner/admin write-gating, write-once refusal, and cross-team isolation.
whatBreaks: A gap could let a secret env value leak in a response or a member without privilege write/delete team secrets.

role: Test suite for the go-live quota/entitlement gate ladder
description: Verifies POST /v1/go-live enforces subscription entitlement (402) before instance-count quota (403), trial auto-start behavior (dwb-13), and TOCTOU-safe concurrent launches that never 500.
whatBreaks: A regression could let teams exceed their plan's instance limit or crash under concurrent launch races instead of cleanly 403ing.

role: Test suite for the read-only Hetzner control-plane proxy
description: Large suite covering GET /v1/hetzner/overview and /catalog: full envelope shape, server-side token custody, per-kind degradation on upstream failure, pagination walking/loop-guard, admin-only authz, decrypt failure handling, Go-Elixir golden-fixture reconciliation, and a hard tripwire that no destroy-tier catalog entry is ever reachable/executable.
whatBreaks: Weakened tests could let a destructive Hetzner action become reachable through the proxy, or leak the account's API token to the browser.

role: Test suite for the console's server-side instance webhook-API proxy
description: Very large suite for /v1/barkparks/:id/api/webhooks*: explicit-route-only surface, golden relay with decrypted bearer, dataset overrides, token custody, team-scope fail-closed 404s, honest degradation states (capability_unavailable vs webhook_gone vs upstream_error), URL-reshaping input rejection, and exactly-once audit logging on mutations.
whatBreaks: A gap could let the instance admin token leak, allow cross-team access to another team's instance, or produce silent double-audit/no-audit on mutations.

role: Regression pin for the POST /v1/launch response envelope shape
description: Small focused test asserting the 201 launch response carries {"barkpark":{"id":_}} for onboarding redirect, and the 402 response carries checkout_path — both contract fields the frontend onboarding flow (A4) reads directly.
whatBreaks: A silent shape drift here would break the onboarding UI's post-launch redirect or checkout upsell without any other test catching it.

role: Test suite for the GET /v1/barkparks/:id/metrics health-series route
description: Asserts the reduced cpu/mem/disk/load metrics envelope, the -1 sentinel becoming JSON null, live/stale/absent beat status thresholds, points clamping, and auth/team-scope fail-closed 404s.
whatBreaks: A regression could make the dashboard show fabricated zero values instead of nil, or leak metrics across teams.

role: Test suite for the deployment rollback/promote control-plane route
description: Covers POST /v1/sites/:id/deployments/:dep_id/promote: minting a fresh queued production deployment pinned to the source artifact (never a pointer flip), preview-not-promotable rejection, build-in-progress conflicts, missing-build-source rejection, audit logging, SSE invalidation firing/silence rules, and 404 isolation across sites/teams.
whatBreaks: A regression could let a promote silently flip the live pointer early, double-audit, or leak deployments across sites/teams.

role: Test: provider-neutral launch (Azure/Hetzner) HTTP contract
description: Exercises POST /v1/launch across cloud providers, proving provider/region/server_type persistence, the provider_not_connected 422 gate for unverified Azure creds, and that the provision-job claim payload threads decrypted Azure creds while keeping the Hetzner claim shape byte-identical.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let Azure launches silently start jobs without valid credentials or corrupt the pinned Hetzner claim contract that the provisioner worker depends on.

role: Test: POST /v1/resurrect archive-restore HTTP contract
description: Covers creating a fresh barkpark row from a portable archive, the 4xx-at-the-button validation gates, bundle_ref resolution (explicit vs newest-archive-server-side vs 404/502 store states), and kind-isolation of the resurrect worker claim vs the provision claim.
whatBreaks: Broken coverage here risks silent data-loss bugs like resurrecting into the wrong archive, leaking a fabricated "no archives" 404 instead of a real 502, or a resurrect job being claimable by the wrong worker kind.

role: Test: on-box agent deployment runtime HTTP surface
description: Verifies GET /v1/agent/pending and the claim/transition routes are scoped strictly to the agent's own Barkpark (404 on foreign deployments), enforce epoch-fenced CAS transitions, and atomically flip a Site's current_deployment_id+port together with a live transition.
whatBreaks: A gap could let one box's agent claim or mutate another tenant's deployment, or leave a site pointing at a stale port after a live cutover.

role: Test: custom-domain attach HTTP + worker contract
description: Proves POST /v1/barkparks/:id/domain's happy path, rejection mapping (invalid/missing/taken/already_attaching), the pinned worker claim/succeed/fail roundtrip for attach_domain jobs, and RBAC/no-existence-leak posture.
whatBreaks: Without this coverage, domain attach could double-enqueue jobs, leak whether a domain belongs to another team, or desync the TLS ask-gate from actual attach state.

role: Test: GET /v1/audit route and audited-mutation invariant
description: Confirms the admin-gated audit read route and that every mutating router path is wrapped in Accounts.audit/3 (or a post-commit record_audit/1 for Stripe webhooks), stamping exactly one audit row per successful mutation and none on failure.
whatBreaks: A silent audit-wrapping regression would let sensitive team/billing actions go unlogged, undermining any later incident investigation.

role: Test: PATCH /v1/barkparks/:id/autoupdate fleet policy setter
description: Small, focused test for the team-facing autoupdate opt-out/pause/pin route, checking PATCH-merge semantics (untouched absent keys), ADMIN-only gate, and team-scope fail-closed behavior.
whatBreaks: A regression could let a non-admin change fleet autoupdate policy or accidentally clobber unrelated fields on a partial PATCH.

role: Test: billing portal/cancel HTTP surface (Stripe-free)
description: Drives POST /v1/billing/portal and password-reconfirmed POST /v1/billing/cancel plus the grace-aware launch gate through the router using a stub gateway, at zero cost against live Stripe.
whatBreaks: A break here risks letting cancellation bypass password confirmation or letting launches proceed for teams that should be in a billing grace-lockout.

role: Test: off-box builder worker HTTP surface (claim/transition/console/detail)
description: The largest file in the batch (697 lines); proves the builder routes require the shared WORKER token (not a user session, since ops are globally scoped across tenants), that claim is atomic under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so racing workers never double-claim, and that transitions are (worker, epoch)-fenced against stale writers.
whatBreaks: Losing this coverage risks cross-tenant deployment claim/observe leaks or two build workers corrupting the same deployment row under a race.

role: Test: email verification/recovery HTTP surface
description: Covers verify-email, always-200 resend-verification, enumeration-safe account/email/change, and account/email/confirm swap+lockout, reading codes back out of the Swoosh test mailbox.
whatBreaks: A regression could leak account-existence via timing/status differences or let an email change bypass confirmation, both auth-security-relevant.

role: Test: GitHub repo import/connect HTTP surface
description: Fake-backed end-to-end test of GET /v1/github/repos and POST /v1/sites/:id/github/connect, proving exactly one webhook is registered with correct url/secret/events, signed pushes to the linked branch enqueue a Deployment (wrong branch/bad signature do not), plus RBAC and cross-team isolation; async:false because it toggles global GitHub app config.
whatBreaks: A gap here could let deployments trigger from unsigned or wrong-branch pushes, or double-register webhooks on reconnect.

role: HTTP test for GitHub App connect/disconnect endpoints
description: Fake-backed Plug.Test suite covering GET/POST/DELETE /v1/github/installation(s): connect/disconnect state, cross-team isolation, no-leak reads, RBAC gate, and the 503 feature_not_configured path when App credentials are absent. async: false because it toggles the global BarkparkCloud.GitHub app env.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a broken or misconfigured GitHub connect flow (leaking installations across teams, or failing to gate unconfigured Apps) ship undetected.

role: HTTP test for POST /v1/github/repos (create-repo-from-template) endpoint
description: Fake-backed end-to-end test of connect -> create repo from blog-starter -> fake records created repo + pushed files -> response shape, plus every error gate (401/422 no_team/503 not-configured/409 no_installation/403 member/422 invalid_name/unknown_template). async: false, toggles GitHub app env.
whatBreaks: Bugs in repo-creation authorization or error handling (e.g. wrong role gating, missing 409 on no_installation) would ship silently, breaking the gh-3 create-repo flow.

role: HTTP test for GitHub link + inbound webhook deploy-trigger endpoints
description: Large (951-line) suite covering POST /v1/sites/:id/github (link repo/branch/secret, user-auth) and the unauthenticated POST /v1/webhooks/github/:site_id, asserting constant-time HMAC-SHA256 signature verification, 401 on bad signature, no-op 200 on non-push/wrong-branch events, and Deployment creation with git_ref = pushed sha on valid push.
whatBreaks: A broken or removed test here could hide a timing oracle in signature verification or a webhook that deploys on unauthenticated/forged requests — a security-relevant regression in the GitHub-triggered deploy pipeline.

role: HTTP test for liveness probes + agent-event/report endpoints
description: Drives GET /up, GET /health (unauthenticated), team-scoped GET /v1/barkparks/:id/events, and POST /v1/agent/report (staleness-latch re-arm), mirroring router_test.exs conventions.
whatBreaks: Health-probe or agent-report regressions (e.g. staleness latch not re-arming) could go unnoticed, causing false-down alarms or missed instance failures in fleet monitoring.

role: HTTP test for internal worker-token-gated fleet-ops endpoints
description: Covers GET/POST /v1/internal/barkparks (cross-team list, adopt) and POST .../deprovision (including stale-host detach mode) behind worker_token, asserting a user session token cannot access them.
whatBreaks: If worker-token gating regresses, internal fleet-management endpoints (used by `bp cloud hetzner instance`) could become reachable with a plain user token, or a legitimate worker action could silently fail across all teams.

role: HTTP test for team invitations + member RBAC endpoints
description: Covers member/invitation routes, unauthenticated accept-preview, copy-paste accept flow, and RBAC regression on billing/go-live (member now 403, admin still allowed). 410 lines, mirrors router_test.exs setup.
whatBreaks: An RBAC regression here (e.g. members regaining billing access, or broken invite accept flow) would compromise team access control or block onboarding.

role: HTTP test asserting invite creation survives mail-relay failure
description: Small, focused test that swaps the Mailer adapter for a FailingAdapter and asserts POST /v1/teams/:id/invitations still 201s with a working copy-paste accept_url even when email delivery errors — the invite persists regardless of mail relay health.
whatBreaks: If this fail-soft guard regresses, a down mail relay could start hard-failing team invitations instead of gracefully falling back to the copy-paste link.

role: HTTP test pinning the POST /v1/launch response contract for the SPA
description: Asserts the exact JSON shapes (201 barkpark row, 402 no_active_subscription+checkout_path, 403 limit_reached+upgrade_path) that the /new SPA parses to drive its launch flow, since the SPA itself isn't browser-tested here.
whatBreaks: Any drift in the /v1/launch response contract (status codes or field names) would silently break the SPA's launch/trial/paywall UI without any browser test catching it.

role: HTTP test for chat-notification settings/events + SSRF/admin gates
description: Drives PUT /v1/notifications/channels + /events, the chat branch of POST /v1/notifications/test, save-time SSRF 422 validation, admin-only gating, and credential no-leak on GET /v1/notifications/settings; uses Oban.Testing to assert ChatNotificationWorker enqueue behavior.
whatBreaks: A regression could allow SSRF via unvalidated webhook URLs, leak stored chat credentials in API responses, or let non-admins alter notification channels.

role: HTTP test for email-notification settings + test-send endpoints
description: Covers GET/PUT /v1/notifications/settings and POST /v1/notifications/test: auth, credential masking, 422 validation, and the 429 rate limit on test sends.
whatBreaks: Loss of masking or rate-limit coverage here could let notification credentials leak in API responses or allow unbounded test-send spam.

role: Test: OAuth/SSO route surface for control-plane router
description: Plug.Test-driven route tests for GET /v1/auth/oauth/providers, /:provider (302 redirect w/ state), and /:provider/callback (mints session, token rides URL fragment). Uses a hermetic BarkparkCloud.OAuthStub for the token-exchange/userinfo legs.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let OAuth/SSO login bugs (broken redirects, leaked tokens, wrong provider gating) reach production undetected.

role: Test: forgot-password HTTP surface (request-reset/reset)
description: Route-level tests for POST /v1/auth/request-reset (enumeration-safe, sends email) and POST /v1/auth/reset (consumes token, sets new password), including a forwarded-TLS-header variant mirroring the Caddy front. Uses Swoosh.TestAssertions for email checks.
whatBreaks: Password-reset regressions (broken tokens, email enumeration leaks, wrong URL scheme behind Caddy) could go unnoticed, locking users out or leaking account existence.

role: Test: Personal Access Token management + PAT-authed routes
description: Covers session-only PAT management routes (GET/POST/DELETE /v1/tokens) and PAT-authenticated access to selected /v1/* routes via require_user_or_pat + require_ability. Largest of the batch (306 lines), exercises auth/ability gating.
whatBreaks: Broken PAT auth/ability checks could let unauthorized API access through or lock legitimate CLI/token usage out entirely.

role: Test: GET /v1/providers/capabilities tier/capability conduit
description: Verifies the capability/tier contract shared by the SPA and bp CLI: providers map keyed by kind with tier, generic capability booleans, and a server-owned reason for every false capability (no reason-less gaps); asserts 401 with no auth.
whatBreaks: If this contract drifts, the SPA and bp CLI could show inconsistent or wrong provider capability/tier info to users.

role: Test: provider-neutral catalog/overview endpoints (Hetzner+Azure)
description: Tests GET /v1/providers/:kind/catalog and /overview returning a normalized server-type/pricing shape for both Hetzner and Azure, plus verify-before-save semantics on credential POST (bad creds never persisted). Uses FakeClient/HetznerFakeHttpClient fakes.
whatBreaks: Catalog/pricing regressions or a broken verify-before-save could let bad credentials persist or show wrong server-type/pricing data during provisioning.

role: Test: control-plane relay for instance self-update trigger
description: Covers POST /v1/barkparks/:id/self-update: relays the request to the instance's admin self-update endpoint using the stored decrypted admin token, enqueues a status-refresh Oban job, and proxies instance status codes (409/503/500/404); checks admin-only gating and cross-team 404 fail-closed.
whatBreaks: A broken relay could fail to trigger real self-updates, leak the admin token, or let non-admins/other teams trigger updates on instances they don't own.

role: Test: account session management + password change routes
description: Route tests for DELETE /v1/auth/logout, GET/DELETE /v1/account/sessions, and PUT /v1/account/password, mirroring router_test.exs's DataCase/Plug.Test setup and call helper.
whatBreaks: Session/logout/password-change bugs could leave stale sessions valid or block legitimate credential rotation.

role: Test: control-plane site-url wiring for deferred webhook activation
description: Tests POST /v1/barkparks/:id/site-url, which uses the stored per-instance admin token to LIST then PUT the bootstrap ISR-revalidation webhook active with the real site URL; covers idempotency, member-gating, cross-team 404, validation (422 blank/non-http url), and instance failure states (409/404/502).
whatBreaks: A regression could leave deployed sites without working ISR revalidation, or leak the instance admin token in a response.

role: Test: Sites + Deployments CRUD/deploy/env/domain/TLS routes
description: Largest file in the batch (529 lines); exercises the full Sites surface (create/list/get, deploy, deployments, env, domains, TLS ask) plus cross-team isolation ensuring a Site 404s (not 403) for non-owning teams.
whatBreaks: Bugs here could break site deployment flows entirely or leak site existence/data across teams.

role: Test: control-plane one-click Studio login-ticket handoff
description: Tests POST /v1/barkparks/:id/studio-link, which mints a single-use login ticket on the instance using the stored admin token and returns the handoff URL; covers cross-team 404 deny, malformed-id 404 (not 500), not-live 409, missing-token 404, and instance-failure 502.
whatBreaks: A regression could break one-click Studio login, leak the instance admin token, or leak instance existence across teams.

role: Test: team-switcher header behavior on /v1/me
description: Proves x-barkpark-team pins current_team to a membership the caller belongs to, degrading to the primary (oldest) team on absent/malformed/foreign header, and that /v1/me lists every membership for the SPA switcher.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let users pin to a team they don't belong to (auth-scope leak) or silently break the multi-team switcher UI go undetected.

role: Test: public GET /v1/templates deploy-button catalog endpoint
description: Asserts the public template catalog is unauthenticated, shapes each row for the marketing card (slug/title/env_keys/repo), never leaks secret values, and stays locked in sync with Registry.known_templates/0 (itself checked against the Go worker's embedded allowlist).
whatBreaks: Drift between the catalog and Registry.known_templates could let the deploy-button UI advertise a template the provisioning worker can't actually build, or leak secret-shaped fields.

role: Large integration test suite for the cloud control-plane JSON API router
description: 2074-line Plug.Test-driven suite covering auth/login, billing webhooks (Stripe-shaped checkout/payment events), provisioning jobs, trial exhaustion, and most other router endpoints end-to-end against a real Ecto sandbox.
whatBreaks: The single largest regression net for the cloud API router; a broken or weakened test here could let core control-plane request handling, billing activation, or provisioning correctness regress unnoticed.

role: Test: HTTP-level two-factor auth flow (login/enroll/confirm/disable)
description: Drives the two-phase login, OTP/recovery-code challenge endpoint with rate limiting, and account 2FA enroll/confirm/disable/status routes directly through the router; runs async:false because the rate limiter is a process-wide ETS singleton.
whatBreaks: A weakened test could let a 2FA bypass, unbounded OTP brute-force, or a broken enroll/confirm flow reach production undetected.

role: Test: GET /v1/barkparks/:id/usage per-instance usage meters endpoint
description: 847-line suite proving the usage-meter composition (flow meters always unmetered, seats from real membership, server-side cross-dataset fetch of documents/datasets/webhooks using a vaulted admin token that never leaks into the response), honest degradation on unreachable instances, and team-scoped 404s.
whatBreaks: Could let a customer's admin token leak into an API response, or let honest-degradation regress into 500s or fabricated zero values on the usage console.

role: Test: GET /v1/usage/summary cached fleet-meter overview endpoint
description: Proves the summary route is a pure cached read with zero live instance HTTP calls, correct per-instance measured_at/meter-set selection from the latest sample, team-scoping of visible instances, and live fleet-quota meter behavior.
whatBreaks: A regression could cause the Overview dashboard to make live instance calls on every load (performance/security) or leak another team's instance data.

role: Test: daily Oban worker pruning agent_events/agent_tokens/usage_samples
description: Backdates rows to exact ages and asserts precise 14/30-day retention boundaries, cron wiring (daily on maintenance queue), and idempotent no-op behavior.
whatBreaks: Retention could silently stop pruning (unbounded table growth) or over-prune live/recent rows, corrupting usage/audit history.

role: Test: Oban worker delivering chat (Discord) webhook notifications
description: Covers 2xx/4xx-terminal/5xx-retry/transport-error delivery paths, the fixed backoff schedule, channel-removed no-op, and a security regression test proving the egress HTTP client disables autoredirect (closing an SSRF-via-redirect hole).
whatBreaks: Loss of the autoredirect:false guard could reopen an SSRF path to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) via a malicious 3xx redirect.

role: Test: daily digest worker behavior + recipient security
description: Covers cron wiring (schedule, uniqueness, queue), honest body/summary rendering including semver-aware latest release, and critically that only platform-admin emails ever receive the digest (non-admins and unregistered ghost addresses are excluded), plus the zero-admin no-op path.
whatBreaks: An undetected regression could leak fleet update state to non-admin users, or silently stop the daily digest from sending/rendering correctly.

role: Test: per-minute Oban worker re-pending stale claimed provision jobs
description: Verifies cron wiring (every minute, maintenance queue), stale-claim re-pending, idempotent no-op, and attempt-cap jobs being failed rather than endlessly retried.
whatBreaks: A broken reaper could leave provisioning jobs stuck forever after a worker crash, or endlessly retry jobs past their attempt budget.

role: Test: hourly Oban worker for free-trial notices and expiry teardown
description: Proves idempotent T-3/T-1 advance notices, expiry-triggered deprovision via the existing job path, the critical money-path guard that a converted/paid team's instance is never torn down, and that a trial→paid webhook cancels any in-flight teardown race.
whatBreaks: A regression could destroy a paying customer's live instance (revenue-critical failure) or fail to reclaim abandoned trial instances, wasting infra.

role: Test for the Oban usage-sampler worker (cloud-console usage caching)
description: Verifies UsageSamplerWorker caches one Usage.Sample row per checkable instance per tick, that down instances degrade meters to "unmetered" (never fake zeros) while control-plane meters stay real, that admin tokens never land in the persisted envelope, and that per-instance failures don't sink the sweep.
whatBreaks: Silent regression in usage sampling could let a broken tick fabricate usage numbers or leak admin tokens into billing data undetected.

role: Test for the create_admin Mix task's testable core
description: Exercises CreateAdmin.create_admin/3 directly against the sandboxed repo, covering happy path, slugified team names, duplicate email, reserved-slug rollback, weak password, and a NUL-byte team name guard against a Postgrex crash.
whatBreaks: A broken create_admin task could silently fail to provision the control-plane's first admin user or leave orphan users on rollback failures.

role: ETS-backed test double for the Azure Retail Pricing transport seam
description: Fakes BarkparkCloud.Azure.Pricing's HTTP transport using a public named ETS table (not a process dictionary) so background refresh tasks spawned under the GenServer can share the same programmed response queue and request log as the test process; empty queue returns :not_programmed to avoid silent 200s.
whatBreaks: Azure pricing tests could pass vacuously (never actually exercising the refresh path) or flake/crash across concurrent async tests.

role: Ecto sandbox test case template for barkpark_cloud DB tests
description: ExUnit CaseTemplate that starts/stops the Ecto SQL sandbox owner per test (mirroring api/'s Barkpark.DataCase) and provides errors_on/1 for changeset assertions; widely `use`d across cloud test files.
whatBreaks: Every DB-touching test in cloud/ would leak state across tests or fail to set up the sandbox, causing widespread flaky/false test results.

role: Fail-closed default network guard for DomainStatus tests
description: Wired in config/test.exs as the default getaddrs/tls/http implementation for BarkparkCloud.DomainStatus's outbound seams, returning {:error, :offline_guard} so tests never make real DNS/TLS/HTTP calls unless they explicitly program their own fake.
whatBreaks: Tests could silently make real network calls (network flakiness, slow CI, or accidental external side effects) instead of being hermetic.

role: Process-dictionary test double for the GitHub.Real HTTP transport
description: Fakes GitHub OAuth/App HTTP calls (token exchange etc.) via a FIFO response queue in the process dictionary, mirroring StudioLinkFakeHttpClient's design; defaults to a generic 200 {} on an empty queue so calls never crash.
whatBreaks: GitHub-integration tests could pass without exercising real request/response handling, or crash unexpectedly on unprogrammed calls.

role: Path-keyed test double for the Hetzner proxy's HTTP seam
description: Fakes the Hetzner overview fan-out (up to nine upstream paths per request) by matching requested URLs against a per-path programmed response map, defaulting to an empty 200 for unprogrammed paths; process-dictionary based, parallel-safe.
whatBreaks: Hetzner proxy tests could return wrong-shaped or default data for unprogrammed paths, masking real fan-out bugs.

role: Test double for the Billing/Notifications HTTP client seam
description: FIFO process-dictionary fake for BarkparkCloud.Billing.HttpClient, used by Notifications.Dispatcher tests to simulate delivery responses (e.g. 503 then 200) without network calls.
whatBreaks: Notification delivery/retry tests could not simulate failure/success sequences, hiding dispatcher bugs.

role: Canned OAuth IdP transport stub for hermetic auth tests
description: Models GitHub + Google OAuth token exchange and userinfo/profile responses with the same request/1 contract as the real HTTP client, letting tests override any leg via put_response/2 (process-dictionary, async-safe) to simulate failure cases like an unverified primary email.
whatBreaks: OAuth login flow tests (GitHub/Google) could not run hermetically or could mask regressions in token-exchange/email-verification handling.

role: Agent-backed, owner-keyed test double for the instance-API transport seam
description: Fakes studio-link login-ticket calls and the usage fan-out (concurrent per-dataset Task.async_stream calls) by storing state in a long-lived Agent keyed by owner pid, resolved via $callers ancestry so concurrent child-process requests are correctly attributed to the programming test; supports FIFO and path-keyed modes plus simulated delay.
whatBreaks: Concurrent usage-fan-out tests (e.g. usage_sampler_worker_test.exs) could silently serve wrong/default responses to Task children or misattribute requests, making cross-dataset aggregation and token-custody assertions vacuously pass.

role: ExUnit bootstrap for the Barkpark Cloud Elixir test suite
description: Starts ExUnit and sets the BarkparkCloud.Repo SQL sandbox to :manual mode so tests can checkout/share DB connections explicitly. Standard Phoenix boilerplate.
whatBreaks: Wrong sandbox mode would cause cross-test DB leakage or connection errors across the entire cloud test suite.

role: Regression test pinning the Cloud SPA static-file allowlist security boundary
description: Asserts real SPA assets (app.js, index.html, styleguide.html) return 200, the dev-only __preview__ harness and unlisted fixtures return 404, and the allowlist never shadows the /v1 API namespace. Guards against accidentally web-exposing dev tooling via Plug.Static's only: list.
whatBreaks: A loosened allowlist could silently ship dev-only preview harness files or private fixtures to the public internet without this test catching it.

role: CLI entrypoint for the on-box transparent health/command agent
description: Parses flags, reads the bearer token, wires disk/CPU/mem/load probes (via /proc and df) plus request-stat and health-gate probes, and runs the agent's report→poll→run loop until SIGTERM. Installed alongside a systemd unit on every provisioned box.
whatBreaks: Broken flag parsing or probes would blind the control plane to server health and stop approved remote command execution on customer boxes.

role: CLI entrypoint for the off-box nixpacks build worker (Cloud P2)
description: Parses flags/token, resolves worker id, and runs a claim→nixpacks-build→docker-save→transition loop against the control plane on a separate build host from the serving box. Supports --once for smoke/test runs.
whatBreaks: A broken builder loop stalls all Cloud deployments — queued Deployments never build or push images.

role: CLI entrypoint for the Go warm-pool/provisioning worker for Barkpark Cloud
description: Large orchestrator: wires Hetzner compute+DNS providers, mail relay, warm-pool reconcile/refresh, resurrect/deprovision/attach-domain drains, orphan sweep, and graceful shutdown, then drains provision_jobs from the Elixir control plane via WORKER_TOKEN. Closes the integration gap where /v1/launch pays but does not provision.
whatBreaks: Barkpark Cloud purchases would create billing/DB rows but never actually spin up a live server, domain, or TLS for the customer.

role: CLI entrypoint for the on-box blue/green deployment executor
description: Runs on the customer's serving box, claims pending Deployments, loads/runs containers blue/green behind Caddy, swaps the reverse-proxy upstream, drains the old container, and reports live. State recovery for the MVP is a placeholder empty LiveSites list rather than parsing the existing Caddyfile.
whatBreaks: A broken runtime executor means customer app deployments never go live or cause downtime during the blue/green swap.

role: CLI entrypoint for the per-site scale-to-zero proxy/waker binary
description: One lightweight process per site; Caddy proxies to it instead of the container directly, and it wakes the container on first request, proxies traffic, then reaps it after an idle timeout. Spawned by barkpark-runtime for sites with scale_mode="zero".
whatBreaks: Sites configured for scale-to-zero would either never wake (downtime) or never sleep (defeats the cost-saving feature) if the waker is broken.

role: TUI test pinning string-array field editing behavior in the barkpark CLI editor
description: Covers seeding the multi-line textarea from JSON string arrays, refusing to edit arrays with non-string elements, committing lines back to a typed JSON array (never a JSON-encoded string) in the mutate wire body, and mirroring into Doc.Extra for immediate re-render.
whatBreaks: A regression here could silently store array fields as stringified JSON in Postgres instead of native JSONB arrays, corrupting field types.

role: TUI implementation of bulk publish/unpublish (Studio-E3 parity) for the barkpark CLI
description: Implements space-to-mark doc rows keyed on the bare published id, ctrl+p/U to bulk publish/unpublish the marked set with per-id mutation and partial-failure reporting, and esc-to-clear-marks-first semantics matching the Studio web UI.
whatBreaks: Bulk actions could silently fail to mutate marked docs or misreport success/failure counts, diverging from Studio's bulk-action UX.

role: Tests for the TUI bulk publish/unpublish feature (mark/toggle/action/render)
description: Covers mark toggling on bare ids, partial-failure reporting during bulk publish, full-success unpublish, marked-row checkmark rendering, and esc clearing marks before navigating away.
whatBreaks: Regressions in bulk mark/publish/unpublish logic in cmd/barkpark/bulk.go could ship unnoticed.

role: Unit test for rune-aware capitalize() helper in TUI
description: Pins that capitalize() upper-cases the first rune (not byte) so multi-byte localized status labels don't corrupt into U+FFFD in the desk tree. Covers ASCII, accented, and CJK cases plus empty string.
whatBreaks: A regression to byte-based capitalization would silently corrupt non-ASCII status labels in the TUI desk tree without this test catching it.

role: Unit test guarding FieldColor swatch rendering safety in TUI
description: Proves the color field editor only paints a terminal background swatch for strict hex values, and that malformed/hostile input (e.g. shell-injection-like strings) renders plain with no escape-sequence injection risk, mirroring pdrender's fieldColorRenderer.
whatBreaks: A regression could let untrusted field values inject raw ANSI/terminal escape sequences via the color swatch, a terminal-injection security issue.

role: TUI test suite for delete (D-D) and task quick actions (claim/close)
description: Exercises the two-press delete confirm flow, task claim/close key bindings hitting the flat /v1/tasks/:id/claim|close endpoints with correct worker_id/epoch bodies, and help-bar hint gating by list type. Large, detailed parity-pin test file.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions could send malformed delete/claim/close mutations from the TUI, corrupting documents or task claim state, or leak task actions onto non-task lists.

role: Test for converting server desk structure JSON into TUI's StructureNode tree
description: Verifies fromDeskNode() correctly translates GET /v1/structure/:dataset payloads (including tiered Plugins/…Rest groups and old-server fallback) into the TUI's desk tree, skipping browser-only link nodes without dropping subtrees.
whatBreaks: A broken conversion could silently drop whole plugin/document groups from the TUI navigation tree or crash on old-server desk shapes.

role: TUI draft↔published field diff modal implementation
description: Implements the `d` key's diff view: fetches the published twin, compares against the draft editor's dirty-aware values per schema field, and renders a scrollable +/- diff modal. Non-trivial scroll-clamp math shared with rendering.
whatBreaks: Users could be shown incorrect diffs before publishing/discarding a draft, or scrolling could desync from the rendered window (dead keypresses).

role: Unit tests for the diff.go draft↔published comparison and scroll logic
description: Covers buildDiffLines correctness (changed/unchanged/dirty-aware/empty markers), openDiffView guard conditions (published doc, no twin, real twin), and a dedicated regression test for a prior scroll over-clamp bug.
whatBreaks: Without this, diff-view regressions (wrong diff content or stuck scrolling) would ship undetected to the TUI.

role: TUI tests for duplicate (y), SSE refresh focus, and discard-draft (R-R)
description: Covers the `y` duplicate-and-drill-in flow, that SSE-triggered DataStoreRefreshMsg doesn't kick focus out of the editor, and the two-press discard-draft flow including its client-side published-twin guard.
whatBreaks: Regressions could cause duplicated docs to carry stray IDs, editor focus loss on background refresh mid-edit, or accidental data loss via an unguarded discard.

role: Unit test for empty doc-list placeholder rendering
description: Small test asserting the empty-doc-list interior text differs for focused vs preview panes (focused advertises the create key, preview doesn't).
whatBreaks: Minor UX regression: an empty list could render blank or offer a create action it can't fulfill in a preview pane.

role: Tests pinning TUI editor against the live v1 document envelope shape
description: Verifies getFieldValue and saveDocument correctly read/patch the flat v1 envelope (_id, values inlined) rather than legacy id/values keys, plus raw-JSON field rendering and long-form scroll-to-field behavior for boxed fields like task claims.
whatBreaks: A mismatch with the live envelope shape would silently break saves (empty patch ID) or hide task claim data, as previously happened before normalization.

role: TUI full-screen help/key-reference overlay (`?`)
description: Defines the curated, grouped key-binding reference shown as a scrollable modal, plus its scroll-clamp and render logic; documents intent, not just bindings, and must be kept in sync when adding TUI keys.
whatBreaks: Users lose the canonical discoverability surface for the TUI's keybindings, or the help overlay's scroll could desync (dead keypresses) like the diff view once did.

role: TUI test: help overlay opens/closes and covers verbs
description: Pins that `?` opens the grouped key-reference overlay from pane/paper focus, esc closes it without disturbing focus, and every load-bearing verb has a curated help row (drift guard for new keybindings).
whatBreaks: A regression in the help overlay or a missing keybinding row would ship silently, leaving users without discoverability for shipped TUI verbs.

role: TUI revision-history modal (list + diff-vs-current)
description: Implements the `H` key's read-only history view: fetches a doc's revision list (bare id) from the API, renders a windowed/cursor-navigable list, and on enter fetches a specific revision and opens a diff modal (`- revision + current`) stacked over the list. Restore is intentionally NOT implemented here (stays in Studio/API) as a deliberate scope cut.
whatBreaks: Broken history fetching or diff building would make revision inspection in the TUI fail or show wrong/corrupted diffs, undermining trust in the audit trail.

role: TUI test: history view list + diff-vs-current pins
description: Uses an httptest server to pin that history is requested under the bare id (never drafts.<id>), and that a fetched revision's scalar content flattens into Doc.Values exactly like a live envelope.
whatBreaks: A regression could silently break history fetching (e.g. querying drafts id and 404ing) or corrupt revision-to-Doc flattening, producing wrong diffs.

role: TUI test: image field value parsing and edit/commit behavior
description: Pins parseImageValue's handling of plain URL, JSON envelope with assetId/id, and malformed JSON (degrades to raw URL string, never errors), plus that editing preserves the asset envelope unless the URL is hand-edited (which downgrades to a bare URL).
whatBreaks: Wrong parsing/commit logic could silently drop asset linkage or corrupt stored image field values when edited via the TUI.

role: TUI test: list_preview badge/meta row rendering + Studio parity
description: Pins that doc-list rows are byte-identical to legacy rendering when no list_preview is declared, and that badge/meta additions degrade gracefully (badge dropped first) under narrow pane widths.
whatBreaks: A rendering regression could silently change list row layout for undeclared schemas (backward-compat break) or overflow narrow panes.

role: Entry point for the single `barkpark`/`bp` binary (CLI + TUI router)
description: main() dispatches to the CLI (cli.Execute) when args are present, or launches the Bubble Tea TUI otherwise; runTUI() handles first-run wizard routing, logged-in-without-server short-circuit, schema loading, desk-structure build (server-canonical or client-fallback), and wires SSE live-refresh into the Bubble Tea program. This is the literal process entry point for the entire Go binary.
whatBreaks: The whole `bp`/TUI binary fails to start, mis-routes CLI vs TUI, or loses live-refresh/schema-loading — a total outage of the Go client surface.

role: TUI test: multi-line text/rich-text field editing pins
description: Pins that FieldText and legacy-string FieldRichText open a textarea editor (enter=newline, ctrl+s commit, esc cancel), while a blocks-doc rich-text projection (present in Doc.Extra, absent from Doc.Values) renders read-only and refuses to open an editor to avoid corrupting the projection with a raw string patch.
whatBreaks: A regression could let a plain-string patch overwrite a structured blocks document, corrupting rich content, or break basic multi-line editing.

role: TUI renderer: flat object-array JSON to aligned mini-table
description: Detects when a raw JSON value is an array of flat (scalar-only) objects and renders it as a column-aligned table (union of keys, width-fitted, row-clamped at 6 with '+N more'); returns ok=false for anything non-conforming so the caller falls back to pretty-printed JSON, never guessing.
whatBreaks: Malformed table rendering (misaligned columns, wrong truncation) would degrade readability of structured array fields in the TUI, though the JSON fallback limits blast radius.

role: TUI test: object-array table shape detection pins
description: Pins that homogeneous flat-object arrays render as an aligned table with correct headers/row-count, and that nested values, mixed non-object items, scalars, and empty arrays all correctly refuse (fall back to JSON).
whatBreaks: A regression could make the table renderer wrongly accept malformed data (producing garbled tables) or wrongly reject valid flat-object arrays (losing the table view).

role: TUI test: list-pane cursor navigation skips non-selectable dividers
description: Pins that dividers (author-inserted via S.divider()) are never a valid cursor rest position — j/k, pgup/pgdn, g/G, and initial pane build must all skip past leading/trailing dividers to a real item, covering the edge case of dividers at both list ends.
whatBreaks: A regression could strand the cursor on a dead divider row, making Enter/l no-ops and effectively freezing navigation in structures that lead/trail with a divider.

role: TUI adapter wiring pdrender paper renderer into Bubble Tea
description: Builds a pdrender.Theme from the TUI's styles.go palette, detects terminal color profile, and renders a selected Paper's block tree read-only in the TUI (width-capped reading column, centered). Also supplies the RefResolver/TaskResolver/ValueResolver seams (cache-only, non-blocking lookups against the loaded datastore) used by pdrender for wikilinks, task chips, and inline live values.
whatBreaks: Papers would render at wrong width/theme, or ref/task-chip/value resolution would silently break or crash the TUI paper viewer.

role: Test pinning TUI doc-list row meta to the shared preview manifest
description: Verifies rowMeta resolves the OG description from the cross-surface preview-contract fixture (mirrored from the API generator) and that it survives into rendered ANSI-stripped rows, including the no-meta degradation case for core-only manifests.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let the TUI's doc-list rows silently drift from the API/web/Studio preview-contract manifest.

role: Test suite for TUI publish/unpublish/create document flows
description: Pins ctrl+p publish (bare id, dirty-guard, no-op on published), U unpublish (optimistic flip back to drafts.), n create (no _id, server-assigned id, drill-in), esc-cancel, and editor footer publish-state rendering.
whatBreaks: Regressions would let the TUI publish/create/unpublish wrong documents, send malformed mutations, or corrupt local doc state.

role: TUI modal for picking/clearing a reference or select field's value
description: Implements the reference-field picker modal (and reused option picker for long selects): fetches candidate docs, supports type-to-filter, writes the bare published id (or option string) into dirtyValues on selection, caches ref titles for display, and renders a windowed, filterable list.
whatBreaks: Reference fields in the TUI editor would fail to pick/clear correctly, or write the wrong wire value (breaking Studio/API parity for reference content).

role: Test suite for TUI reference picker + full-text search flows
description: Pins reference-picker bare-id storage/clear/esc/windowing/type-to-filter behavior and search (/) prompt hitting the scoped search endpoint, results modal rendering, drill-in, no-match status, and help-bar hints.
whatBreaks: Regressions could silently break reference editing or search in the TUI without being caught.

role: TUI schema type aliases + list-preview/meta resolution helpers
description: Re-exports apiclient's schema/field types for TUI code, holds the caller-owned mutable `schemas` slice with findSchema lookup, and implements rowMeta/previewValue/manifestDescription for doc-list preview badges/meta, mirroring the Studio PaneBuilder's degrade-gracefully behavior.
whatBreaks: Every TUI screen that looks up a schema or renders doc-list preview info would break or show wrong/missing badges across all document types.

role: TUI full-text search modal (`/` prompt + results)
description: Opens a help-bar query input, calls the scoped search endpoint via the datastore, renders a windowed results modal with type/badge, and drills into a hit's editor by resolving its schema from `_type`. Read-path only.
whatBreaks: Search would fail silently, drill into the wrong document type, or crash on malformed hits.

role: TUI modal for switching workspace/project/dataset scope
