description: Multi-stage modal (list workspace → list project → dataset entry, with create-new sub-stages and a manual-entry fallback) that applies a new DataStore scope, reloads schemas, and rebuilds the desk/panes. Central to how the whole TUI session's tenancy context changes.
whatBreaks: Users could get stuck unable to switch scope, or the TUI could apply an inconsistent scope leaving schemas/panes out of sync with the datastore.

role: Test suite for scope selector's create-workspace/project flows
description: Pins the `n` new-workspace/new-project name-prompt flow (server-derived slug, seeded child defaults), failure-stays-on-prompt behavior, and the empty-workspaces manual-entry fallback notice.
whatBreaks: Regressions would let workspace/project creation in the TUI silently break or lose error context.

role: Test pinning the TUI status bar's three severity glyphs
description: Verifies error (red ✕), success (green ✓), and info/confirm (neutral ·) statuses render distinct glyphs and that setStatus/setStatusInfo/clearStatus keep severity flags mutually exclusive.
whatBreaks: A regression could make informational notices misleadingly render as errors across the whole TUI status bar.

role: Type aliases + presentation helpers bridging TUI to apiclient
description: Re-exports internal/apiclient's framework-free Client/Doc/WorkspaceInfo/ProjectInfo/DeskNode types under TUI-local names (DataStore, Doc, etc.) so the Bubble Tea code keeps compiling after the client was extracted into a Bubble Tea-free package; also defines DataStoreRefreshMsg (tea.Msg for live-refresh) and small presentation helpers timeAgo/statusIcon.
whatBreaks: Wrong aliasing breaks compilation across the entire TUI package or causes malformed 'Xm ago' timestamps / status glyphs everywhere docs are listed.

role: Client-side desk/structure tree builder (Sanity-style StructureBuilder) for the TUI
description: Defines the StructureNode tree and chainable builders (List/ListItem/DocumentTypeList/Document/Divider) mirroring Sanity's deskStructure, converts the server's canonical desk tree (fromDeskNode) into TUI panes, and falls back to a schema-derived desk (initRootStructure) when the server endpoint is absent — this is the core navigation model for the entire TUI sidebar.
whatBreaks: A bug here corrupts or crashes the TUI's entire navigation tree (Settings, taxonomies, filtered content lists), effectively bricking desk browsing in the Go TUI.

role: Unit test pinning initRootStructure behavior on a minimal/zero schema set
description: Verifies the client-side desk fallback renders correctly for a fresh 'clean profile' install (paper + private media pair) and doesn't panic with zero schemas; pins a known v1 wart (private schemas as Settings singletons).
whatBreaks: A regression in initRootStructure (e.g. panic on empty schemas, or private types leaking into main content list) would ship unnoticed to fresh installs.

role: Lipgloss style/color definitions for the Go TUI, sourced from semrole tokens
description: Centralizes all TUI visual styling (borders, status colors, editor field boxes, buttons) by resolving semantic roles (ok/info/warn/danger) and generated chrome tokens through internal/semrole — the CLI's seam onto design/tokens.json ensuring color parity with the SPA/Studio/task board; roleColor panics on unknown role names as a fail-fast guard.
whatBreaks: Any wrong or missing style constant either breaks compilation (used throughout the TUI's render code) or visually desyncs the TUI's colors from the rest of Barkpark's design system.

role: Generated fixture: cross-surface preview-manifest parity lock for tests
description: Auto-generated by `mix barkpark.preview.gen_parity` from Barkpark.Preview.project/3; encodes expected OG/preview manifest shapes (doc blocks + manifest fields) used to assert parity between Papers reader, web finder, Studio, and Go TUI rendering. Explicitly marked DO NOT hand-edit.
whatBreaks: If stale or hand-edited, the parity test it feeds would either false-pass (masking real cross-surface preview drift) or false-fail CI for unrelated changes.

role: Unit test for the timeAgo relative-time formatter in store.go
description: Table-driven test covering zero time, minutes/hours/days ago, and clock-skew future timestamps (clamped to 'just now').
whatBreaks: A regression in timeAgo's rounding or clamping logic would go undetected, letting negative/garbled timestamps reach the TUI.

role: Unit test pinning Unicode-aware slug generation (toSlug)
description: Verifies toSlug preserves non-ASCII letters (accented Latin, CJK, Cyrillic) rather than collapsing them to empty/lossy slugs, and correctly collapses/trims hyphens and strips pure-symbol input to empty string.
whatBreaks: A regression could silently produce empty or colliding slugs for non-Latin document titles, causing broken/duplicate URLs.

role: Unit test pinning rune-safe, display-width-aware string truncation
description: Ensures truncate() never splits a multibyte UTF-8 rune and never exceeds the requested column width budget, using Norwegian (æøå) and other multibyte test strings as the realistic case.
whatBreaks: A regression could reintroduce invalid UTF-8 output or column-overflow when truncating titles in the TUI, corrupting terminal rendering.

role: TUI document field editor: per-type edit widgets, validation, commit logic
description: Implements the whole in-terminal document editing experience — dispatches each Field type (string/text/richText/array/select/boolean/reference/datetime/color/image/number) to the right Bubble Tea widget, validates and normalizes values on commit (datetime, hex color, number finiteness, regex pattern), and syncs dirtyValues back into the in-memory Doc for immediate display. Central, feature-dense file with many documented edge-case guards (blocks-doc refusal, array non-string refusal, image assetId linkage).
whatBreaks: A bug here could corrupt saved document data (e.g. stringifying arrays, mismatched assetId links, invalid datetimes reaching the server) or make the entire in-terminal editor unusable for a field type.

role: Unit test for the FieldNumber finite-number validation guard
description: Mirrors commitFieldEdit's number-parsing guard to confirm 'inf'/'nan'/'1e999' etc. are rejected (since ParseFloat accepts them but json.Marshal later would reject), while normal finite numbers pass.
whatBreaks: A regression could let non-finite numeric strings be committed as field values, causing a later JSON marshal failure or silent data corruption when saving.

role: TUI editor save/publish mutation logic against the API
description: Implements saveDocument/publishDocument for the desk TUI, including field-type coercion (arrays as raw JSON, numbers, booleans) so patches match the schema's real JSONB types instead of silently corrupting them as strings. Encodes hard-won fixes from a live production bug (silent type flip).
whatBreaks: TUI edits could silently store wrong JSONB types (e.g. numbers/booleans as strings) or fail to save/publish documents with no visible error.

role: TUI list-pane cursor/scroll navigation helpers
description: Provides scrollToField (keeps focused editor field visible via exact line-offset math), clampToItem/movePaneCursor/jumpPaneCursor for divider-aware cursor movement, and syncPaneScroll for persisting scroll state across renders.
whatBreaks: Keyboard navigation in list panes or the editor viewport could desync, stranding the cursor off-screen or landing on non-selectable dividers.

role: TUI pane/list line-accurate rendering primitives
description: Large (1100+ line) file implementing renderListInterior, the single windowing primitive shared by focused list panes and preview panes, plus item rendering with line-accurate clipping/truncation to avoid overflow.
whatBreaks: List panes or previews could overflow their box, misrender items, or diverge visually between focused/preview rendering paths.

role: Bubbletea Update() loop for the desk TUI (message dispatch)
description: Central Update function handling key events, window resize, and DataStoreRefreshMsg (SSE-driven live refresh); refreshDocViews re-syncs panes/selected doc/focus after underlying data changes, fixing a bug where SSE refresh silently stole editor focus.
whatBreaks: Any keypress, resize, or live-refresh event could stop being handled correctly, breaking the entire TUI's responsiveness or losing editor focus after remote edits.

role: Bubbletea View() render entrypoint for the desk TUI
description: Top-level View() assembling toolbar/help bar/panes/editor/preview into the terminal frame, handling collapsed vs multi-pane (Miller columns) layout and modal overlays (selector, ref picker, search, diff, history, help).
whatBreaks: The entire TUI screen could fail to render, overflow terminal bounds, or show the wrong overlay/pane layout.

role: Core TUI model/state definitions (Pane, PaneItem, focus, model struct)
description: Defines the central `model` struct and supporting types (Pane, PaneItem, FocusTarget, layout width constants) that every other tui-*.go file operates on — the schema/state backbone of the desk TUI.
whatBreaks: Any change to these shared types breaks compilation or state consistency across the entire TUI (rendering, navigation, mutations all depend on this model).

role: TUI: field-edit lifecycle (start/commit/toggle) for the doc editor
description: Implements per-field-type editing behavior in the Go TUI's document editor: opening text/textarea/select/boolean/reference editors, validating and normalizing commits (numbers, datetimes, hex colors, patterns), array-of-strings line editing, image URL/assetId parsing, and syncing dirty values back into the in-memory doc.
whatBreaks: Field edits could silently corrupt stored values (e.g. stringified arrays, invalid colors/datetimes, broken image asset links) or refuse valid edits, directly affecting content-editing correctness in the TUI.

role: Test: finite-number guard for FieldNumber commits
description: Verifies numberFieldAccepts (mirroring commitFieldEdit's FieldNumber branch) rejects inf/nan/1e999 and accepts normal finite numbers, since json.Marshal would later reject non-finite floats.
whatBreaks: A non-finite number value (Inf/NaN) could be accepted into a numeric field and later crash or fail JSON marshaling when the mutation is sent to the server.

role: TUI: document CRUD + publish/discard + task claim/close mutations
description: Sends patch/publish/unpublish/create/duplicate/delete/discardDraft mutations to the API via the Client, with typed field coercion (arrays as raw JSON, numbers, booleans) to avoid the server's verbatim-merge patch path silently changing stored types, plus task claim/close using the CmuxWorkerID fencing identity.
whatBreaks: Saves could silently corrupt field types (e.g. storing a JSON array as a literal string), publish/unpublish could desync id/status state, or task claim/close could use the wrong worker identity causing 409 fenced_off failures across cmux panes.

role: TUI: editor viewport scroll + pane cursor navigation helpers
description: Computes exact line-offset scrolling to keep the focused editor field visible (mirroring buildEditorContent's physical line layout), and provides divider-aware pane cursor movement/scroll-offset persistence (clampToItem, movePaneCursor, jumpPaneCursor).
whatBreaks: The viewport could stop following the cursor on long forms (fields become keyboard-unreachable) or list navigation could strand the cursor on non-selectable dividers.

role: TUI: core rendering for list panes, doc editor, and previews
description: Large rendering module: line-accurate windowed list rendering (renderListInterior) shared by focused and preview panes, the full document editor content builder (buildEditorContent/renderField per field type), and preview-pane builders — all clipped so no surface can overflow the terminal frame.
whatBreaks: Rendering bugs here would corrupt or overflow the TUI display across every pane (list scrolling, field editing UI, previews), making the whole desk TUI visually broken or unusable.

role: Bubbletea Update() loop for the Go TUI
description: Handles tea.Msg dispatch (data-store refresh, key events, window resize) for the TUI model, including recomputing layout dimensions and re-syncing the open editor/pane selection after a live refresh.
whatBreaks: Wrong refresh/resize handling strands editor focus, desyncs viewport sizing, or silently drops live-doc updates across the whole TUI.

role: Bubbletea View() renderer for the Go TUI
description: Composes the terminal frame each render: toolbar, help bar, Miller-column panes, editor/preview/empty state, and overlays (selector, ref picker, search, diff, history, help), clamped to terminal width/height.
whatBreaks: Layout math errors overflow the terminal width/height or render a blank/garbled frame across every TUI screen.

role: Regression test for typed field save behavior in the TUI
description: Pins that number/boolean/array fields are sent to the API as real JSON types (not strings) on save, using an httptest server to capture the actual wire payload; guards against the schema validator rejecting stringified values.
whatBreaks: A regression reintroducing the silent-type-flip bug (numbers/booleans saved as strings) would go undetected, causing save failures or corrupted data.

role: Test pinning TUI worker identity derivation vs taskboard.CmuxWorkerID
description: Verifies workerIdentity() matches taskboard.CmuxWorkerID() both inside and outside a cmux pane, guarding against desk/hook worker-id mismatches that would cause 409 self-fencing on task claims.
whatBreaks: A drift between desk TUI and cmux-hook worker IDs would cause task claim/close conflicts (409s) between the interactive board and raw cmux panes.

role: Go-to-WASM entrypoint exposing pdrender as bpRenderTUI for the browser
description: Compiles the real internal/pdrender renderer to WASM, exposing a single JS global bpRenderTUI(blocksJSON, width, mode, themeID) that renders a PortableDoc to ANSI then converts it to self-contained HTML for the browser-based Bulldocs reader.
whatBreaks: The browser Paper reader's terminal-faithful rendering would break or diverge from the CLI's `bp paper view` output.

role: Node smoke test proving the built pdrender wasm blob actually renders
description: Loads the committed wasm loader (bp-wasm-exec.js) and the built bp-pdrender.wasm.gz exactly as the production reader does, calls bpRenderTUI on a sample doc, and asserts valid HTML output; gates CI/`make wasm` on ABI or build drift.
whatBreaks: A broken wasm build or loader ABI drift would ship silently to production and break the browser Paper reader's TUI rendering.

role: bare-metal VPS provisioning script for prod-style server deploys
description: Idempotent bash script that installs Erlang/Elixir/Go/Postgres, clones the repo, generates required prod secrets (SECRET_KEY_BASE, BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY, PREVIEW_JWT_SECRET, BARKPARK_KEK with exact byte-size constraints), builds Phoenix + the Go TUI, installs a systemd unit, opens the firewall, and optionally provisions Caddy TLS. Encodes several past-incident guardrails (DOMAIN vs IP check_origin trap, KEK byte-size bug).
whatBreaks: A fresh VPS deploy fails to boot (missing/malformed secrets), TLS/origin checks reject LiveView websockets, or systemd points at the wrong start script.

role: Canonical doc for the CD pipeline / blue-green deploy design
description: Explains the auto-deploy-on-merge pipeline (path-filtered to control plane vs content instance), zero-downtime blue/green mechanics, staging channel, maintenance-page injection, required GitHub secrets, and manual/emergency rollback procedures. Canonical-for: cd-pipeline; the single source of truth an operator reads before touching deploy scripts.
whatBreaks: Operators misconfigure secrets, mis-diagnose a stuck deploy, or perform an unsafe manual rollback because the documented procedure no longer matches the scripts.

role: From-scratch base-install script for a fresh Azure box
description: Idempotent bootstrap (apt packages, asdf/Erlang/Elixir, Go, repo clone, prod mix build) that gets a bare Azure Ubuntu image to a runnable-but-unconfigured state; invoked by the provisioner's freshen step since Azure has no warm-image snapshot substrate like Hetzner.
whatBreaks: A newly launched or resurrected Azure instance fails to become runnable (wrong Erlang/Elixir/Go pins or missing packages), stalling provisioning for that whole cloud target.

role: Nightly Hetzner warm-image snapshot bake pipeline
description: Runs on the control host under a systemd timer: checks drift vs origin/main (skipping box-irrelevant path changes), boots a bake box from the newest snapshot, fast-forwards + rebuilds + pre-runs migrations with throwaway keys (stripped before snapshotting), then snapshots and labels it so the provisioner picks it up automatically; prunes old bakes.
whatBreaks: New Hetzner instances provision from a stale or broken warm image, causing slow claim-time rebuilds or failed provisions across the fleet.

role: Documented env-var contract for the barkpark-provisioner systemd worker
description: Template/example (not real secrets) listing worker token, warm-pool sizing, DNS token, portable-archive resurrect S3/KEK credentials, and SMTP relay settings consumed by cmd/barkpark-provisioner via /etc/barkpark-provisioner.env.
whatBreaks: An operator omits or mis-sets a required var on the real box, silently disabling resurrect/mail-relay features or breaking the provisioning worker's auth.

role: Dev-only credential template for Bokbasen ONIX API integration
description: Documents the env vars (API base, OAuth token URL, client id/secret, role) needed locally to talk to Bokbasen; explicitly dev-only, never real values.
whatBreaks: A developer can't configure local Bokbasen/ONIX testing; no production impact.

role: Reference Caddy handle_errors block for the branded maintenance page
description: Serves a branded 503 + Retry-After (auto-refreshing spinner page) only on Caddy-raised errors (dial failure/timeout), never masking real app errors; mirrored/baked in by instance-deploy.sh and the Go caddyfile renderers.
whatBreaks: Manually-managed Caddyfiles show a raw 502 during restarts instead of the branded maintenance page, or a copy-paste drift breaks the auto-injection logic that greps for this exact block.

role: Control-plane (barkpark.cloud) zero-downtime blue/green deploy script
description: Run as root on barkpark-cp: pulls origin/main, builds the idle docker-compose slot, health-gates it, flips Caddy's upstream, retires the old slot, pins the provisioner's control-url to the stable public front (fixing a real port-flip lockout incident), and installs the nightly image-bake timer. Serialized via flock; every failure path aborts leaving the active slot untouched.
whatBreaks: Control-plane deploys either take downtime, ship a broken slot live, or silently strand the provisioner worker (the exact '/new froze at Starting' incident this script fixed), stalling all cloud provisioning.

role: Offline unit test for cp-deploy.sh's control-url pin logic
description: Verifies statically (grep) that the pin/sed/daemon-reload exist in cp-deploy.sh, then functionally replays the exact sed rewrite against sample systemd unit lines (space-separated, flipped-port, idempotent re-run) without touching a real server.
whatBreaks: A regression in the control-url rewrite (the fix for the provisioner lockout bug) goes undetected until it recurs in production.

role: Content-instance (e.g. guerrilla) zero-downtime blue/green deploy script
description: The core production deploy script: channel-gated (production strict ff-only main vs staging arbitrary-ref via a .staging marker), builds the idle systemd slot's build root, migrates, health-gates, arms the Caddy maintenance page, flips Caddy upstream, retires the old slot/legacy unit, builds the pdrender wasm blob, and refreshes the monitoring agent. Extensively commented with root-cause history; this is THE script CLAUDE.md's Golden Rules (clean build, systemctl restart) exist to encode.
whatBreaks: A bug here can take down or corrupt the live content API/Studio for guerrilla/prod, deploy the wrong ref to a production box, or silently strand deploys — the single highest-blast-radius script in the deploy pipeline.

role: Offline end-to-end test harness for instance-deploy.sh
description: Drives the real script against fake git/mix/systemctl/install/curl/sleep/flock binaries (real caddy for genuine validation) in a temp dir, covering slot selection both directions, unhealthy-slot abort, staging vs production channel refusal/permission, and the coalesce no-op — without touching a real server.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the production deploy script's slot-flip, channel-gating, or coalesce logic ship undetected, risking a live outage or a wrong-ref deploy to prod.

role: Monthly renewal script for the mail relay TLS cert
description: Issues/renews the Let's Encrypt cert for mail.barkpark.cloud via DNS-01 against Hetzner Cloud DNS (acme.sh), then ships it to barkpark-cp over SSH/SCP, seeds the cloud_postfix_tls docker volume, and reloads postfix. Requires a separate Hetzner DNS token from the server's own credential; retries 3x to dodge DNS-propagation vs Let's Encrypt validation races.
whatBreaks: if this script silently fails (or is run with the wrong token), the mail relay cert expires and all transactional/outbound Barkpark email delivery breaks

role: Template env file documenting SMTP_* vars for Barkpark.Mailer
description: Documents the SMTP_HOST/PORT/USERNAME/PASSWORD/VERIFY_PEER vars read by api/config/runtime.exs; without SMTP_HOST set, Swoosh falls back to the Local adapter and identity emails (verify/reset/already-registered) silently never deliver. Not itself loaded — a real deploy/smtp.env (untracked) is sourced from this shape.
whatBreaks: a wrong/missing var name here misleads whoever authors the real smtp.env, causing prod email delivery to silently no-op via the Local adapter

role: runbook for the public-read token rotation systemd timer/service
description: Describes install/validate/uninstall steps for `barkpark-rotate-public-token.{service,timer}`, which rotates the demo site's weekly public API token and can trigger a Vercel rebuild. Staged in-repo only, not auto-installed.
whatBreaks: Operator misconfigures or fails to rotate the hosted demo's public token, risking a stale/leaked token or a broken demo deploy trigger.

role: systemd unit for the on-box Barkpark monitoring/command agent
description: Runs internal/agent's compiled barkpark-agent binary, reporting health/vitals to the control plane and executing approved queued commands; reads its control URL and token path from /etc/barkpark/agent.env and agent.token, both written by the provisioner (not this checkout) so the unit itself is safely re-installable by instance-deploy.sh on every self-update.
whatBreaks: a broken ExecStart or missing EnvironmentFile stops the agent from reporting health/vitals or executing approved control-plane commands on that instance

role: systemd oneshot unit for the nightly warm-image bake job
description: Invokes /usr/local/bin/barkpark-bake-server-image (snapshot-management) with a 1hr timeout, reading /etc/barkpark-provisioner.env; installed/kept current by deploy/cp-deploy.sh. No-ops when the newest bake already matches origin/main.
whatBreaks: warm-pool instance images go stale, slowing or breaking fast-provisioning of new Barkpark Cloud instances

role: systemd timer scheduling the nightly warm-image bake at 03:37 UTC
description: Fires barkpark-image-bake.service once nightly with a randomized delay (thundering-herd avoidance) and Persistent=true to catch up after a reboot.
whatBreaks: the nightly bake job never fires (or fires at the wrong time), so warm images silently drift stale without any error signal

description: barkpark-rotate-public-token.service
barkpark-rotate-public-token.timer

role: systemd template unit for a blue/green Barkpark content-API slot
description: Instantiated as barkpark-slot@blue / barkpark-slot@green by deploy/instance-deploy.sh; runs api/start.sh with per-slot env from /opt/barkpark/.slots/%i.env (PORT + MIX_BUILD_ROOT), requiring postgresql.service. Exactly one slot is enabled at a time and host Caddy proxies to it — this is the core of Barkpark's zero-downtime deploy mechanism.
whatBreaks: a broken unit definition breaks the blue/green deploy flow entirely — new deploys can't start their slot, or both/neither slot ends up running, causing an outage or failed cutover

role: setup runbook for the Uptime Kuma status-board sidecar on the demo host
description: Explains installing Uptime Kuma via docker compose alongside barkpark.service, SSH-tunnel access, and the two monitors to configure (liveness via /api/schemas, end-to-end via /v1/data/query). Documents notification channel options and future Caddy exposure.
whatBreaks: Operator misconfigures uptime monitoring, delaying detection of a prod/demo outage; no production code path affected.

description: yml config/data file.

role: CI drift gate proving design tokens match every emitted per-surface artifact
description: Re-emits every artifact (CSS, Go literals, paper-editor mirror) from design/tokens.json in memory and byte-compares against committed files, plus a Part B cross-surface parity check (GUI CSS glyph/color tones vs TUI Go lifecycle literals must agree with tokens.lifecycle). Dependency-free Node script; failing this means the Unified Aesthetic token pipeline has drifted from generated output.
whatBreaks: a broken/weakened check.mjs lets GUI and TUI silently diverge in colors/lifecycle glyphs without CI catching it, or lets stale committed CSS/Go ship unnoticed

role: Pure OKLCH color-math compiler deriving theme slots from 3 authored colors
description: Zero-dependency deterministic module implementing sRGB↔OKLab/OKLCH conversion (Ottosson matrices transplanted from an external frick compiler), WCAG contrast, gamut chroma bisection, AA lightness-walking, and derive(theme) which resolves all ~156 theme-varying tokens.json color slots from a design/themes/*.json skin. Core of the theme-system: adding a new theme means authoring one themes/*.json, not touching this file.
whatBreaks: wrong color math here mis-derives every theme's palette across all surfaces (web, studio, TUI), and can violate AA contrast guarantees silently

role: Unit tests for the design/derive.mjs color-math compiler
description: node:test suite covering color parsing (hex/hsl/rgb), the transplanted OKLab math, AA-walk, on-accent contrast flip, serializers, and the full derive() pipeline determinism/shape. Run via `node design/derive.test.mjs`.
whatBreaks: regressions in the theme color-derivation math (e.g. contrast bugs, non-deterministic output) go undetected before shipping

role: The single-source emitter regenerating every per-surface design-token artifact
description: Reads design/tokens.json + the active theme (evergreen.json), overlays derive()'s derived color slots via a clone-and-overlay seam (structuredClone + deep-equality seam guard proving evergreen stays byte-identical to the raw tree), then emits CSS (spliced into BEGIN/END GENERATED markers) and whole generated Go files. Supports --check (default, report drift) and --write (rewrite artifacts); check.mjs imports its builders for the CI gate.
whatBreaks: a bug in the emitter propagates wrong colors/tokens into every generated CSS and Go artifact across web, studio, and TUI surfaces simultaneously

role: Frozen ledger of hand-stamped color literals exempt from tokenization
description: Per-file baseline counts of un-tokenized color literals (hex/rgb/hsl) across root.html.heex, bulldocs.html.heex, cloud app.css, and deploy.sh. design/check.mjs Part E re-counts each file and FAILS on any drift (growth or shrink) — every literal-count change must update this baseline in the same diff, making it a ratchet gate for the theme-system unification effort.
whatBreaks: A stale count makes check.mjs Part E either falsely fail CI on unrelated diffs or silently allow new un-tokenized color literals to creep back into shipped chrome.

role: Test-only second theme fixture proving N-theme emission generality
description: A synthetic {bg,ink,accent} skin living outside design/themes/ so it's never rendered into a real artifact or characterized by check.mjs Part F; used exclusively by design/theme-emit.test.mjs to prove the multi-theme emission path generalizes beyond the single shipped evergreen theme.
whatBreaks: theme-emit.test.mjs's N-theme proofs (distinct blocks, non-collapsing values, mirror de-scoping) would silently stop testing real theme-injection behavior, letting a theme-N+1 regression ship undetected.

role: Standalone static HTML proof of theme identity vs mode nesting
description: A self-contained (no dev server) HTML file demonstrating that data-bp-theme (palette identity) and data-theme (light/dark mode) are independent CSS attribute switches, and that a nested dark island inside a light page correctly re-declares its full var set. Human companion to the machine proof in design/check.mjs Part G.
whatBreaks: A human reviewer loses the visual/interactive proof of the theme-nesting cascade contract, though no automated gate depends on this file directly.

role: Sole transform generating the paper-editor CSS token mirror
description: Parses paper-surface.css token scopes (base + theme + mode) and de-scopes them into the GENERATED marker region of the standalone paper-editor bundle (styles.css), so the editor works outside the Studio host. Shared by design/emit.mjs (writer), design/check.mjs (drift gate), and scripts/paper-editor-mirror-check.sh — a single canonical implementation so all three callers agree; throws MirrorError on structural problems rather than silently skipping tokens.
whatBreaks: The standalone paper-editor bundle's colors/tokens would silently drift from or omit theme/mode scopes, breaking editor rendering outside Studio and defeating the CI drift gate that is supposed to catch exactly that.

role: Single source for the task-status glyph/tone vocabulary
description: Defines the canonical status→role mapping (open/ready/in_progress/blocked/done/cancelled), each role's glyph/spinner/label, and semantic tone colors (info/ok/warn/danger). scripts/status-manifest-check.sh regenerates CSS and gates every consuming surface (Elixir paper emitters, paper-surface CSS, eventually Go pdrender + web) against this file.
whatBreaks: Every surface rendering task status (Studio, papers, eventually TUI/web) would show wrong glyphs or colors, or the status-manifest-check.sh gate would fail across the whole repo.

role: Zero-dep test suite proving the N-theme emission + mirror-scoping contract
description: Node:test suite validating that every DOM-attribute surface (cloud, Studio, web, login, paper-surface) and every generated non-CSS surface (Go builders x4, Elixir TokensGen) correctly emits a distinct, non-collapsing block per injected theme, that evergreen stays byte-identical as themes are added, and that the paper-surface mirror de-scopes (not skips/collapses) theme-identity scopes. Uses the fixture theme to exercise a real second skin end-to-end.
whatBreaks: Regressions in multi-theme emission (theme collapse, evergreen byte drift, leaked passthrough vars) across 8+ generated surfaces would go undetected, since design/themes/ ships only evergreen and can't otherwise prove the N-theme path.

role: Second shipped theme skin — warm terracotta/amber palette
description: Authored {bg,ink,accent} HSL values per light/dark mode plus a handful of formula-override pins (reading-accent, dark surface) with documented reasons, and the standard passthrough family list. Consumed by design/emit.mjs to generate the ember variant across all token-emitting surfaces.
whatBreaks: The ember theme would render with wrong/incoherent colors (off-temperature accents, crushed near-black surface) or fail check.mjs Part F characterization checks wherever it's selected.

role: The flagship/default theme — authored intent, source of derive() parity
description: Defines Barkpark's default {bg,ink,accent} skin plus ~90 documented override pins (paper surface, status colors, callouts, chrome ramps, etc.) where the derivation formula hasn't caught up to shipped bytes. check.mjs Part F proves derive(this) reproduces design/tokens.json byte-for-byte and freezes the override count — this is the theme every other generated surface's base/fallback block is built from.
whatBreaks: The entire default visual identity of Barkpark across Studio, cloud, web, papers, CLI/TUI, and email would be wrong, and the check.mjs Part F parity gate (derive vs tokens.json) would fail repo-wide.

role: Third shipped theme skin — cool blue-slate palette
description: Authored {bg,ink,accent} HSL values per mode plus a small set of override pins (reading-accent, dark surface) with reasons, mirroring ember.json's structure. Consumed by design/emit.mjs to generate the fjord variant.
whatBreaks: The fjord theme would render with incorrect or off-temperature colors, or fail theme characterization checks when selected.

role: Single source of truth for the entire Unified Aesthetic design system
description: The canonical, hand-edited JSON defining every color role, font, type scale, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, z-index, and lifecycle/status vocabulary for Barkpark — generated into Studio CSS vars, web @theme, Go semrole/taskboard/pdrender artifacts, paper-surface.css, and email palettes by W1.2 emitters. Nothing downstream should be hand-edited; it's all regenerated from this file.
whatBreaks: A wrong or malformed value here propagates incorrect colors/spacing/typography across every surface in the system (Studio, cloud SPA, web, CLI/TUI, papers, email) simultaneously, since it is the sole upstream source for all emitters.

role: JSON Schema validating design/tokens.json's shape
description: Draft-07 JSON Schema declaring required top-level keys (color, font, type, space, radius, elevation, motion, zIndex, lifecycle) and value shapes (hslPair, hexPair, lifecycleEntry) for the unified aesthetic token source of truth. Language-neutral; per-surface emitters (CSS, Go, etc.) fan this token set out to every surface.
whatBreaks: A loosened/incorrect schema lets malformed tokens.json pass validation and propagate broken colors/spacing to every emitted surface (Studio, CLI, TUI, web, email).

role: Node script gating design/tokens.json completeness/shape
description: Dependency-free Node validator (the 'W1.1 completeness gate') that checks every token role, color format, lifecycle entry, and cross-reconciliation with internal/semrole/semrole.go, exiting non-zero with itemized errors on failure; W1.2 emitters trust its pass. Notably pins lifecycle.done's teal hex literally to prevent it silently drifting to status.ok's green.
whatBreaks: If this gate is weakened or bypassed, malformed or drifted tokens (e.g. wrong lifecycle color/role) ship silently into every emitted surface, breaking the theme-system's single-source-of-truth guarantee.

role: local dev environment launcher
description: Bash script that starts a tmux session with three panes: Claude Code, Go TUI watcher, and Phoenix API server. Handles prerequisites (air, mix compile) before attaching.
whatBreaks: Local development startup fails; developers must manually start each service.

role: local/staging Docker Compose stack for the Phoenix API + Postgres
description: Defines a `db` (postgres:17-alpine) and `api` (built from ./api) service, wiring required prod secrets (CLOAK/KEK/PREVIEW_JWT) as hard-required env vars and carefully passing BARKPARK_PLUGINS through unset-vs-empty to preserve the plugin kill-switch semantics.
whatBreaks: Docker-based local/staging environments fail to boot or silently disable all plugins / misconfigure encryption secrets.

role: placeholder note describing the (unwired) Fumadocs docs-site directory
description: Short human-tier doc stating this directory is intended for the Fumadocs app (js/docs/) to consume but the build-time wiring isn't implemented yet; only a CI-generated typedoc reference subfolder is real.
whatBreaks: Minimal — a stale note about an already-inert placeholder directory.

role: cold redirect stub pointing to the canonical adding-a-domain doc
description: Two-line stub kept only for URL stability; canonical content lives at docs/ops/adding-a-domain.md.
whatBreaks: Negligible — a dead/broken external link at worst.

description: .gitkeep

role: top-level catalog/index of all docs directories and files
description: Enumerates cards, contracts, decisions, runbooks, setup guides, cheatsheets, frozen specs, domain docs, and beta swarm docs by path, acting as the master table-of-contents referenced by the repo's routing table.
whatBreaks: Agents/humans following the doc routing table can't locate the right doc, causing wasted searches or stale/duplicate documentation.

role: Human-tier prose doc stating Barkpark's open-core/self-host stance
description: Canonical narrative for 'barkpark-philosophy' — explains open-core-first, Barkpark Cloud as an auth tunnel/paid convenience layer, and the binding promise that self-host is never hobbled (referencing decision 0004). Prose-only, no code.
whatBreaks: Nothing breaks at runtime, but stale/incorrect philosophy text misleads contributors and users about the project's open-source guarantees and Cloud's role.

description: 0002-npm-dist-tag-publish.md

role: frozen canonical reference for the entire /v1 HTTP API contract
description: Comprehensive spec covering tenancy hierarchy, auth, document envelope shape, query/get/mutate/listen (SSE) endpoints, schema endpoints, Tickets and Sheets plugin routes, error codes, legacy /api/* sunset, and rate limiting. This is the wire-contract source of truth consumed by SDKs, CLI, and Studio.
whatBreaks: Every API consumer (JS SDK, Go TUI/bp CLI, Studio, external integrators) relies on this as ground truth; drift causes silent wire-format mismatches or broken client implementations across the whole platform.

role: spec for the v1→v2 error envelope negotiation contract
description: Documents the Accept-Version header-based error shape negotiation (validation_failed reshaping only), naming the implementing module/plug and code registry, plus the (currently indefinite) sunset policy for v1.
whatBreaks: Clients or new controllers implementing error handling could diverge from the documented v1/v2 shapes, breaking validation-error rendering in Studio/SDKs/TUI.

role: Agent-tier contract doc for core-auth: users, sessions, MFA, encryption, visibility
description: Canonical reference for Barkpark.Accounts, UserSession lifecycle (hash-at-rest, expiry, idle-logout predicates unwired), TOTP MFA + recovery codes, org-wide required-MFA overlay, field encryption (AES-256-GCM via FieldCipher), and the single visibility-redaction chokepoint Envelope.render/3. Also documents the /v1/auth/* HTTP surface and that these are discovery-only (not bp-executable, since bp uses api_token not user sessions).
whatBreaks: Misdocumenting the redaction chokepoint or session/MFA rules could lead engineers to bypass Envelope.render or wire idle-logout incorrectly, leaking private/encrypted fields or breaking session security across the whole platform.

role: Agent card: auth tokens, roles, tenancy binding
description: Documents the bearer-token API-token model (SHA256 hash + permission list) and the token↔workspace tenancy binding, pointing to auth-user-sessions.md as the canonical doc for the core-auth model (accounts, sessions, MFA, field encryption).
whatBreaks: Agents/devs would misunderstand or misimplement the token/tenancy trust boundary, risking auth or scoping bugs across API and Studio.

role: Agent routing card for the bp Go CLI
description: Describes the manifest-driven verb tree, write-body construction (buildBody), dev-loop builtins, and pointers to canonical CLI references (error-exit table, HANDBOOK, manifest schema); explicitly notes docs/cli/** is path-frozen.
whatBreaks: Agents routed here for CLI work would misuse the manifest-driven dispatch or move frozen files, breaking cli.go references.

role: Agent routing card for the JS SDK monorepo
description: Disambiguates js/ (real SDK) from root sdk/ (Bulldocs ingest SDK) and root packages/client/ (deprecated), lists @barkpark/core and @barkpark/nextjs surface, and flags the root-export throw-only revalidateBarkpark trap.
whatBreaks: Consumers could import the wrong package or hit the throw-only stub in production, breaking Next.js revalidation.

description: Cell-by-cell PROVEN/FIXED/ACCEPTED matrix across register, launch, trial, provision queue, box bootstrap, webhook, studio-link, and deprovision paths, citing the specific tests that guarantee each idempotency property; a key reference for provisioning correctness review.

role: Swarm-candidate doc for Cloud team invitations/RBAC feature
description: Human-tier design doc describing a candidate feature (team invite lifecycle, member management, role gate) added entirely inside cloud/, ported from Coolify's PHP model. Documents data model, files touched, and caveats; the feature is CANDIDATE status pending judge/merge, not yet part of the mainline unless merged.
whatBreaks: Nothing breaks at runtime (it's documentation), but a stale/inaccurate doc could mislead a reviewer into merging or rejecting the invitations feature incorrectly.

role: Go module manifest for the barkpark Go binary (TUI/CLI)
description: Declares module path github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark, Go 1.25, and all direct/indirect dependencies (Azure/AWS SDKs, charmbracelet TUI stack, hcloud-go, MCP go-sdk). Governs what compiles across internal/, cmd/, and the whole Go surface.
whatBreaks: A wrong or missing dependency version breaks `go build`/`go test` for the entire TUI+CLI binary across the repo.

role: Core Agent struct: report/poll/run cycle against control plane
description: Defines the Agent type and its RunOnce/Run/RunWith loop that POSTs health reports, GETs approved commands, executes them, and POSTs results back to the cloud control plane over HTTP with bearer-token auth. Everything (HTTPClient, Runner, probes) is injected for testability; this is the heart of the barkpark-agent binary's control loop.
whatBreaks: A bug here breaks the on-box agent's entire report/command cycle, silently desyncing fleet health monitoring and remote-command execution across managed servers.

role: Unit tests for Agent report/poll/run cycle against fake control plane
description: Uses an httptest-backed fakeControlPlane to verify Agent.RunOnce/Run correctly reports, polls commands, and posts results without a live server. Protects agent.go's core loop from regressions.
whatBreaks: A weakened or broken test lets a regression in the agent's report/poll/execute cycle ship undetected to production servers.

role: Fixed 6-command allowlist and the agent's security boundary
description: Defines Command/CommandResult types and the hardcoded allowlist mapping approved command names (restart/rebuild/backup/update/doctor/logs) to fixed argv; runCommand rejects anything not on the list rather than shelling out. This IS the security policy preventing the control plane from injecting arbitrary commands onto managed boxes.
whatBreaks: A bug that lets an unapproved command name through (or mis-maps a name to the wrong argv) turns the agent into a remote-code-execution vector on every managed production server.

role: Tests pinning the agent's command allowlist to exactly six entries
description: Verifies AllowedCommands() returns exactly the six approved names and that runCommand rejects anything else, using a fakeRunner that never shells out.
whatBreaks: If this test is broken/weakened, a silent expansion of the command allowlist could ship without any automated guard, widening the agent's attack surface.

role: Gathers agent health/vitals Report payload from injected probes
description: Builds the Report struct (git commit/dirty, disk, CPU, mem, load, req/s, p95, backup status, health-gate checks) sent to /v1/agent/report; every signal is behind a nil-safe injected probe so a missing probe yields an honest -1/unknown value rather than panicking or faking data. Includes NewReqStatsProbe, a production HTTP probe hitting the instance's request-stats route.
whatBreaks: Wrong or fabricated health/vitals data would corrupt the control plane's fleet dashboard (health status, disk/CPU/backup alerts), causing missed incidents or false alarms across all managed boxes.

role: Tests for gatherReport's probe wiring and fail-soft behavior
description: Verifies git probe threading (checkout -C flag), and that gatherReport degrades gracefully (sentinel values) when individual probes are nil or error, using fake runners/probes.
whatBreaks: Regression in fail-soft probe handling could go unnoticed, letting a single failing probe crash report gathering or fabricate false health data on real servers.

role: Test for UTF-8-safe string truncation helper in agent package
description: Verifies truncate() cuts on rune boundaries (not byte boundaries) so multibyte characters like Norwegian æ don't produce invalid UTF-8 in truncated error messages.
whatBreaks: Losing this test could let a byte-boundary truncation bug reintroduce invalid UTF-8 in agent error/result messages sent to the control plane.

role: SSE live-update listener + NDJSON poll fallback for API client
description: Implements StartSSE/listenSSE (connects to Phoenix's SSE endpoint, reconnects with backoff, fires OnChange/OnLivePulse callbacks) and pollOnce (NDJSON export-based document-set hash fallback when SSE drops). This is the real-time change-detection backbone consumed by CLI/TUI live views.

role: Tests for SSE mutation-event parsing tolerance and change detection
description: Verifies listenSSE fires OnChange for both spaced ("event: mutation") and spaceless ("event:mutation") SSE frames, guarding against a proxy/server variant silently breaking live refresh.
whatBreaks: A regression here could ship an SSE parsing bug that silently drops live TUI/CLI refresh in production for a subset of server responses.

role: Framework-free HTTP client for the Phoenix API shared by TUI+CLI
description: Core apiclient.Client: builds scoped /v1/ URLs, does Query/Get/Mutate/Publish/Create/Duplicate/Search/History/Revision reads and writes, task quick-actions (claim/close/relabel), graph fetch, and workspace/project tenancy calls. Single owner of the ScopedURL scheme (@canonical marker) and the humanAPIError translator; zero Bubble Tea dependency so it drives both interactive TUI and one-shot CLI.

role: Unit test for humanAPIError's error-envelope-to-human-line translation
description: Verifies the validation-error message format, HTML/opaque-body fallback, and that a long non-ASCII fallback body is clamped on a UTF-8 rune boundary rather than corrupting output.
whatBreaks: A regression in humanAPIError (e.g. clamping mid-rune) ships invalid UTF-8 to the TUI status bar/logs undetected.

role: Test for GetConditional's body-size guard and ETag round-trip
description: Verifies GetConditional rejects oversized manifest bodies with a loud error and no partial result, and round-trips a normal small 200 body with its ETag intact.
whatBreaks: A regression allowing unbounded body reads could OOM the TUI/CLI on a malicious or huge manifest response without this test catching it.

role: Doc type: decodes v1 query envelope into the TUI/CLI document model
description: Defines the Doc struct and its custom UnmarshalJSON that normalizes the flat v1 envelope (_id, _updatedAt, _draft, flattened content fields) onto legacy-shaped fields (ID, UpdatedAt, Status, Values) consumed throughout the Go TUI/CLI; also exposes PaperBlocks, ClaimEpoch, and ContentString helpers used by paper rendering and task claiming.
whatBreaks: Every TUI screen and bp CLI command that reads a document (list, edit, task claim, paper render) would get empty IDs, wrong status, or missing field values.

role: wire-pin tests for Client.Duplicate (TUI doc copy action)
description: Tests Client.Duplicate against a fake HTTP server, pinning the wrapped result envelope shape (doc inside 'result'), verifying that title gets ' (copy)' suffix and content is copied verbatim as raw JSON so nested objects survive.
whatBreaks: Silent regressions in doc duplication — wrong envelope decoding or content truncation — go undetected until users lose nested document structure.

role: test for Go API client envelope normalization
description: Tests that the Go `Doc` type correctly deserializes the live v1 API envelope shape (underscore-prefixed `_id`, `_updatedAt`, flattened content fields) into typed fields (ID, UpdatedAt, Title, Type, Status) and a normalized Values map. Uses a real captured prod response as fixture.
whatBreaks: Regressions in Doc deserialization go undetected, causing the Go TUI/CLI to silently misread document IDs, timestamps, or field values from the API.

role: Client.Export — streams dataset NDJSON export for `bp export`
description: Implements GET /v1/data/export/:dataset, scanning NDJSON lines with a 16MB per-line buffer and invoking a callback per document; a clean EOF is success (unlike Listen's SSE where EOF means a dropped connection).
whatBreaks: bp export would fail, hang, or truncate large documents, breaking dataset backup/migration workflows.

role: Test for Export's NDJSON streaming and request shaping
description: Confirms Export skips blank lines, dispatches each document, returns nil on clean EOF, and sends the correct scoped path/type param/Accept header.
whatBreaks: A broken Export path/query construction or blank-line handling would go undetected, silently breaking `bp export` filtering.

role: test for schema listPreview parsing in LoadSchemas
description: Tests that LoadSchemas correctly parses the listPreview field from schema API responses, handling both bare string and {field, prefix} spec forms, and that malformed specs degrade gracefully to zero ListPreview rather than erroring.
whatBreaks: TUI list views show wrong or missing badge/meta fields for document types if listPreview parsing regresses silently.

role: Client.Listen — resilient SSE change-feed client for `bp listen`
description: Opens the SSE stream at /v1/data/listen/:dataset, parses event/data/id frames, and implements reconnect-with-backoff and Last-Event-ID replay so a server restart/deploy doesn't drop mutation events; strict fail-fast only on the initial connect or a mid-life 4xx.

role: Test for Listen's SSE frame parsing and ctx-cancel exit
description: Verifies Listen dispatches ordered data frames, ignores comment/keep-alive frames, and exits cleanly (nil) on context cancellation without treating it as an error.
whatBreaks: A regression in SSE frame parsing (e.g. comment frames leaking through, or ctx cancel returning an error) would go unnoticed, breaking bp listen's UX.

role: Test helpers/coverage for POST /v1/data/mutate operations
description: Provides a capture server and mutation-body parser used to assert the shape of single mutations (e.g. publish) sent by the client's write operations, guarding the mutate wire contract.
whatBreaks: Undetected drift in the mutation JSON shape (mutations array, op key, fields) would silently break creates/updates/publishes from the CLI/TUI.

role: Test for Client.PaperDoc request shape and envelope unwrap
description: Asserts PaperDoc GETs the scoped /v1/data/doc/:dataset/paper/:slug with bearer auth and perspective param, and returns the unwrapped 'result' object (not the full envelope).
whatBreaks: A broken unwrap or wrong URL would make paper rendering in the TUI receive envelope-wrapped or missing data.

role: Unit test for Client.Query perspective param wiring and env default
description: Asserts empty Perspective sends no query param (CLI/published default) while drafts/raw perspectives append correctly, and that PerspectiveFromEnv defaults to 'drafts' for unset/garbage BARKPARK_PERSPECTIVE values.
whatBreaks: A perspective-wiring regression could leak the wrong dataset view (e.g. drafts appearing where published was expected, or vice versa) undetected by tests.

role: test for API query response parsing
description: Tests that the Go API client correctly unwraps the nested {result:{documents:[]}} envelope from the query controller, plus a fallback for top-level documents. Pins a past TUI empty-lists bug regression.
whatBreaks: Regression in query response parsing goes undetected, causing the TUI to silently return empty document lists.

role: Test for Client.Search request shaping and response decode
description: Verifies Search GETs the scoped /v1/data/search/:dataset with correctly URL-encoded q, limit, and perspective params and decodes the documents array.
whatBreaks: A param-name typo or encoding bug would silently break search results in the TUI/CLI without this test catching it.

role: Schema + desk-structure fetch/parse for the Go TUI/CLI
description: Defines FieldType/Field/Schema/ListPreview/DeskNode types and LoadSchemas/LoadSchemasFor/LoadStructure, which parse GET /v1/schemas and /v1/structure responses into the TUI's form-rendering model, including tolerant decoding of validation/listPreview/filter shapes.

role: Test pinning the field-type string→FieldType mapping contract
description: Locks parseFieldType's behavior: scalar types map to editable field types, v2/non-scalar types collapse to read-only FieldRaw, and unknown types fall back to FieldString — used by both the TUI editor and codegen.
whatBreaks: A dropped or renamed case would silently mis-render a schema field (wrong widget or crash) across every editor screen using that field type.

role: Regression test: trailing-slash base URL doesn't double-slash scoped schema path
description: Guards LoadSchemasFor against a prior bug where a trailing-slash BaseURL produced a malformed "//w/..." wire path. Spins an httptest server and asserts the exact requested path.
whatBreaks: A regression reintroducing the trailing-slash double-slash bug in scoped schema URLs would go undetected, causing 404s for any CLI/API caller passing a trailing-slash base URL.

role: Unit tests for apiclient's scopedURL/ScopedURL path-building helper
description: Verifies workspace/project slugs are percent-encoded in scoped URLs, plain slugs stay byte-identical, and trailing-slash bases normalize without a doubled slash — covering both the package-level ScopedURL func and the Client method that delegates to it.
whatBreaks: Unencoded slugs with special characters or unnormalized trailing-slash bases would silently produce broken/ambiguous request paths across every scoped API call.

role: Tests for TaskClaim/TaskClaimResources/TaskRelabel fencing-epoch and conflict handling
description: Asserts TaskClaim rejects a won claim with no fencing epoch (would silently defeat CAS), TaskRelabel escapes doc ids and surfaces conflict reasons verbatim, and TaskClaimResources correctly encodes resources, omits the key when empty, and distinguishes resource_conflict/not_ready (non-error) from a missing-epoch (hard error).
whatBreaks: Broken epoch/conflict handling would let bp task claims proceed with epoch 0, defeating the CAS-based claim fencing the whole bp task workflow (and multi-agent coordination) depends on.

role: Tests for workspace/project CRUD calls in the apiclient
description: Covers CreateWorkspace, CreateProject, ListWorkspaces, ListProjects — request method/path, slug escaping, JSON body/decoding, and non-2xx error surfacing.
whatBreaks: A regression in tenancy CRUD wiring (e.g. unescaped slugs or swallowed errors) would silently break workspace/project creation flows used by bootstrap and the CLI.

role: Reusable DB-backup executor (bp cloud hetzner backup): pg_dump→gzip→S3 multipart
description: Streams a DumpSource through gzip into an ObjStore via multipart upload with no temp file, writes a JSON manifest with sha256/bytes, and implements List/Restore/Prune (retention by Keep or OlderThan). Depends only on injected DumpSource/ObjStore/RestoreSink interfaces for testability; a dirty producer Close aborts the upload instead of completing a truncated backup.
whatBreaks: A bug here could silently produce truncated or corrupted database backups, or a prune policy that deletes the wrong backups — both are catastrophic for disaster recovery on Hetzner-hosted instances.

role: Byte-level test suite for the backup package against in-memory fakes
description: Uses a fakeObjStore (bucket→key→bytes, put-method log, delete log) to prove Backup/Restore/List/Prune round-trip exactly, with no live Postgres or S3 — verifies gunzip-and-compare of stored vs original bytes and recomputed sha256.
whatBreaks: Without this suite, silent data corruption or truncation in the backup/restore pipeline could ship undetected, risking real backup integrity.

role: Server-side content bootstrap for fresh Barkpark instances (quick-setup)
description: Drives a fresh instance through workspace creation, schema upload, seed+publish, read-token mint, and ISR webhook registration via scoped admin HTTP calls, all idempotent (store-once tokens/secrets) so re-runs converge. Called by the provisioner chain after health-gate + admin-token install; marked @canonical capability:instance-content-bootstrap.
whatBreaks: A broken bootstrap step (e.g. using the flat /v1 alias instead of scoped URLs, or double-minting tokens) would land content in the wrong tenant or leave new customer instances half-provisioned/empty.

role: Tests for the bootstrap package against a stateful fake instance API
description: fakeInstance simulates workspace/schema/mutate/token/webhook endpoints (with duplicate-slug 409, mint/create counters, per-step failure injection) so Run's idempotency and error-propagation can be exercised without a live instance.
whatBreaks: Missed regressions in bootstrap idempotency (e.g. duplicate token mints or webhook creates on re-run) would surface only in production during provisioner retries.

role: Off-box build worker: claims deployments, runs nixpacks, docker-saves images
description: Barkpark Cloud's dedicated build plane — polls /v1/builder/claim, runs nixpacks + docker save via an injected CommandRunner, streams a live build console, and transitions the deployment to pushing/failed via a fenced (epoch-CAS) transition call, handing off to the box agent by clearing claim_worker/claim_epoch on success.
whatBreaks: A bug in claim/transition fencing or the nixpacks/docker invocation would break Barkpark Cloud's deploy pipeline, stalling or corrupting customer site builds.

role: Tests for the builder loop against a scripted fake control plane
description: scriptedCP simulates /v1/builder/claim, transition, and console/detail endpoints with auth checks and canned responses to exercise RunOnce's claim→build→transition cycle and error paths.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in the claim/build/transition cycle could let broken builds silently report success or leave deployments stuck.

role: Streams build narration/captions to control plane, best-effort
description: Implements buildConsole (POSTs console lines + latest-wins detail captions to the control plane per deployment) and consoleTee (mirrors build-log output line-by-line into the console with a bounded partial-line buffer). Includes secret redaction (literal secrets, Bearer tokens, bp_ tokens, env-secret patterns) and a consecutive-failure latch so a down control plane can't stall builds.
whatBreaks: A bug here could either wedge/slow every build (blocking POSTs) or leak secrets into the live build console, or silently break the deploy UI's live narration.

role: Opens/creates the per-build append-truncate log file
description: Tiny helper (var openLog, stubbable in tests) that creates parent dirs and opens the build log file for one build. Simple I/O seam.
whatBreaks: If broken, build logs fail to open and a build could error out entirely, or logs could be lost/corrupted.

role: Pure renderer for Barkpark Cloud's per-box Caddyfile
description: Renders the on-demand-TLS ask-gate block, per-Site reverse-proxy blocks (blue/green port swap), and a studio fallback, plus a branded 503 maintenance page via handle_errors. Deterministic (sorted, deduped) output; strict validDomain() input sanitization prevents Caddyfile injection from hostile/malformed customer domains. Pure in-struct-out-string, no I/O.
whatBreaks: A bad render can wedge Caddy reloads for every hosted site on a box (duplicate/invalid domain crashes the whole config load) or open a cert-issuance DoS / config-injection hole via malformed domains.

role: Unit + golden tests for the Caddyfile renderer
description: Covers determinism, domain sorting/dedup (intra- and cross-site), hostile-domain filtering, maintenance handler shape, and blue/green port swaps via golden fixtures.
whatBreaks: A regression in caddyfile.go (e.g. injection or dedup break) would ship undetected to prod hosting boxes.

role: CLI built-in commands: version, capabilities, whoami, completion
description: Implements bp's non-manifest-driven built-ins — printing version/manifest, the local-first whoami identity report (server/scope/token/cloud session), and generating bash/zsh/fish shell-completion scripts from the noun/verb manifest cache. Ships a static completionNouns list that a test enforces stays in sync with cli.go's dispatch switch.
whatBreaks: `bp whoami`, `bp capabilities`, or `bp completion` misreport the connected server/scope or omit commands from shell tab-completion, degrading CLI usability but not corrupting data.

role: Tests for bp CLI completion scripts (bash/zsh/fish) and whoami
description: Verifies generated shell-completion scripts for bash/zsh/fish contain correct structure, drift-guards that completionNouns/completionGlobals stay in sync with the real dispatch switch and flag maps, executes the bash script through a real bash to prove COMPREPLY correctness, and tests whoami's cloud-session JSON block (including token non-leak).
whatBreaks: Regressions here would let shell-completion silently drift from real CLI commands/flags, or let whoami leak a session token, without being caught.

role: Header-driven color tinting for bp cloud/hetzner CLI tables
description: Maps PROVIDER and STATUS/STATE/LIFECYCLE table columns to design-token colors (GenProviderMark, GenInstanceLifecycle→RoleColor) via lipgloss, tinting only already-padded cells so widths and color-off output stay byte-identical. Column-header-keyed, not value-keyed, to avoid value collisions.
whatBreaks: A bug could inject stray bytes into non-tty/--no-color CLI output (breaking scripts parsing bp cloud output) or mis-tint fleet status in interactive terminals.

role: Golden + structural tests for CLI table chrome tinting
description: Pins TrueColor/Ascii golden renders, proves byte-identity with color off, and verifies header/value vocabulary rules (provider marks, lifecycle role hues) for chrome_table.go.
whatBreaks: A regression in chrome_table.go's byte-identity contract for scripted/piped CLI output would go unnoticed.

role: CLI entry point: Execute() dispatches noun/verb to built-ins or manifest
description: Execute(args) is the top-level router the bp binary calls when any positional arg is present; it parses globals, resolves context, then switches on the noun to either a CLI-native built-in (version, login, task, cmux, mcp, cloud, sites, etc.) or falls through to the manifest-driven dispatcher for plugin/schema commands. Deliberately hand-rolled instead of cobra because the command tree is dynamic (built from the runtime capabilities manifest).

role: Test suite for the CLI dispatcher (Execute) and built-in commands
description: Large (2076-line) table/unit test file exercising Execute's routing, exit codes, and built-in command behavior across nouns; the primary regression guard for cli.go's dispatch logic.
whatBreaks: A broken or deleted test suite lets CLI dispatch regressions (wrong exit codes, misrouted nouns) ship silently.

role: Azure ARM service-principal credential resolution for cloud provider
description: Defines the AZURE_TENANT_ID/CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/SUBSCRIPTION_ID 4-tuple, completeness/validation checks, flag>env>stored precedence resolution (ResolveCredentials), and builds an azidentity.ClientSecretCredential with an injectable transport for offline testing.
whatBreaks: Wrong credential resolution would break all Azure provisioning (silent auth failures or wrong-tenant deploys) for every `bp cloud azure` operation.

role: Self-registers AzureProvider into the cloud.CloudProvider registry
description: init() registers the azure factory under cloud.ProviderAzure; Factory() builds an AzureProvider from stored creds + env fallback; also implements cloud.Pauser via Deallocate/Start so azure supports pause/resume parity with other providers.
whatBreaks: If registration or Pause/Resume wiring breaks, `bp cloud azure` commands (or the pause/resume capability) silently vanish or misroute to the wrong provider.

role: Test fixture: Azure 403 AuthorizationFailed delete-VM response
description: Static JSON fixture used by the azure provider's offline test suite to simulate an ARM authorization failure on VM delete, exercising error-handling paths without live Azure calls.
whatBreaks: If malformed or missing, only the specific error-path test using it would fail/be less accurate; no runtime impact.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure 404 delete response
description: Static JSON fixture simulating an Azure Resource Manager 404 'ResourceNotFound' response body, used by Azure cloud-provider test doubles to exercise idempotent-delete handling.
whatBreaks: Azure delete-idempotency tests would silently pass/fail incorrectly, masking real 404 handling bugs in the Azure client.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure 200 delete response
description: Static JSON fixture simulating a successful (200, empty body) Azure ARM delete response for use in Azure client unit tests.
whatBreaks: Successful-delete test path would not accurately represent Azure's real response shape, risking false-positive test coverage.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure NIC creation response
description: Static JSON fixture representing a successful Azure networkInterfaces PUT response (provisioningState Succeeded, private IP assigned), used to test NIC-provisioning logic in the Azure cloud client.
whatBreaks: NIC provisioning tests would not validate the real Azure response schema, letting parsing bugs in network-interface creation slip through.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure AD OIDC discovery document
description: Static JSON fixture mimicking Microsoft Entra ID's OIDC well-known configuration (token/authorization/issuer endpoints), used to test the Azure auth/token-fetch flow without hitting real Azure AD.
whatBreaks: Azure OAuth token-endpoint discovery tests would validate against a wrong or malformed shape, potentially hiding auth-flow regressions.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure async operation status
description: Minimal JSON fixture representing a completed Azure long-running-operation poll response ({status: Succeeded}), used to test the Azure client's async-operation polling loop.
whatBreaks: Async operation polling tests wouldn't exercise the real completion-detection path, risking infinite-poll or premature-success bugs going unnoticed.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure VM power-op 202 Accepted response
description: Static JSON fixture simulating a 202 Accepted response with an Azure-AsyncOperation header, used to test start/stop/restart VM power-operation handling and async polling kickoff.
whatBreaks: Power-operation (start/stop VM) tests wouldn't correctly validate async-operation header extraction, risking bugs in polling-URL parsing.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure public IP GET response (with IP assigned)
description: Static JSON fixture representing a provisioned Azure publicIPAddresses resource with an allocated IPv4 address, used to test the instance IP-lookup path.
whatBreaks: Public-IP retrieval tests would miss real-world response parsing bugs for the happy-path (IP present) case.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure public IP GET response (IP not yet assigned)
description: Static JSON fixture identical to publicip_get.json but omitting the ipAddress field, used to test polling/retry logic while Azure hasn't yet allocated an IP.
whatBreaks: Tests for the not-yet-allocated IP polling path would not catch regressions in retry/wait logic for public IP assignment.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure public IP PUT (create) response
description: Static JSON fixture representing the response to creating an Azure publicIPAddresses resource; note it shares an identical hash/content with publicip_get_noip.json, suggesting duplicated fixture data across create and no-IP-get scenarios.
whatBreaks: Public IP creation tests would not validate the real PUT response shape, risking undetected bugs in IP-resource creation parsing.

role: Test fixture: mock Azure resource group PUT response
description: Static JSON fixture representing a successful Azure resourceGroups PUT (create-or-update) response, used to test resource-group provisioning in the Azure cloud client's provisioning flow.
whatBreaks: Resource-group creation tests (the first step of Azure host provisioning) would not validate against a realistic response, risking bugs at the very start of the provisioning chain going undetected.

role: Fixture: ARM resources-list pager response for List tests
description: Canned JSON response replaying four VMs (managed+orphaned, managed+warm, unmanaged, and one in a foreign resource group) used to prove List/ListByLabel filter correctly by tag and resource group.
whatBreaks: If the fixture's tags/resource-group values drift from what the test asserts, List/ListByLabel filtering tests would false-pass or false-fail without catching real regressions.

role: Fixture: ARM Tags PATCH (UpdateAtScope) response
description: Canned response for the Tags client's Merge/Delete PATCH used by LabelServer/RemoveLabel roundtrip tests.
whatBreaks: A malformed body would break JSON decoding in the tag-lifecycle test, masking whether LabelServer/RemoveLabel actually work.

role: Fixture: AAD OAuth2 client-credentials token response
description: Fake bearer token payload the fake transport serves for every AAD token exchange, letting tests run with zero real network/credential access.
whatBreaks: If missing/malformed, azidentity's token parsing fails and every ARM-backed test in the package fails at auth, not at the intended assertion.

role: Fixture: ARM VM GET response, provisioningState=Creating
description: First step of the two-step LRO poll sequence proving Create actually polls until terminal state rather than returning on the first response.
whatBreaks: If this always returned Succeeded, TestCreate_HappyPath's poll-count assertion (>=2 hits) could pass without the poller loop actually being exercised.

role: Fixture: ARM VM GET response, provisioningState=Succeeded
description: Terminal-state response ending the Create LRO poll loop in tests; pairs with vm_get_creating.json.
whatBreaks: If it never reports Succeeded, PollUntilDone would hang/timeout, breaking the whole Create test suite.

role: Fixture: ARM VM create/update (PUT) LRO-initial response
description: Response served for BeginCreateOrUpdate on the VM, kicking off the poll sequence continued by vm_get_creating/succeeded.
whatBreaks: A wrong status/body could make the SDK's poller mis-detect LRO shape, causing Create tests to fail for reasons unrelated to actual provider logic.

role: Fixture: ARM VNet create/update (PUT) synchronous-success response
description: Response for the shared VNet+subnet idempotent ensure step in Create; already terminal (Succeeded) so the poller completes on first response.
whatBreaks: If provisioningState weren't Succeeded, the vnet poll step in Create tests could hang or misreport, blocking the whole Create happy-path test.

role: Azure ARM CloudProvider implementation (VM/VNet/PublicIP/NIC/tags lifecycle)
description: Implements cloud.CloudProvider (Create/Delete/List/IP) plus optional label capabilities against Azure Resource Manager for the fleet provisioning system, mirroring the Hetzner provider's contract; owns resource-group-per-fleet naming, orphan-safe create-with-cleanup, idempotent delete, tag-based fleet listing, and deallocate/start power actions.
whatBreaks: Azure-backed fleet provisioning (create/delete/list/tag/power boxes) breaks or silently leaks billed cloud resources (VM/NIC/PublicIP orphans) across the whole Azure hosting path.

role: Unit tests for AzureProvider (create/delete/list/tag/power/creds)
description: Exercises the full lifecycle against the fixture-replaying fake transport: happy-path create, orphan cleanup on failed IP readback, cleanup-failure error surfacing, idempotent delete, tag roundtrip, list filtering, power actions, and credential resolution precedence.
whatBreaks: Regressions in AzureProvider's create/delete/orphan-cleanup/list logic would go undetected, risking billed orphaned Azure resources or broken fleet operations in production.

role: Test-only fake HTTP transport replaying fixtures for Azure SDK tests
description: Implements policy.Transporter as a route-matching fixture player (method + URL-substring predicates, ordered fixtures for LRO poll sequences) plus shared route tables (auth/create/delete/tag/list/power) used across provider_test.go; captures request bodies so tests can assert exact payloads sent to ARM.
whatBreaks: If route matching or fixture sequencing is wrong, all Azure provider tests either false-pass (never really exercising the poll/error paths) or fail/hang for reasons unrelated to the provider code under test.

role: bp-bundle-v1 portable archive format library (cross-provider resurrect)
description: Pure library implementing the cross-provider bundle format: streams a manifest+pg_dump+media tarball+AES-256-GCM-sealed identity secrets under a stamped object-store prefix, with manifest.json written last as a completeness fence. Defines BundleManifest wire shape (PINNED, consumed by control-plane readers S14b/c/d/e), SelectIdentitySecrets (which differs from the export path by including BARKPARK_KEK per Decision D36), WriteBundle, ListBundles/NewestBundle, ReadManifest, OpenObject/OpenSecrets(WithKEK).
whatBreaks: A corrupted manifest shape or broken envelope crypto would make cross-provider instance resurrection silently fail or produce an unreadable/torn archive that the control plane can't restore from.

role: BundleStore object-storage seam + Hetzner Object Storage adapter
description: Defines the narrow 4-method BundleStore interface (PutLarge/Get/List/Delete) that bundle.go reads/writes through, plus objstoreBundleStore, a bucket-bound adapter over the Hetzner Object Storage client. Keeps the bundle library provider-agnostic so future stores (Azure Blob, local disk) can be added by implementing the interface.
whatBreaks: Wrong bucket binding or a broken adapter method would misroute or fail all real bundle reads/writes to Hetzner Object Storage without affecting the tested (fake-backed) logic.

role: Unit tests for the bp-bundle-v1 format (round-trip, KEK auth, torn uploads)
description: Exercises WriteBundle/ListBundles/ReadManifest/OpenSecrets against the in-memory fake store: pinned manifest byte shape, newest-first ordering, torn-upload skip via the manifest fence, wrong-KEK GCM auth failure, and SelectIdentitySecrets D36 behavior.
whatBreaks: A weakened or deleted test would let a manifest-shape or crypto regression in bundle.go ship undetected, silently breaking cross-provider resurrect.

role: DNSProvider seam + FakeDNS + HetznerDNS (legacy REST) implementations
description: Defines the DNSProvider interface (UpsertRecord/DeleteRecord/Resolve) for per-instance subdomain management, an in-memory FakeDNS every test runs against, and HetznerDNS, the real implementation hitting dns.hetzner.com's REST API via an injectable http.Client (auth via HETZNER_DNS_TOKEN). Also defines the shared Fqdn() helper and Record type used across the DNS seam.
whatBreaks: Broken record upsert/delete/resolve logic would misconfigure or fail to configure per-instance subdomains during provisioning/teardown on the legacy Hetzner DNS path.

role: CloudDNS: DNSProvider impl over `hcloud zone rrset` CLI (integrated Cloud DNS)
description: A third DNSProvider implementation that shells out to `hcloud zone rrset` commands instead of the legacy REST API, letting DNS share the same HCLOUD_TOKEN as compute provisioning (with an optional override Token when the DNS zone lives in a different Cloud project). Builds pure, testable argv for set-records/change-ttl/delete/list and treats a 'not found' delete as idempotent no-op.
whatBreaks: Wrong argv or a broken 'not found' idempotency check would break subdomain provisioning/teardown for boxes on the newer integrated Hetzner Cloud DNS path, or cross-project auth for the zone.

role: Unit tests for CloudDNS (hcloud zone rrset argv + behavior)
description: Asserts pure argv builders for set-records/change-ttl/delete/list, upsert/delete/resolve behavior against a recording fake runner, idempotent-delete-on-not-found, stderr surfacing on failure, and the dual-token env-injection path (HCLOUD_TOKEN override vs inherited).
whatBreaks: A weakened test would let an argv or dual-token regression in dns_cloud.go ship, causing silent DNS provisioning failures against the wrong Cloud project.

role: Unit tests for Fqdn helper, FakeDNS, and HetznerDNS (legacy REST)
description: Covers Fqdn() edge cases, FakeDNS upsert/resolve/delete round-trip and idempotency, and HetznerDNS's exact HTTP request shape (method/path/headers/body) plus find-then-delete flow, all against httptest servers so no live DNS is touched.
whatBreaks: A weakened test would let a request-shape or fake-behavior regression ship undetected, risking malformed DNS API calls in production.

role: In-memory CloudProvider + BundleStore fakes for all cloud package tests
description: FakeProvider is the reference CloudProvider every provisioning test runs against (deterministic IDs/IPs, honors every optional seam-v2 capability: labeling, catalog, archive/resurrect, decommission, adopt, audit, pause/resume) so real Hetzner/Azure impls are verified for equivalence against it. FakeBundleStore is the in-memory object store bundle tests round-trip through. Both are widely imported across the cloud package's test suite.

role: Go-live freshness check + on-box rebuild-if-behind step (dwb-17)
description: EnsureFresh runs a cheap SSH check comparing a provisioned box's git HEAD to origin/main, then (only if behind and the drift isn't box-irrelevant) triggers an on-box rebuild via apply-update.sh/deploy-rebuild.sh with remote+local timeout bounds, so warm-pool boxes never silently serve stale code. Distinguishes fail-open (in-chain go-live degrades to baked code) vs fail-closed (warm-pool refill tears down a stale box) caller policy, and narrates only when it actually intervenes.

role: Test pinning FreshenPlan's per-provider descriptor (Hetzner warm-image vs Azure base-install)
description: Small unit test asserting FreshenPlan(provider) returns the warm-image string for Hetzner, a distinct base-install-script-naming string for Azure, and defaults unknown/empty kinds to the Hetzner path.
