whatBreaks: A weakened test would let FreshenPlan drift from the actual per-provider resurrect behavior without being caught, misleading the resurrect step feed's narration.

role: Unit tests for warm-pool box freshen/rebuild logic
description: Tests EnsureFresh's decision to rebuild a warm box when its git HEAD is stale, using a narration recorder and a bareRunner to prove graceful no-op degradation when the runner lacks the hostCommandRunner capability.
whatBreaks: A bug here would let stale-freshen regressions ship silently, but only affects test coverage, not production behavior directly.

role: Core CloudProvider seam: Hetzner shell-out impl + capability interfaces
description: Defines the CloudProvider interface (Create/IP/Delete/List) and a family of optional capability interfaces (Cataloger, Archiver, Resurrector, Decommissioner, Adopter, Auditor, Pauser, label interfaces), plus HcloudProvider, the real implementation that shells out to the hcloud CLI. Also implements dynamic warm-image resolution, ssh-key resolution, and Hetzner create-fallback ladder logic; this is the load-bearing provisioning primitive every other cloud file builds on.

role: Unit tests for provider.go's pure argv builders and DefaultSpec
description: Verifies DefaultSpec env overrides and the exact hcloud CLI argv (create/ip) built without shelling out, guarding against silent flag-order or env-override regressions.
whatBreaks: Silent breakage of the hcloud argv contract could ship (e.g. wrong flag order) without test failure catching it.

role: Committed cross-surface provider capability fixture (canonical contract)
description: Declares, per provider slug (hetzner/fake/azure), which optional capabilities (catalog/archive/resurrect/decommission/adopt/audit/pause/labels) are honestly supported; is the canonical Go source that Elixir control plane and SPA mirror via a byte-drift gate, and that registry_test.go's parity test checks against actual code.
whatBreaks: A stale/wrong entry causes the CLI/SPA to render false capability claims (dead buttons or false promises) across every surface, and can desync from the drift-gated Elixir/SPA copies.

role: Provider slug→factory registry + lifecycle-verb registration + capability fixture loader
description: ProviderFor/Register resolve a provider kind to a CloudProvider; RegisterLifecycleVerbs is the second capability-detection source for hetzner/azure whose lifecycle lives in free CLI functions; LoadCapabilities decodes providers_capabilities.json. Azure self-registers from its own package to avoid an import cycle.
whatBreaks: A broken registry means `bp cloud`/provisioning cannot resolve any provider (hetzner or azure) at all, or reports wrong capabilities.

role: Unit tests for the provider registry resolution and azure import-cycle boundary
description: Asserts hetzner/fake resolve to correct concrete types, unknown providers fail loud, and azure stays unregistered in the cloud package's own test binary (proving the self-registration/import-cycle design).
whatBreaks: Regressions in registry wiring (e.g. accidental azure import cycle) could ship undetected.

role: End-to-end offline integration test: login→launch→barkparks against all fakes
description: Drives the full local→live user flow (bp login, bp launch hetzner, bp barkparks) through a fake control-plane HTTP server backed by real WarmPool.Provision logic and fakes for provider/DNS/runner/gate/registry, proving the whole chain and a fail-closed health-gate case, without touching any real cloud resource.
whatBreaks: Loss of this test would let a regression across the whole provisioning pipeline (provider→DNS→runner→gate→registry) ship without an end-to-end check.

role: RestoreExecutor: real resurrect/restore logic (create, freshen, secure, configure, content)
description: Composes cloud primitives into the full resurrect chain for a bundle-based restore: cold-creates a box, freshens it (from-scratch for azure, marker for hetzner), repoints DNS, unseals+merges identity secrets, streams db.dump+media into the box via SSH stdin feed, runs the on-box pg_restore pipeline, and tears down orphans on failure. Deliberately provider-neutral/import-cycle-free so the provisioner package adapts it.
whatBreaks: A bug here breaks disaster-recovery restores — a resurrected instance could land with wrong/missing identity secrets or corrupted/lost data.

role: Unit tests for RestoreExecutor's pure script builders
description: Pins the exact on-box restore shell script (drop/createdb/pg_restore/media/migrate/restart) and the .env identity-secrets merge script content, without needing a live box.
whatBreaks: A regression in the restore script (e.g. dropped step) could ship without test failure, silently breaking disaster recovery.

role: SSHStepRunner: executes provisioning/restore steps on a remote box over SSH
description: Implements the per-host StepRunner used by warm-pool provisioning and resurrect restore: base64-encodes commands to a temp file to avoid ssh arg-splitting and stdin-eating hazards, supports both closed-stdin Run and stdin-streaming RunFeed, plus WaitReady polling for a freshly-created box's sshd, and RunOutput for capturing script output (e.g. git version checks).
whatBreaks: Any bug breaks all remote provisioning/configuration/restore steps that touch a real box over SSH — go-lives, warm pool config, and resurrect restores all depend on this.

role: Tests for the SSH-based CaddyStep runner (warm-pool boxes)
description: Covers SSHStepRunner.WaitReady retry/timeout behaviour against a booting box (connection-refused races) and other SSH-runner step-execution paths used by the warm-pool go-live chain.
whatBreaks: A regression here lets a broken SSH readiness poll ship, causing go-live provisioning to fail or hang against real freshly-booted boxes.

role: Tests for resolving the newest available Hetzner warm-image snapshot
description: Verifies ResolveWarmImage picks the newest AVAILABLE (not still-creating) snapshot and that results are cached with a TTL, avoiding excessive Hetzner API calls.
whatBreaks: A wrong-image regression could ship undetected, causing new warm-pool/go-live boxes to boot from a stale or half-baked snapshot.

role: Core warm-pool go-live provisioner chaining assign→secrets→dns→caddy→migrate→health→register
description: The capstone provisioning engine: pops a warm host (or creates one, one-shot), mints per-instance secrets (SECRET_KEY_BASE/KEK/CloakKey/PreviewJWT/admin token), runs DNS+Caddy+secrets-install+migrate+admin-token steps over an injected StepRunner, polls a health gate with fail-closed semantics, then registers the LiveServer. Every external touchpoint (Provider/DNS/Caddy/Runner/Health/Registry/SecretGen) is an injected interface for fakeable testing; heavy inline redaction logic guards secrets from leaking into captured shell output/errors.

role: Turns an already-claimed warm host into a live instance without creating a server
description: CreateWarmServer bakes+labels a new pool box (fail-closed teardown if unlabelable); AssignWarm consumes a pre-claimed warm host via ordered label transition (stamp fqdn identity, drop warm label) then runs the shared configureHost chain, tearing down on any failure — the ≤15s go-live fast path.
whatBreaks: A bug could leave a warm box simultaneously mislabeled/orphaned (money leak) or falsely mark a box live without completing provisioning, breaking the fast go-live UX.

role: Tests for the AssignWarm fast-path go-live flow
description: Wires a fake Provider/DNS/Runner/Registry to exercise AssignWarm's identity-labeling, health-gate fail-closed teardown, and success paths.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in the warm-assign fast path could ship a provisioning bug that leaks boxes or falsely marks unhealthy instances live.

role: Large test suite for the WarmPool.Provision/ProvisionOneShot go-live chain
description: Extensive (1791-line) coverage of pool pop/refill, secret generation/validation, DNS/Caddy/migrate/admin-token step ordering, health-gate polling (retry/timeout/deadline), secret redaction in errors, and registry registration for both warm-pool and one-shot provisioning paths.
whatBreaks: A weakened or broken test suite would let real regressions in the go-live provisioning chain (including secret leaks or false-healthy registrations) reach production undetected.

role: Control-plane half of bp Cloud CLI commands (login/signup/launch/go-live/provider/subscribe)
description: Implements every authed Cloud command that talks to the Barkpark Cloud control plane via internal/cloudclient: bp login (password + device-link browser flow with auto-connect), bp signup, bp logout, bp barkparks (authoritative fleet), bp provider add, bp launch, bp go-live, bp subscribe, and bp instance credentials. Owns flag parsing, TTY-gated auto-connect/desk-offer UX, and error-code mapping (401→exitAuth, 402 no_active_subscription→actionable hint).
whatBreaks: Breaks the primary onboarding path for Barkpark Cloud users — login, signup, provisioning, and billing checkout would fail or silently misbehave (e.g. wrong exit codes, leaked credentials, mis-routed auto-connect).

role: Large test suite for the control-plane Cloud CLI commands
description: 1462-line suite covering login/signup/logout, auto-register/auto-connect (single vs multi barkpark, steal-guard), launch/go-live/subscribe error mapping, and JSON envelope stability, using a seeded config + fake control-plane HTTP server.
whatBreaks: A weak test suite would let regressions in login/signup/auto-connect/billing flows ship silently, breaking new-user onboarding.

role: bp cloud autoupdate/rollout CLI verbs
description: Implements per-instance autoupdate policy control (pin/unpin/pause/resume) and fleet-wide rollout brake (status/halt/resume) against the control plane, with honest receipts and error mapping.
whatBreaks: Operators could lose the ability to freeze/pause a bad release or halt a fleet rollout, or receive false receipts implying a rollback that didn't happen.

role: Tests for bp cloud autoupdate/rollout commands
description: Exercises the four autoupdate policy verbs and three rollout verbs against a fake control plane, verifying PATCH bodies, receipts, JSON output, and auth/usage/not-found edges.
whatBreaks: Regressions in autoupdate/rollout PATCH bodies or receipt text could ship unnoticed, misleading operators about fleet update state.

role: Local-only (no network) half of bp Cloud CLI commands (barkparks/attach/agent)
description: Implements bp barkparks (local KnownServers table view, falling back from cloud12's authoritative view when no token), bp attach/register (upsert a self-hosted server into local config via SSH target), and bp agent disable|uninstall (renders but does not execute the SSH command; agent not yet built). Purely reads/writes on-disk config.
whatBreaks: Breaks local server bookkeeping (bp barkparks/attach/agent), corrupting how self-hosted Barkparks are registered and displayed, though it never touches the network so blast radius is contained to the local CLI experience.

role: Golden-file tests for local-only Cloud CLI commands
description: Tests bp barkparks/attach/agent table rendering and JSON envelopes against testdata/*.golden fixtures, with an -update flag to regenerate them.
whatBreaks: A broken or stale test/golden pair would let local Cloud-command output regressions (bad table formatting, wrong JSON) ship unnoticed.

role: CLI `bp cloud deploy` command driving remote blue/green deploys
description: Implements `bp cloud deploy <target>` — resolves a target's SSH host (flag > fleet lookup > env var), streams the local deploy/instance-deploy.sh over SSH, and runs it with DEPLOY_REF/DEPLOY_REMOTE/BARKPARK_HEALTH_HOST env. Hard invariant: never writes local config (no SetActiveServer/RememberServer). SSH exec and fleet lookup are injectable package vars for testability.
whatBreaks: Staging deploys could silently target the wrong host, fail to stream the current script, or accidentally repoint the ambient bp server config.

role: Unit tests for `bp cloud deploy` host resolution and no-config-write invariant
description: Exercises host precedence, ref mapping, the remote-invocation transcript, and the guarantee that deploy never mutates local config, using fake SSH/fleet injections instead of real ssh.
whatBreaks: Regressions in deploy host resolution or the no-config-write guarantee could go undetected.

role: CLI `bp cloud domain status` — renders control-plane domain checklist
description: Calls GET /v1/barkparks/:id/domain-status and renders a per-host DNS/TLS/serving checklist; never probes DNS/TLS itself (control plane does). -o json emits the envelope verbatim and exit code reflects verdict, making it scriptable as a gate.
whatBreaks: Operators could get a wrong or misleading domain-cutover status, or scripted gates using the exit code could pass/fail incorrectly.

role: Unit tests for `bp cloud domain status` rendering and exit codes
description: Verifies checklist glyph rendering, JSON passthrough, and exit-code-follows-verdict behavior for the domain status command.
whatBreaks: Bugs in domain-status rendering/exit-code logic could ship unnoticed.

role: CLI `bp cloud instance archive` — portable bp-bundle-v1 fleet archive verb
description: Implements provider-neutral instance archive/archives-list producing a portable bundle (db.dump + media.tar.gz + secrets.enc) via cloud.WriteBundle, so archives are resurrectable across providers (Hetzner/Azure/fake). --fast is a Hetzner-only escape to the legacy snapshot path. Owns SSH collection and object-storage sink resolution (S3 creds from env, loud error if missing).
whatBreaks: Instance archives could be malformed, unsealed, or fail cross-provider resurrection, risking data loss on disaster recovery.

role: Unit tests for portable-bundle instance archive command
description: Tests target resolution, bundle collection, and store wiring for `bp cloud instance archive` using fakes, without touching real SSH or object storage.
whatBreaks: Archive bundle regressions (missing secrets, wrong format) could go undetected until an actual disaster-recovery attempt.

role: CLI `bp cloud instance` — provider-neutral fleet list/create/delete/ip/label router
description: Routes provider-neutral instance verbs through the cloud.CloudProvider seam (ProviderFor by --provider), degrading gracefully when a provider lacks an optional capability. Also hosts the `bp cloud azure` raw escape hatch talking directly to ARM. Delegates lifecycle verbs (archive/resurrect/decommission/adopt/audit/pause/resume) to the sibling lifecycle file.
whatBreaks: Core fleet management commands (create/delete/list instances across providers) could dispatch to the wrong provider or fail silently, affecting all infra provisioning via CLI.

role: Unit tests for provider-neutral instance list/create/delete/ip/label routing
description: Verifies dispatch to correct provider implementations and capability degradation behavior for the neutral `bp cloud instance` verbs.
whatBreaks: Provider-routing bugs in core fleet commands could ship undetected.

role: CLI provider-neutral fleet-lifecycle dispatch (archive/resurrect/decommission/adopt/audit/pause/resume)
description: Table-driven (provider, verb) dispatcher: Hetzner routes byte-identically to existing hetzner_instance_cmd.go functions; Azure routes to CLI-level decommission/audit/archive/resurrect implementations (no snapshot substrate, unrecoverable decommission). The dispatch table doubles as the capability-registration source via RegisterLifecycleVerbs, so a provider can only claim a capability it can actually execute.
whatBreaks: Lifecycle operations (especially decommission/resurrect) could be misrouted or falsely advertised as supported, risking irreversible instance loss or failed disaster recovery across providers.

role: Unit tests for provider-lifecycle dispatch table and capability registration
description: Verifies the (provider, verb) dispatch table routes correctly (including byte-identical Hetzner forwarding) and that RegisterLifecycleVerbs only advertises real dispatch entries.
whatBreaks: Dispatch or capability-registration regressions could let a provider falsely claim an unsupported lifecycle verb.

role: CLI: provider-neutral `bp cloud instance resurrect` dispatch
description: Implements the portable-bundle resurrect path (POST /v1/resurrect to the control plane) plus the Hetzner-only `--fast` legacy snapshot shortcut and Azure's hard rejection of `--fast`; resolves the newest bundle from the bundle store when `--bundle` is omitted.
whatBreaks: A wrong bundle-resolution or dispatch logic could resurrect the wrong instance state or silently succeed on an unsupported provider path.

role: Test suite for provider-neutral resurrect command
description: Exercises resurrect against a fake control plane: bundle_ref threading, azure --fast rejection, auth/login failures, and no-bundle-found cases.
whatBreaks: Regressions in resurrect dispatch or bundle resolution would ship undetected.

role: CLI: `bp cloud instance top` one-shot vitals/metrics snapshot
description: Fetches the control-plane metrics envelope for a managed box (agent-beat based, provider-agnostic) and renders it as pdrender stat-grid + chart blocks, or emits the raw JSON/YAML envelope verbatim; handles absent/stale beat states honestly without fabricating data.
whatBreaks: Operators would see incorrect or fabricated (e.g. zeroed) vitals for a box, undermining monitoring trust.

role: Test suite for `bp cloud instance top`
description: Verifies rendering across live/stale/absent beat states, verbatim JSON envelope passthrough, gap-handling in the metrics adapter, and one-shot (no --watch) behavior against a fake control plane.
whatBreaks: Vitals rendering bugs (e.g. fabricated zeros for gaps) would go undetected.

role: Go port of SPA's lifecycle-state fold for the fleet table
description: registryLifecycleToken maps a control-plane Barkpark's raw status fields (deprovision/provision status, suspended, host) onto one of seven shared GenInstanceLifecycle keys, mirroring the SPA's lifecyclePillState exactly so CLI and console agree on fleet status coloring.
whatBreaks: CLI fleet table (STATUS column) would show wrong or blank lifecycle states, diverging from the console's view of the same instance.

role: CLI: `bp cloud members` team roster + invitations viewer
description: Lists team members and pending invitations from the control plane, degrading honestly (not failing) when invitations are admin-gated (403) or unreadable; supports verbatim JSON/YAML passthrough and plain-table human rendering.
whatBreaks: Team admins/members could see wrong roster data or the whole command could fail instead of gracefully degrading on permission gaps.

role: Test suite for `bp cloud members`
description: Covers full roster + invitations rendering, 403 admin-gate degradation, verbatim JSON envelope, and the team-not-found 404 mapping against a fake control plane.
whatBreaks: Members/invitations rendering or error-mapping regressions would ship untested.

role: CLI: `bp cloud open <target>` dashboard deep-link opener
description: Resolves a fleet/site/instance target (name or UUID) to a legacy-stable dashboard hash route and opens it in the OS browser (or prints it with --print-only); always prints the URL for scriptability.
whatBreaks: Users could be sent to a broken or wrong dashboard URL, or scripts parsing the printed URL would break.

role: Test suite for `bp cloud open`
description: Verifies hash-route resolution for each target kind, name-to-id resolution, browser-open stubbing, and error mapping using a fake control plane.
whatBreaks: Deep-link resolution or browser-launch regressions would go undetected.

role: CLI: `bp cloud providers` capability matrix viewer
description: Reads the committed cross-surface providers_capabilities.json fixture and renders each provider's registered/planned state, best-effort auth check, and per-verb capability flags (archive/resurrect/decommission/adopt/audit/pause/labels); makes no network calls.
whatBreaks: Operators could be shown an inaccurate picture of which cloud providers/verbs are actually supported, leading to failed operations attempted on unsupported providers.

role: Tests for `bp cloud providers` capability matrix
description: Proves the providers table lists shippable providers (hetzner+azure, dev-tier fake hidden by default), shows honest auth state without shelling out, and -o json matches the Console's machine shape.
whatBreaks: A regression in the providers matrix (wrong capability marks, leaked dev-tier fake, or auth-state drift) would ship unnoticed.

role: Offline cross-provider archive→resurrect round-trip proof
description: Charter S14/Decision 12 test proving Hetzner↔Azure archive/resurrect works end-to-end using a fake Archiver and a recording RestoreDriver, asserting the seven-step restore contract (KEK carried not minted, drop→create→pg_restore→migrate, DNS repoint, fresh agent token) with zero live infra.
whatBreaks: Silent breakage of this test would let a real cross-provider resurrect corrupt data (wrong KEK, wrong DB, stale agent token) before it's caught in production.

role: `bp cloud status` — fleet triage view, terminal twin of dashboard
description: Implements the charter decision-15/32 attention-state classifier (attentionStatus/attentionRank/attentionBucket), ranks and buckets the fleet fetched from GET /v1/barkparks, and renders a painted table or -o json/yaml. The status vocabulary must byte-match the shared attention_order.json fixture that the SPA also asserts against — changing it here alone creates cross-surface drift.
whatBreaks: Operators would see wrong urgency ordering or miscategorized instance health (e.g. a failing box buried under 'healthy'), and CLI/dashboard status vocabulary could silently diverge.

role: Tests for `bp cloud status` attention classification and rendering
description: Pins the decision-15 status/precedence edges (removing beats suspended, degraded beats behind, etc.), bucket assignment, and table/JSON rendering against a fake control plane.
whatBreaks: A precedence bug in fleet triage (e.g. wrong status winning) would go undetected, misleading operators about which instances need attention.

role: Tests for bp cloud status UPDATE/POLICY cell rendering
description: Pins the pure updateCell and policyCell helpers that render version-delta and policy-flag columns in `bp cloud status`, covering both full and older-control-plane (absent-field) cases.
whatBreaks: Status table could show wrong or misleading update/policy info, or break backward compatibility with older control planes.

role: `bp cloud usage` — fleet/per-instance usage meter CLI, console's Usage twin
description: Renders the fleet summary (cached GET /v1/usage/summary) or one instance's meter wall (GET /v1/barkparks/:id/usage) with honest unmetered/quota/state/trend-sparkline handling; meter vocabulary (order+labels) is fixture-pinned against usage_meters.json shared with the SPA so the two surfaces can't drift.
whatBreaks: Usage meters could show fake zeros, wrong units, incorrect over/near-limit coloring, or diverge from the dashboard's meter vocabulary, misleading billing/capacity decisions.

role: Tests for `bp cloud usage` fleet/instance meter rendering
description: Verifies meter vocabulary matches the shared fixture, table rendering for all-unmetered and mixed-metered envelopes, -o json byte-verbatim output, 404 no-existence-leak mapping, and statusRole-painted STATE cells against a fake control plane.
whatBreaks: A drift between CLI usage rendering and the shared fixture/contract would go unnoticed, letting the CLI silently diverge from the dashboard's usage semantics.

role: `bp cloud verify <instance>` — on-demand golden-path re-verification CLI
description: Calls POST /v1/barkparks/:id/verify to re-run the provisioner's birth-certificate probe suite (api/login/studio), rendering a probe table with exit code as a real pass/fail deploy gate; probe vocabulary is fixture-pinned across Go CLI, Go provisioner, and Elixir executor.
whatBreaks: A gate script like `bp cloud verify prod && deploy` could exit 0 on a broken instance or fail to surface an unreachable box as a real failure, risking deploys onto broken infra.

role: Tests for `bp cloud verify` probe rendering and exit codes
description: Verifies probe vocabulary matches the shared verify_probes.json fixture, tests all-pass/one-fail/unreachable table rendering, -o json verbatim envelope, error-code-to-sentence mapping, and that exit code truly gates on full pass.
whatBreaks: A regression allowing a false pass/fail exit code from `bp cloud verify` would go undetected, breaking downstream deploy gating.

role: `bp cloud webhook <verb>` — CLI control of a managed instance's webhooks via control-plane proxy
description: Implements list/show/create/rm/toggle/rotate/deliveries/replay verbs, all routed through the control-plane instance-API proxy (never touching the instance's own admin token directly), with envelope-verbatim JSON, typed-resource delete confirmation, and role-painted status tables mirroring the console's Webhooks panel.
whatBreaks: Operators could accidentally delete webhooks without proper confirmation, fail to rotate compromised secrets, or get incorrect active/disabled status, degrading webhook incident response.

role: Tests for `bp cloud webhook` verb dispatch and proxy semantics
description: Proves the envelope-verbatim JSON contract, painted/piped table parity, toggle-as-PUT-{active} semantics, typed-resource delete gate (mismatch issues zero DELETEs), one-time secret display on rotate, and honest degradation for unreachable/too-old instances, using a fake recording proxy.
whatBreaks: A regression in webhook verb safety checks (e.g. delete confirmation bypass) could go undetected, risking accidental destructive operations on production webhooks.

role: Tests for the cmux hook last-error breadcrumb mechanism
description: Asserts the write side of the fail-safe hook's breadcrumb: a swallowed failure drops a breadcrumb file, an unwritable state dir still exits 0 with empty stdout, and a healthy action clears a stale breadcrumb.
whatBreaks: A regression here could let the cmux hook's diagnostics silently break, making a dead worker bridge undiagnosable without failing the build.

role: Top-level `bp cmux` verb dispatcher and `bp cmux status` implementation
description: Client-side builtin (intercepted before manifest dispatch) that routes `bp cmux hook|dispatch|install|status`; also implements `status`, which reports the pane's worker id, owned task, and live lease/claim health by reading the task doc and any breadcrumb. Core of the CMUX x Barkpark bridge (task-TUI epic wave 14).
whatBreaks: Wrong verb dispatch or status rendering breaks all `bp cmux` subcommands and hides/misreports lease health for every cmux-driven agent pane.

role: Tests for `bp cmux install --print` and `bp cmux status` rendering
description: Verifies the printed hooks block is valid JSON naming all four Claude Code events and that install/status never write unintended output; guards the human/machine status renderers.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions could ship a malformed hooks block or broken status output to users installing the bridge.

role: `bp cmux dispatch`: spawns the task frontier into new cmux agent panes
description: Reads the shared taskboard.Frontier model and, per non-colliding pick, launches a cmux workspace running an agent with BARKPARK_TASK set (optionally pre-claiming with --claim); defaults to dry-run when cmux isn't on PATH, never aborts the batch on one spawn failure.
whatBreaks: A bug could spawn duplicate/colliding agent panes, leak claims without lease info, or silently fail to dispatch any ready work.

role: Tests for `bp cmux dispatch` frontier spawning behavior
description: Spins up a fake task API with two ready tasks in distinct areas and asserts dispatch picks/spawns correctly, exercising the shared Frontier model and dry-run/claim paths.
whatBreaks: Regressions in dispatch's spawn/claim logic could go unnoticed, risking duplicate or lost task claims in production cmux panes.

role: Claude Code hook adapter implementing the fail-safe cmux worker lifecycle
description: Maps SessionStart/PreToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd hook events to claim/renew/close task actions keyed on BARKPARK_TASK + the pane's worker id; guarantees exit 0 always (panic-recovered, no stdout writes) per the cardinal fail-safe contract, and leaves a breadcrumb on any swallowed failure. Central to autonomous cmux agents self-managing Barkpark task claims.
whatBreaks: A bug could break the Claude Code agent's turn (violating the fail-safe contract), falsely close unfinished tasks, or leave leases stuck/lost across every cmux-driven worker pane.

role: Source-level tripwire enforcing the cmux hook's fail-safe contract
description: Greps cmux_hook.go for banned patterns (os.Exit, fmt.Print*, os.Stdout) to guarantee it can never exit non-zero or write stdout, since that would break the enclosing Claude Code agent turn.
whatBreaks: If this guard is weakened or removed, a future edit could reintroduce a stdout write or process exit in the hook, silently breaking every Claude Code agent session using cmux.

role: Tests for the cmux hook's claim/renew/close behavior against a fake server
description: Simulates the drafts task read, claim, and close endpoints to verify SessionStart claims, PreToolUse renews (throttled), and Stop/SessionEnd only closes on proven acceptance criteria, including epoch/rev handling for the digest-fence bypass.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions could let tasks close prematurely (losing unfinished work) or never close (starving the dispatch frontier) across all cmux-driven agents.

role: `bp cmux install`: prints the Claude Code hooks block and worker-id shell line
description: Print-first (and default) command that shows the settings.json hooks fragment and shell export line for wiring a cmux pane into the bridge; dispatches to the --merge writer for the additive on-disk install.
whatBreaks: Malformed or incomplete printed instructions would break manual bridge setup for new cmux users, or (if --merge dispatch breaks) prevent automated installs.

role: `bp cmux install --merge`: additive writer that folds hooks into ~/.claude/settings.json
description: Parses the user's settings.json as raw JSON, appends the four `bp cmux hook <event>` entries per event (deduped by exact command, foreign hooks preserved), and previews or writes with a timestamped backup; falls back to print-only guidance on any unparsable/unwritable file rather than risking data loss.
whatBreaks: A bug could corrupt or destructively overwrite a user's ~/.claude/settings.json, breaking all of their Claude Code hooks, not just the cmux bridge.

role: Test for `bp cmux install` hook-settings merge/dedup logic
description: Drives cmuxInstallMergeAt against a temp settings.json, asserting hook groups are merged/deduped correctly across events (table + json output). Includes a helper to count hook-command occurrences per event as the dedup invariant probe.
whatBreaks: A regression in the settings merge (e.g. duplicate hook registration) would go undetected, causing hooks to fire multiple times per event in real Claude Code settings.

role: Test for `bp cmux status` breadcrumb/health surfacing
description: Verifies `bp cmux status` surfaces the last-error breadcrumb (text and JSON), disambiguates not-found vs server-unreachable, and derives lease health from claim.ts_iso + TTL rather than expired_at.
whatBreaks: Silent regressions in cmux status diagnostics would leave the cmux bridge harder to debug when claims fail or the server is unreachable.

role: On-disk CLI config: server/token/scope + Cloud credentials persistence
description: Defines the Config struct persisted to disk (0600) holding the active server/token/workspace/project/dataset plus separate Barkpark Cloud control-plane credentials (CloudURL/CloudToken/CloudTeam) and KnownServers history; CloudClient()/HasCloudToken() are the seam every Cloud command (login, barkparks, provider, launch) depends on.
whatBreaks: Corrupts or loses saved credentials/active context, breaking `bp` auth persistence and every Cloud-authenticated command across sessions.

role: Test suite for Config load/save/scope-resolution logic
description: Unit tests for config.go's persistence and precedence behavior (flags > env > active > defaults); guards against credential file corruption or wrong context resolution.
whatBreaks: Config persistence bugs (lost tokens, wrong active server) ship undetected.

role: `bp doctor` CLI command running the 7-check server health gate
description: Implements the `bp doctor [--name|--url|--token]` built-in that resolves a target Barkpark server, runs setup.RunHealthGate, and renders a pass/fail report (table/json/yaml) with non-zero exit on any failing check; also wires an opt-in Cloud-sites probe when a Cloud token is present.
whatBreaks: Operators would get false READY/NOT READY verdicts when diagnosing prod deploys, masking real issues like the websocket-403 footgun or TLS failures.

role: Test for `bp doctor` against a fake HTTP server
description: Runs `bp doctor` through the REAL setup.RunHealthGate against an httptest server, covering an all-green case and a 403-websocket failure case, with the volatile test URL redacted for golden comparison.
whatBreaks: A broken doctor_cmd.go change (wrong exit code, wrong report rendering) could ship undetected, undermining trust in the post-deploy health gate.

role: Canonical API error.code -> CLI exit-code mapping
description: Defines apiError and the codeExit map, the single canonical translation from server envelope error.code strings to the CLI's stable exit-code scheme (docs/cli/error-exit-table.md); the CLI never re-derives exit codes from HTTP status, only from this table.
whatBreaks: Scripts relying on stable `bp` exit codes (e.g. CI checking exit 6 for conflict) get wrong codes, silently breaking automation that gates on them.

role: `bp export` CLI command streaming dataset as NDJSON
description: Built-in (not manifest-driven) command that streams the active dataset via apiclient.Export as NDJSON to stdout, one document per line, with --type/--perspective flags and clean Ctrl-C cancellation; used as a simple backup mechanism (`bp export > backup.ndjson`).
whatBreaks: Users relying on `bp export` for backups or data migration would get corrupted/incomplete NDJSON output or wrong perspective data silently sent to the server.

role: Test for `bp export` flag validation and error prefixing
description: Asserts an invalid --perspective is rejected before any server call, and that a failed export prints exactly one 'export: ' error prefix (guards against double-wrapping regressions).
whatBreaks: A regression could let bad --perspective values reach the server silently, or produce confusing doubled error prefixes for users.

role: Parses CLI-wide flags (-s/-o/--token/etc.) before noun dispatch
description: Defines the globals struct and hand-rolled flag parsing (valueFlags/boolFlags maps) that runs before the noun/verb split in Execute, stopping at the first positional token so command-local manifest flags are parsed separately.
whatBreaks: Global flags like --server, --token, -o, --dry-run parse incorrectly across every CLI command, corrupting output format or targeting the wrong server.

role: `bp cloud hetzner backup` CLI wiring pg_dump/psql to S3 backups
description: Implements create/list/restore/prune Postgres backup commands over internal/backup, wiring pg_dump as DumpSource and psql as RestoreSink; notably strips DB password out of argv into PGPASSWORD env to avoid CWE-214 exposure via ps/proc.
whatBreaks: Broken backup/restore wiring could silently produce empty or corrupt Postgres backups, or leak DB passwords via process listing, threatening prod data safety.

role: Test for `bp cloud hetzner backup` pipeline incl. password safety
description: Drives the real backup pipeline (streaming, gzip, manifest) against a recording S3 transport and a fake pg_dump DumpSource; explicitly proves DB passwords never appear on pg_dump/psql argv.
whatBreaks: A regression reintroducing the password-in-argv bug or breaking the multipart/gzip wire format would go unnoticed, risking credential leaks or corrupted backups.

role: `bp cloud hetzner` CLI: native Hetzner Cloud control via hcloud-go SDK
description: Large (1092-line) built-in command tree for direct Hetzner Cloud API control (servers, ssh-keys, networking, storage, backup) without needing the `hcloud` binary; resolves auth token from flag/env/hcloud-context and ensures every mutating verb waits for its Action(s) to complete before reporting. Also hosts the top-level `bp cloud` dispatcher (hetzner/azure/instance/providers/status/open/webhook/verify).
whatBreaks: Server lifecycle operations (create/delete/reboot/resize) could fire-and-forget or report false success, causing infra drift or destructive ops against the wrong Hetzner project.

role: Test for `bp cloud hetzner` against a fake api.hetzner.cloud server
description: 661-line test suite driving the CLI against an httptest fake of the Hetzner API, asserting real wire request shapes (method/path/body) and output; action-polling tests return RUNNING first to catch fire-and-forget regressions.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the large Hetzner command surface (wrong endpoint, malformed request body, premature success reporting) would ship undetected, risking bad infra operations.

role: Destroy-op confirmation gate for bp cloud hetzner CLI
description: Implements hzConfirmDestroy, the single funnel every destroy-tier hetzner verb (delete/rm/rebuild) passes through: --yes or non-TTY stdin skips the prompt, interactive mode requires the exact resource name typed back before proceeding. Also provides hzConfirmAbort (error envelope) and hzOneTargetYes (shared arg parsing for one-target destroy commands).
whatBreaks: A bug here could let a destructive hetzner delete fire without confirmation (or block scripted/non-interactive deletes across the whole hetzner CLI surface), risking accidental data/infra loss.

role: Tests for the hzConfirmDestroy destructive-op gate
description: Covers the pure hzConfirmDestroy contract (--yes and non-TTY pass through; interactive mismatch/empty input aborts) and wired commands (piped delete still fires the DELETE; interactive mismatch sends nothing to the API).
whatBreaks: A weakened or deleted test would let a regression silently remove the destroy-confirmation safety net without CI catching it.

role: CLI verbs for Hetzner Cloud DNS zones/records (bp cloud hetzner dns)
description: Implements `bp cloud hetzner dns zone|record {list,get,create,update,delete}` against Hetzner's integrated Cloud DNS API (hcloud-go v2.44), the same surface internal/hetzner's DNS provider uses. Handles rrset semantics (apex addressed as "@") and zone/record row shaping for table/json/yaml output.
whatBreaks: DNS record management via bp CLI (used in domain cutover / instance resurrect flows) would misbehave — wrong records created/deleted or apex handling broken, risking site outages.

role: Fleet-lifecycle admin CLI: archive/decommission/resurrect/adopt/eject/audit
description: Large (1500 line) command file treating a whole Barkpark instance (server + DNS + control-plane registry row) as one atomic unit for archive, decommission, resurrect, adopt-to-SaaS, eject-from-SaaS, and cross-check audit. Coordinates three separate credentials (compute, DNS, registry) and prefers the control-plane's deprovision queue over direct teardown, always ending in a residue verification.
whatBreaks: A bug could strand a billed server, leave a dangling DNS record, or leave a stale registry row after decommission — or destroy the wrong instance during teardown, causing real infra/data loss.

role: Tests for the instance fleet-lifecycle CLI verbs
description: Drives `bp cloud hetzner instance …` against httptest fakes of both the Hetzner Cloud API and the control-plane's internal barkparks endpoint, specifically asserting the division of labor between registry-path (worker owns teardown) and direct-path (CLI owns teardown) decommissioning.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the destructive decommission/resurrect logic (e.g. CLI deleting a server it shouldn't) would go undetected.

role: Portable instance export/import CLI (pg_dump + media + secrets tarball)
description: Implements `bp cloud hetzner instance export/import` to move a Barkpark instance as a provider-agnostic tarball (db.dump, .env identity secrets, uploads, manifest) rather than a Hetzner-project-bound snapshot. Import drops+restores the DB, merges identity secrets from the export while keeping host-specific env vars, replays migrations, and health-gates the restart.
whatBreaks: A broken import could corrupt or destroy the target instance's database/media, or restore with mismatched encryption keys (BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY) leaving data unreadable.

role: Tests for instance export/import SSH stream plumbing
description: Substitutes in-memory pipes for the two SSH stream seams (instSSHStream/instSSHFeed) to verify remote scripts carry required pieces (dump, secret merge, restore, health sentinel) and that bytes flow correctly end-to-end between export and import.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in the export/import byte-streaming or script content could silently corrupt instance migrations.

role: CLI verbs for Hetzner load balancers, IPs, placement groups, certificates
description: Large (1785 line) file implementing `bp cloud hetzner load-balancer|lb-types|floating-ip|primary-ip|placement-group|certificate` commands (list/get/create/delete plus service/target/algorithm/type management), sharing resolver/table plumbing from hetzner_cmd.go and hetzner_net_cmd.go.
whatBreaks: Traffic-routing and IP/cert management via the CLI would fail or misconfigure load balancers, potentially causing service outages for provisioned instances.

role: CLI verbs for Hetzner volumes/networks/firewalls + shared PR3 plumbing
description: Implements `bp cloud hetzner volume|network|firewall` commands and also hosts the generic resource-resolution (hzResolve) and mutation-receipt (hzResDone) helpers shared across all PR3 hetzner resource files (dns, lb, net).
whatBreaks: Since hzResolve/hzResDone are shared plumbing, a bug here would ripple into DNS, load-balancer, and network commands (wrong not-found errors, malformed mutation output) across the whole hetzner CLI surface.

role: Tests for volume/network/firewall/lb/ip/dns hetzner CLI commands
description: Drives the PR3 resources against a shared httptest fake of api.hetzner.cloud, asserting exact wire requests (method/path/body) and that mutating verbs returning an async action are polled to completion (catching fire-and-forget bugs).
whatBreaks: Regressions in async-action polling or wire-request shape for these resources would go undetected, risking silent partial-completion failures in production use.

role: bp cloud hetzner overview verb: fan-out estate summary + golden envelope contract
description: Implements `bp cloud hetzner overview`, concurrently listing all nine Hetzner resource kinds and assembling a charter-frozen JSON envelope ({ok, fetched_at, provider, resources, counts, errors}) that is byte-asserted against a golden fixture shared with the control-plane proxy and dashboard. A degraded kind rides as null with an errors entry rather than zeroing the whole response.
whatBreaks: Drift in the envelope shape breaks the golden-fixture contract and desyncs the CLI, control-plane proxy, and Infrastructure dashboard panel that all assert against the same fixture.

role: test suite pinning the hetzner overview golden-fixture contract
description: Exercises runHetznerOverview against a fake Hetzner API, asserting byte-for-byte equality with the committed golden fixture, per-kind field pinning, partial/total failure handling, and table rendering. Supports UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 regeneration.
whatBreaks: A weakened or deleted test would let the overview envelope drift silently, breaking the shared GUI/CLI contract without any signal.

role: CLI verbs for Hetzner ssh-keys plus read-only discovery (types/locations/images/pricing) and hetzner help text
description: Implements ssh-key CRUD and read-only discovery views (server-types, locations, datacenters, images, isos, pricing) for `bp cloud hetzner`, plus the namespace's help text constants. Depends on shared plumbing (client/auth, table rendering) defined in hetzner_cmd.go.
whatBreaks: Broken ssh-key or discovery verbs block server provisioning workflows (e.g. can't list images/locations needed for server create) and stale help text misleads users on the whole hetzner namespace.

role: bp cloud hetzner storage: S3-compatible Object Storage bucket/object CLI
description: Implements `bp cloud hetzner storage bucket|object …` over the internal objstore S3 client (SigV4, virtual-hosted addressing), using separate S3 credentials (flags or HETZNER_S3_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY env) rather than the Hetzner Cloud API token, since Hetzner has no API to mint S3 creds (Console-only gate). Shared by the backup command via the same client seam.
whatBreaks: Broken bucket/object commands would break Postgres backup storage flows (bp cloud hetzner backup builds on this same client) and any manual data-plane operations against Object Storage.

role: test suite for the Hetzner Object Storage CLI using a recording fake S3 transport
description: Drives bucket/object commands (create/get/list/delete/put/get/rm/presign) through a real objstore client with only the network faked, asserting exact SigV4 wire requests, multipart stdin uploads, and the no-credentials error message. Also tests the duration parser used by backup retention.
whatBreaks: Regressions in SigV4 signing, virtual-hosted addressing, or multipart upload assembly would go undetected, risking silent data-plane failures in production backups.

role: bp listen built-in: streams the live SSE change feed to stdout
description: Implements `bp listen [types]`, a long-lived SSE stream over apiclient.Listen, printing NDJSON events to stdout with strict argument validation and TTY-only status/reconnect banners on stderr. Special-cased as a built-in (not manifest-driven) because it's a streaming response.
whatBreaks: A broken listen command would break any tooling relying on real-time change notifications (webhooks alternative, live dashboards, sync scripts) piping bp listen output.

role: test suite for bp listen argument validation, help, and error prefixing
description: Covers rejection of bad input (extra positional, unknown flag), help output, and that a failed connection error is not double-wrapped.
whatBreaks: Loosened validation could let bp listen silently swallow bad flags/positionals or double-print error prefixes, confusing scripted consumers.

role: CLI capabilities manifest loader with file/env/network precedence
description: Loads the /v1/capabilities manifest via --manifest flag, BARKPARK_MANIFEST env var, ETag cache, or live HTTP fetch in that precedence order. Guards first-run installs by refusing to silently fall through to a localhost default.
whatBreaks: The CLI fails to bootstrap its command set or silently connects to the wrong server on first run, breaking all bp subcommands.

role: browser device-authorization login flow shared by bp login and the first-run wizard
description: Implements the Claude-Code-style copy-a-link device login: starts a device session against the control plane, renders a boxed verification URL/code to stderr, best-effort opens a browser, polls until approval, and persists {token, team_id} identically to password login. Exposes gating logic (deviceRequested) deciding device vs password path, and error classification into auth vs generic failures.
whatBreaks: A broken device flow blocks the primary `bp login` UX for interactive TTY users and the first-run wizard reusing this exact routine; incorrect gating could silently switch users to (or away from) the password path unexpectedly.

role: test suite for the device login flow, gating table, and related open-desk prompt
description: Covers the full device flow (start→pending→approve), slow-down backoff, denial/timeout auth errors, JSON envelope stdout cleanliness, the login gating table (device vs password path across credential/TTY combinations), and the offerOpenDesk / LoggedInWithoutServer helpers used by bp login's post-login UX.
whatBreaks: Weakened tests could let a regression silently break backward compatibility of `bp login` (e.g. device path engaging when credentials are supplied) or leak chrome/device codes onto stdout.

role: bp make schema built-in: emits a fill-the-blanks schema v2 JSON skeleton
description: Purely local (no network) generator producing a commented JSON skeleton covering every schema v2 field type (v1 primitives plus composite/arrayOf/codelist/localizedText), used to bootstrap new content-type schemas without reading the docs. Writes to stdout or --out file.
whatBreaks: An outdated or malformed skeleton would mislead schema authors into invalid schema JSON, but has no runtime/production blast radius since it's a local dev-tool generator.

role: Tests for `bp make schema` skeleton generation
description: Asserts `runMakeSchema` prints valid JSON with every supported v1/v2 field-type placeholder, correct name/type, and that `--out` writes to a file instead of stdout.
whatBreaks: A regression in the schema skeleton generator (missing field types, broken --out) would ship silently to users scaffolding new content types.

role: Unit test for rune-safe titleCase helper
description: Guards titleCase against byte-slicing multi-byte UTF-8 runes (e.g. 'über', '日本語') into invalid output, used when deriving human-readable names in `bp make`.
whatBreaks: Non-ASCII schema/type names would render corrupted (U+FFFD) titles in generated skeletons.

role: Generic manifest→MCP tool bridge (`bp mcp serve --tools all`)
description: Walks every manifest Command and auto-registers it as an MCP tool (bp_<noun>_<verb>) with a derived JSON-Schema input, skipping IDs already curated by mcp_tasks.go (bridgeShadowedIDs). Reconstructs the CLI positional+flag tail from MCP args and dispatches through the same execManifestCommand/run.go path as the CLI, so it can never drift from `bp` semantics.
whatBreaks: Every non-curated bp capability exposed over MCP (--tools all) would mis-map arguments or double-expose a curated command, corrupting tool calls from Cursor/Claude Desktop.

role: Tests for the generic manifest→MCP bridge
description: Spins up a real mcp.Server with in-memory transport, registers bridge tools from the full-manifest fixture, and asserts tool names/pagination/schema derivation are correct.
whatBreaks: A broken bridge tool-registration or pagination bug would go undetected until an MCP client with 100+ tools failed unpredictably.

role: MCP resources: published Barkpark Papers as browsable/readable resources
description: Registers a barkpark://papers/{id} resource template (always) plus best-effort concrete resources enumerated via doc.ls at startup; reads route through doc.get and return raw JSON. All failures degrade to template-only with a stderr warning — never fatal to server startup, and nothing is ever written to stdout (the JSON-RPC stream).
whatBreaks: Papers would be unbrowsable/unreadable from MCP clients, or worse, a bug could leak diagnostic bytes onto stdout and corrupt the JSON-RPC protocol stream.

role: Tests for paper MCP resources
description: Stands up a fake Barkpark API (doc.ls/doc.get) and an in-memory MCP client session, asserting title derivation (heading vs _id fallback), verbatim round-trip of doc.get bodies, and 404→ResourceNotFoundError mapping.
whatBreaks: Silent regressions in paper title derivation or 404 handling for MCP resource reads.

role: `bp mcp serve` entrypoint: stdio MCP server for Barkpark Tasks
description: CLI built-in (intercepted before manifest dispatch) that loads the capabilities manifest once, registers curated task tools plus optionally the generic bridge and paper resources, then serves JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout until disconnect/signal. Enforces the sacred-stdout invariant (all diagnostics to stderr) and forces g.yes since there's no interactive stdin to confirm writes.
whatBreaks: The entire MCP integration for Cursor/Claude Desktop would fail to start, hang, or corrupt its JSON-RPC stream, breaking every MCP-native client's access to Barkpark.

role: Live in-memory tests for `bp mcp serve` tool dispatch
description: Drives the full MCP server (initialize → tools/list → tools/call) over the SDK's in-memory transport against a stub Barkpark API, asserting the curated six tools work, empty-queue 200s aren't errors, HTTP>=400 sets IsError, and zero bytes hit the real os.Stdout.
whatBreaks: Regressions in tool dispatch, error-flagging semantics, or a stdout leak would go undetected before shipping to real MCP clients.

role: Real-process stdio smoke gate for `bp mcp serve`
description: Builds the actual bp binary and drives a scripted JSON-RPC session over real OS pipes (not the SDK's in-memory transport), asserting the real stdout stream is byte-pure newline-delimited JSON-RPC exposing exactly the six curated task tools. Skips loudly if the `mcp` command isn't wired yet in a parallel-built worktree, so it's never vacuously green.
whatBreaks: A stray print/log statement anywhere in the MCP code path could corrupt the real stdio protocol stream in production, breaking every MCP client silently — only this exec-level test can catch it (in-memory tests can't).

role: Curated six MCP task tools (task_ready/next/show/close/create/prime)
description: Hand-mapped, richly-described MCP tools implementing the claim-first/epoch-CAS task doctrine for MCP-native clients; each tool's description embeds the barkpark-tasks.mdc workflow so a model drives the queue correctly. task_create has no manifest verb and rides sendTaskMutations directly; all handlers dispatch via execManifestCommand and write nothing to stdout. Carries the @canonical capability:mcp-task-tools marker.
whatBreaks: MCP-native agents (Cursor, Claude Desktop) would be unable to correctly claim, close, or create Barkpark tasks — breaking the entire 'path B' task-tracking integration and risking epoch-CAS races or lost work.

role: `bp migrate` command: cross-server document migration logic
description: Implements a CLI-native built-in for migrating documents between two Barkpark servers (source/dest), including batched createOrReplace mutations, paginated source queries, and scoped URL construction via apiclient.ScopedURL.
whatBreaks: `bp migrate` corrupts, drops, or mis-scopes documents when moving data between servers/environments.

role: Unit tests for bp migrate --help/error paths
description: Covers runMigrate honoring --help (usage to stdout, exit 0) and the argument-missing error path (stderr, non-zero exit), plus migrateError's -o json / -o yaml structured envelope emission versus the human stderr line.
whatBreaks: A regression here means bp migrate --help could start dumping the argument error, or -o yaml could silently leak the human 'bp:' error line into scripted pipelines.

role: Pins migrateEndpoint.scopedURL as a delegate to apiclient.ScopedURL
description: Table test asserting the migrate command's URL-building method produces byte-identical output to the canonical apiclient.ScopedURL (including escaping of special characters and trailing-slash normalization), guarding against the migrate copy silently forking from the shared implementation.
whatBreaks: If migrateEndpoint.scopedURL drifts from apiclient.ScopedURL, bp migrate could build malformed workspace/project-scoped URLs (e.g. double slashes, wrong escaping) without any test catching it.

role: Implements `bp onramp <target>` — emits/writes MCP config for AI agents
description: Core logic for the onramp verb: builds per-target (cursor, claude-code, codex, cursor-cloud, windsurf, gemini-cli, copilot, agents-md) config stanzas with the correct env-var dialect and merge metadata, and renders them as human text or JSON; delegates actual file writes to onramp_write.go. Notable seam: doc blocks in docs/setup/*.md are meant to be byte-identical to what this file prints (charter decision 14), so editing one without the other is a drift risk.
whatBreaks: A wrong stanza or dialect here means every AI-agent onboarding flow for that tool (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Copilot) prints/writes broken MCP config, breaking the whole agent-onramp initiative end-to-end.

role: Golden tests for every `bp onramp` target's emitted config
description: Asserts byte-parity between each target's rendered stanza and its published doc block, checks dialect isolation (no cross-tool leakage), flag handling (--server/--token overrides, --force needs --write, unknown flags rejected), -o json shape, and the AGENTS.md wrapper drift gate across .cursor/.claude/docs files.
whatBreaks: Loosening or breaking these tests would let onramp_cmd.go silently drift from the documented config blocks or leak one tool's env-var dialect into another's stanza, corrupting agent setup instructions across the fleet.

role: The `--write` engine: safe JSON merge of the barkpark entry into agent configs
description: Implements atomic, idempotent JSON merging (server-map / flat / toml strategies) that inserts/updates only the barkpark entry in a user's MCP config file while preserving all foreign keys byte-for-byte; writes via temp-file+rename for crash safety. TOML (codex) merging is deliberately deferred to wave 3 and reported 'skipped'.
whatBreaks: A bug here could clobber a user's existing MCP server config (foreign servers or unrelated keys) or corrupt their .cursor/.claude/.gemini config files with a malformed partial write.

role: Unit tests for the onramp_write.go JSON-merge engine
description: Verifies file creation with correct permissions (0644/0755), idempotent re-runs, skip-vs-force behavior on a differing barkpark entry, preservation of foreign servers/keys during force overwrite, the servers-vs-mcpServers TopKey parametrization (copilot shape), flat-file merging, codex TOML skip behavior, and both JSON/human --write reports.
whatBreaks: Without these tests, a regression in the merge engine (e.g. losing a user's foreign MCP servers on write) could ship undetected, silently damaging developers' agent configs.

role: Central output-rendering writer (table/json/yaml, color, TTY detection)
description: Defines the writer type wrapping stdout/stderr that every CLI command writes through, resolving output shape (table/json/yaml/minimal), TTY-vs-pipe defaults, and color-profile degradation for lipgloss rendering.
whatBreaks: All CLI command output (human and machine `-o json` modes) renders incorrectly or loses machine-parseable stability, breaking scripts and terminal UX repo-wide.

role: Unit tests for the CLI's YAML/JSON output renderer
description: Covers renderYAML's key/value quoting rules (YAML indicator chars, type-ambiguous 'Norway problem' strings like "true"/"null"), no-HTML-escaping guarantee shared by JSON and YAML paths, large-float overflow safety in scalarYAML, and correct inline rendering of empty nested vs top-level containers.
whatBreaks: A bug in the shared output writer would corrupt every `bp ... -o yaml`/`-o json` command's machine-readable output across the entire CLI, breaking scripted/automated consumers.

role: Tests for --all pagination's envelope-key detection
description: Verifies runPaginatedAll and extractListRows correctly detect and re-wrap list rows under whatever envelope key a response uses (documents/docs/hits), fetching multiple pages and preserving the original key rather than assuming 'documents' — regression guard for a real bug where `task ready --all` returned zero rows.
whatBreaks: If extractListRows regresses to only recognizing 'documents', any --all pagination against endpoints using other envelope keys (tasks, media search) would silently return empty results.

role: `bp paper view <slug>` command: terminal render of a Bulldocs paper
description: CLI-native built-in that fetches and renders a Bulldocs paper to the terminal via internal/pdrender, the headless counterpart to the HTML reader and TUI paper pane; supports theme/perspective/width flags and `-o json` raw output.
whatBreaks: `bp paper view` fails to render or renders papers incorrectly in the terminal, breaking the CLI's paper-reading surface.

role: Tests for bp paper argument parsing (--perspective/--theme/--profile)
description: Ensures parsePaperArgs rejects invalid/typo'd flag values (which would otherwise silently fall back to a default, e.g. rendering a published paper instead of a draft) while accepting all valid aliases and case/whitespace variants, and that a full flag set round-trips correctly.
whatBreaks: A regression allowing invalid --perspective/--theme/--profile values through would cause silent wrong-content rendering (e.g. showing a published paper when the caller asked for --perspective draft with a typo).

role: Manifest-driven command build+send pipeline (generic dispatch)
description: Implements the core manifest dispatch machinery — buildManifestRequest (splitArgs/bindArgs/BuildURL/applyQuery/buildBody/authHeaders) and sendManifestRequest — the shared seam used by both the CLI render path and the headless MCP dispatch path so every generic manifest noun/verb command resolves and sends the same way.
whatBreaks: Every manifest-driven command (the bulk of `bp` nouns not hand-coded as built-ins, plus MCP tool dispatch) fails to build correct requests or send them, breaking most of the CLI and the MCP server.

role: Tests for the CLI's --dry-run request preview across output formats
description: Verifies dryRun renders method/url/headers/body correctly and consistently across JSON (body parsed as structured JSON when possible), YAML (headers nested as a real mapping, not a Go map literal), and human/table output, plus that Authorization headers are always redacted and stderr carries the dry-run notice.
whatBreaks: A regression could leak an unredacted Authorization token in dry-run output, or corrupt the YAML/JSON preview shape that scripts rely on to inspect outgoing requests before they fire.

role: Unit tests for readCapped body-size guard
description: Tests the readCapped helper's over/under/at-limit boundary behavior, ensuring bodies exceeding a cap fail loudly instead of silently truncating.
whatBreaks: A regression in readCapped's boundary check (silent truncation of large response bodies) would go undetected, risking corrupted/partial data being parsed as valid.

role: Implements `bp seed <type>` dev-fixture generator command
description: Fabricates schema-valid sample documents (recursing through v1/v2 field shapes including composite, arrayOf, richText/Portable Text, localizedText) and writes them via POST /v1/data/mutate as createOrReplace, optionally publishing; includes prod write-guard and JSON/YAML error envelope support.
whatBreaks: Developers seeding a fresh dataset get invalid/malformed documents (e.g. non-Portable-Text richText, wrong types) that fail schema validation or break downstream renderers, or a prod dataset gets silently seeded without confirmation.

role: Unit/integration tests for bp seed command
description: Covers deterministic IDs, per-type field generation correctness, richText Portable Text shape, pattern-safe strings, --count parsing, publish body construction, and JSON/YAML/table error-envelope parity across help/failure paths.
whatBreaks: Regressions in seed's document generation or error-envelope parity (e.g. leaking JSON to stderr, or breaking Portable Text shape) would ship undetected to CLI users.

role: `bp use`/`bp servers` built-ins for the named-server switching layer
description: Implements the local, no-network `bp use <name|url>` (switch active server, refusing to persist a staging server as default without --force) and `bp servers` (list saved servers with kind/active/tier/last-connected). Shares helpers (activeEntry, knownNames) with setup_cmd.go's connect flow.
whatBreaks: Users could silently switch bp's ambient target to a disposable staging server, or `bp servers`/`bp use` would print wrong active/known-server info, corrupting every subsequent command's implicit target.

role: Test for `bp servers` table header rendering
description: Asserts the servers list table prints a NAME/KIND/SERVER header with a dashed separator before rows, fixing a previously headerless table.
whatBreaks: A regression could reintroduce the headerless/unlabeled servers table, confusing CLI users about column meaning.

role: Tests for -o yaml error-envelope parity on use/doctor errors
description: Asserts useUnknown, useError, and doctorNoTarget emit a parseable `ok: false` YAML envelope on stdout under -o yaml, with no human-formatted stderr leak, matching existing -o json parity.
whatBreaks: Scripted YAML-mode consumers of `bp use`/`bp doctor` would get unparseable human text instead of a structured failure envelope.

role: embedded deploy.sh asset for bp CLI
description: Embeds the repo's deploy.sh script into the bp binary via go:embed so `bp deploy` can stream the installer over SSH without requiring a local checkout.
whatBreaks: `bp deploy` falls back to or fails without the embedded script, breaking remote deploy via the CLI for users without a checkout.

role: Bash script that provisions a bare VPS into a running Barkpark prod instance
description: Installs Erlang/Elixir (ASDF), Go, Postgres, clones the repo, generates .env secrets (SECRET_KEY_BASE, CLOAK, PREVIEW_JWT, KEK with strict byte-length requirements), builds Phoenix + the Go TUI, wires systemd + firewall, and optionally installs Caddy for TLS. Embeds hard-won incident lessons (PHX_HOST/DOMAIN mismatch caused 403 LiveView breakage) and idempotent secret-backfill logic for upgrades.
whatBreaks: A bad DOMAIN/PHX_SCHEME or malformed KEK/secret generation bricks a fresh deploy at boot (raises) or reproduces the historic 301/403 LiveView-dead incident; this is the canonical `bp setup --target deploy` server-side payload.

role: Generates Caddy/TLS provisioning steps for a managed barkpark.cloud server
description: Pure step-generator (no I/O) that renders a Caddyfile (reverse_proxy + automatic ACME) and builds the ordered shell steps to install Caddy, write the config, set PHX_HOST/PHX_SCHEME env vars, restart the app, reload Caddy, and firewall off the app port; used by the Cloud go-live provisioning chain.

role: Tests for Caddy provisioning step generator
description: Golden-file assertions on the rendered Caddyfile, per-name parameterization, bad-opts rejection, step count/shape (including SkipAppRestart variant), and a fake-runner exercise proving the generator never touches a real box or triggers ACME issuance.
whatBreaks: A regression could silently leak a hardcoded prod domain into the Caddyfile template or drop the PHX_HOST restart step, both of which have caused live Studio outages before.

role: Executes the `bp setup --target cloud` login+connect flow
description: Drives Barkpark Cloud device-login via an injected CloudLogin hook, then either finishes logged-in-only or delegates to the unchanged executeConnect path to probe/persist the picked Barkpark; also builds the structured dry-run plan for JSON consumers.
whatBreaks: Users running `bp setup` for Cloud could fail to connect to their picked Barkpark, get a nil-hook crash instead of a clear error, or have a dry-run accidentally hit the network/log in.

role: Tests for the cloud setup target (login/connect/wizard)
description: Covers target validation, nil-hook error, hook-to-connect delegation (persisting server/token/tier), logged-in-only as a valid completion, hook error propagation, dry-run never calling the hook, dry-run plan shape, and the TUI wizard's cloud row/short-circuit behavior.
whatBreaks: Regressions could let `bp setup` silently skip persisting a Cloud connection, invoke the login hook during a dry-run, or break the wizard's Barkpark Cloud selection path.

role: Executor for `bp setup --target connect` — probes and persists a server connection
description: Confirms reachability/auth tier via GET /v1/capabilities (+best-effort /v1/meta), rejects a supplied token that resolves to anonymous, then persists the connection via the ConfigStore seam and renders human/JSON summaries with next-steps. Also builds the dry-run Plan for connect.

role: Test: CLI setup connect error-hint paths
description: Go tests for executeConnect and probeCapabilities: covers 401 → token-hint, closed-port → reachability-hint, tier-none with explicit token → rejection error, and tokenless anonymous connect success.
whatBreaks: Error-hint logic regressions in bp setup connect go undetected, confusing users with wrong diagnostic messages on auth or reachability failures.

role: bp setup deploy subcommand implementation
description: Implements remote server deployment over SSH by streaming deploy.sh (embedded or from checkout) to the target host with DOMAIN/PHX_SCHEME/BARKPARK_PLUGINS env. Includes dry-run, validation, live progress, and post-deploy verification against /v1/capabilities and /studio.
whatBreaks: bp setup deploy fails or silently misconfigures remote Barkpark servers, requiring manual SSH intervention.

role: Post-deploy health gate proving a Barkpark server is genuinely ready
description: Runs a battery of checks (capabilities, Studio scoped-redirect walk, LiveView websocket-not-403, TLS verification, Postgres-via-API, stub agent/backup probes, optional Cloud-sites check) against a live server and rolls up an OK/not-ready report with per-check pass/fail details; core gate for Cloud go-live provisioning.

role: Unit tests for the setup wizard's post-provision HealthGate
description: Covers HealthGate.checkWebsocket/checkCapabilities/checkStudio/checkTLS/checkPostgres/checkAgentConnected/checkBackupScheduled and the top-level RunHealthGate aggregator, including the websocket-403 (check_origin/PHX_HOST drift) regression and the 302-to-scoped-studio follow logic.
whatBreaks: A silently-broken health gate would let a mis-provisioned or unreachable Barkpark box pass as healthy, shipping a broken instance to a customer.

role: bp setup local executor
description: Implements executeLocal: orchestrates bringing up a local Barkpark dev server via docker-compose or the native Elixir/Postgres toolchain, applying plugin selection and pointing bp at localhost:4000. Includes dry-run and destructive-action confirmation gates.
whatBreaks: bp setup local fails to start the dev server or silently runs destructive DB reset steps without confirmation.

role: test for local setup plan builder
description: Unit tests for buildLocalPlan — verifies that the clone step is prepended when outside a checkout, and that plan steps contain correct git commands and repo paths.
whatBreaks: Regressions in local setup plan construction go undetected, potentially shipping broken setup flows to users.

role: platform-specific background process helper (Unix)
description: Provides the Unix implementation of backgroundCommand, which detaches a child process into its own session via Setsid so it outlives the bp CLI exit. Used during local server setup to start background services.
whatBreaks: Background server processes started during bp setup would die when the CLI exits on Unix/macOS.

role: platform-specific background process helper (Windows)
description: Provides the Windows implementation of backgroundCommand, using CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP to detach a child process from the CLI's console so it outlives bp exit. Functional analog of local_unix.go for Windows builds.
whatBreaks: Background server processes started during bp setup on Windows would receive Ctrl+C signals and terminate when the CLI exits.

role: bp setup dry-run plan data structures
description: Defines the Plan, PlanStep, PlanPlugins, PlanNeed, PlanKnownServer, and Result structs used for structured JSON output from bp setup dry-run mode. Provides planPlugins() and addStep() helpers used by all setup executors.
whatBreaks: bp setup --dry-run JSON output is malformed or missing fields, breaking automation and AI agents that consume the structured plan.

role: plugin discovery for bp setup wizard
description: Provides `DiscoverPlugins()` which unions a curated fallback list of plugin slugs with on-disk discovery of `api/priv/plugins/` so the `bp setup` wizard can offer plugin selection without hardcoding every slug.
whatBreaks: The `bp setup` wizard fails to list available plugins or misses newly added plugin directories.

role: cloud provisioning executor
description: Implements staged cloud provisioning (Hetzner/Azure) for the bp CLI setup command — always defaults to dry-run plan, only creates real infrastructure when --yes and provider CLI/credentials are present, then chains into deploy.
whatBreaks: bp setup provision produces wrong CLI commands or skips the dry-run gate, potentially auto-creating cloud infrastructure without confirmation.

role: Core dispatch/foundation package for `bp setup` (SetupPlan, Execute, BuildPlan, Options)
description: Defines the five setup targets (connect/cloud/local/deploy/provision), the declarative SetupPlan struct, Validate, the ConfigStore/CloudLoginFunc/WizardFunc seams, and the Execute/BuildPlan dispatchers every executor (connect.go, wizard.go, etc.) plugs into. Deliberately avoids importing the cli package to dodge an import cycle.

role: setup step runner and plan renderer
description: Defines the step struct and shared execution primitives (runStep, runStepWithStdin, runCapture, printPlan) used by all three setup targets (local/deploy/provision) to render dry-run plans and execute real commands.
whatBreaks: All setup subcommands lose their dry-run rendering and execution substrate, breaking bp setup local/deploy/provision entirely.

role: admin token generator for fresh installs
description: Generates a cryptographically random admin bearer token (bp_admin_ + 32 URL-safe chars) during clean-profile setup. Ensures the token is minted at execute time (not plan/dry-run time) and threaded into the seed.
whatBreaks: Fresh bp setup installs would lack a valid admin token, leaving the server with no admin access or a predictable/insecure credential.

role: test for admin token generation and plan env threading
description: Pins the format of GenerateAdminToken (bp_admin_ + 32 base64url chars) and verifies the local plan carries the correct profile env vars and redacts the token placeholder.
whatBreaks: Token format regressions or incorrect env threading in setup plans go undetected.

role: post-install server health gate
description: Verifies a freshly provisioned server by checking GET /v1/capabilities (2xx) and GET /studio (non-5xx) before marking setup complete. Acts as the final correctness gate before bp connects to the new instance.
whatBreaks: A broken server could pass setup verification and leave bp configured against a non-functional instance, causing all subsequent CLI operations to fail silently.

role: Bubble Tea interactive TUI wizard driving `bp setup` on a TTY
description: Implements the full linear stage flow (target select → server pick-list/inputs → profile → plugin multi-select → confirm) that builds a SetupPlan for RunInteractive to execute; styled via the shared semrole palette. Handles the connect-history pick-list, plugin kill-switch semantics, and profile-driven plugin prechecks.

role: Unit tests for the setup wizard's connect pick-list flow
description: Drives the Bubble Tea wizardModel with synthetic key messages (no real TTY) to verify the remembered-server pick-list renders and that selecting a saved server correctly fills the resulting SetupPlan and skips the text-input stage.
whatBreaks: A regression in the wizard's server pick-list (e.g. wrong stage transition or plan fields) would ship silently to interactive users without this test catching it.

role: CLI glue connecting the setup wizard to Barkpark Cloud login/fleet-pick
description: Implements cloudLoginHook (the sole seam between the pure setup engine and cloudclient): logs the user in via the same device-flow/password path as `bp login`, lists their fleet, auto-connects a lone Barkpark or prompts a numbered pick, and resolves admin credentials — every branch (empty fleet, no admin token, still provisioning) finishes as a complete outcome rather than a dead end.
whatBreaks: `bp setup`'s Barkpark Cloud target could dead-end, leak an admin token in output, or connect to the wrong Barkpark, breaking first-run onboarding for cloud users.

role: Unit tests for the setup wizard's cloud login/fleet-pick flow
description: Exercises cloudFleetPick and cloudSetupDeviceLogin against a fake cloudFleetClient/device server: empty fleet, single vs multi Barkpark auto-connect, blank/out-of-range picks, no_admin_token manual paste, still-provisioning, host-only URL canonicalization, and token-leak-into-output checks.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the cloud onboarding fleet-pick logic (dead ends, leaked tokens, wrong Barkpark chosen) would ship unnoticed.

role: The `bp setup` CLI built-in — flag parsing, TTY gating, and JSON/human output
description: Bridges the cli package's on-disk Config to the setup package's ConfigStore/KnownServerInfo seams, parses setup-local flags, enforces the never-prompt/never-hang contract (wizard only on a genuine TTY, else a clean usage error), implements the active-saved-server reconnect convenience, and renders dry-run/real-run/help output. Also backs RunFirstTimeSetup (bare-`bp` first-run path).
whatBreaks: This is the entry point every `bp setup` invocation and the bare-`bp` first-run flow goes through; a bug here could open /dev/tty in automation (hanging agents), mis-parse flags, or leave users unable to connect/onboard at all.

role: Unit tests for `bp setup`'s JSON dry-run and active-server reconnect behavior
description: Seeds a temp config with an active saved server and asserts `bp setup --target connect` (no --server) resolves connect_to to that server via runSetup's JSON envelope.
whatBreaks: A regression in the active-server reconnect convenience or JSON dry-run envelope shape could ship undetected, breaking agent automation that relies on `bp setup --target connect -o json` without --server.

role: `bp sites` / `bp deploy` CLI commands for Barkpark Cloud hosted sites (P6)
description: Implements list/show/create/deployments/env set/domain add/github connect/logs sub-commands plus `bp deploy`'s default tar+upload flow, all thin wrappers over cloudclient calls with table/JSON rendering; site/Barkpark handles resolve via UUID-or-slug lookup.
whatBreaks: Users could not manage or deploy hosted sites from the CLI — create/deploy/env/domain/github-webhook wiring for Barkpark Cloud's Sites product would fail or silently misbehave (e.g. leaking secrets, wrong site targeted).

role: Unit tests for the `bp sites`/`bp deploy` CLI surface
description: Uses a scripted httptest router (scriptedCloud) to assert wire paths/bodies, rendered output, and exit codes across the sites sub-commands, mirroring the cloud12_cmd_test.go idiom.
whatBreaks: Regressions in `bp sites`/`bp deploy` request shaping or output formatting would go undetected.

role: Streaming tar.gz packer for `bp deploy`'s default artifact upload
