description: Implements streamTarball/writeTarball (io.Pipe-based streaming tar+gzip of the project dir) plus .gitignore-aware ignore-set building (loadGitignore/isIgnored/defaultTarballIgnores), including a hardcoded dotenv-secret exclusion list and a MaxBytes safety cap that aborts mid-file.
whatBreaks: A bug here could either fail every no-flag `bp deploy` (breaking the 'heroku moment' default flow) or, worse, ship secrets (.env files) into an uploaded deployment artifact.

role: Unit tests for the deploy tarball packer's size cap and ignore logic
description: Proves MaxBytes aborts mid-file (not after a full oversized file streams) and exercises .gitignore parsing/ignore-set behavior for the tarball builder.
whatBreaks: A regression allowing the tarball size cap to be bypassed could let a runaway deploy upload waste bandwidth or hang, undetected.

role: `bp style` built-in — renders CLI/TUI design tokens as a terminal preview
description: One-shot, pure render of status roles, lifecycle glyphs, priority severity, spinner frames, and a per-theme slate, all sourced live from internal/semrole and taskboard's generated token tables (tokens_gen.go) so it can't drift from the design source; honors NO_COLOR/pipe via ASCII fallback.
whatBreaks: A visual regression here only affects the `bp style` preview tool itself, not core functionality, though it would undermine confidence in the design-token pipeline's correctness.

role: Golden-fixture test for the `bp style` rendered output
description: Freezes styleguide_color.txt and styleguide_nocolor.txt byte-for-byte outputs of renderStyleSheet, pinning TrueColor/dark and Ascii lipgloss profiles respectively; guards against tofu/escape-byte regressions in the ASCII fallback (AC3).
whatBreaks: An undetected drift in `bp style` output would let unintended design-token or rendering changes ship silently.

role: Human-readable table renderer for CLI JSON payloads (-o table, the default)
description: Turns list/single-object API JSON payloads into aligned, display-width-aware (runewidth) tables or key:value views, with a hardcoded registry of list/single-object envelope keys per endpoint family, status-role coloring via internal/semrole, and cell sanitization/truncation. The default output mode for nearly every `bp` command.
whatBreaks: Nearly every `bp <noun> ls/get` command's default human output goes through this file; a bug here (e.g. missing an envelope key, wrong column widths, or breaking color byte-identity guarantees) degrades or corrupts the primary human-facing CLI experience across the whole surface.

role: Unit tests proving task lifecycle statuses colorize via the shared semrole vocabulary
description: Verifies statusRole maps task lifecycle states (in_progress/blocked/done/etc.) to the same four semantic roles used by cloud/deploy tokens, and that renderTable paints lifecycle_status cells accordingly in `-o table` output.
whatBreaks: `bp task ... -o table` could lose its lifecycle color coding or misclassify status severity, hurting scannability but not correctness of underlying data.

role: Test suite for CLI table status-role coloring and color-profile resolution
description: Pins the status→role color mapping (statusRole), ANSI16/256/truecolor paint-cell behavior, the BP_COLOR env escape hatch, and byte-identity of table output with color off vs on. Cross-checks lifecycle teal vs status-role green to prevent regressions.
whatBreaks: A regression in status-color mapping or the no-color byte-identity guarantee would ship silently and break piped/scripted bp table output or mis-color statuses in terminals.

role: Test suite for CLI table rendering: truncation, sanitization, row/column layout
description: Covers truncateCell (rune-safe, display-width aware for CJK), cellString control-char sanitizing, renderRows handling of long strings, scalar arrays, empty results with count meta, and wide-rune column alignment.
whatBreaks: Broken truncation or alignment logic would corrupt bp CLI table output (overflow, misaligned columns, dropped values) across every table-rendered command.

role: Implements `bp tasks`, the interactive full-screen task board TUI command
description: CLI built-in that launches the Bubble Tea taskboard.Run program with resolved server/workspace/token/cache-dir config; requires a TTY and rejects stray positional args, cross-referencing the scriptable `bp task` verbs in help text.
whatBreaks: The `bp tasks` interactive board would fail to launch, misconfigure its server connection, or wrongly accept/reject arguments and non-TTY environments.

role: Test suite for the `bp tasks` board command's TTY gate, help, and arg validation
description: Verifies non-TTY environments are refused with a helpful cross-reference message, -h prints usage before the TTY check, and stray positional args are rejected with a suggestion.
whatBreaks: A broken TTY gate could let `bp tasks` scribble escape codes into piped/CI output, or silently swallow user typos instead of guiding them.

role: Implements `bp task create`, the ergonomic task-document creation CLI verb
description: CLI built-in (not manifest-driven) that injects the task schema's required kind/lifecycle_status defaults, parses --title/--description/--set/--publish flags, and POSTs create+optional-publish mutations to /v1/data/mutate/<dataset>, reusing the generic mutate contract so it never drifts from the doc-create path.
whatBreaks: Task creation via `bp task create` (and the MCP task_create tool that shares sendTaskMutations) could fail validation, create malformed tasks missing required fields, or silently lose a created draft if publish fails.

role: Test suite for `bp task create` argument parsing and body-shape contract
description: Verifies required-default injection (kind/lifecycle_status), flag/typed --set parsing, --set override of defaults, error cases, isProdServer heuristic, and the exact flat top-level body shape sent to the mutate endpoint.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let `bp task create` silently start sending malformed or nested-field mutation bodies that the server rejects or mis-stores.

role: Implements `bp task frontier`, the parallel-dispatch-safe task-set CLI command
description: CLI built-in computing the maximal set of ready tasks with non-colliding blast radii using taskboard.Frontier, enriched with cross-root `blocks` edges fetched from the graph API only when ≥2 ready roots exist (zero-fetch guard), and reporting claimed-collision overlaps; supports --max/--proven-only flags and table/json/yaml output.
whatBreaks: Multi-agent dispatch (`bp task frontier`) could wrongly claim independence between tasks that actually collide, causing merge conflicts, or over-fetch the graph API breaking the zero-fetch performance guarantee.

role: Test suite for `bp task frontier`: flags, rendering, JSON shape, cross-edge fetch guard
description: Covers flag parsing, table/JSON rendering of picks and overlaps, and critically the zero-GraphShow-call guard for single-root ready sets plus correct fetch-and-fold behavior for multi-root sets.
whatBreaks: Loss of the zero-fetch guard test could let a regression silently reintroduce unnecessary graph API calls or break the frontier JSON contract consumed by dispatch scripts.

role: Implements `bp task lint`, an advisory nudge for missing area:/files: task labels
description: CLI built-in scanning ready leaf tasks (excluding parents) for missing authored `area:` and `files:` labels that starve the frontier's interference model; always exits OK (never a gate), suggesting phase-band-derived area hints where available.
whatBreaks: If lint's leaf/ready classification drifts from the frontier's own logic, its nudges would misguide task authors or fail to surface real metadata gaps, degrading frontier dispatch precision over time.

role: Test suite for `bp task lint`'s area/files finding logic and advisory exit code
description: Exercises every lint branch (parent exclusion, tagged vs untagged, phase-derived suggestion, non-ready exclusion) for both area and files nudges, and proves the advisory exit-code-0 guarantee even when findings exist.
whatBreaks: A regression could make the lint command incorrectly flag/exclude tasks or accidentally turn the advisory nudge into a hard failure, breaking CI or scripted usage that assumes exit 0.

role: CLI: frontier-aware atomic claim for `bp task next --frontier`
description: Implements the client-side frontier claim loop: fetches the board snapshot, computes the maximal non-colliding ready set via taskboard.Frontier, and claims the top pick by ID through the epoch-CAS claim endpoint, declaring its file scope so the server's resource fence rejects collisions. On a lost race or resource conflict it skips to the next pick, bounded by frontierClaimRounds, and also powers the `bp task ready` capacity header.
whatBreaks: Multiple agents running `bp task next --frontier` could double-claim colliding files or spin forever instead of honestly reporting frontier exhaustion.

role: Go tests for the frontier-claim CLI command
description: Table-style httptest-server tests covering the happy path, lost-race skip-to-next, resource_conflict holder naming, missing-epoch hard failure, and bounded-round exhaustion for `bp task next --frontier`, plus the `bp task ready` frontier header.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the frontier claim loop (e.g. infinite spin or silent double-claim) would ship undetected.

role: Golden fixture for `bp agent disable` dry-run output
description: Expected text output showing the SSH command that would run to disable a cloud agent, without executing it; used to assert CLI output formatting stays stable.
whatBreaks: A CLI test comparing against this golden file would fail or falsely pass if the fixture drifts from real output.

role: Golden fixture: generated AGENTS.md onramp snippet for task tracking
description: Expected markdown block documenting `bp task` verbs (ready/next/get/close/create/prime) that the onramp generator injects into a target repo's AGENTS.md; used to pin the generated content.
whatBreaks: Onramp doc generation could silently drift without a test catching stale/incorrect bp task guidance shipped to consumer repos.

role: Fixture: fleet-ranking test cases for the attention-order algorithm
description: Synthetic Barkpark fleet list (shuffled) with an expected_order field pinning the exact name order rankBarkparks must produce, covering every rank plus a case-insensitive name tiebreak; companion to cloud/priv/static/__fixtures__/attention_order.json which is the canonical cross-surface fixture.
whatBreaks: The CLI's fleet attention/priority ordering could regress (wrong barkpark surfaced first) without test coverage catching it.

role: Golden fixture: `bp barkparks` fleet table rendering
description: Expected ASCII table output (name/provider/url/status/mode/health/agent columns) for a multi-instance fleet listing, used to assert table-formatting stability.
whatBreaks: Fleet table rendering regressions (column misalignment, wrong status text) would go undetected.

role: Golden fixture: `bp barkparks` local/cloud table rendering
description: Expected small table output showing local vs cloud target rows (dev/acme) including the active-target star marker, used to pin CLI table output.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the barkparks list table (e.g. losing the active-target star) would go untested.

role: Golden fixture: plain ASCII fleet table (no color)
description: Expected non-colorized table output for a fleet listing, used to test the ASCII-only rendering path of the CLI's table chrome.
whatBreaks: Loss of ASCII fallback formatting (e.g. for non-TTY output) would ship untested.

role: Golden fixture: ANSI-colorized fleet table output
description: Expected output with embedded 24-bit ANSI color escape codes for provider/status cells, pinning the CLI's colorized table rendering (status/provider color coding).
whatBreaks: Color-coding regressions in terminal table output (wrong or missing ANSI codes) would go undetected.

role: Golden fixture: `bp doctor` all-checks-passed output
description: Expected human-readable output listing all 7 doctor checks (capabilities, studio, websocket, tls, postgres-via-api, agent-connected-stub, backup-scheduled-stub) passing, used to assert the doctor command's success-path formatting.
whatBreaks: Regressions in `bp doctor`'s health-check summary formatting or check count would go untested.

role: Test fixture: a foreign + barkpark MCP server config
description: Sample mcp.json-style config with an unrelated 'filesystem' MCP server entry plus a 'barkpark' entry (stale API URL) and an unrelated top-level key. Used to test that `bp onramp`/MCP-config writers merge in place without clobbering foreign entries or unrelated keys.
whatBreaks: A bad fixture could let an onramp merge-writer regression pass silently, risking real user MCP configs being overwritten in production.

role: Golden output for `bp cloud register` SSH-mode instance flow
description: Expected stdout snapshot for registering a cloud instance over SSH, pinning the exact success message and the agent-install hint. A golden-file diff test compares CLI output against this.
whatBreaks: Wrong text lets a CLI output-format regression in `bp cloud register` ship unnoticed (or, if edited carelessly, spuriously fails CI).

role: Golden output: CLI style tokens rendered in 16-color mode
description: Snapshot of the `bp styleguide`-type command's ANSI-16-color rendering of status roles, lifecycle glyphs, and priority severity, generated from internal/semrole + tokens_gen.go. Pins exact ANSI codes for the 16-color terminal profile.
whatBreaks: A silent drift in 16-color token output (e.g. wrong color code) would go undetected in low-color terminals.

role: Golden output: CLI style tokens rendered in 256-color mode
description: Same style-token snapshot as styleguide_16.txt but using xterm-256 color escape codes; part of the same generated-tokens golden family.
whatBreaks: 256-color terminal rendering regressions in status/lifecycle/priority tokens go undetected.

role: Golden output: CLI style tokens rendered in truecolor mode
description: Style-token snapshot using 24-bit RGB ANSI escapes (38;2;r;g;b), the highest-fidelity color profile in the same generated-tokens golden set.
whatBreaks: Truecolor rendering regressions in the CLI's semantic role/theme tokens go undetected.

role: Golden output: CLI style tokens rendered with color disabled
description: Plain-text fallback rendering of the same status/lifecycle/priority tokens (ASCII glyphs like ##, ~, !, v, x, o instead of ANSI colors) — pins the NO_COLOR/non-tty degraded path.
whatBreaks: A regression in the no-color fallback could leak ANSI codes into piped/non-tty output or lose glyph legibility, breaking scripting consumers.

role: Golden output: per-theme CLI color slate (evergreen/ember/fjord etc.)
description: Snapshot enumerating each registered theme's status/glyph/chrome color triples via semrole.Themes(), used to catch unintended token drift as new themes are added.
whatBreaks: New or edited themes could silently break color consistency across the CLI/TUI without this pinning test catching it.

role: Golden output for `bp webhook deliveries` table rendering
description: Expected table-formatted stdout for a webhook delivery list (id, status, attempts, last_attempt, latency_ms, status_code columns), used to pin the CLI table renderer's column layout for this noun.
whatBreaks: Column layout or missing-value formatting (e.g. the em-dash placeholder) regressions in webhook delivery listing go undetected.

role: Golden output for `bp webhook ls` table rendering
description: Expected table-formatted stdout for the webhook list command (id, name, status, events, failures, url columns), pinning array-field (events) and status rendering.
whatBreaks: Table formatting regressions (e.g. events array rendering, column order) for webhook listing ship silently.

role: Unit tests for the `bp ticket`/`bp ticket-key` CLI table/minimal rendering and manifest dispatch
description: Tests the ticket inbox/show/keys table rendering (column presence, subject-leads-header, envelope unwrapping), minimal-output id listing, colorlessness of ticket tables, NO_COLOR enforcement, manifest-driven dispatch (URL building, path-param exclusion from body, --close query flag) and the quickstart-card verbatim render for ticket-key mint/rotate — all manifest-first with zero bespoke Go command code per noun.
whatBreaks: Regressions here would let ticket inbox/show tables silently degrade to crammed unreadable cells, leak ANSI color, or break the manifest-to-HTTP dispatch for the whole ticket/ticket-key noun family (mint, rotate, pause, revoke, answer, close).

role: bp tinker built-in: interactive authenticated REPL against a live dataset
description: Implements `bp tinker` — a thin read/write shell (schemas/query/doc/mutate/perspective/help/exit) resolving the same server/workspace/dataset/token context as other commands. Line parsing (parseTinkerLine), body-wrapping (tinkerMutateBody), and typo suggestions (tinkerSuggest via nearestToken) are pure functions factored out for unit testing.
whatBreaks: The interactive tinker REPL would misparse commands, send malformed mutate bodies, or hit the wrong dataset/perspective, but no other command path depends on it.

role: unit test for tinker REPL's unknown-command typo suggestion
description: Verifies tinkerSuggest maps mistyped verbs (quer→query, muate→mutate, etc.) to the right suggestion and rejects unrelated input.
whatBreaks: A regression in the tinker typo-hint logic would go undetected, giving misleading or missing suggestions in the REPL.

role: test suite for the CLI's streaming HTTP transfer client (upload/download timeouts)
description: Proves doRequestStream and fetchToFile correctly use ResponseHeaderTimeout (not an absolute timeout) so slow-but-alive uploads/downloads survive while a genuinely stalled server still errors out. Uses httptest servers and a trickleReader to simulate slow connections.
whatBreaks: Large file uploads/downloads (e.g. bp media upload, bp upgrade binary fetch) could either hang forever or get incorrectly killed on slow connections without this test guarding the timeout semantics.

role: The `bp uninstall` built-in — removes local bp state (config, optionally dev stack)
description: Implements dry-run-first, confirm-gated teardown of ~/.config/barkpark/config.json and, with --local, the docker/native dev stack + ~/.barkpark. Never touches remote servers or the binary itself; TTY-safe (--yes required on non-interactive runs).
whatBreaks: A bug could either fail to clean up local state (leaving stale tokens) or, more dangerously, delete the wrong path/database without proper confirm gating on a non-interactive run.

role: test for bp CLI uninstall command
description: Tests runUninstall with an in-memory writer in non-TTY mode, verifying the --yes gate and JSON output envelope for the bp CLI uninstall subcommand.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the uninstall command go undetected, potentially leaving orphaned state or breaking agent-driven uninstall flows.

role: quiet background CLI-update notice: at-most-once-per-release stderr nudge
description: Implements the anti-spam self-update notice: checks a persisted cache at most once per 24h, fetches the latest cli-v* release in the background (started at command launch, awaited briefly at exit), and prints one stderr line per release, never touching stdout or exit codes. Every failure mode (missing cache dir, corrupt file, network down) degrades to silence.
whatBreaks: Users would either never get notified of new bp releases, or the notice could spam repeatedly or corrupt stderr output for scripted/CI callers.

role: test suite for the update-notice anti-spam gates and cache lifecycle
description: Covers all silence gates (dev build, env kill-switch, upgrade/version subcommand, non-TTY), fresh/stale cache behavior, network failure, corrupt cache recovery, and up-to-date silence — pinning the exact anti-spam contract of update_notice.go.
whatBreaks: A regression letting the update notice leak into CI/script output or spam repeatedly would go undetected.

role: bp upgrade builtin — self-update from GitHub cli-v* releases
description: Resolves latest cli-v* tag via the /releases/latest redirect (no GitHub API), compares semver, downloads the platform asset, verifies its sha256 against checksums.txt, then atomically renames it over the running binary. Refuses on dev builds and gives a sudo re-install hint on permission errors.
whatBreaks: bp upgrade could install a corrupted/mismatched binary or silently fail to update, stranding users on stale CLI versions or bricking their install path.

role: unit tests for the bp upgrade self-update flow
description: Covers version comparison edge cases, the fake GitHub release-tree redirect flow, checksum mismatch/missing-entry handling, and end-to-end runUpgrade behavior including --check and --help paths.
whatBreaks: Regressions in upgrade.go (e.g. a checksum bypass or version-compare bug) would ship undetected.

role: renders all CLI help/usage text from the manifest tree
description: Prints top-level usage, per-noun verb lists, per-command signatures (args/flags/pagination/write hints), and Levenshtein-based 'did you mean?' suggestions for mistyped nouns/verbs — entirely manifest-driven, no hardcoded command list.
whatBreaks: Every `bp <noun> -h`, top-level help, and typo-suggestion output becomes wrong or missing, degrading CLI discoverability across the whole tool.

role: test suite for manifest-driven `usage:` help rendering and typo-suggestion helpers
description: Verifies usageCommand renders arg summaries, flags, write-body block, and pagination globals correctly from a manifest.Command, plus tests the shared levenshtein/nearestNoun/nearestVerb fuzzy-matching helpers used across the CLI's did-you-mean hints.
whatBreaks: Every `bp <noun> <verb> --help` output could silently drop argument docs or leak inappropriate sections (body/globals) for read-only commands, and noun/verb typo suggestions could regress across the whole CLI.

role: bp vercel quick-setup built-in: provisions Barkpark + deploys to Vercel in one shot
description: Go port of the shell quick-setup flow: creates a workspace, applies schema, seeds+publishes content, mints a scoped read token over HTTPS, then shells out to the `vercel` CLI (link/disable-protection/env/deploy). Also supports a --static mode that skips all Barkpark provisioning. Critically routes all Barkpark API calls through the SCOPED /w/<site>/p/<project> prefix, never the flat /v1/ alias, to avoid landing content in the wrong tenant.
whatBreaks: A misrouted scoped-prefix or mis-ordered step would provision/write content into the wrong workspace (silent tenant confusion), leak a token in output, or fail Vercel deploys for every `bp vercel quick-setup` user.

role: test suite for bp vercel quick-setup (scoped URLs, arg parsing, static mode, JSON envelopes)
description: Pins the critical scoped-vs-flat URL invariant, flag parsing (including inline form and --static), required-flag validation, seed-id extraction, publish payload shape, and the machine (-o json) envelope contract including that static mode skips all Barkpark concerns.
whatBreaks: A regression sending Barkpark provisioning writes to the flat/wrong-tenant URL, or breaking the JSON machine envelope for scripted callers, would go undetected.

role: regression test for extracting the deploy URL from `vercel deploy` output
description: Covers both plain-text and JSON output shapes of the `vercel deploy` CLI, guarding against a prior bug where the JSON shape's last line ('}') was mistakenly picked as the URL.
whatBreaks: bp vercel quick-setup could print a bogus '}' as the deployed site's URL instead of the real vercel.app link.

role: Tests for Barkpark autoupdate/rollout JSON decode
description: Verifies the cloudclient.Barkpark struct decodes the full self-update field set correctly and tolerates an older control plane that omits them (zero values, no error).
whatBreaks: A decode regression could crash or silently misreport autoupdate state when talking to older control planes.

role: framework-free HTTP client for the Barkpark Cloud control plane
description: Mirrors apiclient's hand-rolled net/http idiom but talks to a separate control-plane service scoped to the user's whole fleet (not one content server): login/register/device-auth, billing checkout, list/launch/go-live/resurrect Barkparks, credentials, verify/domain-status/metrics probes, and the sites/deployments/webhooks proxy surface. Every `bp cloud`/`bp sites`/`bp barkparks` command routes through this client; deliberately shares no code with apiclient so the two services can drift independently. File also continues past line 1199 (not fully read) with more webhook-proxy methods.
whatBreaks: Every Barkpark Cloud CLI surface — login, fleet listing, launch/go-live/resurrect, sites, deployments, webhooks, verify/metrics/domain-status — would break or silently misdecode control-plane responses, since this is the sole HTTP seam to that service.

role: Test suite for the Barkpark Cloud control-plane HTTP client
description: Exercises Client methods (Login, Register, ListBarkparks, GetCredentials, ConnectProvider, Launch, GoLive, sites/deployments/env/domains CRUD, UploadArtifact, CreateCheckout, VerifyInstance) against httptest fakes, asserting request shape, auth headers, omitempty body behavior, and error-surfacing including a wall-clock-timeout regression guard for streaming uploads.
whatBreaks: A regression here lets the cloud CLI/client silently break auth, billing, or deploy flows against the control plane without any test catching it.

role: Test suite for the OAuth-device-flow login client methods
description: Covers DeviceStart/DevicePoll against fakes: pending/slow_down/approved states, RFC-8628 error-code aliasing, and terminal-error handling, guarding `bp login` device-link UX.
whatBreaks: Device-link login (bp login) could silently misclassify pending/approved/denied states, hanging or falsely succeeding the CLI login loop.

role: Native Hetzner Cloud API client wrapper (hcloud-go SDK) + token resolution
description: Wraps hcloud.Client with test-friendly options (endpoint/http-client/poll-backoff overrides) and defines ResolveToken, the HCLOUD_TOKEN → hcloud-CLI-context resolution ladder used by all `bp cloud hetzner` provisioning.
whatBreaks: Every Hetzner-backed CLI/provisioner call (servers, DNS, object storage) fails to authenticate or talks to the wrong API endpoint.

role: cloud.DNSProvider implementation over Hetzner's native Cloud DNS SDK
description: Implements UpsertRecord/DeleteRecord/Resolve against hcloud-go's zone/rrset resources, mirroring cloud.CloudDNS's semantics (apex handling, idempotent delete, TTL) as the SDK-native alternative path.
whatBreaks: DNS record provisioning for domain cutover/go-live could silently create wrong records or fail to detect existing ones, breaking site domains.

role: Test suite for the native hcloud DNS provider (dns.go)
description: Verifies create-vs-replace upsert branching, apex '@' addressing, idempotent delete on 404, and sorted Resolve results using a fake hcloud HTTP server.
whatBreaks: DNS upsert/delete regressions in dns.go could ship undetected, corrupting domain records during provisioning.

role: Parser for the official hcloud CLI's cli.toml to extract the active token
description: Implements a tolerant subset TOML parser reading ~/.config/hcloud/cli.toml (or HCLOUD_CONFIG) to find the active_context's token, the third rung of ResolveToken's fallback ladder; unknown syntax is skipped rather than erroring.
whatBreaks: Users relying on an existing hcloud CLI context (no HCLOUD_TOKEN env var) get token-resolution failures or, worse, silently read the wrong context's token.

role: Test suite for the hcloud cli.toml context parser
description: Covers active_context resolution, HCLOUD_CONTEXT override, unknown-context error, and parser tolerance of comments/unquoted values/unknown sections.
whatBreaks: Parser regressions in hcloud_context.go could go unnoticed, silently breaking the hcloud-CLI-context token fallback.

role: Test suite for Hetzner Object Storage bucket operations (create/list/delete)
description: Uses a recording HTTP transport to assert PUT/DELETE/GET requests hit the correct virtual-hosted bucket subdomain with SigV4 auth, and that bucket-listing XML parses correctly, with no real network dial.
whatBreaks: Bucket-lifecycle regressions in objstore/client.go (wrong host/path/auth) could ship undetected, breaking backup bucket provisioning.

role: S3-compatible client for Hetzner Object Storage (aws-sdk-go-v2 based)
description: Wraps s3.Client against https://<location>.your-objectstorage.com with virtual-hosted addressing and SigV4 static credentials; provides bucket CRUD, object put/get/list/delete, presigned GET URLs, and a manual multipart PutLarge for large/unbounded streams (e.g. pg_dump backups).
whatBreaks: Backup uploads/downloads and any future object-storage-backed feature (media, exports) fail or corrupt data, especially large multipart uploads used for streaming DB dumps.

role: Test suite for the Hetzner Object Storage S3 client (endpoint/addressing/presign)
description: Verifies per-location endpoint derivation, virtual-hosted (not path-style) addressing end-to-end, and presigned GET URL shape/params, all via a recording transport with no live bucket.
whatBreaks: Addressing or presign regressions in client.go could ship undetected, breaking object storage access or backup restore links.

role: Test for S3 multipart-upload PutLarge (Hetzner object storage)
description: Fake RoundTripper stands in for S3 multipart operations (create/upload-part/complete/abort) to test single-part, zero-byte, multi-part chunking, and abort-on-failure behavior without opening a socket.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a broken large-file upload (e.g. failure to abort a half-finished multipart, or wrong part chunking) ship undetected, risking stuck storage costs or corrupted backups.

role: hcloud SDK-backed implementation of the cloud.CloudProvider interface
description: APIProvider implements Create/IP/Delete/List/LabelServer/ListByLabel against api.hetzner.cloud via the hcloud-go SDK, mirroring the argv-based HcloudProvider's contract (same labels, idempotency, ssh-key resolution) so the provisioner can swap providers transparently.
whatBreaks: Server provisioning, teardown, or orphan-sweep for the whole Hetzner-hosted fleet (guerrilla, prod boxes) could fail silently or leak billed orphan servers.

role: Test suite for the hcloud SDK CloudProvider implementation
description: Uses an httptest fake of api.hetzner.cloud to assert the full wire conversation for Create/Delete/List/LabelServer/token-resolution, including the no-billed-orphan cleanup guarantee and idempotent delete semantics.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in provider.go (e.g. orphaned billed servers, wrong ssh-key resolution) would slip through since this is the primary guard on that provider.

role: on-disk ETag cache for the fetched CLI capabilities manifest
description: Keys cache entries by sha256(baseURL+token-salt) so tokens never touch disk in clear; Store validates the body parses and writes atomically via temp+rename. Backs the 304 Not Modified fast path in Fetch.
whatBreaks: A broken cache could serve a stale/wrong-tier manifest (e.g. admin caps to an anon caller) or corrupt on concurrent writes, breaking command discovery for every bp invocation.

role: unit tests for the manifest on-disk cache
description: Verifies round-trip, per-token cache-key salting/isolation, atomic overwrite (no stray temp files), and rejection of a non-parsing body on Store.
whatBreaks: A cache-isolation or atomicity regression (e.g. admin/anon manifest leak) would go unnoticed.

role: CLI context resolution (flags > env > active > defaults)
description: Defines the `Context` struct (server, token, workspace, project, dataset, output) and implements `Resolve()` with a strict precedence chain: flags > env > active saved context > baked defaults. Every CLI command derives its target from this.
whatBreaks: Every CLI command resolves against the wrong server, token, or dataset — silent misdirection of all API calls.

role: HTTP fetch of GET /v1/capabilities with ETag-conditional caching
description: Fetch() sends If-None-Match using the cached ETag, returns the cached manifest on 304, parses and re-caches on 200, and surfaces the server's error body on other statuses. This is the CLI's bootstrap call — first request every bp invocation makes.
whatBreaks: If Fetch mishandles statuses or caching, the CLI could crash on startup, silently use a stale/wrong manifest, or fail to build its command tree entirely — every bp command depends on this.

role: Test for the ETag-cached manifest Fetch used by every CLI invocation
description: Verifies 200→cache→304 conditional-fetch behavior, nil-cache unconditional fetch, and error-body surfacing (e.g. 401 with message) for the /v1/capabilities fetch that underlies all bp CLI commands.
whatBreaks: A caching or error-surfacing regression in the manifest fetch would degrade every bp CLI command's startup (stale schema, unclear auth errors, or unnecessary refetches).

role: typed model + strict parser for the CLI capabilities manifest
description: Defines Manifest/Server/Noun/Command/Arg/Flag structs mirroring docs/cli/manifest.schema.json exactly, and Parse() which rejects unknown fields and trailing data. The package hardcodes no noun/verb/route — the entire CLI command tree is a pure function of this document, so a plugin adds commands with zero code changes here.
whatBreaks: A parsing bug or schema drift here breaks manifest ingestion for the whole CLI — every noun, verb, and command in bp is derived from this struct definition.

role: unit tests for manifest parsing, tree-building, URL-building, and context precedence
description: Exercises fixture parsing (admin/anon tiers), Tree() purity (no hardcoded nouns), BuildURL flat-vs-scoped-mirror behavior and percent-escaping, and Resolve() flag>env>active>default precedence.
whatBreaks: Regressions in manifest parsing/tree/URL-building or context precedence resolution would ship undetected, risking wrong-tier command leaks or malformed request URLs.

role: manifest noun-verb command tree builder
description: Builds the noun→verb dispatch tree from a parsed Manifest, with O(1) lookup by noun+verb. Synthesizes noun nodes for commands whose noun wasn't declared, ensuring no capability is silently dropped. Used by the CLI for dispatch, help, and tab completion.
whatBreaks: CLI command dispatch, help output, and tab completion would break — commands from the manifest would not be routable.

role: fills flat path_template placeholders into an absolute request URL
description: BuildURL resolves :dataset/:workspace/:project and arbitrary arg placeholders, percent-escapes path segments, and gates the scoped_prefix mirror prepend behind ctx.ScopedMirror (currently inert since no server implements it). ArgLocation infers whether a declared arg rides in path/query/body.
whatBreaks: Every manifest-driven CLI command constructs its HTTP request URL through this file — a bug here sends requests to wrong/malformed/unescaped paths across the entire CLI surface.

role: Test for Command.ArgLocation/PathPlaceholders arg-routing inference
description: Covers every branch of deciding whether a CLI arg becomes a path segment, query param, or body field, based on placeholder names, method, explicit hints, and write flag.
whatBreaks: A misclassified arg location would send a value to the wrong place on the wire, silently breaking manifest-driven CLI commands.

role: Regression test for scope-named positional args in BuildURL
description: Locks in a previously-fixed bug where an explicit positional arg (e.g. dataset) sharing a name with an ambient ctx scope must win over the ctx fallback when building a manifest command's URL.
whatBreaks: Without this guard, a command like onixedit.export could silently target the wrong dataset by discarding the user's explicit positional argument.

role: Rectangularity lock for box-rendering TUI fixtures (columns/lanes/grid)
description: Asserts every non-blank line of box-producing pdrender fixtures is padded to the exact target width so borders/walls stay aligned; also proves the check isn't vacuous by reconstructing a known short-border bug.
whatBreaks: A ragged box render (misaligned borders) in the terminal Papers renderer could ship unnoticed, degrading visual quality of TUI diagrams.

role: loosely-typed JSON attribute readers shared by all pdrender block renderers
description: Helpers (attrStr, attrBool, attrInt, attrSlice, toStr) that coerce decoded JSON block attributes tolerantly, mirroring Elixir's to_string/1 and compose_block/2 coercion so the Go TUI renderer stays wire-compatible with the Phoenix side.
whatBreaks: Any pdrender block type reading a malformed/mistyped attribute would crash or render garbage in the terminal PortableDoc renderer — this is shared low-level plumbing for every block.

role: Test for attrInt float64-to-int coercion helper in pdrender
description: Checks attrInt handles whole floats, int64-range overflow, NaN, and Inf by falling back to a default rather than producing implementation-defined int() overflow.
whatBreaks: Malformed numeric attrs in a rendered document could crash or silently corrupt pdrender output for edge-case values.

role: Test for toStr float64-to-string formatting helper in pdrender
description: Verifies small integers render without trailing '.0' and very large floats fall back to FormatFloat rather than overflowing int64 conversion.
whatBreaks: Numeric block attributes could render incorrectly (garbled or wrong) for very large or edge-case values in TUI Papers.

role: M0 core block renderers: heading/paragraph/list/callout/divider/section/fallback
description: Implements the foundational block renderers (heading with underline rule, paragraph word-wrap, hanging-indent lists, tinted callouts, divider rule, and the recursing section renderer with grid-mode layout via the shared Flex solver) plus the never-crash fallback box for unknown block types. Direct port of render.ex's compose_block clauses for these types.

role: 2x4 braille dot-canvas rasteriser for TUI chart line-plots
description: Provides brailleCanvas with set/line(Bresenham)/column/rows to pack terminal-cell plots into Unicode braille glyphs at 8x spatial resolution; reused by chart.go's line/bar rendering, colored under TrueColor and mono-stable otherwise.
whatBreaks: Chart/line-plot blocks in the TUI Papers renderer would draw incorrectly or crash (out-of-range dot coordinates, wrong glyph composition) across all sparkline/chart-consuming surfaces.

role: TUI renderer for the `chart` PortableDoc block (braille line/bar plot)
description: Renders one or two numeric series as a braille step-line or bar chart in the terminal, with auto/pinned y-axis scaling, compact tick formatting, x-labels, and a legend. Enforces a hard 2-series cap and degrades gracefully on empty/malformed data; TrueColor-only per-series color, mono union otherwise.
whatBreaks: Chart blocks in Papers/CLI would render blank, panic, or show misleading scale/series data in the TUI reader.

role: Unit tests for chart.go (braille rasterization, axis pinning, series cap)
description: Pins exact braille glyph output for known strokes, verifies min/max axis pin behavior (including malformed-pin fallback), the 2-series cap fencing scale/plot/legend, and compact tick formatting thresholds.
whatBreaks: Regressions in chart scaling, series capping, or tick formatting could ship silently to the TUI reader.

role: standalone Bubble Tea demo binary exercising pdrender end-to-end
description: A `go run ./internal/pdrender/cmd/demo <paper.json>` CLI that decodes a portable-doc fixture and renders it in a scrollable viewport, used to visually verify pdrender output without the full barkpark TUI.
whatBreaks: Only the standalone demo tool breaks; no production surface depends on this binary.

role: CLI tool: renders a Bulldocs paper JSON fixture to stdout at fixed width
description: Non-interactive twin of cmd/demo used by verification scripts; reads a paper.json file, decodes it via pdrender.Decode, and prints the rendered doc using DefaultRegistry/DarkTheme at ANSI256.
whatBreaks: Verification/golden-fixture scripts that pipe paper JSON through `go run ./internal/pdrender/cmd/dump` would fail or produce wrong output, but no production path depends on it.

role: syntax-highlighted `code` block renderer via chroma with memoization
description: Renders code blocks with chroma-based highlighting, choosing a formatter by terminal color profile (avoiding truecolor ANSI-bleed in viewports) and caching renders keyed by content hash/width/theme/profile with a bounded cache size.

role: Unit tests for the code-block render memo cache (bounded size, theme/mode keying)
description: Verifies the code renderer's LRU-like cache stays bounded under heavy distinct input, hits on repeats, and is correctly keyed by both theme identity and light/dark mode (regression guard for a past cross-theme cache-collision bug).
whatBreaks: A long-running TUI session could leak memory (unbounded cache) or serve stale/wrong-theme code renders.

role: Cross-surface golden-parity test suite for TUI component renderers
description: Loads shared golden fixtures (generated by Elixir mix task, mirrored across api/web/TUI trees) and asserts the Go pdrender renderers (task-board, status-legend, note, card, pipeline, stage, task-detail, roadmap, columns, terminal) realize the same structural projection as the other two surfaces — the load-bearing spine proving TUI/web/Elixir agree on component structure.
whatBreaks: Silent three-surface divergence (TUI showing different labels/order/counts than web/Elixir) for every composed component block would go undetected.

role: TUI renderers for note/stage/card composition widgets
description: Implements terminal counterparts of the web reader's composition widgets: note (bar-prefixed definition row), stage (stacked kicker/title/detail/provenance cell), and card (bordered box with model-B media/title/body/action slots, including an image fast-path coercion). All degrade rather than panic on malformed/empty attrs.

role: Unit tests for note/stage/card renderers in composeblocks.go
description: Verifies never-panic degradation across malformed/empty inputs, the media-slot image fast-path (including scoping to just the media slot), and correct rendering order/content for each widget including MinWidth flat-degrade behavior.
whatBreaks: Regressions in note/stage/card rendering (panics, wrong slot order, leaked coercion) would ship unnoticed.

role: Regression tests for three specific TUI rendering bugs (width, multiline code, heatmap alignment)
description: Guards against bordered containers force-wrapping children (lipgloss padding-width bug), multi-line code collapsing to one line under colored profiles, and labeled heatmap columns drifting off their header — all defects surfaced by the portabledoc-showcase paper on 2026-07-08.
whatBreaks: Previously-fixed layout bugs (split borders, collapsed code lines, misaligned heatmap columns) could silently regress.

role: TUI renderer for the `dashboard` tabbed-container block
description: Renders authored tabs plus the active tab's child blocks arranged in a two-track grid via the shared Flex layout solver; the sole container-of-containers in the TUI creative slate. Go-only (web reader lacks a dashboard case, an accepted divergence); handles height budgeting, tab-strip rail geometry (ANSI-strip-safe active indicator), and $span token pass-through (inert, future resolver hook).
whatBreaks: Dashboard blocks would fail to compose child blocks correctly, mis-highlight the active tab, or blow past height budgets in the terminal reader.

role: JSON→[]Block decoder for portable-doc documents, with depth-cap DoS guard
description: Parses the `{version, blocks[]}` envelope (or bare block array) into pdrender's Block tree, recursing into section.blocks/figure.child up to maxBlockDepth=64 to prevent a maliciously nested document from crashing the process via Go's goroutine stack limit.
whatBreaks: A decode bug either crashes/DoSes the TUI on hostile documents or silently drops/corrupts nested block content for every rendered paper.

role: Unit tests for pdrender's block decoder (skip-invalid, depth-cap safety)
description: Asserts non-object/null block entries are skipped rather than crashing the reader, and that pathologically deep nested documents (figure.child and section.blocks chains) are truncated at maxBlockDepth instead of overflowing the stack — a forward-compat and DoS-safety guard for arbitrary document input.
whatBreaks: Malformed or adversarially deep PortableDoc JSON could crash the TUI/CLI reader (stack overflow) or render bogus unknown-type boxes.

role: Go tests for the embed block terminal renderer
description: Verifies embed blocks render their target (URL as OSC-8 hyperlink, or plain text for non-URL references) instead of falling through to the generic unknown-block fallback, and that empty targets degrade honestly with a placeholder glyph.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let embed blocks silently show 'Unsupported block' in the TUI/CLI while the web reader renders them fine, a cross-surface divergence that would go undetected.

role: Go tests for definition-list-style field block column alignment
description: Asserts that consecutive field-* blocks (field-string, field-slug, etc.) share one label column so all values line up, and that a single field still renders without panicking.
whatBreaks: A misaligned or reverted-to-per-field layout would make Papers with metadata fields (title/slug/dates) render as a ragged, harder-to-scan list in the TUI/CLI.

role: field-* leaf block renderers + aligned field-group definition-list layout
description: Renders field-string/boolean/select/datetime/color/reference/image as labeled two-line boxes, and RenderDoc collapses consecutive field blocks into an aligned label/value definition list (renderFieldGroup) reusing each field's own value logic.
whatBreaks: Document metadata fields (very common block type) would render misaligned, mislabeled, or with wrong resolved values (e.g. broken reference titles or color swatches).

role: render-only `form`/`questionnaire` block renderer (no input wiring)
description: Draws each question as a bordered fieldset with static radio/checkbox/scale/text placeholders, mirroring the HTML render-only contract; includes a DoS guard capping the scale ladder length.
whatBreaks: Form/questionnaire blocks would render incorrectly or, without the scale cap, could be abused for a render-time resource exhaustion.

role: Go regression test for scale-block ladder overflow guard
description: Single test proving a scale block with min/max whose span overflows int64 falls back to a compact '... ' rendering instead of panicking in a make([]string,...) call sized by the overflowing span.
whatBreaks: A crafted or malformed scale block (min/max far apart) could panic the whole RenderDoc call, taking down rendering for an entire document in the TUI/CLI.

role: TUI renderer for the gauge-list block (proportion-bar rows)
description: Implements the terminal counterpart of a meter/gauge-list widget in two modes: 'count' buckets a verbatim bp task-list snapshot by a groupBy field (status/worker/phase/priority), 'share' draws author-supplied {label,value} rows; both render via the shared statBar fill primitive so the datum survives ANSI stripping. Degrades honestly to a placeholder when required data is absent, and explicitly refuses to fake 'epic' grouping until a dedicated aggregate resolver exists.
whatBreaks: Task-list dashboards rendered in the TUI/CLI/Papers reader would show wrong bucket counts, misaligned bars, or a divide-by-zero panic on all-zero/degenerate task data.

role: Shared test harness enforcing the pdrender ANSI 'strip law' invariant
description: Executable counterpart of the TUI render doctrine: renders the same block at NoColor/ANSI256/TrueColor and asserts stripping all ANSI escapes from the colored renders yields byte-identical output to the NoColor render, i.e. color is reinforcement only, never the sole data carrier. Also documents a load-bearing gotcha that pdrender's Profile enum and termenv's Profile enum are numbered in opposite directions.
whatBreaks: Every data-viz block (heatmap, chart, stat, gauge-list, image mosaic) could silently ship a color-profile bug — e.g. a NO_COLOR terminal receiving unreadable output or losing data that only existed as color — without any test catching it, since this file is the shared assertion all of them rely on.

role: TUI renderers for notes/pipeline/cards/status-legend grid widgets
description: Implements the terminal counterparts of four PortableDoc grid widgets that previously fell through to the unknown-block fallback: notes and pipeline reuse the singular note/stage renderers on synthesized child blocks and stack vertically by default with an opt-in side-by-side grid layout via the shared Flex solver; cards draws its own tone-tinted rounded box per item; status-legend renders a fixed 6-rung status ladder that must stay byte-synced with design/status-manifest.json (checked by scripts/status-manifest-check.sh). Also defines the shared role→glyph/label/meaning vocabulary (roleGlyph, roleLabel, roleMeaning) reused by task-list/detail/board/roadmap widgets.

role: Go tests: grid-block renderers never panic on malformed input
description: Exercises notes/pipeline/cards/status-legend with missing keys, wrong types, empty lists, all-empty items, unknown tones, and non-object elements across multiple widths, asserting no panic since PortableDoc content is API-served and attacker-controllable.
whatBreaks: A malicious or malformed grid block in a document could crash the entire RenderDoc call in the TUI/CLI, taking down rendering for a whole page rather than degrading gracefully.

role: diagram/asciicast/image "honest fallback" placeholder renderers
description: Renders Mermaid diagrams (falling back to folded-source box when not drawable), asciicast metadata placeholders, and image placeholders/mosaics — each labeled rather than faking an unsupported terminal capability; shares boxStyle/boxLines chrome helpers used across the package.

role: TUI renderer for heatmap block (legacy grid, calendar, matrix modes)
description: Draws a 2D numeric grid as a row-major intensity heatmap with three modes: legacy linear value/max shade or truecolor ramp, a GitHub-style contribution calendar (quantile-binned), and matrix marginals/values. Auto-degrades truecolor to shade glyphs outside a TrueColor profile so raw 24-bit escapes never leak to incapable terminals; defines HeatQuantileBins as the canonical quantile-binning capability reused across modes, and the shared cell primitives (heatCell/heatShadeGlyph/heatTrueColor) that later slate blocks build on.

role: Go tests for heatmap truecolor auto-degrade behavior
description: Proves the load-bearing invariant that a 24-bit foreground escape appears in heatmap output IFF ramp is 'truecolor' AND ctx.Profile is TrueColor, and that a NoColor profile falls back to the shade ladder with no truecolor escape emitted.
whatBreaks: A profile-detection regression could leak raw ANSI truecolor escape sequences into a NO_COLOR pipe or 256-color terminal, corrupting output or making it unreadable.

role: TUI renderer for embedding real images via half-block mosaic
description: Decodes PNG/JPEG/GIF bytes and renders them as a scroll-safe half-block (▀) truecolor mosaic — two vertical pixels per terminal cell via foreground/background SGR — chosen over graphics protocols (kitty/iTerm2/sixel) because those don't survive bubbletea viewport line-slicing. Box-sample downscales without upscaling, composites alpha against the theme's page background, and auto-degrades to a labeled '(view in Studio)' box outside TrueColor profile, on decode failure, oversized input, or a nil image resolver.
whatBreaks: Images embedded in Papers/PortableDoc content would either crash the TUI/CLI on malformed or oversized image bytes, or fail to render correctly (wrong colors, wrong scale, or broken viewport scrolling) in truecolor terminals.

role: Test for pdrender's terminal image-mosaic (truecolor) renderer
description: Builds synthetic PNGs and asserts the mosaic renderer emits correct 24-bit SGR runs, using a TrueColor termenv profile override helper (withTrueColor) shared across tests.
whatBreaks: A regression in the image-mosaic ANSI color mapping would ship unnoticed, corrupting inline image rendering in the TUI/CLI.

role: inline node renderer (marks, links, wikilinks, valueref, task chips) + sanitizers
description: Ports render.ex's compose_inline/apply_marks to ANSI styling, handles link OSC 8 hyperlinks, wikilink task-chip resolution, valueref live-value resolution, and defines the security-critical sanitizeText/sanitizeURL functions that strip terminal control bytes and enforce a URL scheme allowlist across the whole package.

role: Shared Flex layout solver for terminal side-by-side surfaces
description: Defines the single Measure/Arrange/ArrangeGrid two-pass algebra (Flex, Node, joinColumns, gridRows) that columns, section grids, and task-board lanes all delegate to for width division, degrade-to-stack decisions, and ANSI-aware padding/joining; also hosts gap/track/span/order attribute parsing mirroring compose.ex.

role: Unit tests for the Flex layout solver (Measure/Arrange/gridRows)
description: Pins the divide-formula, MinWidth boundary behavior, and ANSI-aware column joining of joincols.go with exact boundary-case expectations, guarding the shared layout primitive against regression.
whatBreaks: A weakened or removed test would let a silent regression into the shared side-by-side layout arithmetic used by three+ renderers.

role: Renderers for PortableDoc `columns` and `terminal` container blocks
description: Implements the TUI/CLI counterparts of the web reader's columns and terminal-chrome container widgets, using the Flex solver for side-by-side layout with degrade-to-stack, and recursing children through the block registry; every string is sanitized before display.

role: Panic-safety and rendering tests for columns/terminal blocks
description: Feeds layoutblocks.go a battery of empty/malformed/degenerate Attrs across multiple widths to assert it never panics on attacker-controlled PortableDoc content, only degrades gracefully.
whatBreaks: Losing this coverage risks a crash-on-malformed-input regression reaching production, since document content is API-served and untrusted.

role: Unit test for markHref link-mark href resolution
description: Small table-driven test covering nested attrs.href vs top-level href fallback logic feeding the OSC-8 terminal hyperlink path.
whatBreaks: A regression in markHref lookup could drop or mis-target terminal hyperlinks in rendered documents, unnoticed without this test.

role: Dependency-free Mermaid flowchart/sequenceDiagram subset parser
description: Hand-rolled, regexp-based parser turning Mermaid flowchart/graph and sequenceDiagram source into neutral mmGraph/mmSequence models consumed by the layout renderers; unparseable input degrades to kind=="" so callers fall back to a folded-source box rather than a half-drawn diagram.
whatBreaks: A parsing bug misreads node shapes, edges, or sequence messages, producing wrong or missing terminal Mermaid diagrams across the TUI/CLI reader.

role: Unit tests for the Mermaid subset parser (shapes/edges/labels)
description: Covers node-shape, edge-style, and label grammar parsing that the flowchart layout engine (mermaidflow.go) depends on for correctness.
whatBreaks: Weakened coverage lets a Mermaid grammar regression (wrong shape/edge parsing) reach the rendered terminal diagrams undetected.

role: Test for many-to-many flowchart band-crossing deferral to legend
description: Verifies that when a connector band would need an ambiguous many-to-many bus, mermaidflow.go correctly draws only unambiguous vertical edges and defers crossing edges to the edge legend rather than drawing a misleading tangle.
whatBreaks: Regression here could let ambiguous crossing edges render as a misleading tangled bus, or silently drop edges from both the diagram and the legend.

role: Layered-DAG terminal renderer for parsed Mermaid flowcharts
description: Turns an mmGraph into ranked rows of box-drawn nodes joined by orthogonal connector bands (Sugiyama-style rank assignment + median crossing reduction), deferring skip-rank/back/ambiguous edges to a text legend; every emitted line is width-padded to guarantee rectangularity.

role: Left-to-right Mermaid flowchart canvas renderer (Go TUI)
description: Draws Mermaid flowchart LR/RL diagrams onto a fixed 2-D rune canvas with a per-cell style mask (wire vs text), routing horizontal connector bands between ranks and returning nil when the layout can't fit so the caller falls back to the TD engine. Core rendering logic for pdrender's terminal Mermaid diagram support.
whatBreaks: LR-oriented and auto-oriented chain flowcharts in the TUI Paper/PortableDoc renderer would misdraw boxes/arrows or silently fail to degrade to TD, corrupting diagram blocks.

role: Unit tests for the LR flowchart canvas renderer
description: Verifies renderFlowchartLR produces perfectly rectangular output at multiple widths and non-vacuously draws boxes and arrows for linear/tree/fan graph shapes.
whatBreaks: A regression collapsing LR rendering to blank or overflowing output would go undetected, letting broken diagrams ship.

role: Heuristic strategy selector for Mermaid flowchart rendering (TD/LR/tree)
description: Measures a parsed flowchart graph (chain, overflow, mesh) and picks between TD box-art, LR box-art, or an indented tree-text degradation, then implements the tree-view renderer itself; this is the decision layer that all flowchart rendering flows through (renderFlowchartAuto).
whatBreaks: Any Mermaid flowchart in the TUI/Paper renderer could pick the wrong layout strategy (crushed boxes, misleading legend-heavy diagrams, or wrong orientation), affecting every diagram block in Papers.

role: Unit tests for flowchart strategy heuristics
description: Asserts chain graphs auto-orient LR when wide and stay TD when narrow, forks stay TD, and overflow/mesh graphs fall to the tree view.
whatBreaks: Strategy-selection regressions (e.g. wrong TD/LR/tree choice) would ship silently, degrading diagram readability across the TUI.

role: Mermaid sequenceDiagram lifeline-ladder renderer (Go TUI)
description: Lays out sequenceDiagram participants as columns using the shared Flex solver and draws a responsive message ladder (arrows, self-loops, dashed/cross styles) into a fixed-width buffer; returns nil to fall back to folded-source when columns can't fit even compacted.
whatBreaks: Sequence diagrams in Papers/PortableDoc would render garbled ladders, misaligned arrows, or fail to degrade gracefully at narrow widths.

role: Unit tests for Mermaid sequence diagram parsing/rendering
description: Covers actor declaration parsing (participant/actor/alias) and arrow-style decoding, including a greedy-dash edge case (DB-->>API must not misparse a phantom actor).
whatBreaks: A parser regression (e.g. the greedy-dash trap) could silently create phantom actors or wrong message styles in rendered sequence diagrams.

role: Unit tests for distinct Mermaid node shape glyphs
description: Asserts each Mermaid node shape (rect, rounded, stadium, circle, diamond, hexagon, subroutine, cylinder) renders a distinct signature glyph and stays width-locked, guarding against shape families collapsing together.
whatBreaks: A shape-rendering regression could make diagrams visually ambiguous (e.g. diamonds and hexagons looking identical) without any test failing.

role: Cross-widget no-overflow regression lock for pdrender fixtures
description: Renders a curated set of fixtures (columns, task lanes, grids, breakpoint reflow, side-by-side widgets) at multiple widths and asserts no line ever exceeds the target width — the broadest blast-radius guard for column-math off-by-one bugs across the whole renderer.
whatBreaks: Any width-overflow bug across columns/grid/pipeline/notes/cards widgets in the TUI renderer would go undetected, corrupting terminal output layout broadly.

role: pdrender package root: Block/RenderCtx/Registry types + resolver seams + DefaultRegistry wiring
description: Defines the core Block, RenderCtx, Renderer interface, all resolver seams (RefResolver/CodelistResolver/TaskResolver/ValueResolver/ImageResolver), and DefaultRegistry which wires every block-type renderer (heading through dashboard) into the dispatch map. It is the terminal counterpart to api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render.ex and is import-clean (only lipgloss/x/ansi/stdlib) by design so the package can be extracted as a standalone module.

role: Adapter: pipeline blocks with layout:flow render as a linear Mermaid flowchart
description: Builds a neutral mmGraph directly from pipeline node data (no mermaid text round-trip) and hands it to renderFlowchartAuto, giving pipeline blocks the same LR-fits-else-TD degrade ladder as native flowcharts; only active when a block opts in via layout:{mode:"flow"}.
whatBreaks: Pipeline blocks opting into flow layout would render incorrectly (wrong chain order, missing labels, or crash) while default pipeline rendering stays unaffected.

role: Golden test for M10 side-by-side grid layout (notes/pipeline/cards)
description: Renders a fixture with notes/pipeline/cards blocks using layout:{mode:"grid"} and checks the shared Flex solver lays them horizontally at wide widths and collapses to vertical stacks at narrow widths, byte-stable via NoColor pinning.
whatBreaks: A regression in the shared Flex/grid solver for these widget types would silently break horizontal-to-vertical responsive collapse in the TUI Paper renderer.

role: Golden test for TUI heatmap block renderer (slate W1)
description: Renders the M11 heatmap fixture (shade grid + truecolor ramp) at pinned NoColor profile across golden widths and byte-diffs against checked-in goldens under testdata/golden. Proves truecolor ramps auto-degrade to the deterministic shade ladder with no 24-bit escapes; regenerate via -update flag.
whatBreaks: A regression in heatmap rendering or its NoColor degrade path would go undetected, letting broken TUI heatmap output ship silently.

role: Golden test for TUI stat/KPI block renderer (slate W2)
description: Renders the M12 stat/KPI fixture (big-number, bullet-bar, standalone cells) at NoColor profile and byte-locks output against goldens at multiple widths. Establishes the baseline statCell rendering later extended by M19's denom feature.
whatBreaks: Silent breakage of KPI/stat block layout in the TUI renderer, and the M19 backward-compat guarantee (denom-less cells unchanged) would lose its anchor.

role: Golden test for TUI braille chart block renderer (slate capstone W3)
description: Renders the M13 braille-glyph chart fixture at NoColor profile and diffs against goldens across widths; braille glyphs are ANSI-plain so output is deterministic without color stripping concerns beyond the norm.
whatBreaks: Chart rendering regressions (braille plotting, axis/tick logic) would ship undetected in the TUI.

role: Golden test for TUI task-detail timeline block (au-w5 capstone)
description: Renders the M14 task-detail-timeline fixture at NoColor profile and byte-locks it against goldens; this is the content-parity capstone proving the task-detail TUI view matches other surfaces.
whatBreaks: Task-detail timeline rendering could drift from the GUI/CLI without detection, breaking cross-surface content parity.

role: Golden test proving live-data query resolution flows into TUI renderers
description: Renders resolved chart/heatmap/stat Attrs (exactly as Elixir's TaskResolver.shape/2 stamps them) to prove the Go renderer draws live data correctly and unresolved (query-only) blocks degrade to a dim placeholder; also covers the max-2-series cap on charts. Golden-locks output at four widths.
whatBreaks: The Elixir query-resolution → Go-render contract (shape/2 output shape) could silently diverge, breaking live data visualization in the TUI/offline renders across all consuming surfaces.

role: Golden test for TUI card block with image media slot (model-B shape)
description: Renders a warn-tone card fixture with a typed image media slot at NoColor profile, verifying border structure, image fast-path box, and media-first slot ordering survive color stripping; byte-locked across widths.
whatBreaks: Card layout regressions (border chars, media slot positioning) in the TUI would go unnoticed.

role: Golden test for TUI heat-family blocks: quantile calendar + matrix
description: Renders the M17 heat-family fixture covering calendar mode (quantile dual-encoded, week-dropping at narrow widths) and a rows x cols matrix with sum marginals; byte-locked at multiple widths, cross-referenced against sample_m26 for the full-year >80-col path.
whatBreaks: Calendar/matrix heat-family rendering (week truncation logic, marginal sums) could regress silently in the TUI.

role: Golden test for TUI gauge-list block (meter bars, count/share modes)
description: Renders the M18 gauge-list fixture (count-by-worker and share modes) at NoColor profile, asserting the label column, bar-length geometry, and right-aligned digits survive since color/tint is stripped — embodies the 'detail-ceiling doctrine' that geometry carries the datum.
whatBreaks: Gauge/meter bar length or alignment regressions in the TUI would ship undetected, misrepresenting proportions to users.

role: Golden test for stat KPI cell optional denominator feature
description: Renders the M19 fixture mixing denom-bearing and denom-less stat cells (grid, singular, and bullet-bar-with-both) to prove the dim '/<denom>' rendering and that denom-less cells stay byte-identical to pre-existing M12/M15 goldens (backward-compat law).
whatBreaks: The denom feature could break either its own rendering or silently regress the pre-existing statCell backward-compatibility guarantee.

role: test for pdrender reference-resolver seam (M1)
description: Golden-file test suite for pdrender M1 milestone covering reference block rendering with a stub ref-resolver seam, asserting terminal output at multiple column widths.
whatBreaks: Reference block rendering regressions in the TUI paper-viewer go undetected across all PortableDoc fixtures.

role: Golden test for chart compact-unit y-ticks + max-2-series cap
description: Renders the M20 fixture proving formatTickCompact SI-style tick formatting (e.g. 12500 -> '12.5k') activates only above the 10000 threshold, and that a 3-series chart is capped to the first two series for both plotting and auto-scaling; byte-locked at four widths plus a separate strip-law test across profiles.
whatBreaks: Chart tick formatting could regress to crowded raw digits, or the series cap could stop being enforced, letting an unbounded chart overflow the render or mis-scale the axis.

role: Golden-render regression test for M21 typed table columns
