role: Golden fixture for PortableDoc 'stage' component structural parity
description: Generated by `mix barkpark.paper_components.gen_golden_parity`; asserts pdrender's stage/gate node structural projection matches design/status-manifest.json via Render.StatusVocab, mirrored against api View tests and the web reader.
whatBreaks: pdrender's stage component test would no longer catch drift from the status vocabulary shared with the web/api renderers.

role: Golden fixture for status-legend component glyph/role parity
description: Generated golden file listing the six status rows (open/ready/progress/blocked/done/cancel) with glyphs and roles, used to assert pdrender's status-legend renders the same structural vocabulary as the api and web surfaces.
whatBreaks: A status-legend rendering regression or glyph/role mismatch across surfaces would go undetected.

role: Human-readable snapshot of emitted pdrender design tokens
description: Plain-text table of status tones, chrome/reading role colors, and reading font/type tokens as emitted from design/tokens.json — likely a golden/reference doc consumed by a styleguide test or doc, not executable code.
whatBreaks: If stale relative to tokens_gen.go, a styleguide golden comparison could false-pass or false-fail, but no runtime behavior is affected directly.

role: Golden fixture for task-board PortableDoc component structural parity
description: Generated golden file with expected board columns (open/ready/progress/etc.), card titles, and counts, used to lock pdrender's task-board rendering against the shared status vocabulary and other surfaces.
whatBreaks: Task-board rendering regressions or cross-surface structural drift (columns/roles/counts) would go undetected.

role: Golden fixture for task-detail PortableDoc component structural parity
description: Generated golden file asserting task-detail's sections (meta/timeline/criteria/labels), timeline roles, and criteria counts render consistently in pdrender vs api/web.
whatBreaks: Task-detail component structural regressions across surfaces would go undetected by tests.

role: Golden fixture for terminal PortableDoc component structural parity
description: Generated golden file locking the 'terminal' block's container role, title, footer, live flag, and children (paragraph) projection for cross-surface parity testing.
whatBreaks: Terminal block rendering regressions or drift from the shared status/structural vocabulary would go undetected.

role: pdrender's injected color/style palette (Theme) builder
description: Defines the Theme struct (lipgloss styles for headings, body, callouts, buttons, etc.) and buildTheme/ThemeFor/DarkTheme/LightTheme which resolve a theme identity + light/dark mode into concrete styles without importing package main's styles.go, keeping pdrender decoupled while mirroring the same palette via a re-emitted internal Palette.

role: Generated Go source of pdrender's design-token color/theme palettes
description: Auto-generated (via design/emit.mjs from design/tokens.json) file defining lipgloss AdaptiveColor tone/chrome/reading tokens and the genPalette map (evergreen/ember/fjord themes) with Resolve(theme) lookup; the styleguide golden test depends on these exact bytes, and theme.go's buildTheme reads Resolve(). DO NOT EDIT by hand.

role: pdrender renderers for v2 nested field block types
description: Implements Render for composite/arrayOf/codelist/localizedText block types, flattening nested JSON field values into readable labelled rows (mirroring Elixir's Render.Compose.composite_scalar/1), with a JSON-dump opt-out via ctx.V2AsJSON.
whatBreaks: Documents using composite, arrayOf, codelist, or localizedText v2 fields would render incorrectly or crash in the TUI/CLI/WASM reader, or silently diverge from the Elixir Studio rendering.

role: Go tests for pdrender's inline live-value (valueref) resolution/fallback
description: Tests the ValueResolver seam: resolved values, empty/nil resolver fallback, dot-path fields never resolving, ANSI-injection sanitization, and unknown-inline-type degrade-gracefully behavior, driven by shared JSON fixtures under testdata/portable-doc-inline/.
whatBreaks: Regressions in live-value fallback safety or terminal-injection sanitization for inline valueref nodes in TUI-rendered PortableDocs would go undetected, risking terminal hijack or blank/incorrect text.

role: Provisioner worker logic to attach a custom domain to a live cloud instance
description: Implements the attach-domain job: validates the control-plane payload defensively (regex-gated custom host/DNS label, IP, port), upserts a DNS A record, merges the origin into BARKPARK_EXTRA_ORIGINS, appends an on-demand-TLS Caddy vhost, validates+reloads Caddy, and restarts the app — all steps idempotent so retries are safe.
whatBreaks: A validation gap could let a hostile/malformed custom_host reach a live Caddyfile or shell script (RCE/config-corruption risk), while a logic bug could leave a live box with 403'd LiveView (missing check_origin) or a broken/duplicated Caddy vhost, taking the attached domain offline.

role: Tests for the custom-domain attach worker executor (DNS+SSH)
description: Exercises DefaultAttachDomain/attachDomainSteps end-to-end via fake DNS + fake StepRunner: happy path (DNS-before-SSH ordering), hostile-spec validation aborts (shell metachars, foreign zone, label mismatch), fail-reporting on SSH failure, idempotency of the env-merge/vhost-append scripts, and nil-seam no-op. Encodes the security contract that the worker never trusts control-plane input before it reaches a shell script or Caddyfile.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a hostile or malformed attach-domain job execute shell/DNS mutations on a customer box, or silently break custom-domain attachment.

role: Tests wiring the dwb-4 content bootstrap into the provision chain
description: Proves ProvisionWith runs the injected Bootstrap seam only when a job carries a Template, with the correct BootstrapRequest (base URL, admin token, job identity); that a bootstrap failure tears down the box+DNS and fails through existing machinery; and that bootstrap outputs (read token, env map) ride the worker's succeed body to the control plane, while template-less jobs keep the succeed body back-compat lean.
whatBreaks: A break here could leave a provisioned box half-alive (server running, no content) after a failed template bootstrap, or leak/omit the read token from the control-plane succeed report.

role: Embedded deploy-template catalog for the provisioner binary
description: go:embed's the three deploy templates (blog-starter, place-directory, website-starter) copied from repo-root templates/, parses+validates each barkpark.template.json manifest at package init (panics on malformed bundle), and exposes Get(name)/Names() so the post-provision bootstrap step can stand up content with no checkout on the worker host.
whatBreaks: A bad or missing embed would panic the provisioner binary at startup, or make dwb-4 template bootstrap fail/produce wrong schemas+seed content for every new customer instance using that template.

role: Tests for the embedded template catalog + repo-root drift tripwire
description: Verifies Names()/Get() return the three known templates with valid schema/seed bytes, unknown-slug returns (nil,false), and TestEmbeddedCatalogMatchesRepoRoot fails the build if the embedded copy under catalog/templates/ ever drifts byte-for-byte from the canonical repo-root templates/ (both directions: missing sync and un-embedded new templates).
whatBreaks: Without this drift tripwire, editing only the repo-root template (or only the embedded copy) would silently ship stale/inconsistent schema or seed content to new customer instances.

role: Manifest for the blog-starter deploy template (embedded copy)
description: Declares the blog-starter template's Next.js framework, dataset, seed config, and required env vars (API URL, read token, workspace/project/dataset, webhook secret) that dwb-4 bootstrap wires into a freshly provisioned instance. Must stay byte-identical to the repo-root templates/blog-starter/barkpark.template.json (enforced by catalog_test.go).
whatBreaks: Wrong schema/seed/env wiring here breaks the blog-starter one-click deploy flow for every new customer picking that template.

role: Schema definition for the blog-starter 'post' content type
description: Defines the post document type's fields (slug, excerpt, body, published_at) that gets applied to a fresh instance's Barkpark schema during template bootstrap. Embedded copy synced from repo-root templates/blog-starter/schemas/post.json.
whatBreaks: A malformed or mismatched schema would break blog-starter provisioning or make the seeded posts fail to validate/publish.

role: Seed content mutations for a new blog-starter instance
description: Two demo `post` documents (createOrReplace mutations) published into a freshly bootstrapped blog-starter instance so the site isn't empty on first deploy.
whatBreaks: Broken seed JSON would fail the bootstrap seed step, leaving a new blog-starter instance with no demo content (cosmetic, not fatal).

role: Manifest for the place-directory deploy template (embedded copy)
description: Declares the place-directory template (powers hundesteder.no-style map sites): Next.js framework, dataset, seed config, and env vars including a literal NEXT_PUBLIC_FINDER_LANDING=map flag plus the standard read-token/workspace/webhook-secret set. Must stay byte-identical to the repo-root canonical copy.
whatBreaks: Wrong env/schema wiring here breaks the place-directory one-click deploy flow, including the public landing-page flag that switches the demo site into map mode.

role: Schema definition for the place-directory 'place' content type
description: Defines the place document type's fields including composite geo (lat/long) and address sub-objects, category/city/tags — the schema a fresh place-directory instance validates seed and future editorial content against.
whatBreaks: A malformed schema would break place-directory provisioning or make map pins/seed data fail to validate against the deployed schema.

role: Seed content mutations for a new place-directory instance
description: Twelve demo `place` documents (Norwegian cafés/parks/sights with coordinates) published as createOrReplace mutations so a freshly bootstrapped place-directory instance ships with a populated map on first deploy.
whatBreaks: Broken seed JSON would fail the bootstrap seed step, leaving a new place-directory instance with an empty map (cosmetic, not fatal).

role: Catalog manifest for the website-starter provisioning template
description: Declares the minimal marketing-site template (a `page` schema, seed content, and the server-side env vars a Next.js site needs) that dwb-4 bootstrap wires into a freshly provisioned instance. Consumed by internal/provisioner/catalog at embed time.
whatBreaks: A malformed manifest breaks template bootstrap for every new instance launched with website-starter, or ships the wrong env var names to the generated site.

role: Schema definition for the website-starter template's `page` document type
description: Defines the fields (slug, heading, subheading, body) bootstrap creates in a new instance's schema registry; referenced by barkpark.template.json's `schemas` list.
whatBreaks: Seed content (seed-pages.json) would fail to publish or the generated site would render missing/wrong fields.

role: Seed content mutations for a new website-starter instance
description: Two createOrReplace mutations (home, about pages) applied and published during dwb-4 content bootstrap so a fresh site isn't empty.
whatBreaks: New website-starter instances launch with no home/about pages, or bootstrap errors if the mutation shape drifts from the page schema.

role: Manual, build-tagged live E2E harness for the real Hetzner provisioning chain
description: go:build manual test that runs the actual one-shot ProvisionOneShot chain against live Hetzner (creates real billed servers/DNS), never run in CI; includes belt-and-suspenders cleanup sweeping bp-*/warm-* stragglers.
whatBreaks: Only affects manual operator verification of the live provisioning path; broken harness risks orphaned billed servers during a manual run, not production correctness.

role: Live console-narration reporter + redaction for the provisioning worker
description: Defines ConsoleReporter/HTTPConsoleReporter (POSTs narration lines to control-plane's per-job console endpoint) and consoleEmitter, which redacts secrets (admin tokens, env-secret patterns) and latches off after maxConsoleFails consecutive failures; pure telemetry, never fails a provision.
whatBreaks: Broken redaction could leak secrets (admin tokens, DB URLs, KEK) into the persisted/streamed console log — a real security exposure; broken reporting silently kills the /new live console UX but not provisioning itself.

role: Unit tests for console redaction and failure-swallowing behavior
description: Verifies redactConsoleLine scrubs admin tokens, KEK values, and registered literal secrets, and that a first-call-failing reporter never breaks the provision (via consoleRec fake).
whatBreaks: A regression in secret redaction (e.g. leaked KEK) would ship undetected, risking cross-tenant secret exposure via console narration.

role: Worker-side handler that deletes a claimed instance (server + DNS)
description: DeprovisionSpec is the wire shape from the control-plane's claim endpoint; DeprovisionWith/DefaultDeprovision bridge to cloud.WarmPool.DeprovisionByIP, idempotent by design (delete-if-exists).
whatBreaks: A broken deprovision path leaves paid Hetzner servers and DNS records orphaned after a user deletes their instance, or worse, deletes the wrong server if IP matching is wrong.

role: Tests for the deprovision worker against a fake control-plane HTTP server
description: fakeDeprovisionControlPlane stands in for the Elixir claim/succeed/fail endpoints (dwb deprovision-queue), asserting claim-token echoing and request/response wire shape.
whatBreaks: A wire-shape mismatch between worker and Elixir control plane could go undetected, causing deprovision jobs to fail silently or double-claim in production.

role: Core create-to-live provisioning chain orchestrator (ProvisionWith)
description: The central function that runs the full go-live chain for one job: provider routing (Hetzner vs Azure/registry), warm-pool assign-or-one-shot acquisition, content bootstrap, golden-path VERIFY gate, and teardown-on-failure at every step; also hosts SweepFunc for orphan recovery and Seams struct wiring every injected dependency. This is the highest-criticality file in the batch — the money-and-correctness hot path for all instance provisioning.
whatBreaks: Any bug here can create billed orphan servers, provision instances with leaked/wrong secrets, skip the golden-path verify (shipping login-dead instances), or misroute Azure jobs onto the Hetzner warm pool.

role: Test proving Azure jobs route through the provider registry, not the Hetzner warm pool
description: Asserts kind=azure jobs use cloud.ProviderFor (registry-resolved provider) with pool forced to zero even when a ready Hetzner warm box exists, guarding S6's multi-cloud routing contract.
whatBreaks: A routing regression could provision an Azure job onto a Hetzner warm box (wrong cloud, wrong credentials) or leave the Hetzner pool silently drained by non-Hetzner jobs.

role: Unit tests for the normal provision (launch) flow
description: Exercises the happy-path and failure-path provision worker logic with fake HealthChecker, StepRunner and freshen/warm-create seams, including redaction of secrets from error output. Large table-driven test file covering the core provisioning state machine.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a broken provision flow (e.g. leaked tokens, wrong teardown-on-failure behavior) ship unnoticed.

role: Resurrect (portable-restore) orchestration chain for provisioner jobs
description: Implements provisionRestore, the seven-step (create→freshen→secure→configure→content→verify→ready) state machine that rebuilds an instance from a bundle archive onto a fresh box, cold-creating and never warm-assigning, carrying (not minting) the KEK, and tearing down half-restored boxes on any step failure. Defines the RestoreDriver interface seam that the real cloud executor and test fakes both implement.
whatBreaks: A bug here could restore the wrong database, fail to tear down a billed half-restored box (orphan cost), or mint a fresh identity instead of carrying the sealed one, breaking cross-provider disaster recovery.

role: Worker-side adapter wiring resurrect claims to the real cloud RestoreDriver
description: Decodes the control-plane's resurrect claim JSON (bundle_ref as string) into a JobSpec with a resolved *BundleRef, resolves object-store/KEK credentials from worker env (never from claim JSON), and implements CloudRestoreDriver which delegates to cloud.RestoreExecutor plus reuses the golden-path verify gate.
whatBreaks: Wrong translation of a resurrect claim or leaking KEK/credentials via the claim path would break restores or leak secrets across the control plane boundary.

role: Component tests for resurrect worker-env resolvers
description: Covers ResolveBundleEnv's required-var validation and success path, plus other pure helpers not reached by the full resurrect scenario tests.
whatBreaks: A missing required bundle-store var could silently pass, causing resurrect jobs to run with incomplete restore configuration.

role: End-to-end offline test of the resurrect/restore round trip
description: Uses a recording StepRunner/StdinStepRunner plus tar/gzip bundle fixtures and an httptest fake instance to prove the whole restore chain (create, freshen, configure, restore-data with piped stdin, verify) works without touching real infra.
whatBreaks: Loss of coverage here would let regressions in the cross-provider resurrect path (a Decision-12 bet) go undetected.

role: Tests for warm-image/snapshot generation resolution and recycling
description: Sets up a hermetic TestMain that stubs cloud.WarmImageLister/WarmServerImageLister (never shelling out to hcloud in tests) and provides fixture installers for warm-image generation matching logic used by warm-create/freshen paths.
whatBreaks: If hermeticity here fails, tests could hit the live Hetzner API; if the generation-matching logic is wrong, stale warm images could be reused for launches.

role: HTTP client that POSTs provision step-transition telemetry to the control plane
description: HTTPStepReporter.Report sends coarse step status (started/progress/done/failed) to /v1/internal/provision-jobs/{id}/step with a short timeout and shared WORKER_TOKEN; explicitly telemetry-only (errors are swallowed by callers, never fail a provision).
whatBreaks: A bug would only degrade live provision narration in the control-plane UI, not the correctness of provisioning itself, since callers swallow its errors.

role: Component tests for HTTPStepReporter
description: Drives the production step-reporter's HTTP calls (auth header, body marshaling, status handling) against an httptest control plane across success/error/transport-failure branches.
whatBreaks: A broken step reporter could silently fail to report provisioning progress to the control plane, hiding real failures from operators.

role: Unit test for a UTF-8-safe string truncation helper
description: Small focused test proving truncate() cuts on rune boundaries (not byte boundaries) so multibyte characters like Norwegian æ stay valid UTF-8 with correct rune counts.
whatBreaks: Only risk is malformed UTF-8 in truncated error/log strings shown to operators; no functional provisioning impact.

role: Golden-path VERIFY gate run after provisioning, before a box is marked ready
description: Runs three ordered HTTP probes (verify.api, verify.login with a deliberately-wrong sentinel credential, verify.studio via the shared health-gate hop walker) against a live instance to catch the #957 class of failure where a box answers health checks but the auth/session stack is dead on arrival (bad SECRET_KEY_BASE). First red probe fails the whole provision and triggers teardown.
whatBreaks: A weakened or broken verify gate would let broken/insecure boxes (dead auth stack, or leaked tokens in evidence strings) go live and be marked ready, directly undermining the safety net for every launch and resurrect.

role: Cross-language fixture-parity test for the verify probe vocabulary
description: Reads the shared cloud/priv/static/__fixtures__/verify_probes.json fixture (also asserted against by the Elixir on-demand executor) to ensure the compiled Go VERIFY gate and the Elixir re-runnable executor never drift in probe names/order/pass-rules — explicitly named as the D53 one-fixture-two-asserters tripwire.
whatBreaks: Undetected drift between the Go and Elixir verify implementations would mean a box's birth-certificate verify and its later on-demand re-verify could silently disagree.

role: Unit tests for the golden-path VERIFY gate against a fake instance
description: Spins up an httptest fake instance with tunable behavior (fakeInstanceBehavior) to drive each verify probe green/red, including simulating the #957 dead-on-arrival 500 on login and a redirect-loop on /studio to prove the gate correctly fails.
whatBreaks: Regressions here would let the verify gate's pass/fail logic degrade without detection, risking broken boxes being marked ready.

role: Go warm-pool client + reconcile/refill/refresh logic for cloud go-lives
description: Implements the WarmPoolClient HTTP transport to the Elixir control plane's warm-server claim store, plus the orchestration that assigns a claimed warm box into a go-live (tryWarmAssign), refills/reconciles the pool to target size, and self-refreshes idle boxes to origin/main. Load-bearing money-safety logic: fail-closed on new-box freshen, fail-open on existing-box refresh, claim-fence tokens to avoid double-consuming a row.
whatBreaks: A bug here could double-assign a warm box to two customers, leak billed orphan Hetzner servers, or serve a stale (pre-deploy) box on a fast go-live.

role: Tests for warm-pool region/server_type pin-compatibility guard
description: Verifies warmSpecCompatible and that a pinned go-live whose region/type differs from the pool's baked spec falls through to a one-shot create instead of wrongly consuming a warm box; also verifies unpinned launches still take the fast warm path.
whatBreaks: An unnoticed regression could let a pinned go-live silently receive a wrong-region/wrong-size warm box.

role: Test suite for warm-pool claim/assign/reconcile/refill/HTTP transport
description: In-memory fake WarmPoolClient plus tests covering empty-pool fallback, warm-assign happy path + async refill, assign-failure teardown, reconciler grow/shrink and claimed-box protection, fail-closed freshen behavior, concurrent-claim uniqueness, and the HTTP wire contract including claim-token fencing.
whatBreaks: A weakened test here could let a warm-pool double-claim, orphan-box leak, or claim-fence bypass regress unnoticed into production.

role: Go provisioning worker: polls control plane, drains provision/deprovision/attach-domain/resurrect job queues
description: The core bridge between the Elixir control plane's job queues and the cloud-package provisioning chain (WarmPool.Provision). Implements claim→provision→succeed/fail reporting with retry-by-status-class (5xx transient retry, 4xx terminal), graceful-shutdown claim release, and the money-edge invariant that a live box is never orphaned from the control plane's knowledge. Very large, heavily documented file; central to the whole cloud go-live/deprovision/attach-domain/resurrect system.
whatBreaks: A bug could leave paid Hetzner/Azure boxes billed but invisible to the control plane, silently drop failed jobs, or fail to release claims on shutdown causing stuck 'provisioning' rows.

role: Test suite for the provisioner Worker's claim/report/shutdown lifecycle
description: Exercises the happy path, admin-token forwarding, empty-queue no-op, provision failure/timeout, the succeed-report retry/teardown money-edge scenarios (persistent 5xx, transient 5xx, 4xx terminal, idempotent 200, transport blips), periodic sweep, and graceful-shutdown claim release with claim-token echoing.
whatBreaks: A regression in these tests could hide a real orphaned-box or dropped-report bug that costs money or corrupts job state in production.

role: Real-disk FS implementation for the on-box deployment runtime
description: Tiny OSFS struct implementing WriteFile (atomic tmp+rename) and ReadFile for internal/runtime.Executor's Caddyfile writes; the only production FS backing the deploy executor.
whatBreaks: A non-atomic or buggy write could leave a corrupted Caddyfile mid-deploy, breaking Caddy's config reload on a live box.

role: On-box Docker/Caddy blue-green deployment executor for Barkpark Cloud
description: Executor.RunOnce claims a pending deployment from the control plane, docker-loads the image, runs a fresh container on an allocated port, health-checks it, rewrites/reloads Caddy, drains the old container, and reports live/failed back via a fenced transition — including preview-vs-production activation semantics (gh-6) where previews never repoint the production slot.
whatBreaks: A bug could serve a broken/unhealthy container to real traffic, corrupt the shared Caddyfile across all sites on a box, or wrongly repoint a production domain to a preview deploy.

role: Test suite for the on-box deployment Executor (blue-green, preview, failure paths)
description: Covers empty queue, first-deploy happy path, preview deployment isolation from production, docker-load/caddy-reload/write failures with container reaping, blue-green port swap, and OSFS temp-file cleanup on rename failure.
whatBreaks: Weakened coverage here could hide a regression that leaks containers or corrupts live-site Caddy config on real customer boxes.

role: Generated CLI/TUI chrome color-role tables per theme (from design/tokens.json)
description: Auto-generated (DO NOT EDIT) lipgloss AdaptiveColor maps for CLI/TUI chrome roles (accent, ink, borders, etc.) across the evergreen/ember/fjord themes, plus provider-identity and instance-lifecycle glyph/hue tables. Regenerated via design/emit.mjs.
whatBreaks: A stale or corrupted generated file would desync CLI/TUI chrome colors from the rest of the theme system, but is regenerable from source tokens.

role: Canonical status/lifecycle → semantic color-role vocabulary shared across CLI/TUI/SPA
description: Owns the single mapping from status-like tokens (cloud/deploy/health states and task-lifecycle states) to the four semantic roles (ok/info/warn/danger) plus lifecycle-specific hues, consumed by the CLI ANSI painter and the taskboard renderer so color meaning never drifts between surfaces. Includes disjointness/parity guarantees enforced by tests elsewhere.
whatBreaks: A wrong or drifted mapping would make status colors inconsistent or misleading across `bp` CLI tables, the TUI, and the web dashboard (e.g. a failure state rendering as neutral).

role: Unit tests pinning the semrole vocabulary + disjointness contract
description: Tests For() against the pinned cloud/deploy/health token vocabulary (verbatim-moved from internal/cli statusRole) and a disjointness tripwire between the cloud and task-lifecycle token sets. Guards a subtle cross-package contract: silent overlap between vocabularies would shadow tone decisions.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a cloud status token silently lose its color role or collide with a task-lifecycle token without any test catching it.

role: Generated adaptive-color/tone tables for status + lifecycle roles
description: Code generated by design/emit.mjs from design/tokens.json (DO NOT EDIT); defines the lipgloss AdaptiveColor palette for ok/info/warn/danger status tones, lifecycle glyph hues, and ANSI-16 fallback codes consumed across the TUI/CLI for consistent semantic coloring.
whatBreaks: Wrong or missing color mappings here desync the unified color system across every surface that renders status/lifecycle tones (TUI, CLI), producing incorrect or missing colors, since it's the single generated source of truth.

role: Task-board claim/close action layer translating API results to UI strip messages
description: Implements DoClaim/DoClose/DoCloseRev wrapping apiclient task-claim/close calls, plus humanizeReason/resyncGuidance error translation, rail-awareness notice folding, worker-id resolution, and Studio deep-link building. Never silently reports success on a server-declined mutation; the CAS-epoch fencing contract lives here.
whatBreaks: A bug here could report a claim/close as successful when the server rejected it (or vice versa), corrupting the task board's trust in mutation outcomes and misleading the operator/agent about task state.

role: HTTP-level tests for the claim/close action layer
description: Uses httptest servers to assert DoClaim/DoClose send the correct request path/body and correctly interpret success/failure responses, including humanized error messages.
whatBreaks: Without these tests, a regression in request shape or error handling in actions.go (e.g. wrong path, dropped worker_id) could ship silently and break real task claims.

role: Tests for the NEXT intent strip resolution rules (resumables/ready curation)
description: Verifies BuildBoard's Next field: resumable (dropped-lease) tasks surface first, followed by a D65-curated ready head that favors continuity/leverage/well-formedness over raw priority label. Also guards the retired NOW/NEXT display band contract.
whatBreaks: A regression could surface the wrong 'what to work on next' guidance in the TUI, e.g. burying a dropped-lease resumable behind a cold P0 task.

role: Pure deterministic animation/aliveness logic for the task board heartbeat
description: Defines Alive() (whether the board needs another render frame), the flash fade ladder (bright/dim/gone), snapshot diffing for change detection, and flash pruning. Kept pure so motion is deterministic/testable and the board's ticker stops cleanly at rest.
whatBreaks: A bug could make the heartbeat never stop (wasting CPU/battery on a supposedly idle board) or never start (missed live-claim/flash animation), and would break golden/deterministic tests relying on this purity.

role: Table tests for the flash-level fade ladder and change diffing
description: Pins exact boundary behavior of FlashLevel (bright <1.5s, fading <4s, gone after) including clock-skew edge cases, and tests changedDocIDs snapshot diffing.
whatBreaks: An off-by-one regression in the flash ladder boundaries could ship unnoticed, causing visually wrong or flickering board animations.

role: Core pure policy engine building the whole portrait task-board view model
description: The central BuildBoard function and its large supporting policy: NOW band, epic/orphan/cluster grouping and ranking, focus windows, done-folding, NEXT intent-strip curation/scoring (shared with the dispatch Frontier), twin detection, staleness, dormancy. Pure function of (snapshot, repo, now) — no wall clock, no I/O — making the entire TUI board deterministic and testable.
whatBreaks: Since this is the single source of truth for how every task renders/ranks/groups in the TUI board (and shares its D65 scorer with the dispatch Frontier / 'bp task next'), a bug here would corrupt task ordering, hide live work, or make the parallel-dispatch capacity count wrong across both the TUI and CLI.

role: Fixture-driven tests for BuildBoard against a realistic task snapshot
description: Loads testdata/tasks_fixture.json through the same decode+compose pipeline as production, exercising the derived-ready overlay and giving BuildBoard's policy end-to-end regression coverage against a fixed reference clock.
whatBreaks: Loss of this fixture-based coverage would let board.go's complex ranking/grouping/curation logic regress silently across releases.

role: On-disk first-paint snapshot cache for the task board
description: Best-effort, tolerant local cache of the last-seen board snapshot keyed by sha256(server/workspace/project), so `bp tasks` paints instantly instead of blank on launch. Atomic write via temp-file+rename; any load/save failure is swallowed, never surfaced as an error.
whatBreaks: A bug could either crash/block the board on a corrupt cache (violating its 'never a liability' contract) or corrupt the cache file such that stale/wrong data briefly flashes on next launch.

role: Tests for the task-board local snapshot cache round-trip
description: Exercises marshal/unmarshal of the frozen Snapshot type (claims, criteria, labels, counts, events, FetchedAt) and its on-disk cache file behavior. Uses a fully-populated sampleSnapshot fixture to catch any field regression.
whatBreaks: A cache round-trip regression (e.g. dropped field) would silently corrupt the TUI's offline/stale task board without this test catching it.

role: Worker-id derivation for CMUX-pane task claims (task-TUI epic)
description: Defines CmuxWorkerID(), the single four-tier precedence function (BARKPARK_WORKER_ID > cmux-<SURFACE_ID> > cmux-<WORKSPACE_ID> > ResolveWorker fallback) that every `bp cmux` subcommand and the install shell-line must agree on, so a pane's claim and its close/renew always speak the same worker id and never get fenced off.
whatBreaks: A prefix/precedence mismatch here causes cmux panes to claim under one worker id and close under another, producing 409 fenced_off errors on task close inside cmux panes.

role: Regression test pinning the cmux claim/close worker-id self-fence fix
description: Sets only CMUX_SURFACE_ID (mimicking a raw cmux pane) and asserts both claim ('c') and close ('x') verbs use the same CmuxWorkerID(), guarding against the historic bug where close fell back to ResolveWorker()'s tui-<host> and got fenced off by the server.
whatBreaks: Without this test, a future refactor could silently reintroduce the claim/close worker-id mismatch, breaking task closing inside cmux panes.

role: Unit test for CmuxWorkerID's four-tier env precedence
description: Table-driven test covering the full env-var matrix (including explicitly-blank vars) for CmuxWorkerID, asserting exact ids for tiers 1-3 and a hostname-agnostic prefix check for the tier-4 ResolveWorker fallback.
whatBreaks: An untested precedence bug in worker-id resolution would misroute task claims between cmux panes and non-cmux TUI sessions.

role: Core low-level render primitives for the taskboard TUI (rows, glyphs, meta)
description: Width-safe string helpers (disp, truncate, truncateMiddle), lifecycle glyphs (StatusGlyph, boardGlyph styling), section-header dotted-leader rendering with phase rollups, and TaskRow — the single rich-line row renderer used throughout the board. Heavily documented per the design-language spec/charter; any drift here changes the board's visual vocabulary everywhere.
whatBreaks: A bug in truncate/disp or TaskRow corrupts row alignment and title clipping across the entire task board TUI, including CJK/multi-byte title handling.

role: Tests for glyphs, badges, row rendering and width-safe truncation
description: Pins StatusGlyph's design-language vocabulary, AgeBadge formatting, stale-badge thresholds, and TaskRow's width-degradation behavior, including ANSI/rune-width correctness for styled and multi-byte strings.
whatBreaks: Losing this coverage lets row-rendering or truncation regressions (e.g. broken CJK title clipping) ship unnoticed into the TUI.

role: Adaptive compositor: wide/narrow frame layout, breadcrumb, mouse routing
description: Compose()/composeAt() build the whole painted frame — narrow full-frame push vs wide two-pane board+reading layout with ±4 hysteresis — plus Breadcrumb, windowFrame scrolling, and the wide-mode mouse click/hover router that must stay pixel-exact with the paint geometry. This is the top-level shell seam for the entire taskboard TUI's visual composition and input routing.
whatBreaks: A geometry mismatch between paint and mouse routing here breaks click/hover targeting across the whole wide-mode board, or corrupts layout switching between narrow and wide modes entirely.

role: Golden + behavioral tests for the compositor (both wide and narrow modes)
description: Full-frame golden snapshots at multiple widths (60/80/100 narrow, 120 wide) plus behavioral tests for the navigation stack, breadcrumb, hysteresis boundaries, and reading-cursor grammar. Reuses render_test.go's -update flag for golden regeneration.
whatBreaks: Losing this coverage allows silent layout/breadcrumb/scroll regressions across both TUI compositor modes.

role: Wave-5 pure data layer for the task detail reading view
description: FetchSnapshotFull hydrates the TaskDetail model in the same fetch as the board list (zero extra round-trips); ChildrenOf/DrivenTasks/PaperRefs derive parent/child and paper-linkage views from the in-hand snapshot with a frozen tolerance contract (malformed fields degrade to zero-value, never error).
whatBreaks: A decode or derivation bug here would show wrong children, missing paper links, or a detail view contradicting its board row in the TUI's task detail pane.

role: Tests for FetchSnapshotFull hydration and detail derivations
description: Uses an httptest server plus a fixture file (testdata/detail_fixture.json) split into list and prime bodies to verify the detail hydration pass matches the board decode, and exercises ChildrenOf/DrivenTasks/PaperRefs edge cases.
whatBreaks: Without this test, regressions in detail hydration or paper/child derivation logic could ship unnoticed, desyncing the detail pane from the board.

role: TUI task-detail reading view renderer (pure)
description: RenderTaskDetail builds the full-page task reading frame (title, meta, timestamps, derived timeline, prose via pdrender/mdlite, criteria checklist, facts, claim/lease info, reason strips, code refs, children+papers rails) as lines+stops for the shell to window and the mouse hit map to mirror. Pure function of (data, width, clock); frozen wave-5 charter contract with heavy design-law commentary (color=state only, honest truncation, shared 72-col prose measure).
whatBreaks: Task detail pane in the TUI renders garbled/misaligned or drops sections (prose, criteria, rails), and stop indices could desync from the mouse hit map (hitmap.go) causing clicks to select the wrong row.

role: Golden + behavioral tests for RenderTaskDetail
description: 509-line test file with ANSI-stripped whole-frame goldens at 60/80/100 cols across RICH/THIN/BLOCKED/DONE fixtures, verifying section conditionality, stop indices, lease-alarm suppression, and inline close_reason behavior.
whatBreaks: A regression in detail_render.go's layout or stop indexing would go undetected, letting broken detail-pane rendering or mis-wired rail navigation ship silently.

role: HTTP fetch + wire-decode layer for the task board (Go TUI)
description: FetchSnapshot composes board state from GET /v1/tasks and /v1/tasks/prime, decoding render_doc envelopes into board Task and TaskDetail models with permissive/tolerant JSON decoding (priority coercion, acceptance-criteria/evidence parsing, code_refs flattening, claim lease fields) and overlaying the server-derived "ready" lifecycle onto tasks.
whatBreaks: The entire Go task-TUI board would show wrong/missing tasks, wrong ready counts, corrupted claim/criteria data, or silently drop the whole board on a decode error — it's the sole IO boundary translating the API contract into every downstream renderer.

role: Tests for fetch.go's wire decoding via httptest fixtures
description: 378-line test using a shared testdata/tasks_fixture.json split into list+prime bodies served by an httptest server, verifying FetchSnapshot's composition and decode tolerance.
whatBreaks: Wire-decode regressions in fetch.go (malformed claim/criteria/code_refs handling, ready overlay) would ship undetected, corrupting the TUI's task data silently.

role: Core type definitions for the TUI navigation-stack/reading frames
description: Frozen wave-5 contract defining TaskDetail, DetailIndex, FrameKind (Board/Task/Paper), Stop, Frame, and PaperState — the shared data shapes every render/hitmap/compose file in the package depends on.
whatBreaks: A change to these struct shapes breaks compilation or silently changes semantics across detail_render.go, hitmap.go, frontier.go and the whole navigation-stack/compose machinery — this is the package's central schema.

role: Dispatch-frontier interference model (parallel-safe task picker)
description: Implements the conservative MWIS-based algorithm computing which ready tasks can be dispatched to agents in parallel without blast-radius collisions, using area:/files:/proj: labels, phase-band derivation, and cross-root block edges; shared by both the TUI capacity count and the `bp task frontier` CLI verb so the two never drift.
whatBreaks: Multi-agent dispatch could either under-parallelize (wasting orchestration capacity) or, worse, admit two tasks that actually conflict — causing agents to collide/clobber the same files or blocked work across the whole fan-out system.

role: Tests for the dispatch-frontier interference model
description: 642-line table-driven test suite covering areasOf label/phase-band derivation, file-edge overlap, containment (parent/child), and the greedy admission algorithm's risk classification.
whatBreaks: Interference-model regressions (e.g. a broken area-overlap or containment check) would ship undetected, risking unsafe parallel dispatch decisions across the fleet.

role: Guard test enforcing the closed non-ASCII glyph vocabulary
description: Asserts every non-ASCII rune appearing in regenerated goldens is in a small allowlist (spinner frames, status/connection/momentum/structure glyphs), preventing unreviewed glyph vocabulary creep in the calm-board design language (charter D14/D44).
whatBreaks: A stray new glyph (e.g. a reintroduced spinner or chip-hue icon) could sneak into the board's rendered output without review, violating the design-language contract.

role: Narrow-width regression test for the board header shed ladder
description: 35-line test sweeping widths 8-90 to confirm the header never overflows, the "tasks" label survives, and the server name shows only its first DNS label — never the FQDN or scheme.
whatBreaks: A narrow-terminal header could overflow the pane or leak a full server FQDN/scheme, a cosmetic but security/privacy-adjacent regression that would go unnoticed without this guard.

role: Pure mouse hit-map builder mirroring the painted TUI frame
description: Builds a []LineTarget parallel to each rendered line (board or reading frame) so the mouse reducer can resolve a click Y-coordinate to a cursor stop, scroll affordance, or chrome with zero ad-hoc coordinate math; must stay byte-for-byte length-mirrored with render.go/compose.go's painting logic (charter wave-16, D89-D93).
whatBreaks: Mouse clicks in the TUI would resolve to the wrong row or panic/misbehave on length mismatch versus the painted frame, breaking the entire mouse interaction layer for the task board.

role: Test: mouse hit-map matches painted board line-for-line
description: Tests ComposeHitMap against the rendered View() output at every cursor position, asserting the mouse hit targets exactly mirror the ▎-marked spine rows (the D91 tripwire). Also provides shared helpers (leftClick, syncScroll) used by other mouse-interaction tests.
whatBreaks: A regression here means mouse clicks in the Go taskboard TUI silently target the wrong row with no test catching it.

role: Live-refresh loop: SSE dirty-bit, debounce, backstop poll, connection state
description: Core reducer/command set wiring apiclient SSE change/pulse events into debounced full-snapshot refetches, honest connection-state (Live/Polling/Offline) derivation, per-row forward-only merge application, flash-diff stamping, first-paint cache write, and heartbeat arm/disarm. Central to the Go TUI taskboard's live-update model; heavily commented charter-decision code (never applies event payloads incrementally, always refetches).
whatBreaks: The taskboard would show stale data, spuriously flicker/revert rows, or lie about connection status (fake ● live) across the whole live TUI experience.

role: Manual liveprobe: real-server smoke test for FetchSnapshot/BuildBoard
description: Build-tag-gated (go:build liveprobe) manual test that hits a real Barkpark server via BP_SERVER/BP_TOKEN env vars and prints board stats plus regression-guard assertions against real live-data shape; never runs in CI.
whatBreaks: Only a manual diagnostic tool breaks; no CI or production impact, but real-corpus shape regressions could go undetected.

role: Unit tests for live.go's debounce/refetch/connection-state reducers
description: Uses a fakeClock to deterministically test debounce coalescing (a burst of SSE events collapses to one refetch) and other live-loop time-dependent behavior in live.go.
whatBreaks: Debounce/connection-state bugs in live.go could ship undetected, causing fetch storms or a dishonest connection dot.

role: Golden/regression test: BuildBoard against a real-corpus-shaped fixture
description: A large charter-driven guard test feeding an authored Snapshot fixture (mass-close floods, merged live-claim neighborhoods, dormant/cancelled epics) through the real BuildBoard, asserting rendered output at several widths matches golden expectations and pins activity-focus policy invariants (D49-D51).
whatBreaks: Board-layout regressions for real-world pathological task corpora (mass-close floods, dormant epics) could ship unnoticed.

role: Minimal markdown → pdrender.Block adapter for task descriptions
description: Parses a small markdown subset (paragraphs, `- ` bullets, fenced code, ATX headings 1-3) into pdrender Block literals so task prose renders through the same typography engine as Papers; everything else degrades gracefully to a paragraph, never errors/panics.
whatBreaks: Task descriptions in the TUI/board would render garbled, panic, or lose content instead of degrading safely to plain text.

role: Unit tests for the mdlite markdown adapter
description: Verifies MarkdownBlocks produces correct pdrender.Block shapes for the four supported structures and safely degrades/never panics on empty or hostile input, plus a real-registry render smoke check.
whatBreaks: Malformed or panic-inducing markdown in task descriptions could slip through untested and crash or corrupt rendering.

role: Per-row forward-only snapshot reconciliation (server-time ordering)
description: mergeForward reconciles an incoming snapshot against currently-displayed tasks by doc id, using server UpdatedAt/claim Epoch (not client fetch time) to guarantee a displayed row only ever advances forward, preventing flicker/reverts from stale backstop polls or reconcile fetches.
whatBreaks: Live task rows could visibly flicker backward (e.g. CLAIMED → unclaimed → CLAIMED) whenever a stale poll response races a fresher one.

role: Unit tests for mergeForward's forward-only ordering guarantee
description: Exercises stale-vs-newer incoming rows, added/dropped rows, and UpdatedAt-tie epoch tie-breaking to pin the forward-only merge contract in merge.go.
whatBreaks: A broken merge.go ordering rule (row flicker/reversion) could ship without test coverage catching it.

role: Pure motion/animation helpers: live elapsed timer + flash styling
description: LiveElapsed renders a ticking seconds/minutes stopwatch for claims under 10 minutes old (handing off to AgeBadge beyond that), and flashStyle renders the one-shot foreground flash emphasis for recently-changed rows; both are pure functions of injected clock/frame state per charter decision 16 (no time.Now, no hidden state).
whatBreaks: Live claim ages or change-flash highlighting in the TUI would render incorrectly, jump unstably, or animate when nothing changed.

role: Unit tests for live-elapsed/motion formatting in the task TUI
description: Tests LiveElapsed's clock-driven time formatting (seconds/minutes/hours/days vocabulary, clock-skew clamping) used by the board's flash/claim-age rendering.
whatBreaks: A regression here means claim ages or flash timers render wrong on the taskboard TUI, but no other package is affected.

role: Integration tests wiring mouse hover/routing through the full reducer
description: Exercises the fused wave-16 mouse reducer end-to-end (Update -> handleMouse -> mouseMotion/handleWideMouse), proving hover, narrow/wide routing, and the MouseReleased guard all wire together correctly.
whatBreaks: A break here would let a mouse-reducer wiring regression (e.g. hover state or wide/narrow routing) slip through even if the per-slice unit tests still pass.

role: Unit tests for clickable footer verbs and mouse-mode etiquette
description: Verifies footer verb click-span alignment against the shed/truncate ladder, that a verb click dispatches the same reducer as its key (claim/close/studio), and the M mouse-toggle behavior/etiquette footnote.
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions could make footer clicks land on the wrong verb or desync from the keyboard-equivalent action in the taskboard TUI.

role: Computes claimed-task file/area collision pairs for the task frontier
description: ClaimOverlaps pairwise-compares in-progress claimed tasks (board.Now) and reports collisions when declared files or authored area surfaces intersect, reusing the same FilesOf/areasOf truth as the dispatch frontier so `bp task frontier` output can never drift from admission logic.
whatBreaks: A bug would cause the CLI's frontier/overlap report to miss real claim collisions (silent merge conflicts) or falsely flag disjoint work as colliding.

role: Unit tests for ClaimOverlaps collision detection
description: Covers file-collision, directory-prefix, and area-overlap cases plus ordering/worker-carrying invariants for overlaps.go.
whatBreaks: A gap here lets overlaps.go regress (missed or false-positive collisions) without test failure.

role: Fetches and renders a Barkpark Paper inside the taskboard TUI's FramePaper
description: FetchPaper does one scoped read of a paper doc and decodes it into PaperState; renderPaperBody decodes+renders it wholesale via pdrender (cached by slug/rev/width) and RenderPaperFrame composites title, body, and a 'driven tasks' rail whose rows are the frame's selectable Stops.
whatBreaks: Breakage here would blank or crash the in-TUI Paper reading pane (`bp tasks` paper drill-down), or desync the driven-tasks rail from the live task snapshot / wikilink chip resolution.

role: Golden/unit tests for the FramePaper render surface
description: Exercises paper.go's fetch/decode/render pipeline against fixture blocks and an updatable golden, including wikilink task-chip resolution and driven-tasks rail rendering.
whatBreaks: A silent regression in paper.go's rendering or chip resolution could ship without failing tests.

role: Bubble Tea shell/model for the `bp tasks` portrait task TUI
description: Defines the Model (board+UIState+navigation stack+injected seams), Config (server/scope), the message reducer (keyboard, mouse, live-refresh, paper-load, action results), and the navigation-stack/frame push-pop machinery plus claim/close/open act-verb dispatch — the central orchestrator of the whole taskboard package.
whatBreaks: Breaking this file breaks the entire `bp tasks` TUI: navigation, claiming/closing tasks, mouse handling, and live updates would misbehave or crash for every user of the terminal task board.

role: Large unit-test suite for the taskboard Model/reducer
description: Covers navigation, fold/expand modes, keyboard/mouse handling, claim/close flows and other reducer behavior in program.go via fixtures and injected seams (no real terminal/server).
whatBreaks: Gaps here let core TUI reducer logic (navigation, act-verbs, live loop) regress without being caught before release.

role: Pure renderer painting the taskboard TUI frame from Board+UIState
description: Render() draws the whole portrait pane (identity strip, scrolling epic/cluster/orphan spine, momentum/progress bar, ticker, footer) with no I/O; also houses hover-tint painting, footer verb spans for mouse clicks, and scroll-position computation (SpineTopFor) shared with the shell.
whatBreaks: A bug here corrupts the visual output of `bp tasks` for every invocation — misaligned rows, wrong scroll position, broken hover/click targeting, or garbled ANSI output.

role: Test for ANSI-aware truncation of the TUI header
description: Forces truecolor rendering and asserts a long styled header line truncates without SGR escape bytes eating the visible content (regression test for a real bug where the branch text was destroyed).
whatBreaks: Header truncation could silently regress to destroying visible text under long branch/repo names and go unnoticed.

role: Golden-frame test harness for the taskboard TUI renderer
description: Loads a fixed board fixture and pinned UI state, renders at multiple widths (60/80/100) with ANSI stripped, and compares against golden files via a -update flag; defines fixedNow/loadBoardFixture/plainFrame helpers reused by other test files in the package.
whatBreaks: Renderer regressions (layout, spacing, truncation) across widths would go undetected, and other golden tests depending on its shared helpers would fail to compile/run.

role: Pure git-commit/branch correlator linking commits to tasks
description: Two-layer design: CorrelateRepo is a pure, no-I/O text scanner matching task doc_ids (bare and drafts.-prefixed forms) and title slugs against commit subjects/branch names; GatherRepoContext/gatherGit shell out to git with a 3s timeout and fail closed to a zero RepoContext outside a repo. Advisory-only — never filters/hides tasks, just feeds a rank boost and a dim badge.
whatBreaks: Task-to-commit correlation (rank boost, git badge) would misfire or crash the board paint if the shell-out isn't fail-closed; a boundary-matching bug would misattribute mentions between similarly-named tasks.

role: Table + integration tests for repoctx.go's git correlator
description: Extensive table tests for CorrelateRepo (id boundary matching, drafts.-prefix aliasing, slug matching) plus real-git integration tests (GatherRepoContext, gatherGit) using temp repos; skips gracefully when git is unavailable.
whatBreaks: Regressions in id/slug boundary matching or the fail-closed git shell contract would ship silently.

role: Single ordered spine producer for the taskboard TUI cursor+render
description: Core structural file (charter D42): builds spineRows(), the ONE ordered list both the shell's cursor index and the renderer's flattened lines consume, guaranteeing cursor-parity by construction. Handles epic/cluster/orphan sections, phase-band grouping/derivation, cancelled-epic tombstones, finished-section demotion, and task tree nesting (nestTasks).
whatBreaks: Cursor position and rendered rows could desync (clicking/selecting the wrong task), or sections/phase-bands/tombstones would misorder or vanish across the whole TUI task board.

role: In-progress spinner glyph vocabulary for the TUI
description: Maps a heartbeat frame to a Braille spinner glyph (10 frames) or ASCII fallback, honoring NO_MOTION (reduced motion, freezes on ⠿) and BP_TASKS_ASCII escape hatches; boardGlyph combines it with the static per-lifecycle StatusGlyph.
whatBreaks: In-progress tasks would show a broken/tofu/incorrect glyph or ignore accessibility env vars, a cosmetic but visible bug.

role: Golden test rendering the lifecycle color/glyph vocabulary table
description: Renders a style-guide table straight from generated tokens (GenLifecycle/GenLifecycleOrder/GenBrailleFrames) and diffs against a golden file, serving as the TUI's drift-visibility check when design/tokens.json changes.
whatBreaks: Token/design drift between design/tokens.json and the TUI's rendered vocabulary would go undetected.

role: Fixture board data for taskboard render golden tests
description: JSON fixture representing a Board (Now list with tasks, claims, criteria) used by render_test.go and render_degrade_test.go to produce deterministic golden renders.
whatBreaks: All render golden tests depending on it would fail to build a valid Board or would silently test wrong/incomplete scenarios.

role: Fixture loose-task-queue data exercising cluster policy scenarios
description: JSON fixture modeling a live-guerrilla-shaped parentless task queue with labels covering proj:/area: clustering keys, plain-label fallback, phase: exclusion, singleton/twin/stale cases — decoded via the real decode+compose path for deterministic clustering tests.

role: Golden text fixture for an 80-col rendered Paper-linked task frame
description: Plain-text golden output showing a paper-frame charter view with a linked task and bash instructions, at 80 columns, used to lock rendering of the paper-driven task compose view.

description: Same task-detail composition snapshot as the 100-col variant but at a narrow 60-column width, exercising narrow-terminal wrapping/truncation in the TUI test suite.

description: Wide-terminal (120-column) snapshot variant of the taskboard composition, guarding layout at large widths.

role: Reference table: lifecycle-status glyph/color vocabulary for TUI

role: JSON fixture: canonical task/doc corpus for taskboard unit tests

Central input fixture likely reused across many taskboard rendering/logic tests.

role: Semantic color/role engine for the TUI task board
description: Defines the Role enum (neutral/ok/info/warn/danger) and builds the board's theme-resolved palette (buildPalette) by reading generated lifecycle tokens (tokens_gen.go) and semrole status/chrome tones, never hand-coding hex. Maps lifecycle state, claim-lease age, and staleness to colors/styles consumed by the renderer.
whatBreaks: Wrong role mapping or a broken buildPalette panics the board at startup or paints every task the wrong severity color, destroying the board's color=state guarantee.

role: Drift-guard tests locking board colors to generated tokens/semrole
description: Asserts theme.go's colors are sourced (not re-hand-coded) from tokens_gen.go and semrole, checks lifecycle const parity with the generated vocabulary, and pins the claim-lease escalation ladder and staleness thresholds.
whatBreaks: A silently broken test lets someone re-hand-code a color or desync the lifecycle vocabulary without detection, reintroducing drift across CLI/board/cloud surfaces.

role: Generated lifecycle glyph/color tokens for the task board
description: Machine-generated (design/emit.mjs from design/tokens.json, DO NOT EDIT) mirror of lifecycle state glyphs/colors per theme (evergreen/ember/fjord), plus spinner braille frames and Resolve(theme) lookup. Sole color source for theme.go's buildPalette.
whatBreaks: A bad regeneration or manual edit desyncs board colors/glyphs from the design manifest, breaking the single-source-of-truth theming contract and any theme other than evergreen.

role: Core data model (Task/Board/Epic/Cluster/UIState) for the TUI task board
description: Central struct definitions for the board's render-ready model: Task, Claim, Criteria, Snapshot, Board (with epics/clusters/orphans/NEXT strip), Epic, Cluster, UIState (cursor, hover, mouse mode, flashes), and ActionStrip. Heavily commented with design-decision rationale (focus windows, folding, staleness).
whatBreaks: Any field mismatch or bad zero-value breaks board construction, rendering, or interaction handling across the entire TUI task board feature.

role: Parser/validator for barkpark.template.json deploy-descriptor manifests
description: Defines the Template/Seed/EnvVar structs and Load()/Validate() for the 'Deploy with Barkpark' template manifest format, strictly rejecting unknown fields and enforcing cross-field rules (e.g. publish requires publishType). Marked @canonical capability:template-manifest.
whatBreaks: A parsing/validation bug lets a malformed template manifest through or rejects a valid one, breaking the deploy-button provisioner (dwb-4) for any template site.

role: Tests for the template manifest parser/validator
description: Covers valid-manifest load, dataset default, unknown-field/trailing-data rejection, every Validate() failure branch, script-seed exemption from publishType, and a drift gate that loads every real checked-in barkpark.template.json and checks referenced schema/seed paths exist on disk.

role: Docker-CLI-backed ContainerManager for Barkpark Cloud's scale-to-zero waker
description: DockerContainer shells out to `docker run/start/stop/inspect` to bring a site's container up/down and health-checks it by polling / until non-5xx or timeout. All subprocess calls go through an injectable CommandRunner for testability.
whatBreaks: A bad docker invocation or misparsed inspect state leaves a scale-to-zero site's container never started (permanent cold-hit failure) or never stopped (cost/resource leak).

role: Tests for DockerContainer's run/start/stop/inspect state machine
description: Uses a scripted fake CommandRunner to drive already-running/stopped/missing paths and asserts correct docker subcommands and args (name, image, memory/cpu caps) are issued, plus a real httptest upstream for the health check.
whatBreaks: Undetected regression in DockerContainer's state transitions could ship a waker that never starts or restarts containers correctly in production.

role: Scale-to-zero HTTP front door: cold-wake, reverse-proxy, idle reaper
description: Waker.ServeHTTP touches activity, ensures the backing container is up (single-flight via upMu), then reverse-proxies to it; a background reaper stops idle containers after IdleTimeout, with careful race-avoidance between touch/wake/reap ordering and self-healing on transport errors (markDown). Central to Barkpark Cloud's cost model for low-traffic sites.
whatBreaks: A race or logic bug here can serve permanent 502s, kill a container mid-request, or leave every deployed site always-on (defeating the scale-to-zero cost model) across the whole Cloud fleet.

role: Tests for Waker cold-wake, idle-sleep, concurrency, and self-heal
description: Exercises cold-wake-then-proxy, no-redundant-start on warm path, idle sleep/rewake timing, single-flight under 5 concurrent cold requests, the touch-during-wake race guard, and self-heal after a warm container crashes (dead port dial -> markDown -> rewake).
whatBreaks: Weakened concurrency/race tests could let a real production race (double-start, premature stop, permanent 502 loop) ship undetected across the Cloud site fleet.

role: JS monorepo ESLint configuration
description: Flat ESLint config for the js/ monorepo, enabling TypeScript parsing, unused-var errors, consistent type imports, and no-floating-promises rules across all TS/TSX files.
whatBreaks: Linting rules drift or fail to apply, allowing type errors and bad patterns to ship in the JS SDK.

role: Root manifest for the js/ pnpm+turbo monorepo (SDK packages)
description: Defines workspace-wide scripts (build/test/typecheck/lint/size/changeset/release via turbo), pnpm/node engine pins, and shared devDependencies (turbo, tsup, vitest, size-limit, changesets, eslint); also carries pnpm security overrides for transitive deps (ws, form-data, postcss, brace-expansion, js-yaml).
