role: size-limit config enforcing codegen bundle budget
description: Caps `dist/index.mjs` at 15KB, excluding prettier/zod/chokidar/cac/@barkpark/core from the count; feeds the CI `pnpm size` gate that fails on >2% regression.
whatBreaks: CI silently passes an oversized codegen bundle, or false-fails a legitimate build if the budget/exclusions are wrong.

description: @barkpark/codegen

role: Package README for @barkpark/codegen documenting CLI behavior
description: Explains `barkpark generate` (schema → typed TS, one interface per schema type + BarkparkTypeMap + BarkparkAnyDocument union), the `--from`/`--schema` network-free flag used by the CI drift gate, pairing with core's `typedClient`, and the scoped vs flat schema-path selection rule (workspace+project both-or-neither).
whatBreaks: Consumers misuse the CLI (e.g. mixing workspace/project flags) or misunderstand narrowing semantics, causing broken codegen setups; doc-only, no runtime effect itself.

role: npm package manifest for @barkpark/codegen CLI/library
description: Defines the `barkpark` CLI bin (dist/cli.mjs), dual ESM/CJS exports, build/test/typecheck/lint/size scripts, and deps (@barkpark/core, cac, chokidar, zod, prettier). Publishable preview package (1.0.0-preview.0).
whatBreaks: The published `@barkpark/codegen` npm package fails to install, resolve its bin, or expose correct type exports, breaking every downstream codegen consumer.

role: Entry point for the `barkpark` CLI (schema-path + generate commands)
description: cac-based CLI wiring `schema-path` and `generate` subcommands; resolves config from barkpark.config.{ts,js,mjs} overlaid with CLI flags/env, enforces workspace+project both-or-neither, supports `--from`/`--schema` for network-free generation (the CI drift-gate path) and `--watch` for config-file-driven regeneration via chokidar.
whatBreaks: The `barkpark generate` command fails to fetch schemas, resolves the wrong scoped/unscoped path, or the CI drift gate silently stops validating committed type output against the schema fixture.

role: Codegen module fetching+validating a dataset schema envelope from the API
description: Calls `GET /v1/schemas/:dataset` (optionally workspace/project-scoped) with a bearer token, then validates the response with `schemaEnvelopeSchema` (zod). Throws clear errors on missing token/apiUrl, network failure, non-2xx, non-JSON, or failed validation; this is the entry point `barkpark generate` uses to obtain the schema that `generate.ts` turns into TypeScript.
whatBreaks: If this fetch/validation is wrong, `barkpark generate` either silently accepts a malformed schema or fails to fetch it, breaking typed-client codegen for every consumer of @barkpark/codegen.

role: Codegen core: maps a Barkpark schema envelope to a TypeScript module
description: Converts field/schema definitions (BarkparkSchemaJson) into a deterministic, prettier-formatted `.ts` module: per-schema interfaces extending BarkparkSystemFields, a BarkparkTypeMap type consumed by `@barkpark/core`'s `typedClient<TMap>`, and a discriminated BarkparkAnyDocument union. Handles field-type mapping (primitives, select/codelist enums, arrays, composite/object recursion with depth cap, richText, localizedText), identifier/string-literal escaping, and fails loud on malformed composite sub-fields (missing `name`).
whatBreaks: A bug here produces incorrect or non-compiling generated TypeScript types for every Barkpark project using `barkpark generate`, breaking the typed-client narrowing contract (`doc`/`docs`/`getDocuments`) across the whole JS SDK ecosystem.

role: Public library entry point for @barkpark/codegen (re-exports + defineConfig)
description: Re-exports types/functions from types.ts, schema-url.ts, fetch-schema.ts, generate.ts, and provides the identity helper `defineConfig` used for IDE-typed authoring of barkpark.config.ts.
whatBreaks: Programmatic (non-CLI) consumers of @barkpark/codegen lose access to generateTypes/fetchSchema/buildSchemaPath or defineConfig loses type-checking in config files.

role: Schema introspection URL builder
description: Exports `buildSchemaPath` which constructs the API path for schema introspection, supporting both scoped (workspace+project) and flat (back-compat) URL forms.
whatBreaks: Codegen fetches schema from the wrong API path, silently failing or hitting 404s for scoped workspace/project configurations.

role: Core type definitions and zod validation schema for codegen's schema-envelope input
description: Defines BarkparkCodegenConfig, FieldDef (handling both `required`/`required?` key spellings and v1 array-of-descriptors vs v2 arrayOf-single-descriptor disambiguation), SchemaDef, BarkparkSchemaJson, and the `schemaEnvelopeSchema` zod validator used to safe-parse both fetched and `--from`-file schema envelopes before generation.
whatBreaks: Malformed or version-drifted schema JSON passes validation incorrectly (or valid schemas get rejected), and the type mapper mis-generates TS interfaces (wrong optionality, wrong array-of-v1-vs-v2 handling) for every generated barkpark.types.ts.

role: Vitest committed snapshot for codegen full-output test
description: Golden-file snapshot of the generated TypeScript module (interfaces, prelude, type map) produced from the production-schema.json fixture. Any intentional codegen output change requires updating this snapshot; an unintentional diff is a regression signal.
whatBreaks: A stale or hand-edited snapshot masks real codegen regressions or causes false-positive test failures on legitimate output changes.

role: Vitest test for codegen CLI --workspace/--project scoping validation
description: Exercises resolveConfig and the built `schema-path`/`generate` CLI binary to ensure workspace/project flags are enforced both-or-neither, preventing silent mis-scoped schema paths.
whatBreaks: A regression here could let the CLI silently emit types from the wrong (unscoped) schema instead of failing loudly.

role: Vitest test for `barkpark generate --from <file>` network-free codegen path
description: Verifies the CLI's `--from`/`--schema` local-file flag produces byte-identical output to generateTypes() without any network/API calls — this is the exact path the CI drift gate exercises.
whatBreaks: If the network-free --from path breaks or drifts, the CI schema-drift gate becomes unreliable or fails to catch real drift.

role: Large realistic schema fixture used by codegen tests
description: A full BarkparkSchemaJson envelope (45 schemas: game design docs like ability/arena/bossType, ONIX book schema, etc.) used as ground truth input across multiple codegen test files and the committed snapshot; changing it invalidates the snapshot and several assertions tied to exact counts (e.g. 45 schemas).
whatBreaks: Editing this fixture without updating the snapshot and dependent count-based assertions breaks generate.test.ts, cli-from.test.ts, and the snapshot test simultaneously.

role: Main Vitest suite for @barkpark/codegen's generateTypes() output
description: Comprehensive test of the codegen mapper: snapshot match, self-contained prelude (no @barkpark/core import), per-type field mapping spot checks, completeness across all 45 schemas, and edge cases (non-identifier names, malformed options).
whatBreaks: A broken or weakened test here lets the generated TypeScript client types silently diverge from the schema (wrong types, dropped fields, invalid TS).

role: Regression test for malformed nested schema descriptors in codegen
description: Guards against an opaque `TypeError` crash when a composite sub-field is missing `name` (zod envelope validation doesn't recurse into nested fields), and checks localizedText.languages tolerates non-string entries.
whatBreaks: Without this guard, a malformed --from schema (hand-authored or CI drift fixture) could crash the CLI with an unlocatable error instead of a clear message.

role: Duplicate/legacy field-mapping test suite (note plural 'tests/' dir)
description: A second, narrower generateTypes test file living in a differently-named `tests/` directory (vs the canonical `test/`) covering per-field-type mapping and JSDoc emission in isolation; likely a legacy or parallel suite that risks confusion/duplication with test/generate.test.ts.
whatBreaks: Duplicate coverage split across two directories risks one being forgotten on future codegen changes, letting a regression slip through unnoticed by the other.

role: test for codegen schema URL builder
description: Tests `buildSchemaPath` in the JS codegen package — verifies scoped path construction when workspace+project are provided, flat-path fallback for back-compat, and URL encoding of each segment.
whatBreaks: Schema URL path regressions in codegen go undetected, causing generated code to point at wrong API endpoints.

role: Smoke test for @barkpark/codegen scaffold exports
description: Minimal vitest suite asserting defineConfig returns its input and BarkparkSchemaJson type shape is reachable. Placeholder-level coverage, not a real integration test of code generation.
whatBreaks: A break here only means the codegen package's most basic export sanity check silently stops catching regressions, not a runtime failure.

role: TypeScript build config for the codegen package
description: Extends the monorepo base tsconfig, includes src/tests/test globs, sets rootDir to package root. Standard boilerplate.
whatBreaks: Wrong include globs or rootDir would break codegen's typecheck/build step (tsup/tsc), failing CI for that package.

role: Codegen package build config
description: tsup bundler configuration for the @barkpark/codegen package, specifying entry points, output formats, and build options.
whatBreaks: Codegen package fails to build or produces malformed output, breaking the codegen CLI tool.

role: Vitest configuration for codegen package
description: TypeScript vitest configuration for the @barkpark/codegen package. Defines node environment, coverage providers (v8 with json/lcov/text reporters), include globs over src/**, and shared test setup (../../test-utils/vitest.setup.ts). Minimal but required for the JS test gate to run.
whatBreaks: Codegen tests won't run or will run with wrong environment/coverage settings. Coverage reporting breaks for the codebase-quality tooling ingest (it reads coverage-final.json). The js-tests CI job fails on codegen due to missing/broken config.

role: Bundle-size budget config for @barkpark/core
description: Defines size-limit thresholds (15.5KB ESM, 16.25KB CJS gzip) enforced by the CI size gate mentioned in js/CLAUDE.md — a >2% regression fails the build.
whatBreaks: A misconfigured or loosened limit would let the core SDK's bundle silently bloat past its budget, defeating the CI size gate for the edge/browser-critical core client.

description: @barkpark/core

role: Primary usage documentation for @barkpark/core SDK
description: Comprehensive doc-tier:human README covering client creation, typed client, all read/write/listen/webhook/auth/tenancy operations with code examples — the canonical reference for the JS SDK's core package.
whatBreaks: Stale or wrong examples mislead every downstream SDK consumer (nextjs, react packages, external developers) into calling the API incorrectly, though no runtime code breaks.

role: npm package manifest for @barkpark/core
description: Defines dual ESM/CJS exports, build/test/lint/size scripts, and dependencies (optional undici, dev toolchain incl. vitest/tsup/size-limit/playwright). This is the package every other JS SDK package (nextjs, react, codegen) depends on.
whatBreaks: Wrong exports map or entrypoints breaks module resolution for every consumer of @barkpark/core across Node, edge, and browser runtimes, cascading to nextjs/react packages and any app using the SDK.

role: live regression test script
description: Standalone script that hits the prod API to verify defects #16 (docs.find) and #18 (doc by id) are fixed. Imports from the built dist and asserts envelope shape.
whatBreaks: Regression coverage for those two defects goes undetected; does not affect production runtime.

role: SDK function: GET dataset content-stats analytics endpoint
description: Thin wrapper calling `GET /v1/data/analytics/:dataset` for document counts (published/draft) and recent activity; token-required scoped read, exposed as `client.getAnalytics()`.
whatBreaks: Studio/consumer dashboards showing content stats would get wrong counts or fail entirely if this wire contract breaks.

role: SDK module: user auth (register/login/me/logout/MFA/password-reset)
description: Wraps the global (untenanted) `/v1/auth/*` endpoints — register, login (returns bearer session token), me, logout, TOTP MFA enroll/verify/disable, email verification, and password reset flows. Core seam for all authenticated client usage.
whatBreaks: Any bug here breaks login/registration/MFA for every consumer of @barkpark/core (Next.js integration, CLI, web demo), locking users out or leaking auth-state incorrectly.

role: SDK function: fetch inbound references (backlinks) for a document
description: Wraps `GET /v1/data/backlinks/:dataset/:id`, requires a token (404s anonymously for existence-hiding), exposed as `client.getBacklinks()`; validates non-empty id before requesting.
whatBreaks: Backlink/reverse-reference UI features (e.g. Studio's 'referenced by' panel) would fail or leak/hide data incorrectly if this contract drifts from the server.

role: Core factory wiring the entire BarkparkClient surface together
description: createClient() validates config, freezes it, and assembles the full client object (doc/docs/search/backlinks/graph/history/auth/media/schemas/webhooks/patch/transaction/listen/export/tenancy/handshake) by delegating to per-feature modules. This is the single seam every SDK operation flows through.

role: Single-document GET implementation (client.doc)
description: Builds the /v1/data/doc/:dataset/:type/:id request with expand/fields/perspective query params, unwraps the tolerant envelope, extracts ETag, and converts 404 into { data: null }. Core read primitive used by client.doc and getDocuments.
whatBreaks: Wrong envelope unwrapping or 404 handling breaks single-document reads and the getDocuments batch helper across the whole SDK, and the ETag/ifMatch optimistic-concurrency flow.

role: Fluent query (list) operation implementation (client.docs)
description: Wires createDocsBuilder's executor/countExecutor/pageExecutor to the /v1/data/query endpoint, handling the tolerant envelope, count queries, and paginated find with total. Backs every filter/order/limit query in the SDK.
whatBreaks: Wrong query-path construction or envelope unwrapping breaks all list/filter/paginate reads (.docs(type).find()/.count()/.findPage()) across every SDK consumer.

role: Error class taxonomy for the entire JS SDK
description: Defines BarkparkError base + subclasses (Auth/Network/Timeout/RateLimit/NotFound/Validation/Hmac/SchemaMismatch/EdgeRuntime/Conflict) each carrying a code equal to its class name, plus the isBarkparkError cross-bundle type guard used everywhere errors are inspected.
whatBreaks: Every module in core (doc, docs, transport, auth, media, webhooks) throws these types — a bug breaks error discrimination (e.g. 404→null conversion, MFA-required handling, cross-bundle instanceof checks) throughout the SDK and any app relying on isBarkparkError.

role: NDJSON dataset export streaming client (core SDK)
description: Async-generator that streams `GET /v1/data/export/:dataset` NDJSON via fetch + ReadableStream reader, yielding parsed documents one line at a time so large datasets never load fully into memory. Backup/portability counterpart to Sanity's dataset export; wraps malformed-line/auth/network errors into typed Barkpark*Error.
whatBreaks: Dataset backup/export tooling would silently corrupt, truncate, or hang on large datasets.

role: JS SDK escape-hatch raw HTTP fetch
description: Implements fetchRawDoc() — an escape hatch that sends an arbitrary authenticated request via transport, applying scopePrefix when workspace+project are configured, and returning the raw Response. Used by client.fetchRaw().
whatBreaks: client.fetchRaw() calls fail or route to wrong paths, breaking callers that rely on the escape hatch for endpoints not covered by typed methods.

role: Pure fluent query-builder + Phoenix wire-format encoder
description: Implements createDocsBuilder (the DocsBuilder chain: where/eq/neq/in/order/limit/offset/expand/select/find/count/findPage) plus buildQueryString, which encodes filters into Phoenix's filter[field][op]= param format, and validation helpers (makeFilterExpression, normalizeFieldList, assertNoCommaEntries) shared across docs/search/media.

role: Content-graph traversal client (getGraph/getOrphans/getDangling)
description: Calls the global (non-scoped) `/v1/graph/*` routes to traverse references from a root doc, list orphaned docs, and list dangling references; validates depth/kinds/sources and fails loud on unsupported 'raw' perspective rather than silently downgrading.
whatBreaks: Reference-graph UI (orphan/dangling detection, backlink traversal) returns wrong or unsafe results across all consumers of client.getGraph().

role: Lazy-cached /v1/meta handshake fetcher for the JS SDK client
description: Builds a dedupe/cache layer keyed by projectUrl+workspace+project+dataset around GET /v1/meta, used for schema-drift detection. Concurrent get() calls share one inflight promise; entry is dropped on rejection so the next caller retries.
whatBreaks: Wrong cache key collisions would leak one scope's schema metadata into another's drift-detection results, or a failed handshake would poison the cache and block all subsequent reads.

role: Document revision history client (list/get/restore revisions)
description: Wraps `/v1/data/history` and `/v1/data/revision` endpoints for listing a document's past versions, fetching one, and restoring it as a new draft (Sanity-style history). Null-on-404 semantics for single-revision fetch.
whatBreaks: Version history/restore feature breaks across every SDK consumer, risking silent data loss on restore.

role: Preset-based image URL builder (Sanity urlFor equivalent)
description: Pure function `imageUrl()` turns a stored image field (ref, expanded asset, or bare URL) into a rendition URL under `/media/renditions/<id>/<preset>` or original `/images/<id>`; no width-parametric transforms, only fixed named presets matching server-side `Barkpark.Media.Renditions`.
whatBreaks: Every image rendered via the SDK (React/Next.js renderers, demo apps) could point at broken or wrong-sized URLs sitewide.

role: Public API barrel/entry point for the @barkpark/core npm package
description: Re-exports every public function, class, and type of the core SDK (client factory, operation factories, errors, typed-client helper). Explicitly documented as a permanent contract surface — every export here is an API guarantee for downstream consumers (nextjs, react packages, codegen, external apps).

role: SSE realtime listen-stream client for GET /v1/data/listen/:dataset
description: Implements createListenHandle, a hand-rolled SSE parser over fetch+ReadableStream (EventSource can't send Bearer auth), with reconnect/backoff, idle-timeout watchdog, buffer-overflow protection, and edge-runtime detection. Dense, heavily-commented logic with several named failure-mode fixes ([idle-timeout-stall], [buffer-unbounded], [clean-close-infinite-silent], [backoff-jitter], [signal-listener-leak]).
whatBreaks: Realtime subscriptions (client.listen) would silently stall, leak memory/listeners, spin in a reconnect loop, or fail to detect half-open sockets, breaking live-update features across every app using the SDK's listen API.

role: Media/asset + collections REST client module (core SDK)
description: 533-line module covering upload, list/get/delete/update assets, checkout/undo-checkout editorial locks, relations, search + suggestions, and full collections CRUD (members, share links) against `/v1/media/*`; heavy param/id validation guards throughout.
whatBreaks: The entire media library feature (upload, browse, search, collections, sharing) across all SDK consumers breaks or misbehaves.

role: Single-document patch/mutation builder (set/unset/inc/dec/append/prepend)
description: Implements createPatch used by client.patch(id), validating fields (rejecting system fields like _id/_type), assembling a patch body, and POSTing to /v1/data/mutate. Also exports selectorField(), shared with transaction.ts so patch semantics stay identical inside and outside transactions.

role: Publish/unpublish/discardDraft lifecycle operations for the JS SDK
description: Thin wrappers issuing single-mutation POST /v1/data/mutate requests for the draft→published lifecycle transitions, threading CommitOptions (idempotency key, retry, timeoutMs) consistently with the transaction/patch commit paths.
whatBreaks: client.publish/unpublish/discardDraft calls would fail to transition documents between draft and published state or lose idempotency/retry guarantees on those writes.

role: Generic exponential-backoff retry engine for the SDK transport layer
description: Provides RetryPolicy configs (read/write/idempotent-write), defaultShouldRetry classification, jittered/capped backoff computation, and an abortable retry() loop used by transport.request for every SDK call.
whatBreaks: Incorrect retry logic could cause writes to be duplicated (non-idempotent retries), reads to hammer a struggling server without backoff, or aborts to hang instead of cancelling immediately.

role: Schema introspection/upsert client (core SDK)
description: Wraps `/v1/schemas/:dataset[/:name]` for listing, fetching, upserting, and deleting content-type schemas — used by dynamic/generic UIs and by codegen tooling to introspect schema shape.
whatBreaks: Schema-driven UIs and the codegen package's introspection step would get wrong or missing field definitions, cascading into typed-client generation errors.

role: Builds the /w/:workspace/p/:project URL prefix for scoped requests
description: Tiny leaf module (depends only on ./types) computing scopePrefix(config); returns '' for back-compat flat routes when workspace/project aren't both set. Deliberately kept leaf/acyclic so every operation module can import it without re-entering client.ts.
whatBreaks: Every scoped SDK operation (patch, transaction, publish, listen, handshake, docs) would build the wrong URL — either hitting the wrong workspace/project or falling back incorrectly to flat routes.

role: Full-text document search + suggestions client (core SDK)
description: Wraps `GET /v1/data/search/:dataset` (flat, not result-enveloped) and its suggestions endpoint; enforces mutually-exclusive type/types params and non-empty query, respects client perspective with per-call override.
whatBreaks: Document search-as-you-type/search-box features across all SDK consumers return wrong hits or throw incorrectly.

role: Top-level workspace/project/dataset listing + creation API client
description: Implements listWorkspaces/listProjects/listDatasets/createWorkspace/createProject against the un-scoped /api/workspaces... endpoints (not scopePrefix-prefixed, not dataset-scoped) — the tenancy drill-down used e.g. by onboarding/multi-tenant UIs.
whatBreaks: Apps relying on the SDK to enumerate or create workspaces/projects/datasets (e.g. onboarding flows, admin tooling) would fail to discover or create tenancy resources.

role: Multi-mutation atomic transaction builder for the JS SDK
description: Implements createTransaction (client.transaction()) supporting create/createOrReplace/createIfNotExists/patch/publish/unpublish/discardDraft/delete chained into one atomic POST /v1/data/mutate. Reuses patch.ts's selectorField and mirrors its validation for a consistent inner-patch semantics.
whatBreaks: Any multi-step atomic write (e.g. patch+publish in one transaction) used by SDK consumers would fail to validate correctly or could bypass atomicity guarantees, risking partial/corrupted writes.

role: Core HTTP request engine underlying every @barkpark/core SDK call
description: The `request<T>()` function that every other module (client, handshake, docs, patch, transaction, fetchRaw, tenancy) goes through: builds URLs/headers, runs onBeforeRequest/onResponse hooks, manages per-attempt AbortController timeouts, decodes the Phoenix error envelope into the typed error taxonomy (errors.ts), and delegates retry to retry.ts with idempotency-key injection for opted-in writes.
whatBreaks: A bug here breaks literally every SDK operation — reads, writes, auth headers, timeouts, retries, and error classification would all be wrong across every consumer of @barkpark/core (nextjs, react, codegen, and all downstream apps).

role: Public TypeScript type surface for @barkpark/core SDK
description: Defines every public interface/type of the runtime-agnostic Barkpark JS client: config, query/patch/transaction builders, document/media/webhook/auth/tenancy shapes, and the full BarkparkClient surface. Derived from ADRs 002/005/006/007/009/010/011 — explicitly marked not to be shape-broken without an ADR amendment; consumed by every other core module and by @barkpark/nextjs, @barkpark/react, and codegen'd typed clients.

role: Pure heuristic detector for Edge/Workerd runtimes
description: Zero-side-effect, import-safe function that inspects globalThis for Vercel Edge, Next.js edge, and Cloudflare Workers/workerd signals so client.listen() can throw BarkparkEdgeRuntimeError before attempting an SSE connection that can't stream reliably.
whatBreaks: A wrong or missed detection lets listen() attempt SSE on an edge runtime that can't stream, causing silent hangs or misleading errors instead of the intended fail-fast.

role: HTTP header utilities
description: Builds the base Accept/Content-Type headers every request carries, generates RFC 9562 UUIDv7 tokens for Idempotency-Key, and normalizes the Phoenix request_id snake/camel casing from error envelopes.
whatBreaks: Every SDK request sends wrong vendor Accept headers (breaking API content negotiation) and idempotency keys become non-unique or malformed.

role: Incoming-webhook HMAC signature verifier (runtime-agnostic)
description: Web Crypto-based `verifyWebhookSignature` validates the `x-barkpark-signature: t=…,v1=…` HMAC-SHA256 header with a replay-window check and previous-secret rotation support; also exports `parseWebhookEvent` and the `WebhookEvent`/`WebhookEventKind` wire types. Zero node:crypto dependency, so it's Edge-safe.
whatBreaks: A broken/bypassable check here lets forged webhook deliveries be accepted as authentic (security-critical) or legitimate deliveries get silently rejected everywhere webhooks are consumed.

role: Webhook management (admin CRUD) client — outbound control plane
description: Wraps `/v1/webhooks/:dataset` CRUD (list/get/create/update/delete) for registering and managing a dataset's outbound webhook subscriptions; validates absolute http(s) URLs client-side. Deliberately separate module from webhook.ts (signature verification) to keep the verify path transport-free/tree-shakeable.
whatBreaks: Webhook registration/management UI (e.g. in Studio) can't create or update subscriptions, or ships malformed delivery URLs to the server.

role: Vitest test for core SDK's getAnalytics() client method
description: MSW-mocked test verifying getAnalytics() fetches `/v1/data/analytics/:ds`, correctly maps the content-stats response shape, and propagates server errors (401) as rejected promises.
whatBreaks: Only regression coverage for the analytics client method is lost/incorrect; no runtime behavior changes.

role: Vitest suite for @barkpark/core auth.* client methods
description: Covers register/login/me/logout/mfa enroll+verify+disable/verify-email/password-reset flows against msw-mocked /v1/auth/* endpoints, asserting request bodies, URLs, and error surfacing (serverCode on 422).
whatBreaks: A regression here would let a broken auth client method (wrong endpoint, dropped field, or swallowed error) ship undetected to every app using @barkpark/core auth.

role: Vitest suite for client.getBacklinks() in @barkpark/core
description: Verifies GET /v1/data/backlinks/:ds/:id unwraps {backlinks,count}, handles empty results, URL-encodes ids, and rejects an empty id client-side with BarkparkValidationError before any network call.
whatBreaks: A broken getBacklinks (bad path, missing id validation) would go live undetected, breaking reverse-reference lookups in consuming apps.

role: JS SDK client integration test
description: Integration tests for @barkpark/core's createClient using MSW mock server, covering doc(), query(), mutate(), handshake(), and error handling against the /v1/data/* API contract.
whatBreaks: JS SDK client regressions against the HTTP API contract go undetected, shipping broken doc/query/mutate calls to all JS consumers.

role: Unit tests for createClient() config validation
description: Verifies createClient freezes its config and validates projectUrl, apiVersion format, dataset charset, and warns on drafts/raw perspective without a token.
whatBreaks: Regressions in client config validation (e.g. accepting a malformed apiVersion) would go undetected, letting bad configs reach the server.

role: Vitest suite proving CommitOptions.timeoutMs is forwarded through commit/create/delete
description: Uses a hanging fetch + fake timers to assert transaction/patch commits and the create/delete shortcuts all honor a caller-supplied timeoutMs and reject with BarkparkTimeoutError rather than hanging on the 60s write default.
whatBreaks: If timeoutMs stopped being forwarded, callers could hang up to 60s on a stuck write with no way to bound it, undetected by this suite.

role: Unit tests for getDoc/createDocsOperation single & list reads
description: Large (567-line) MSW-backed test suite covering doc()/docs() read paths, perspective/expand/fields options, and a protective import from the public index to guard exported types (GetDocOptions, DocResult, DocsOperationOptions).
whatBreaks: Read-path regressions (wrong etag, perspective, or expand/fields handling) in the core SDK's most-used operations would ship undetected.

role: Regression test locking Phoenix's flat query/doc envelope shape
description: Uses byte-level fixtures captured from the live Phoenix API to guard against defects #16/#18 (server re-wrapping responses in a `result` key); fails first if the wire contract regresses.
whatBreaks: If Phoenix's envelope shape silently changes, the whole SDK read path would break for every consumer without this test catching it first.

role: Vitest suite for the isBarkparkError() type-guard in @barkpark/core
description: Checks isBarkparkError accepts real error instances, narrows by code, matches duck-typed cross-bundle copies (no instanceof), rejects null/plain Error, and that TypeScript narrowing exposes subclass-only fields without a cast.
whatBreaks: A broken guard would make error handling across SDK consumers silently misclassify or fail to narrow Barkpark errors, especially across bundle boundaries.

role: Vitest suite for client.exportDataset() NDJSON streaming
description: Verifies the async-iterable NDJSON parser yields one doc per line including a trailing line with no newline, forwards type+perspective query params, wraps malformed JSON lines as BarkparkAPIError (not raw SyntaxError), and surfaces non-ok HTTP as a typed error.
whatBreaks: A regressed NDJSON parser could drop the last document of every export or leak untyped SyntaxErrors that consumers' isBarkparkError() checks miss.

role: Unit tests for the fluent DocsBuilder filter/order/query-string logic
description: Tests createDocsBuilder/buildQueryString/makeFilterExpression: fluent chaining, semantic sugar methods (eq/neq/in/nin/has/contains/gt/gte/lt/lte), and validation errors.
whatBreaks: Broken filter-op mapping would produce wrong server queries (e.g. eq mistaken for neq) without detection.

role: Shared MSW mock-server handlers simulating the Phoenix /v1 API
description: Runtime-agnostic MSW 2.x handlers/fixtures (meta, query, mutate, listen, error envelopes) shared across most core test files; shapes are kept in sync with types.ts and api/lib/barkpark/content/envelope.ex.
whatBreaks: Drift between these fixtures and the real Phoenix API would let many core SDK tests pass against a stale/wrong contract, masking real breakage.

description: ts fixture file.

role: MSW fixture handler smoke test
description: Validates that the MSW (Mock Service Worker) test fixture handlers for the JS core package correctly mock /v1/meta and /v1/data/query endpoints, including scalar vs map schemaHash responses and error envelopes.
whatBreaks: Broken fixture handlers would silently produce false-positive results in all core SDK tests that depend on these MSW mocks.

role: Vitest suite for getGraph/getOrphans/getDangling in @barkpark/core
description: Covers /v1/graph/:id traversal options (depth, direction, kinds, perspective inheritance/override), client-side validation (depth range/type, empty id, comma-in-kinds/sources injection guard, raw perspective requiring explicit override), and orphans/dangling array unwrapping.
whatBreaks: Loss of the comma-injection or depth-range guards could let malformed graph queries reach the server or silently broaden edge/source filters; broken perspective inheritance could leak drafts into published-perspective calls.

role: Vitest suite for createHandshakeCache scope-aware keying
description: Proves the /v1/meta handshake cache keys strictly on projectUrl+workspace+project+dataset so two scopes sharing projectUrl+dataset never collide, that repeat gets within one scope dedupe to a single request, and that invalidate() only drops the targeted scope.
whatBreaks: A cache-key regression could cross-contaminate schema-drift detection between two tenants/workspaces sharing a projectUrl, silently corrupting one scope's schema-hash with another's.

role: Vitest suite for getHistory/getRevision/restoreRevision in @barkpark/core
description: Covers revision-history listing with limit validation, 404-to-null semantics on getRevision, restoreRevision's POST body/response shape, and client-side BarkparkValidationError guards for empty type/id/revId before any network call.
whatBreaks: Missing empty-id guards would collapse URL paths (e.g. /v1/data/revision/:ds/) into opaque server errors instead of clear client-side validation failures.

role: Vitest suite for the imageUrl() helper and client.imageUrl in @barkpark/core
description: Exercises rendition-preset URL building from _id/_ref/inline-url assets, encoding of reserved characters in ids and presets, baseUrl trailing-slash trimming, workspace/project pathPrefix scoping (and its absence for inline URLs), and defaulting baseUrl to projectUrl on the client.
whatBreaks: A broken encode or pathPrefix rule would emit malformed or wrongly-scoped URLs across every app rendering Barkpark media, including cross-tenant path leaks in multi-workspace setups.

role: Vitest suite for input-validation guards across search/getDocuments/uploadAsset
description: Verifies search's type/types mutual-exclusion guard, getDocuments' pre-network validation of ids (rejecting bare strings, non-arrays, non-string elements) and type, and uploadAsset's Blob duck-type guard (rejecting null/path-strings, accepting real Blobs) — all failing client-side before any fetch.
whatBreaks: Losing these guards would let malformed calls (e.g. a bare string id treated as an array) slip past validation and crash deep inside request building instead of failing fast with a clear BarkparkValidationError.

role: end-to-end barrel integration smoke test
description: Drives the full public barrel (createClient → doc → docs → patch → publish → withConfig) through MSW-mocked HTTP and verifies every named export is present in the barrel.
whatBreaks: Missing barrel exports or lifecycle regressions ship undetected to SDK consumers.

role: Unit tests for the SSE listen()/createListenHandle real-time client
description: Large (572-line) suite covering SSE subscription, eq-only ListenFilter type guard, and edge-runtime error throwing (BarkparkEdgeRuntimeError) via createListenHandle.
whatBreaks: Regressions in real-time listen() (wrong event parsing, missed edge-runtime guard) would break live-update consumers silently.

role: Vitest suite for @barkpark/core media (assets/collections) API surface
description: Covers uploadAsset multipart POST, listAssets/getAsset/deleteAsset, search/suggestions and collections endpoints against MSW-mocked handlers. Exercises paging, error handling, and response shape mapping for the media SDK module.
whatBreaks: A regression in the core media client (upload, asset listing, collections) could ship silently to every JS/Next.js consumer of @barkpark/core.

role: Vitest suite asserting shared assertPaging guard across all core read endpoints
description: Table-driven test that runs the same invalid/valid limit+offset assertions across searchDocuments, listAssets, searchAssets, getAssetSearchSuggestions, listCollections, getCollectionAssets — guarding one shared validation helper used by many entrypoints.
whatBreaks: If the shared paging validation regresses, malformed limit/offset (negative, NaN, zero) could pass through unchecked into API requests across every core read function.

role: Unit tests for the createPatch fluent single-document patch builder
description: Verifies set/inc/dec/setIfMissing/unset/append/prepend patch ops and commit() behavior against MSW fixtures, including validation error cases for system fields and unsupported ops (insert, diffMatchPatch).
whatBreaks: Undetected regressions in patch-op serialization could corrupt document mutations sent to the server.

role: Vitest suite for X-Barkpark-Request-Tag observability header
description: Small, focused test verifying the client attaches a bp-prefixed request tag header by default, honors a custom prefix, and omits it when opted out via empty string.
whatBreaks: Loss of request tagging would degrade observability/debugging for API requests traced through this header, but wouldn't break functional behavior.

role: Vitest suite for core retry policy logic (defaultShouldRetry, retry())
description: Tests which errors are retried (network/timeout/rate-limit, 5xx but never 4xx) and the retry loop's attempt/backoff control flow using zero-delay policies.
whatBreaks: A broken retry policy could cause the SDK to retry non-idempotent writes on 4xx errors or fail to retry legitimate transient failures, affecting reliability of every core-based client.

role: browser runtime environment check
description: Verifies that globalThis.fetch and ReadableStream exist under the browser vitest environment, and that createClient exposes its full method surface.
whatBreaks: Browser runtime incompatibilities (missing globals, missing methods) go undetected.

role: workerd/edge runtime environment check
description: Minimal 8-line test confirming globalThis.fetch is available under the workerd (Cloudflare Workers) vitest environment.
whatBreaks: Edge runtime breakage (missing fetch) goes unnoticed before publishing.

role: Vitest suite for core schema-introspection API (schemas(), getSchema())
description: Verifies schemas() unwraps the for-sdk envelope into a list, signal abort propagation, and getSchema(name) single-schema/404-null behavior.
whatBreaks: Broken schema introspection would break codegen and any consumer relying on runtime schema discovery via @barkpark/core.

role: tests for workspace/project scope URL prefix
description: Verifies that listen() and handshake() prepend /w/<workspace>/p/<project> to /v1/ paths when workspace+project are set, and remain flat otherwise for back-compat.
whatBreaks: Multi-workspace routing breaks — scoped clients hit wrong API paths silently.

role: Vitest suite for core document search API (bp.search)
description: Confirms the GET /v1/data/search request shape (q/limit/engine) and full response mapping including facets, highlights, correctedTo, recovery, and truncation flags.
whatBreaks: A regression here could silently drop or misparse search facets/highlights for every consuming search UI.

role: Package-export smoke test for @barkpark/core's public index
description: Small (66-line) sanity suite asserting createClient/error classes/typedClient are exported and that key public types (QueryEnvelope, MediaAssetPage, ListenOptions, etc.) remain re-exported from the package root — a compile-time guard against accidental un-exports.
whatBreaks: A dropped export from index.ts would silently break downstream consumers (Next.js/React packages, typed clients) that import from the package root.

role: Test suite for tenancy API (workspaces/projects/datasets) in core SDK
description: Verifies listWorkspaces/listProjects/listDatasets/createWorkspace/createProject hit the correct top-level (never scope-prefixed) endpoints, unwrap response envelopes correctly, and surface typed BarkparkValidationError instead of raw TypeErrors on malformed responses. Uses MSW to mock HTTP.
whatBreaks: A regression here would let tenancy endpoint paths or error handling silently drift without being caught before release.

role: Vitest suite distinguishing user abort vs real network failure in core transport
description: Regression test ensuring a user-initiated AbortSignal surfaces as a non-retried AbortError (not wrapped/retried as BarkparkNetworkError), while a genuine fetch failure still retries per the read policy.
whatBreaks: Without this guard, aborting a request (e.g. React unmount, route navigation) would incorrectly retry ~3x with backoff instead of failing fast, wasting time and network calls across every core consumer.

role: Vitest suite for core transport's default/per-call request timeouts
description: Uses fake timers and a hanging fetch to verify the documented 60s write default timeout applies when unconfigured, and that a per-call timeoutMs overrides it.
whatBreaks: If the default timeout regresses, unconfigured clients could hang indefinitely on a stalled server instead of failing with BarkparkTimeoutError.

role: Vitest suite for uploadAsset's distinct (120s) timeout default
description: Verifies uploadAsset honors a per-call timeoutMs override and applies a longer 120s default (not the 60s generic write default) for large file uploads.
whatBreaks: Wrong upload timeout defaults would cause legitimate large uploads to abort prematurely, or hangs to persist too long, degrading the upload UX for every SDK consumer.

role: Vitest suite for core webhook signature verification (Web Crypto HMAC)
description: Cross-checks verifyWebhookSignature (Web Crypto) against an independent node:crypto HMAC-SHA256 reference implementation, covering valid signature, wrong secret, tampered body, and stale-timestamp replay defense.
whatBreaks: A broken webhook signature verifier is a security-critical failure — it could let forged/replayed webhook payloads be accepted as authentic across every consumer (including the Edge-compatible nextjs webhook subpath).

role: Vitest suite for @barkpark/core webhook CRUD client methods
description: Covers listWebhooks/getWebhook/createWebhook/updateWebhook/deleteWebhook against an msw-mocked API: response unwrapping ({webhooks}/{webhook}), 404-to-null mapping, client-side validation guards (empty name/url/id, scheme-less url) that fast-fail without a network round-trip, and AbortSignal threading.
whatBreaks: A regression here would ship with undetected breakage in the SDK's webhook management surface (wrong unwrap key, missing validation, or a wasted round-trip on a bad id/url) used by every consumer building CI/deploy hooks.

role: Test suite for core SDK write path (transactions, publish/unpublish, patch ops)
description: Exercises createTransaction/create/patch/publish/unpublish/discardDraft mutation building, scopePrefix behavior (flat vs /w/.../p/... URLs), idempotency-key headers, and typed error taxonomy on malformed 2xx/422 responses; uses a fetch spy to assert exact request bodies.
whatBreaks: Broken coverage here would let mutation request-shape bugs (wrong body, missing scope prefix, untyped errors) ship undetected, corrupting SDK write reliability across every consuming app.

whatBreaks: Tests would fail to run in the correct environment; coverage metrics would not be generated. CI gate would break since the test suite wouldn't execute.

create-barkpark-app

description: Documents quick-start commands, CLI flags, available templates, and the local vs hosted-demo workflow for scaffolding a new Barkpark app.
whatBreaks: Stale docs would mislead new users into wrong CLI usage or a broken local setup flow, but nothing in the running system depends on it.

role: Package manifest for the create-barkpark-app npm scaffolder CLI
description: Declares the two CLI bin entrypoints (create-barkpark-app, cba), dependencies (@clack/prompts, commander, execa, cross-spawn, picocolors), and build/test scripts (tsup, vitest). Files array controls what ships to npm.
whatBreaks: A wrong bin path, missing dependency, or incorrect files list would break `pnpm create barkpark-app` / `npx create-barkpark-app` entirely for all new users.

role: scaffolder constants (version, templates, demo URL)
description: Defines BARKPARK_VERSION (injected at build time or falling back to preview), the list of available starter templates, the default template name, and the hosted demo URL for create-barkpark-app.
whatBreaks: Wrong version string or missing template names cause the scaffolder to offer stale/invalid options or stamp wrong version metadata into new projects.

role: Applies --hosted-demo mode to a freshly scaffolded app
description: Removes docker-compose files, writes a .env.local pointing at the public hosted demo API, and rewrites app/layout.tsx to enable a HostedDemoBanner component via a marker-comment replace, so scaffolded apps can skip local Docker setup.
whatBreaks: If the env values or banner-injection regex are wrong, --hosted-demo apps would fail to connect to the demo API or silently miss the banner, degrading the onboarding demo path.

role: Main CLI entrypoint orchestrating the create-barkpark-app scaffold flow
description: Parses CLI flags (commander), runs interactive prompts, validates the target directory is empty, scaffolds the chosen template, optionally applies hosted-demo settings, installs deps, runs git init, and prints next-steps guidance. This is the top-level control flow tying together prompts.ts, scaffold.ts, hosted.ts, install.ts, post-install.ts.
whatBreaks: A broken entrypoint would make `pnpm create barkpark-app` fail or scaffold apps into an unusable/half-configured state for every new user of the CLI.

role: Dependency installer helper
description: Small helper that invokes the detected package manager to install dependencies in the scaffolded project directory.
whatBreaks: create-barkpark-app silently skips or fails dependency installation, leaving new projects in a broken state.

role: Package manager detector
description: Detects which package manager (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) is in use by inspecting lockfiles and the npm_config_user_agent env var, returning the install command.
whatBreaks: Scaffolder uses the wrong package manager, producing install errors or wrong lockfiles in new projects.

role: Post-scaffold git init + next-steps printer for create-barkpark-app CLI
description: Runs `git init` + initial commit non-fatally, and prints tailored next-step instructions depending on whether --hosted-demo or local docker-compose was chosen and whether deps were installed.
whatBreaks: Failure here would leave scaffolded projects without a git history or give users incorrect/missing next-step instructions, a UX-only impact.

role: Interactive/non-interactive prompt flow for create-barkpark-app CLI inputs
description: Collects and validates project name, template choice, hosted-demo flag, install/git choices via @clack/prompts; includes projectNameError guard so a bad non-interactive name (e.g. '.', empty) fails fast with a clear message instead of a confusing downstream 'directory not empty' error.
whatBreaks: Broken validation or defaulting here could scaffold into the wrong/unsafe directory (e.g. cwd) or silently corrupt CLI flag handling for both interactive and -y non-interactive runs.

role: Template-copy engine for create-barkpark-app scaffolder
description: Recursively copies a chosen template directory into the target project dir, renaming `_gitignore`/`_npmrc`, stripping `.tmpl` suffixes, and running a `{{var}}` mustache-style substitution over text files (project name, package name, pm command, barkpark version). Also exports `toPackageName` slugification used to derive a valid npm name from the user's project name.
whatBreaks: Every `create-barkpark-app` run (blog-starter etc.) would scaffold broken/unsubstituted files or crash, breaking the primary onboarding path for new Barkpark users.

role: Env-var template for the blog-starter scaffolded project
description: Documents required env vars (API URL, dataset, workspace/project scoping, dev tokens, preview secret, Postgres, Phoenix SECRET_KEY_BASE) that a new blog-starter app copies to `.env.local`. Purely a template asset, copied verbatim (minus rename) by scaffold.ts.
whatBreaks: New blog-starter users get missing/incorrect env var names and can't connect to the API or enable preview/webhooks; wrong secrets guidance could also lead to shipping dev secrets to prod.

role: README template shipped inside the scaffolded blog-starter app
description: End-user-facing doc covering quick start, auth token rotation, draft-mode preview, realtime webhook revalidation contract, deploy steps, and project layout for the generated blog. Contains `{{projectName}}`/`{{pmCommand}}` template vars rendered by scaffold.ts.
whatBreaks: Misleads new users setting up the starter (wrong token, wrong webhook contract) but doesn't break running code.

@barkpark/nextjs

role: Package README indexing @barkpark/nextjs's eight subpath entry points
description: Canonical (doc-tier: agent, canonical-for: nextjs-package) map of the package's exports (server/client/actions/webhook/draft-mode/revalidate/preload plus root) and the critical warning that the root export's revalidateBarkpark is a throw-only stub — use ./revalidate instead.
whatBreaks: Developers (and agents) import revalidateBarkpark from the wrong subpath and hit a throw-only stub in production, or miss which subpath owns which capability, causing broken cache revalidation.

role: npm manifest and multi-entry exports map for the @barkpark/nextjs package
description: Defines the eight dual-format (ESM/CJS) subpath exports (., server, client, actions, webhook, draft-mode, revalidate, preload), peer deps on next 15-16/react 19/optional zod, and build/test/size-limit scripts; this is the real, actively-consumed integration package (unlike groq/nextjs-query stubs).
whatBreaks: A wrong/missing subpath export or peer-dependency mismatch breaks module resolution across every Next.js app consuming @barkpark/nextjs (server fetching, live subscriptions, webhooks, draft mode, revalidation, preload, actions all ride this manifest).

role: Factory for Barkpark Server Actions (create/patch/publish/etc)
description: Builds a BarkparkActions bundle wrapping the core authoring client's mutate/patch/publish/unpublish/discardDraft/delete calls, validating input against optional Zod-like schemas and fanning out canonical revalidate tags (bp:...:doc:/type:) via next/cache revalidateTag after each mutation. Guards against empty _type, non-object schema.parse results, and pins _type back after Zod strips unknown keys.
whatBreaks: App Router apps using generated Server Actions would silently corrupt writes or fail to invalidate cache after create/patch/publish, leaving stale content or dropped mutations.

role: Barrel export for the actions/ subpath
description: Re-exports defineActions and useOptimisticDocument plus their types; the public surface of @barkpark/nextjs/actions.
whatBreaks: Consumers importing from @barkpark/nextjs/actions would get missing/broken exports, breaking the actions subpath entirely.

role: React client hook combining useOptimistic + Server Action + conflict handling
description: Merges patches into an optimistic view immediately, commits via a passed server action inside a transition, and surfaces BarkparkConflictError details (serverEtag/serverDoc) on failure. Uses refs to track in-flight/committed/latest payloads so overlapping mutations don't clobber each other, and matches conflict errors by string 'code' literal to survive duplicate class copies across pnpm-hoisted bundles.
whatBreaks: Optimistic editors built on this hook would show incorrect state, lose in-flight edits on concurrent mutations, or fail to surface/resolve write conflicts.

role: Barrel export for the client/ (browser) subpath
description: Re-exports BarkparkLive, BarkparkLiveProvider, startLiveSubscription, detectEdgeRuntime and their types from live.tsx — the public surface of @barkpark/nextjs/client.
whatBreaks: Consumers importing from @barkpark/nextjs/client lose access to the live-reload components entirely.

role: Client component: SSE-driven live-refresh subscription (BarkparkLive)
description: Mounts a debounced SSE subscription to a BarkparkClient and calls router.refresh() on events; renders nothing. Has a 3-layer Node-runtime guard (throws BarkparkEdgeRuntimeError if run on Edge), HMR-safe teardown via beforeunload + module.hot.dispose, and a dev-only 'no SSE event received' warning. startLiveSubscription is exported standalone (no React deps) for direct/testable use.
whatBreaks: Live-preview/auto-refresh in Next.js apps would silently stop working, leak SSE connections across HMR/navigation, or crash when misdeployed to an Edge route.

role: HMAC-signed draft-mode preview route factory (Phase 5)
description: createDraftModeRoutes builds GET/DELETE route handlers implementing a signed preview-URL contract (HMAC-SHA256 over path+expiry, constant-time compare, 10-min default TTL) that enable/disable Next's draftMode(); signDraftModeToken produces the signed payload. Uses node:crypto — the js/CLAUDE.md-documented sole violator of the 'no node: imports in edge subpaths' rule, pending an ADR decision.
whatBreaks: Preview/draft links could be forged (auth bypass into draft content) or legitimate editors could be locked out of preview mode; deploying this route to Edge would crash.

role: draft-mode config and handler types
description: Defines TypeScript interfaces for draft/preview mode configuration (DraftModeConfig) and the GET/DELETE handler shape returned by createDraftModeRoutes. Includes dual-secret rotation pattern for preview token reissuance.
whatBreaks: Type errors in draft-mode consumers; incorrect interface shapes cause compile failures in anything importing DraftModeConfig or DraftModeHandlers.

role: Package root export — intentionally minimal, contains a throwing stub
description: Re-exports core types and barkparkMetadata; revalidateBarkpark here is a deliberate throw-only guard stub so the real server-only implementation (src/revalidate/index.ts) never gets bundled into client code. Documented repo-wide as the 'root-export stub trap' in js/CLAUDE.md.
whatBreaks: If the stub were removed or accidentally made real, Next.js server cache APIs could leak into client bundles, or callers importing revalidateBarkpark from package root would get a confusing runtime throw instead of working revalidation.

role: Barkpark-doc-to-Next.js Metadata builder helper
description: barkparkMetadata(doc, overrides) maps a loosely-typed Barkpark document into Next.js Metadata/OpenGraph shape, with title/description fallback chains and article-vs-website OG type based on publishedAt. Pure, framework-safe, exported from package root.
whatBreaks: Every consuming app's generateMetadata/OG tags would render wrong titles, leak empty descriptions, or mis-tag article vs website type across all pages using this helper.

role: Request-scoped document preloader (parallel data fetching helper)
description: createPreloader wraps a server's barkparkFetch with a dedup Map + React cache() so preloadDocument (fire-and-forget) and loadDocument (await) share one in-flight request; must be instantiated per-request (via React cache()) or it becomes a cross-request stale-data leak — explicitly documented as a known held risk (preload-request-scope-tradeoff memory). Also exports a simpler one-shot preloadDocument function.
whatBreaks: Misuse (module-scope instantiation) leaks one request's document data into another user's response; correct usage failures would cause duplicate fetches or lost preload benefit.

role: Server-only cache revalidation entrypoint for Phoenix webhook payloads
description: revalidateBarkpark parses a Phoenix webhook body (or manual fields) into revalidateTag/revalidatePath calls, preferring server-emitted sync_tags verbatim and falling back to constructing scoped (workspace/project) or legacy flat dataset tags via the shared formatTagPrefix. Path-based revalidation is gated behind BARKPARK_ALLOW_ALL_REVALIDATE env var and throws if unset. This is the REAL implementation the package-root stub points to.
whatBreaks: Webhook-driven cache invalidation would fail silently (stale content served indefinitely) or over-invalidate, and an unguarded path revalidation could allow unrestricted cache-busting of arbitrary paths.

role: Core server-side fetch engine — draft-mode-aware data fetching + tagging
description: barkparkFetchInner/runFetch build the actual fetch() call against Phoenix's /v1/data endpoints, branching on Next's draftMode(): published reads use force-cache with a canonical tag set (dataset/type/doc tags matching the webhook's revalidateTag grammar), draft reads use no-store + Authorization Bearer + one auto-retry on 401 via reissuePreviewToken. defineLive/createBarkparkServer are the public factories; deliberately does NOT export the client-only Live components to avoid pulling React.createContext into the RSC server graph.
whatBreaks: Every server-rendered page using @barkpark/nextjs would fetch wrong/stale data, break draft preview auth, or emit cache tags that don't match webhook invalidation (silent stale content across the whole app).

role: Public entry for @barkpark/nextjs server subpath
description: Re-exports createBarkparkServer, defineLive, and barkparkFetch (aliased from ./core) plus server-only types; deliberately withholds BarkparkLive/BarkparkLiveProvider (client-only) to keep the react-server graph clean. Marked 'server-only' so importing it in a client component fails the build.
whatBreaks: SSR/RSC data fetching for every Next.js app using @barkpark/nextjs (draft-mode + published-branch reads) would fail to import or leak client-only React context into the server graph.

role: Type contract for BarkparkServerConfig and barkparkFetch options
description: Defines the config shape (client, serverToken, workspace/project scoping, fetchOptions, reissuePreviewToken) and per-call BarkparkFetchOptions (type/id/expand/fields/query/perspective/tags/revalidate/syncTags) consumed by the server core implementation.
whatBreaks: Wrong or drifted types here would silently mistype server-side fetch calls across every consuming Next.js app, or break workspace/project URL scoping.

role: Single source of truth for cache-tag namespace prefix format
description: formatTagPrefix(dataset, workspace?, project?) produces the scoped bp:ws:...:p:...:ds:... prefix or legacy bp:ds:... fallback; this exact string format is a contract shared by write-side defineActions, read-side server tagging, and the webhook revalidate fallback.
whatBreaks: Any drift in this format silently breaks cache invalidation — writes/webhooks stop revalidating matching reads across every Next.js app using @barkpark/nextjs caching.

role: App Router webhook handler factory (HMAC verify + dedup)
description: createWebhookHandler verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature via @barkpark/core's Web Crypto verifyWebhookSignature (Edge-compatible), enforces a freshness window, and dedupes replayed deliveries using a module-scoped LRU + in-flight promise map so concurrent retries don't drop or double-fire onMutation. Exposes __resetDedupForTests for test isolation.
whatBreaks: Broken signature/dedup logic would let forged webhook payloads through, drop legitimate cache revalidations, or double-invalidate on retry storms.

role: Types for the webhook handler config/payload/handlers
description: WebhookPayload extends @barkpark/core's WebhookEvent with an optional deliveryId fallback field; WebhookConfig/WebhookHandlers type the factory's input/output.
whatBreaks: Type drift from core's WebhookEvent could let the wire contract silently diverge between dispatcher and handler.

role: Unit tests for defineActions Server Actions helper
description: Exercises createDoc/patchDoc/publish/unpublish/deleteDoc/discardDraft against a mocked BarkparkClient, covering Zod-schema pass/transform/reject paths, empty-_type fail-closed guard, non-object schema-parse rejection, and flat-vs-scoped (workspace/project) cache-tag namespacing.
whatBreaks: A regression in defineActions' revalidation tagging or schema validation would slip through untested, e.g. stale cache after a mutation or corrupted document bodies.

role: Test for draft-mode token signing and route handlers
description: Vitest suite that verifies HMAC-SHA256 token generation, expiry, rejection of empty inputs, and the GET/POST route handlers for enabling/disabling Next.js draft mode preview.
whatBreaks: Regressions in draft-mode token signing or route handling go undetected, potentially breaking preview deployments.

role: CI gate: forbids next.tags + cache:no-store together in dist bundle
description: Scans the built dist/server.mjs for the Next.js 15.5.15 footgun where next.tags silently no-ops when combined with cache:'no-store' (would make revalidateTag() a no-op post-webhook). Skips if dist isn't built yet.
whatBreaks: If this regex-based static gate misses a regression, webhook-triggered cache revalidation could silently stop working in production with no test failure signal.

role: test suite for Next.js live-subscription client
description: Tests BarkparkLive, BarkparkLiveProvider, and startLiveSubscription including edge-runtime detection, debounce coalescing, teardown, HMR dispose, and beforeunload cleanup.
whatBreaks: Bugs in the live subscription client (debounce, teardown, edge guard) go undetected, leading to duplicate refreshes or leaked subscriptions in production apps.

role: Unit tests for barkparkMetadata helper
description: Covers article vs website OG type, title/description fallback chains, override precedence, blank-description omission, and null/undefined doc handling.
whatBreaks: Regressions in SEO/OG metadata generation (wrong titles, leaked blank descriptions) would ship undetected to all consuming Next.js apps.

role: test for document preloader deduplication
description: Unit tests for the createPreloader and preloadDocument helpers, verifying that concurrent preloads for the same id are deduplicated to a single fetch and that different ids fire separate requests.
whatBreaks: Preloader deduplication bugs cause redundant fetches or stale document values in Next.js RSC preloading flows.

role: Unit tests for revalidateBarkpark cache-tag translation
description: Covers sync_tags passthrough/dedup, legacy {_id,_type}/{ids,types} shapes, flat vs workspace/project-scoped tag construction, the BARKPARK_ALLOW_ALL_REVALIDATE path-based revalidation gate (throws before any tag invalidation otherwise), and malformed-input hardening (non-array sync_tags/ids/types not char-iterated).

role: Unit tests for barkparkFetch/createBarkparkServer/defineLive
description: Covers published vs draft-mode branch behavior (cache mode, Bearer token, perspective forcing), 401 retry/reissue flow, workspace/project URL scoping (flat vs /w/.../p/... routes), and scoped-vs-flat cache tag namespacing; mocks next/headers draftMode and global fetch.

role: Package export-surface smoke test for @barkpark/nextjs
description: Asserts the root package guards against importing revalidateBarkpark from the wrong subpath, and that actions/webhook/draft-mode/server subpaths export their expected factory functions.
whatBreaks: A silently broken or missing export from any subpath (root-stub trap, actions, webhook, draft-mode, server) would go undetected until a consumer's build fails.

role: Unit tests for the cache-tag prefix contract function
description: Pins scoped vs legacy prefix format behavior, including empty-string workspace/project edge cases, guarding the cross-cutting cache-invalidation contract.

role: Unit tests for the client-side optimistic-update hook
description: Renders useOptimisticDocument in happy-dom, testing initial state, optimistic mutate+settle, accumulating rapid successive mutations against stale in-flight state, BarkparkConflictError handling (instanceof and code-string fallback for duplicate-bundle scenarios), clearConflict, and non-conflict error propagation to an ErrorBoundary. role: BarkparkImage component — renders image assets to /custom component

role: PortableText renderer — Portable Text JSON to React elements
description:
Core rendering engine: block/mark/list/custom-type dispatch with component-override seams, nested list grouping by level, newline-to-

role: BarkparkReference component — resolves and renders a document reference

role: RSC-safe entry point (react-server condition) for @barkpark/react
description: Re-exports only the context-free renderers (PortableText, toPlainText, BarkparkImage, imageUrl) and Reference's types — deliberately omits the BarkparkReference component itself since it calls createContext, which crashes under Next's react-server condition. whatBreaks: Adding a createContext-using export here (or drifting from index.ts) crashes Next.js App Router RSC builds for every consumer.

whatBreaks: Excerpts, SEO meta descriptions, and search indexing built from Portable Text content would render blank, garbled, or throw during generateMetadata/server rendering.

role: Test suite for BarkparkImage

role: Test suite for PortableText renderer
description: Covers block styles, marks (built-in and custom via markDefs), nested list grouping/levels, defensive guards (fractional level, missing children), custom types, unknown-style/mark fallback + onMissingComponent callback, and hard-break newline handling.
whatBreaks: Regressions in the core content renderer's list/mark/fallback logic would ship unnoticed, risking crashed or malformed rich-text rendering across all consumers.

role: Vitest suite for the React BarkparkReference resolver component

Encodes the contract that the API's doc route is 3-segment only, guarding against silent regression to a legacy 2-segment path.
whatBreaks: A regression to a stale doc-route shape or broken cycle/depth guard in @barkpark/react's Reference component would ship silently since this is the only test coverage for it.

role: Regression test guarding the client (src/index.ts) export surface
description: Asserts all three public components (PortableText, BarkparkImage, BarkparkReference) plus imageUrl/toPlainText exist at runtime, and that every public data-shape type is still exported (compile-time type-union guard).

role: Box-side deploy entrypoint: swap precompiled artifact or fall back to full rebuild

role: Scripted golden-path: provision a Barkpark-backed site and deploy it to Vercel
description: End-to-end script creating a workspace/schema/seed/publish/read-token in Barkpark and linking+deploying a Next.js app (or a static site) to Vercel, setting canonical BARKPARK_API_URL/DATASET/TOKEN env vars and disabling Vercel SSO protection; each Barkpark step is idempotent/re-runnable.

role: CI script: compile api/_build/prod once and package as a versioned deploy artifact
description: Runs a clean MIX_ENV=prod compile in CI, records an exact runtime stamp (elixir/otp/erts/arch) the artifact is valid for, and tars+zstd-compresses _build/prod+deps with a checksum; boxes only apply the artifact on an exact stamp match, else fall back to on-box compile.
whatBreaks: A bad or mis-stamped artifact could get applied to an incompatible runtime (crashing NIFs/bytecode) or the fast-deploy path would silently degrade to slow on-box compiles across the fleet.

role: CI gate enforcing byte-size caps on the doc spine files

role: Opt-in real-Claude-binary E2E lane for Studio chat resume

role: Manual live E2E smoke for CMUX x Barkpark bridge

whatBreaks: A stale or broken smoke script would let real cmux bridge regressions go undetected since unit tests don't cover cross-process wiring.

role: End-to-end acceptance demo/proof script for Living Values valueref propagation

Large, detailed, self-contained integration proof; not part of CI/mix test.

role: Legacy single-box build-aside-and-swap deploy engine for the API
description: Shared by the post-merge git hook, `make rebuild`, and the self-update admin endpoint; builds Phoenix fresh into api/_build_next under a flock, swaps into api/_build/prod, then non-fatally builds the Go TUI and pdrender wasm, and restarts systemd LAST (since restart can SIGTERM this script's own cgroup). Guards against running on blue/green slot boxes.
whatBreaks: A broken swap or restart-ordering bug can leave the single-box prod deployment either not updated or completely down after every `git pull`/manual rebuild.

role: CI gate validating doc links, anchors, headers, and canonical-for uniqueness
description: Large bash 3.2-compatible script checking routing-table targets resolve, INDEX.md entries resolve, card Code-anchor paths/symbols exist, G1 doc-tier headers present, canonical-for values unique repo-wide, _attic ARCHIVED banners, cross-doc .md link resolution, plus @canonical capability marker uniqueness/public-entry-point checks (new §8) and WARN-only duplication tripwires.
whatBreaks: A broken gate lets stale doc links, duplicate canonical-for owners, or dangling @canonical capability markers merge silently, rotting the whole agent-facing doc/code navigation system this repo relies on.

role: Read-only local-checkout staleness/health report (make doctor)
description: Checks git behind/ahead of origin, bp CLI build staleness, pending dev-DB migrations, vendored deploy.sh drift, and working-tree hygiene; never mutates state and always exits 0 (advisory). Has a --hook mode used by the Claude Code SessionStart hook to print only problems.
whatBreaks: Developers/agents get false confidence their checkout is current (or noisy false alarms), leading to work on stale code or unnecessary busywork.

role: Box-side fetcher/swapper for CI-precompiled API build artifacts
description: Given a git SHA, fetches a stamp.json + tarball from a GitHub release, verifies exact elixir/erts/arch match and checksum, then swaps it into api/_build/prod under the same flock as deploy-rebuild.sh, restarting last. Always falls back safely (exit 1) to an on-box compile via the caller (apply-update.sh) on any mismatch or failure.
whatBreaks: A bad runtime-match gate could swap in bytecode-incompatible BEAM artifacts and crash the running service; a checksum or lock bug could corrupt the deployed build.

role: One-click localhost tool to create the Barkpark GitHub App via manifest flow
description: Serves a tiny local HTTP server that auto-submits a pre-filled GitHub App manifest (issues:write, minimal scopes) using the operator's browser session, then exchanges the returned code for app id/private key/webhook secret and writes them to a chmod-600 JSON file. One-time bootstrap tool, not used at runtime.
whatBreaks: Only affects the manual one-time GitHub bridge App setup flow; a bug just means a human has to create the App by hand instead.

whatBreaks: Only affects initial GitHub Projects board provisioning; failure just means the board/fields must be created manually.

role: Wires GitHub App creds into a Barkpark instance's plugin_settings via admin API

One-time/occasional ops script reading from ~/.config/barkpark/config.json for base/token defaults.

role: CI merge gate: bans inline #hex color literals in Go CLI/TUI source

whatBreaks: A weakened gate would let inline hex colors reintroduce theme drift in the CLI/TUI without any test catching it, silently breaking the unified-aesthetic token invariant.

role: Opt-in live SSO interop lane: boots real Keycloak, runs idp_interop tests

whatBreaks: Studio chrome silently regains hard-coded colors that drift from the theme-system token manifest, breaking light/dark or brand-swap consistency across the admin UI.

role: Mirrors starter templates into cloud provisioner assets
description: Node script that copies the canonical blog-starter/website-starter templates from js/packages/create-barkpark-app into cloud/priv/templates so the Cloud provisioner serves identical files.
whatBreaks: Running it stale or skipping it lets the Cloud-provisioned starter templates drift from the published npm package, shipping outdated or inconsistent starter code to new projects.

role: CI gate: forbids raw color literals in web/ chrome
description: Python-in-bash script that scans web/app/** and web/components/** (.tsx/.ts/.css) for inline hsl()/hex color literals not routed through design tokens, with a string-safe comment stripper and lit-allow escape hatch. Enforces the unified-aesthetic token discipline as the web-scoped twin of scripts/studio-literal-check.sh; failing it blocks merges that reintroduce copied color literals.
whatBreaks: A false negative lets un-tokenized colors merge silently (drift from design tokens); a false positive blocks unrelated merges on the web-literal-check CI gate.
