Bulldocs ingest SDK — NOT the general JS SDK; see js/
ts config/data file.
json config/data file.

role: Typed PortableDoc block union + constructor functions for the Bulldocs ingest SDK
description: Defines the full Block/Inline TypeScript type union (heading, paragraph, list, callout, code, diagram, image, table, section, etc.) mirroring exactly what Barkpark.PortableDoc.Render.compose_block/2 reads on the API side, plus constructor functions and a deterministic monotonic block-id minter (for byte-reproducible output). This is a hand-maintained wire-contract shadow of Elixir render.ex/patch.ex field names.
whatBreaks: If these types/field names drift from Barkpark.PortableDoc.Render.compose_block/2, every SDK-authored PortableDoc (ingest, patches keyed by block id) could silently produce blocks the renderer misreads or drops.

role: Bulldocs HTTP ingest client
description: BulldocsClient wraps POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers and POST /papers/:slug/ops with Bearer token auth, error surfacing via BulldocsError, and an injectable fetch for testing.
whatBreaks: All SDK publish and op-submit calls fail or swallow errors silently.

role: Bulldocs SDK barrel entrypoint
description: Re-exports all public symbols from the four Bulldocs authoring SDK submodules (blocks, ops, paper, client). Seven lines; the entire @barkpark/bulldocs-sdk public surface passes through here.
whatBreaks: Any consumer importing from @barkpark/bulldocs-sdk gets nothing — all exports are broken.

role: PortableDoc patch-op type definitions and constructors
description: Defines the Op discriminated union (append-block, insert-after, patch-block, replace-block, remove-block, move-block) with constructors that mirror the Elixir Patch module's wire keys exactly.
whatBreaks: Op constructors produce wrong discriminator keys or field names, causing the server to reject or misapply patch batches.

role: Paper builder
description: Paper class accumulates blocks and serialises the publish body {slug, blocks, title?, style?} that BulldocsIngestController expects. Provides a chainable add() API and a toJSON() method.
whatBreaks: Publish bodies are malformed, causing ingest to fail or drop fields like title/style.

role: Unit tests for block constructors
description: Node test-runner suite verifying every block constructor produces the exact shape and id that the renderer expects, using resetBlockIds() for deterministic output.
whatBreaks: Block constructor regressions go undetected in CI.

role: Unit tests for BulldocsClient
description: Tests publish() and submitOps() against a recorder mock-fetch, verifying URL construction, Authorization header, Content-Type, request body shape, error parsing via BulldocsError, and ifRev optimistic-concurrency guard.
whatBreaks: Client wire-format regressions (wrong headers, body shape, error handling) go undetected.

role: Unit tests for op constructors
description: Verifies every Op constructor emits the correct 'op' discriminator key and field names, including that patchBlock uses 'patch' not 'fields' and moveBlock defaults after to null.
whatBreaks: Op shape regressions (wrong key names) go undetected, breaking server-side patch application.

role: Unit tests for the ingest SDK's paper() builder
description: Pins the contract of paper()/Paper from sdk/src/paper.js — opts passthrough, chainable add(), copy-returning getBlocks()/toJSON(), and only-set-keys serialization. Guards against silently breaking the JS SDK's top-level content-authoring entry point.
whatBreaks: A regression in Paper's serialization or mutation-copy semantics would corrupt publish bodies sent to the ingest endpoint by every SDK consumer, undetected until this suite is run.

description: json config/data file.

role: Human runbook for deploying a new Barkpark-backed Vercel site
description: Canonical doc (doc-tier: human) walking the one-command quick-setup script plus the manual six-step golden path (workspace, schema, seed/publish, read-token, Vercel env, deploy), with a table of canonical env var names and 7 hard-won gotchas (scoped-URL requirement, draft-vs-publish, tenancy 403s, response envelope shape, Vercel SSO-protection trap). Cross-references internal/cli/vercel_cmd.go as the native Go implementation.
whatBreaks: Operators following stale/wrong steps here can write content into the wrong (Default) workspace, ship a public site 302-redirecting to Vercel SSO, or leave documents unpublished — real deploy failures for downstream site launches.

role: Spec doc for the barkpark.template.json manifest format
description: Canonical (doc-tier: human) description of the declarative template-manifest shape (schemas/seed/env), pointing to the JSON Schema and the Go loader/validator (internal/template) plus the CI drift gate (TestRealManifests) that checks every checked-in manifest against this spec.
whatBreaks: Divergence between this doc and the actual schema/validator misleads template authors into producing manifests that fail Load/Validate or the provisioner's contract, breaking the deploy-button flow.

role: JSON Schema (draft-07) defining the template manifest contract
description: Machine-enforced schema for barkpark.template.json files: required fields, name/slug pattern, seed format enum with conditional publishType requirement, and env entry shape with conditional literal-value requirement. This is the executable contract every template manifest (and the Go internal/template loader) is validated against.
whatBreaks: An incorrect schema would let malformed template manifests pass validation (breaking server-side provisioning) or reject valid ones (blocking new template onboarding) across every deploy-button template.

role: Deploy manifest for the blog-starter template
description: Declares the blog-starter's schema (post), seed (mutations, published), and required env vars (API URL, read token, workspace/project/dataset, webhook secret) consumed by the provisioner's embedded catalog to server-bootstrap a Barkpark-backed blog.
whatBreaks: A malformed or drifted manifest breaks provisioning of new blog-starter deploys (missing env, wrong schema path, or failed publish step).

role: Content-type schema for the blog-starter's post document
description: Flat schema definition (slug, excerpt, body, published_at fields, public visibility) applied via POST /v1/schemas when provisioning a blog-starter site.
whatBreaks: Blog-starter sites would fail schema application or render posts with missing/mismatched fields.

role: Sample seed content for the blog-starter template
description: Two createOrReplace mutations seeding demo blog posts, applied and then published during blog-starter provisioning to give a new site non-empty demo content.
whatBreaks: New blog-starter deploys would launch with an empty blog instead of demo content; low blast radius, cosmetic only.

role: Human guide for the place-directory vertical-slice template
description: Walks running the web/ map demo standalone (bundled sample data) and wiring it to a real local Barkpark instance via install.sh + env vars, documenting the fetchListings() contract (web/lib/listings.ts) and the three API calls involved (schema install, seed mutate, published query).
whatBreaks: Developers following incorrect steps could fail to see real data on the map demo, or misconfigure LISTINGS_TYPE/dataset env vars for the hundesteder.no-style site.

role: Deploy manifest for the place-directory template (powers hundesteder.no)
description: Declares the place schema, seed-places mutations (published), and env vars including a literal NEXT_PUBLIC_FINDER_LANDING=map flag that flips the web demo's landing page into the places map, consumed by the provisioner to stand up map-backed listing sites.
whatBreaks: Breaks provisioning of place-directory-based sites (including the live hundesteder.no pattern), e.g. missing the landing-page flip or failing to publish seeded places.

role: Shell installer that seeds the place-directory starter template into a dataset
description: POSIX sh + curl script that upserts the `place` schema and seeds sample places into a Barkpark dataset via the API, then smoke-tests the public read the frontend depends on. Idempotent (createOrReplace + schema upsert), warns if seeds land as unpublished drafts.
whatBreaks: Users following the place-directory template quickstart would fail to install the schema/content or get a false smoke-test result, but no running system depends on this script.

role: Schema definition for the `place` document type in the place-directory template
description: Declares the `place` content type (slug, description, category, city, composite geo/address, website, price range, tags) consumed by install.sh and the template's frontend demo.
whatBreaks: Malformed fields would break schema install or mismatch what the place-directory frontend expects to render, affecting only that template.

role: Seed data (mutations) of sample Norwegian dog-friendly places for the template
description: A `mutations` array of `createOrReplace` place documents (cafes, parks, beaches across Oslo/Bergen/Trondheim/Stavanger/Tromsø) used by install.sh to populate a fresh dataset with demo content.
whatBreaks: Only affects demo/seed content quality for the place-directory template; no functional breakage elsewhere.

role: Manifest describing the website-starter template (schemas, seed, required env vars)
description: Declares template metadata (name, framework nextjs, dataset) plus the schema file and seed file to install, and the server-side env vars (API URL, token, workspace, project, dataset, webhook secret) a deployed site needs. Likely read by a template-bootstrap/deploy tool (Deploy-with-Barkpark flow) to know what to provision.
whatBreaks: Bootstrap tooling that provisions the website-starter template (schema install, seeding, env wiring for ISR webhook) would misconfigure or fail to deploy a new site from this template.

role: Schema definition for the `page` document type in the website-starter template
description: Minimal public `page` type (slug, heading, subheading, body) that a Next.js site built from this starter renders.
whatBreaks: Breaks the website-starter template's page rendering/schema install only.

role: Seed data (mutations) for the website-starter template's demo pages
description: Two `createOrReplace` page documents (Home, About) used to populate a freshly bootstrapped website-starter site with placeholder content.
whatBreaks: Only affects starter demo content quality; no functional system impact.

role: Top-level doc for the codebase-intelligence tooling suite (ASSESS/ENRICH/PUBLISH/RELATE)
description: Explains the nine-root scoring model, the pipeline of programmatic passes plus agent-only-on-drift, the four composites (Priority/Hotspot/Critical-untested/Refactor-worth), the single entry point `node tooling/status/status.mjs`, CI calibration loop, multi-vote verification, and directory map. Human-tier doc, not code.
whatBreaks: A stale/wrong README would mislead engineers and agents operating the codebase-intelligence tooling but does not affect runtime app behavior.

role: Canonical signals spec: one root metric per owning pass, no double-counting
description: Defines the 'measure each root once, compose only across roots' rule and documents which pass owns each canonical root (reach, churn, complexity, defects, tests, conventions, ownership, relationships, filebase), plus the Phase 0/2 composite formulas. This is the design contract the whole tooling/ scoring pipeline must obey.
whatBreaks: Violating this contract (double-counting a root across composites) would silently corrupt the codebase-quality scorecard's meaning, but has no effect on the shipped Barkpark product.

role: Gitignore for the aesthetics tool's generated report output
description: Ignores `aesthetics-report.json`, the generated output of aesthetics.mjs, so the analysis artifact isn't committed.
whatBreaks: Worst case the generated report gets accidentally committed and creates diff noise; no functional impact.

role: Filebase-mess analyzer: scores repo Bloat + Aesthetics (the YAGNI critic)
description: Dependency-free Node script (via `git ls-files` + fs + optional `bp task ls`) that computes two deterministic 0-100 scores — Bloat (root source clutter, tracked build artifacts, directory fan-out, spotlight-clutter dirs) and Aesthetics (dead docs in _attic/, dead/unscoped bp tasks, YAGNI orphan files) — with explainable, path-level findings and fix suggestions. Writes aesthetics-report.json; complements Cody's per-file code grading, which is blind to filebase-level mess. Read/consumed by compare.mjs for CI regression checks.
whatBreaks: A broken/miscalibrated scoring formula would produce false or misleading structural-mess findings feeding the CI aesthetics-guard workflow and any orchestrator relying on the report to drive cleanup, though the guard itself is advisory and never blocks merges.

role: CI regression-diff module comparing base vs PR-head aesthetics reports
description: Pure Node module (exports compareReports/renderMarkdown, also runnable as a CLI) that diffs two aesthetics-report.json files, flagging only NEW deterministic structural findings a PR introduces (root-clutter, dead-doc, dir-fanout, yagni-orphan, removable tracked-artifact roll-ups) while excluding the bp-dependent dead-task signal since bp is absent in CI. Always exits 0 — advisory only, emits a markdown summary and an AESTHETICS_GUARD_FLAGGED marker for the CI workflow to surface as a warning.
whatBreaks: Incorrect diff logic would cause the CI aesthetics-guard to silently miss real new mess or spuriously flag clean PRs; since it's advisory-only it wouldn't block merges but would erode trust in the signal.

role: Unit test for compare.mjs's regression-diff logic (no test runner, plain Node)
description: Asserts four contracts: a new root-clutter finding is flagged and dead-task drift is ignored; identical reports raise no alarm; a growing build-output roll-up flags only the new sample path; a new deliberate/typedef artifact (no `sample`) is not flagged as structural. Run via `node tooling/aesthetics/compare.test.mjs`.
whatBreaks: A weakened or broken test would let a regression in compare.mjs's diff logic ship unnoticed, degrading the CI aesthetics-guard's reliability.

role: Unit test for the aesthetics Bloat critic's spotlight-clutter detector
description: Builds a throwaway git repo fixture with clutter cases and false-positive guards (real packages, projects, infra dirs, populated content trees), runs the real aesthetics.mjs against it, and asserts the finding shape and penalty math. Self-contained, no network.
whatBreaks: A regression in the spotlight-clutter detector (false positives/negatives in the Bloat critic) would ship undetected, silently miscalibrating aesthetics scores.

role: VCS Housekeeping
description: Standard gitignore (entries: nodes.json, codebase-graph.html, .last-push-hash). Keeps generated outputs out of version control.
whatBreaks: Generated graph artifacts leak into git history, bloating the repo; easily fixed by adding patterns to .gitignore. No logic impact.

role: Graph Generator (Core Seam)
description: Generates nodes.json: one node per code file with all quality metrics (importance, reach, churn, complexity, defects, ownership, etc.) + dependency edges (Elixir xref, JS imports, Go packages) + intention refs + co-change edges. The single source of truth for the codebase graph structure.
whatBreaks: The dependency graph is broken or incomplete — all reach/fan-in/dependentCount calculations become wrong. Intention and co-change edges do not materialize. Every downstream analysis (usefulness, combined scores, papers) reads stale or corrupt data. The entire intelligence pipeline is invalidated.

role: Renders the codebase content-graph to a self-contained interactive HTML
description: Fetches /v1/graph from a Barkpark host and renders it with Barkpark's own bp-graph.js renderer into codebase-graph.html, coloring nodes by language/stack and wiring node-click to open the corresponding paper. Dev/diagnostic tool, not part of any served path.
whatBreaks: Only the local codebase-graph.html visualization breaks; no production or CI path depends on it.

role: Pushes the codebase content-graph as per-file Papers into a Barkpark dataset
description: Creates a `paper` schema, writes one paper per code-graph node (metrics + role/description fields), links typed dependency/intention references, publishes, then ingests full content blocks (source, git history, dependents) via the Bulldocs ingest endpoint. Hard-refuses to target the 'production' dataset — always defaults to the isolated 'codebase' dataset, a deliberate safety guard.
whatBreaks: Codebase-intelligence papers would fail to publish or, worse, leak per-file code papers into production if the production guard were removed/bypassed.

role: gitignore for blast-radius tooling cache
description: Excludes derived caches (index.json, last-impact.json, dossiers/) from version control while intentionally keeping verdict-cache.json committed as the persistent hash-keyed agent verdict store.
whatBreaks: Derived cache files or ephemeral dossiers accidentally committed, polluting history; verdict-cache accidentally excluded, losing persistent agent verdicts.

role: Human doc explaining the blast-radius impact-analysis pipeline
description: Describes the build-index → check → dossier pipeline, the seam-detection concept (cross-language wire-contract breakage), and how the agent layer will later consume last-impact.json/dossiers. Canonical explainer for the whole blast-radius subsystem.
whatBreaks: Nothing executes; a stale/wrong doc just misleads a developer or agent operating the blast-radius tools.

role: Builds the cached reverse-dependency graph (index.json) across Go/Elixir/JS
description: Slow, out-of-band script that shells out to `go list -deps -json`, `mix xref graph`, and parses package.json workspaces to build forward/reverse dependency graphs, caching Elixir's xref output keyed by a content signature so unchanged trees skip the ~minute-long mix compile. Feeds index.json, which the fast pre-push hook (check.mjs) and file-importance/consistency passes read.
whatBreaks: A wrong or stale index.json makes blast-radius impact detection, fan-in scoring (file-importance), and dead-code detection (consistency) silently wrong across the whole repo.

role: pre-push blast-radius checker
description: The fast (~70ms) pre-push hook that reads index.json and config.json to compute per-stack reachable packages and flag cross-language seam touches. Writes last-impact.json for the agentic layer; exits non-zero with --strict when a seam is touched.
whatBreaks: Cross-language breaking changes go undetected at push time — a capabilities or HTTP API change can silently break the Go CLI or JS SDK with no warning.

role: Config: per-stack file globs and the cross-language wire-contract seam map
description: Declares which globs belong to go/elixir/js stacks, and — the highest-value part — the `seam.surfaces` list mapping API/manifest/schema/webhook source files to their cross-language consumers (Go CLI, JS SDK) and guard tests, so a change to e.g. router.ex can be flagged as risking the Go/JS clients. Also holds `dynamicEdges` for agent-discovered blind-spot edges.
whatBreaks: A missing or wrong seam surface/consumer means a breaking cross-language API change goes undetected by the pre-push blast-radius hook.

role: agent-ready dossier builder with verdict cache
description: For each seam/dynamic edge in last-impact.json, assembles a self-contained JSON payload (diff hunks, consumer code slices, guard contents) so an AI agent can judge breakage with zero exploration calls. Content-hash cache skips unchanged edges, committing verdict-cache.json for sharing.
whatBreaks: Agents receive incomplete or stale dossiers, either misjudging breaking changes or spending tokens re-evaluating already-cached edges.

role: git hook installer
description: Shell script that copies pre-push to .git/hooks/pre-push and marks it executable. Refuses to overwrite a non-blast-radius hook; additive and reversible with no core.hooksPath changes.
whatBreaks: The pre-push blast-radius check is never wired in for new checkouts, so cross-language seam changes are pushed without any impact analysis.

role: git pre-push hook entrypoint
description: Minimal shell wrapper: checks for node, then runs check.mjs in warn-only mode (|| true). Installed into .git/hooks/pre-push by install-hook.sh.
whatBreaks: Blast-radius analysis never runs on push, silently skipping all seam and reachability checks.

role: VCS Housekeeping
description: Standard gitignore (entries: cochange-report.json, crossval-report.json). Keeps generated co-change analysis outputs out of version control.
whatBreaks: Generated reports leak into git. No logic impact; easily fixed.

role: Relationship Cross-Validation (Core Signal)
description: Computes temporal coupling (co-change pairs from git history), cross-validates against dependency and intention graphs, classifies pairs as REAL/ASPIRATIONAL/ACCIDENTAL/STRUCTURAL, flags accidental-coupling smell. Adds the third relationship dimension (temporal) to the graph.
whatBreaks: Temporal coupling is not computed; generate.mjs has no co-change edges or accidental-coupling flags. The intelligence suite loses the ability to detect implicit coupling smells and validate that relationships are enacted (≥2 of 3 edge kinds agree). Risk signal accuracy drops.

role: Human doc explaining Cody, the code↔Barkpark tuning-variable sync agent
description: Describes bound variables (the four vtype rungs int/list/expr/piecewise), connection resolution via barkpark.json, preflight gating, and the scan/status/set/apply/watch command set. Central reference for anyone using or extending Cody.
whatBreaks: Stale/incorrect doc would mislead contributors into misusing Cody's write-back (apply/watch) against source code, risking incorrect literal rewrites.

role: Configuration / Tunable Parameters
description: Central registry of tunable parameters and formulas (fragile_density, consensus_band, content_cap, collinearity_cut, hotspot_percentile, priority_percentile, untested_score, js_scan_roots, bug_fix_words, defect_formula, effort_formula) with their locations (file + regex). Enables centralized control of all scoring thresholds.
whatBreaks: Scoring thresholds are no longer tracked or tunable. Changes to thresholds are scattered; auditing and updates become manual and error-prone. The calibration loop and scoring composites cannot be safely reconfigured. Risk control is lost.

role: "Bound variables" tool: syncs tuning values between Barkpark papers and code literals
description: POC CLI (scan/status/set/apply/watch) that extracts literal values bound to code locations via regex anchors (bindings.json), stores/edits them as Barkpark 'tuning' documents, detects drift across duplicated copies, and can rewrite every bound code location on apply, with a verified round-trip. Gates apply/watch behind a 'preflight' freshness check of the whole codebase-intelligence pipeline.
whatBreaks: A buggy anchor rewrite could corrupt source files with wrong literals during `apply --write`; scope is limited to files listed in bindings.json.

role: Git ignore rules for combined worklist output
description: Three-line gitignore for combined worklist artifacts: combined-report.html, combined-report.csv, combined-report.json. These are derived outputs (regenerated, never committed).
whatBreaks: Generated reports would be accidentally committed. Negligible impact on code semantics, but violates the invariant that derived outputs are gitignored.

role: Priority worklist synthesizer (root-clean)
description: Pure-programmatic (zero tokens) prioritized worklist generator. Joins reach (value axis from usefulness), issue-severity (from consistency verdicts), defect-amplifier (from risk), and untested-boost (from risk testScore inverted). Produces combined-report.{html,csv,json} with quadrant analysis (high-reach & inconsistent = the worklist), per-file role/detail, and interactive filtering.
whatBreaks: The prioritized worklist disappears—no clear improvement plan ranking. Priority composites (reach × defect × untested × issue-sev) collapse. Teams cannot triage high-leverage fixes. The worklist is a daily-use artifact for developers; its loss directly impacts improvement velocity.

role: Gitignore for concept-map's propose-only output dirs
description: Excludes .scaffold-staging/ (dry-run scaffold proposals) and .proposals/ (decomposition plans) from version control so generated, non-authoritative output never gets committed.
whatBreaks: Missing entries would cause generated scaffold/proposal artifacts to be accidentally committed, cluttering the repo.

role: Overview doc for the cqv8 concept/feature-architecture analysis suite
description: Explains the thesis (feature architecture = filesystem matching the dependency graph), lists each tool (concepts, anatomy, grade, manifest, scaffold, boundary) and its role, run commands, and design invariants (computed-live, propose-only, learned-per-repo).
whatBreaks: Wrong doc would misdirect contributors on how to run/interpret the concept-map suite, but doesn't affect runtime code.

role: cqv8 Phase-1 acceptance gate for the concept/coupling model
description: Runs runConcepts() live against the real symbol graph and asserts KERNEL/CLEAN-FEATURE/CLEAN-NONPLUGIN band classification and Ca/cohesion ranges for named concepts (content, tenancy, sheets, onixedit, release, portable_doc); exits non-zero on failure so it gates CI/build.
whatBreaks: A broken or silently-passing gate would let a regression in the concept-map coupling model (band misclassification) merge undetected.

role: cqv8 Phase-2 acceptance gate for the anatomy-learner
description: Asserts runAnatomy() picks ground-truth exemplars (sheets, onixedit), excludes media/frt, derives the recurring role-set (core/registration/test/engine/session/live), and computes valid allowedKernelDeps — all live off the real graph, never hardcoded.
whatBreaks: A regression in exemplar selection or skeleton extraction (feeding P3 grading and P4 scaffolding) would go undetected, corrupting downstream grade/scaffold output.

role: cqv8 Phase-3 acceptance gate for the grade pass (five-gap verdicts)
description: Large acceptance suite asserting gratuitous-core detection, sideways-edge clustering, test-scatter, verdict assignment (kernel/clean/clean-lib/improvable/tangled), Mix-task entry-point exclusion, and web-layer edge exclusion all compute correctly live off the graph.
whatBreaks: Grade-pass regressions (wrong verdicts, false sideways knots, broken entry-point exclusion) would ship silently, corrupting the quality signal cqv8 reports to Cody/agents.

role: cqv8 Phase-4 acceptance gate for manifest + scaffold generation
description: Asserts `new pricing` projects FEATURE-FOLDER and `new billing-core --touches content,tenancy` projects CROSS-FOLDER, validates propose-only behavior via git-status diffing (nothing written outside .scaffold-staging/), and checks manifest schema validation.
whatBreaks: A regression could let the scaffold generator write outside its staging sandbox (repo pollution) or emit invalid manifests, undetected.

role: cqv8 Phase-5 acceptance gate for the boundary gate + recolocation/decycle
description: Asserts gateBoundary flags sideways and wrong-direction synthetic edges while passing legitimate inward edges, proposeRecolocation is lose-none and propose-only (verified via git status diff), and proposeDecycle's residual-aware cycle-cut math and entry-point exclusion hold.
whatBreaks: A broken boundary/recolocation/decycle gate could let destructive or incorrect refactor proposals pass unnoticed, or fail to catch real architecture violations.

role: cqv8 Phase-2 anatomy-learner: derives the repo's feature skeleton from exemplars
description: Picks exemplar concepts (high cohesion, low Ca, real plugin registration) from P1's CLEAN-FEATURE band, extracts their recurring role-set (core/registration/test/engine/session/live/etc.), registration call shape, and allowedKernelDeps intersection; falls back to a curated skeleton if fewer than 2 clean exemplars exist. Feeds both grade.mjs (P3) and scaffold.mjs (P4).
whatBreaks: Wrong exemplar selection or skeleton extraction would corrupt the grading criteria (P3) and generated scaffolds (P4) across the whole concept-map suite, since both depend on this module's output.

role: Architecture-debt baseline for the ci-boundary never-worse gate
description: Captured JSON snapshot of sideways/wrong-direction/feature-cycle edge counts and identities, generated via `ci-boundary.mjs --write-baseline`. CI compares live boundary state against this file and fails only on regression beyond it; existing debt is grandfathered, never re-baselined to silence a real regression.
whatBreaks: A stale or hand-edited baseline would either mask new architectural debt (silent regressions merge) or make ci-boundary.mjs fail spuriously on every PR.

role: cqv8 P5 — boundary violation gate + propose-only recolocation/decycle engine
description: Detects sideways (feature→feature) and wrong-direction (kernel→feature) edges and scatter-increase on proposed changes, and computes never-worse propose-only plans to recolocate a scattered concept or decycle a mutual feature dependency. Pure computation over the live symbol graph — never hardcodes concept names/counts, never mutates real files (writes only to gitignored `.scaffold-staging`).
whatBreaks: A broken gate function would let CI (ci-boundary.mjs) pass architecture regressions through undetected, or falsely flag legitimate PRs as boundary violations.

role: CI entrypoint wiring boundary.mjs's never-worse gate into the build
description: Rebuilds the symbol graph, runs grade.mjs as a sanity check, runs boundary.mjs, and diffs the resulting sideways/wrong-direction/feature-cycle counts and edge identities against boundary-baseline.json, exiting non-zero on regression. Also supports `--write-baseline` to intentionally re-baseline accepted debt.
whatBreaks: A bug here would either let real architecture regressions merge silently or block all PRs with false-positive CI failures on the concept-map/architecture gate.

role: cqv8 P1 — detects feature concepts from the symbol graph and computes coupling
description: Structurally derives 'concept' clusters from file paths (plugins/domain modules, folded with web/test files), then computes Martin's component-algebra coupling (Ca/Ce/instability/cohesion) per concept and bands each into KERNEL / CLEAN-FEATURE / CLEAN-NONPLUGIN / UNSTABLE-EDGE / mixed / noise. This is the foundational vocabulary reused by grade.mjs, boundary.mjs, manifest.mjs, and scaffold.mjs — the single source of concept assignment and banding.
whatBreaks: Since every other cqv8 phase (grade, boundary, manifest, scaffold) imports runConcepts()/assignConcepts, an error in concept detection or coupling math would silently corrupt the whole architecture-analysis toolchain's verdicts.

role: shared ENTRY-POINT predicate (web-layer / Mix-task) for cqv8 passes
description: Defines isWebLayerFile, isMixTaskFile, and isEntryPoint — the single definition of 'this file orchestrates a feature rather than being a member of it', imported by concepts.mjs, grade.mjs, and boundary.mjs so all passes agree on exclusions from sideways/cycle counting and concept membership.
whatBreaks: If the predicate misclassifies files, entry-point edges could be double-counted as real domain-boundary violations (or vice versa) across every cqv8 pass at once, since it's a shared single source of truth.

role: cqv8 P3 — grades every concept against five architecture gaps
description: For each concept computes gratuitous-core, test-scatter, sideways-edges, manifest-absence, and framework-scatter, then emits a verdict (kernel/clean/clean-lib/tangled) with named remediation edges. Reuses concepts.mjs's bands and registration.mjs/entrypoints.mjs predicates; feeds ci-boundary.mjs's sanity check.
whatBreaks: Incorrect grading would misdirect refactoring priorities (wrong colocate/cut recommendations) and break the sanity gate ci-boundary.mjs relies on before trusting boundary numbers.

role: cqv8 P4 — per-feature manifest schema + synthesis from the graph
description: Defines the 5-field manifest schema (name/surface/deps/ownedTables/roles), validateManifest, and synthesizeManifest which derives a concept's declared boundary from the live symbol graph and anatomy.mjs's learned skeleton. Intended to make feature boundaries exact instead of guessed by regex.
whatBreaks: A malformed synthesized manifest would produce an inaccurate declared feature surface/deps, undermining any tooling that later relies on manifests as the exact boundary source instead of the fuzzier regex-based concept detection.

role: shared plugin-registration-surface predicate (isRegistered)
description: Checks whether a concept's plugin entry file (api/lib/barkpark/plugins/<concept>.ex) defines register_schemas/register_routes, distinguishing CLEAN-FEATURE (registered plugin) from CLEAN-NONPLUGIN in concepts.mjs's banding. Mirrors anatomy.mjs's REGISTRATION_CALLS constant so both passes agree.
whatBreaks: Misclassification here would flip a concept's band between CLEAN-FEATURE and CLEAN-NONPLUGIN across every cqv8 report, skewing grading and boundary analysis for that concept.

role: cqv8 P4/P6 — propose-only generative scaffolding for NEW concepts
description: Projects a not-yet-existing concept's coupling position from declared --touches concepts, picks FEATURE-FOLDER vs CROSS-FOLDER template, and emits a dry-run file plan written only under a gitignored .scaffold-staging directory — never touches real repo files. Reuses concepts.mjs bands, anatomy.mjs skeleton, and manifest.mjs synthesis.
whatBreaks: A bug could misdirect a new feature's initial anatomy/placement recommendation, or (if the staging-root guard failed) risk writing outside the intended sandbox, though the assertUnderStaging guard is the actual safety net.

role: gitignore for consistency outputs
description: Excludes all generated consistency artifacts (report JSON/HTML, batch counts, verdict cache, batches/, results/) from the repo.
whatBreaks: Stale consistency verdicts get committed, causing incorrect drift/intentional judgments to persist across repo clones.

role: consistency pass configuration
description: Declares thresholds (min group size, common-pattern ratio, dup Jaccard threshold, shingle size) and the two Elixir layering rules (web-bypasses-context, core-imports-web) that the consistency scanner enforces.
whatBreaks: Layering violations go undetected or false positives flood the report, making the consistency pass useless or misleading.

role: Peer-group consistency scanner: naming, structure, layering, dead-code, near-dup
description: Groups sibling files by directory, derives each group's dominant naming/structural pattern via regex signatures, flags outliers, checks layering back-edge rules and Go dead-package detection (via blast-radius index), and does Jaccard-similarity near-duplicate detection; writes consistency-report.json/html plus incremental agent-verdict batches with a verdict cache keyed by content signature.
whatBreaks: Consistency/duplication findings and the codebase-quality report would misreport groups' conformance and miss real layering violations or dup code.

role: gitignore rule excluding deps-report.json from version control
description: One-line .gitignore scoping tooling/deps/ so its generated deps-report.json output isn't committed.
whatBreaks: Worst case a generated report file gets accidentally committed and clutters the repo; no functional impact.

role: Dependency/supply-chain audit script feeding Cody's Dependencies dimension
description: Runs mix hex.audit, npm audit, pnpm audit, and govulncheck across api/, root, sdk/, js/ ecosystems, degrading gracefully when a tool is missing, and writes tooling/deps/deps-report.json plus a one-line stderr summary. Free/local signal, no network beyond the package manager audits themselves.
whatBreaks: Cody's Dependencies score silently reports 0 vulnerabilities or crashes the quality pipeline, masking real supply-chain risk.

role: Gitignore for the onboarding critic's local analysis artifact
description: Single line ignoring onboarding-report.json, the generated report from onboarding.mjs, consistent with other tooling critics keeping their JSON reports out of git.
whatBreaks: onboarding-report.json could get accidentally committed, bloating the repo with a stale generated artifact.

role: Original audit snapshot for the Onboarding/Time-to-Value critic
description: Human-authored, point-in-time audit (mostly resolved per its own banner) documenting the original 32/100 onboarding score, the Cloud-onboarding-surface gap, per-doc scorecard, and a ranked list of highest-leverage fixes; superseded in large part by KNOWN-ISSUES.md tracking what's since been fixed.
whatBreaks: No functional breakage — it's historical record; a wrong reading could mislead someone into re-fixing already-closed onboarding gaps or missing the still-open DOC-6 items.

role: Live backlog of onboarding issues needing decisions or code changes
description: Doc-tier agent-budgeted tracker (canonical-for onboarding-known-issues) listing BLOCKER-1 through DOC-6 with fix/done status, gated on quality-gate discipline (check-doc-budgets.sh, docs-anchors-check.sh); several items marked done 2026-06-28, some (DOC-6 sub-items) still open.
whatBreaks: A stale entry could cause a future editor to re-do already-fixed work or skip genuinely open onboarding gaps (e.g. js/README.md consumer path).

role: Charter/spec for the Onboarding critic — the 14th Cody dimension
description: Defines sub-axes (time-to-first-value, currency-feature-coverage, lead-with-value, pedagogical-waterfall, path-completeness), scoring bands, the 10 programmatic signals onboarding.mjs computes, agent-judgment batches, and explicit wiring instructions for SIGNALS.md/quality.mjs/status.mjs (deliberately not applied here, left for the wiring author).
whatBreaks: Anyone wiring the onboarding critic into the composite Cody score would misweight or mis-integrate it, or a future editor could misinterpret which signals are load-bearing vs advisory.

role: Full 250-defect claim-by-claim doc-truth audit report across the repo
description: Large canonical report (budget 9000tok) enumerating every confirmed false/stale/misleading/unverifiable doc claim found in a repo-wide sweep, grouped by file, with 234 auto-fixed and 16 left for human sign-off in governance files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/SKILL.md); includes an honest-limits section acknowledging it's a floor not a census.
whatBreaks: Misplaced trust in this audit (treating a since-fixed defect as still-open, or vice versa) could cause wasted rework or missed real doc drift; it's a point-in-time snapshot against a moving tree.

role: Executable programmatic analyzer for the Onboarding/Time-to-Value critic
description: Pure-Node, dependency-free script that parses a hardcoded onboarding doc surface (README, QUICKSTART, cheatsheets, cloud/README, etc.) for CTA/grade-table ordering, zero-install demo framing, Cloud command coverage, provisional language, unguarded destructive steps, pricing presence, and decision-tree routing; computes weighted sub-axis scores and an overallScore, writes onboarding-report.json, and emits agentJudgmentBatches for a follow-on agent pass to refine.
whatBreaks: The Onboarding dimension of the Cody composite quality score would be silently wrong (false confidence in onboarding quality) and downstream findings/fix priorities in KNOWN-ISSUES.md would be based on bad signal.

role: Charter and usage guide for the doc-truth verifier pipeline (P1-P6)
description: Canonical doc describing the whole doc-truth tool family: P1 verify-docs.mjs (claim extract/verify/re-verify with never-worse guarantee), code-comment citation scanning, retired-terms dead-tech denylist, P2 waterfall (restatement/dedup), P3 highways (routing-table resolution), P4 priority (coverage-vs-reach queue), P5 remake (safe-restructure gate), P6 metric-currency (live-metric drift guard); ties together all the acceptance test files in this batch.
whatBreaks: A maintainer following stale usage instructions could run the wrong acceptance test or misunderstand the re-verify/never-worse guarantees, undermining trust in the whole doc-truth pipeline's findings.

role: Acceptance/regression test for the code-comment citation guard
description: Hard-gate test script validating verify-docs.mjs's code-comment scanning (@moduledoc/// etc.) and retired-terms.mjs against a frozen fixture corpus: fail-before (frozen defects caught), pass-after (fixed defects gone from live tree), never-cry-wolf on clean/historical files, catches-a-plant, and never-worse-elsewhere (markdown acceptance still passes); exits non-zero on any failure and is wired into doc-gates.yml CI.
whatBreaks: CI's citation-truth guard could pass falsely (missing real drift/dead-tech regressions) or fail spuriously blocking merges on .ex/.go/.ts/.md changes.

role: Acceptance test for the P2 doc-truth waterfall (restatement detector)
description: Runs waterfall.mjs's restatement detector against root CLAUDE.md, asserting it finds the Golden Rules ↔ Past Mistakes duplication cluster with ≥4 shared anchors (DETECTION) and that the proposed collapse loses zero verifiable facts (LOSE-NO-FACT); exits non-zero on failure, self-contained ESM/node builtins only.
whatBreaks: A regression in waterfall.mjs's restatement/dedup logic (e.g. losing facts during a proposed collapse) would go undetected, risking silent fact-loss if that P2 machinery were ever wired to auto-apply.

role: Acceptance test for doc-truth P3 routing/uniqueness/budget gates
description: Runs runHighways() from highways.mjs and checks two must-pass metrics: every routing-table Load target resolves to one canonical owner in ≤2 hops, and no canonical-for topic has more than one owner doc; also prints the byte-budget gate as informational-only. Dependency-free ESM script.
whatBreaks: A silently-broken routing table or duplicate canonical-for ownership would go undetected, letting the CLAUDE.md doc-routing contract drift without CI catching it.

role: Acceptance test for doc-truth P4 (priority/reach) scorer
description: Independently re-fetches reach via what-breaks.mjs --json for the top under-documented file the priority queue surfaces, and asserts it is genuinely top-decile reach (not a heuristic guess); also asserts a canonical build-spec doc is named. Guards against the priority scorer gaming its own metric.
whatBreaks: The doc-priority queue could recommend documenting low-impact files while high-blast-radius files stay undocumented, with no test catching the drift.

role: Capstone acceptance gate for doc-truth P5 never-worse remake
description: Builds a real Golden-Rules↔Past-Mistakes collapse candidate via P2's proposal, runs it through gateRemake (from remake.mjs), and asserts POSITIVE passes (no lost facts/links/anchors, verdict=human) while two NEGATIVE mutations (dropping a fact, dropping a link) correctly get rejected; also asserts the gate never writes to disk. Exercises P1+P2+P3 together against the real repo CLAUDE.md.
whatBreaks: A broken remake gate could let a doc restructure silently drop verifiable facts or outbound links (e.g. from the verbatim-exempt Golden Rules/Past Mistakes sections) without failing CI.

role: Acceptance test for the core doc-truth verifier (recall + never-worse gate)
description: Measures verifier recall against a human-graded audit fixture (informational) and enforces a hard gate: the verifier must emit zero false/stale findings against .github/workflows/js-tests.yml, which exists on disk — the canonical never-cry-wolf regression check for verify-docs.mjs.
whatBreaks: The doc-truth verifier could start emitting false positives on known-good files without any test catching the regression, eroding trust in the whole doc-truth tooling.

role: Generated map of doc file -> referenced paths/anchors for doc-truth checks
description: A generated (timestamped 2026-06-21) JSON index recording, per markdown/skill doc, the list of paths/anchors it references (e.g. CLAUDE.md's routing table targets); consumed by doc-truth resolution/verification tooling to check those references still exist. Data artifact, not hand-maintained.
whatBreaks: Stale or corrupt reference data would cause the doc-truth verifier to miss real broken links or flag false positives across the doc corpus.

role: Fixture: list of doc files covered by the 2026-06-21 human audit
description: Small JSON fixture (ctx + batches arrays of doc paths) enumerating exactly which docs the human-graded 53-agent audit examined; used by acceptance.mjs to scope recall measurement to docs that still exist on disk.
whatBreaks: acceptance.mjs's recall metric would be computed over the wrong doc set, giving a misleading (inflated or deflated) recall percentage.

role: Fixture: human-graded false/stale doc findings from the 2026-06-21 audit
description: 77KB JSON of the ground-truth findings (falseAll/staleAll) produced by the original 22-LLM-agent doc audit; acceptance.mjs matches the mechanical verifier's output against this to compute recall. Frozen historical baseline, not regenerated.
whatBreaks: Recall metric in acceptance.mjs becomes meaningless or wrong if this ground-truth data is corrupted, undermining confidence in the doc-truth verifier's coverage claims.

role: Frozen fail-before/pass-after fixture for code-comment citation guards
description: Records the mechanically-reproducible citation-truth defects (stale linerefs, wrong paths, dead terms) on the pre-fix tree from a 53-agent citation sweep, including the flagship examples (capabilities.ex:1527, listen.ts:10) that verify-docs.mjs --code and retired-terms.mjs must detect against frozen snapshots. Also tracks 'liveLeads' as advisory drift on the live tree.
whatBreaks: The verify-docs --code and retired-terms guards would lose their fail-before/pass-after proof, letting a regression in code-comment citation checking go undetected.

role: Never-cry-wolf control fixture for code-comment citation/retired-term verifiers
description: A fixture-only (not compiled) Elixir-shaped file with only correct path citations and negated/historical retired-term mentions; the verifier and retired-terms denylist must emit ZERO findings against it, proving they don't false-positive on clean code comments.
whatBreaks: Without this control, the code-comment citation guard could false-positive on legitimate historical mentions (e.g. 'Cytoscape was removed') with nothing to catch the false alarm.

role: Frozen snapshot of capabilities.ex used as citation-guard fail-before evidence
description: A pinned text snapshot of api/lib/barkpark/plugins/capabilities.ex (CLI/API command manifest source, including the auth.* core_cmd definitions and the stale router.ex:716-734 citation) used so the citation-truth guard verifies against the exact pre-fix line numbers rather than a live file whose line numbers can drift.
whatBreaks: The citation-truth acceptance test (acceptance-code-comments / citation-corpus fixture) would verify against a moving target and could spuriously pass or fail as the live capabilities.ex changes.

role: Frozen fixture snapshot of PortableDoc.Patch source for doc-truth
description: A frozen .txt copy of api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/patch.ex used as ground truth by the doc-truth verification tooling (verify-docs.mjs and friends) to detect drift between real source and documented behavior. Not live code; a fixture snapshot keyed by hash.
whatBreaks: Stale/incorrect frozen fixture would make doc-truth checks compare against outdated source, producing false pass/fail verdicts on PortableDoc.Patch documentation.

role: Frozen fixture snapshot of JS SDK listen.ts for doc-truth
description: A frozen .txt copy of js/packages/core/src/listen.ts (the SSE live-stream transport) used as ground truth by doc-truth tooling to verify documentation claims about listen/SSE behavior stay accurate over time.
whatBreaks: Doc-truth checks against SSE/listen behavior would validate against a stale snapshot, missing real drift in reconnect/backoff/idle-timeout documentation.

role: Frozen fixture snapshot of BarkparkWeb.Router for doc-truth
description: A dated frozen copy of the Phoenix router (api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex) captured 2026-07-04, used as a fixed reference point by doc-truth verification scripts (verify-docs.mjs references ROUTER) to test claim-verification logic without depending on the live, constantly-changing router.
whatBreaks: Doc-truth's router-claim verification tests could pass/fail incorrectly against a stale router shape, undermining confidence in the P1 verifier's accuracy tests.

role: Doc-truth P3: validates root CLAUDE.md routing table resolves to owners
description: Parses the root CLAUDE.md routing table, follows pointer/redirect chains up to 2 hops to a canonical-for owner doc, and checks canonical-for topic uniqueness, orphaned topics, and byte-budget/7-card-cap compliance via scripts/check-doc-budgets.sh. Dependency-free ESM script; part of the doc-truth 5-phase (P1-P5) tooling suite.
whatBreaks: A broken highways.mjs would silently let the routing table drift (broken links, duplicate owners, orphaned topics) undetected, degrading the agent-facing doc navigation contract described in root CLAUDE.md.

role: Guards README's live Cody-grade numbers against quality-report.json drift
description: Compares the README '## Codebase grade' section (overall score, per-critic scores, critic count) against the live tooling/quality/quality-report.json and reports/fixes drift; supports --fix to regenerate the README table from the live report. Report-only by default (exit non-zero on drift), dependency-free node script.
whatBreaks: Without this guard the README's hand-maintained grade numbers silently rot out of sync with the live quality report, misleading anyone trusting the codebase score.

role: Doc-truth P4: ranks doc coverage gaps by code reach/blast-radius
description: Joins doc coverage (inverted doc-refs.json) against code reach/importance (what-breaks.mjs closure size, file-signals.json) and churn (cochange-report.json) to emit a ranked queue of under-documented high-reach files vs over-documented trivia. Candidate set restricted to the 335 Elixir files in the symbol graph for grounded reach numbers.
whatBreaks: A broken priority ranking would misdirect documentation effort toward low-impact files while high-blast-radius code stays undocumented, degrading agent onboarding quality over time — not a runtime break.

role: Doc-truth P5: gates proposed doc restructures against fact/link loss
description: Capstone gate that evaluates a proposed doc remake (merge/split/promote/rewrite) by diffing extracted claims and links before/after; routes anything touching verbatim-exempt sections or losing a claim/link to human review, auto-approves only pure prose reorders that pass all checks. Propose-only — never writes docs itself; composes verify-docs.mjs, waterfall.mjs, and highways.mjs.
whatBreaks: A faulty gate could let a destructive doc restructure (losing facts or breaking links) auto-apply instead of routing to human review, corrupting the doc corpus silently.

role: Context-aware denylist catching prose that claims dead tech is live
description: Scans docs for mentions of retired dependencies (e.g. 'cytoscape', 'bin/bd-shim') used in a live-claiming context, distinguishing legitimate historical/negated mentions from stale assertions via negation-window heuristics and pragma/allowlist exceptions. Gated never-worse against a frozen fixture corpus; exits 1 only on novel violations.
whatBreaks: Missed or false-positive dead-tech detection would let docs keep asserting a gutted dependency (e.g. Cytoscape) is current, misleading anyone reading them, or would noisily flag legitimate historical prose.

role: Advisory check: hand-maintained doc enumerations match manifest/SDK ground truth
description: Verifies every capabilities.ex CLI op appears in the CLI HANDBOOK/cheatsheet, and every public @barkpark/core client method appears in its README, catching the recurring drift class where a new verb/method ships without a matching doc mention. Advisory only (always exits 0), with explicit IGNORE sets for intentional omissions.
whatBreaks: A newly added CLI verb or SDK method could ship undocumented indefinitely with no automated signal, degrading discoverability for both humans and agents.

role: Doc-truth P1: core claim-extraction and ground-truth verification engine
description: Parses markdown docs into typed claims (paths, commands, code refs) and verifies each against ground truth (symbol graph, manifest.json, router.ex), applying a re-verify gate so only confidence-checked findings surface; low-confidence leads route to human review. Exports extractClaims/sectionsOf/slugify, consumed by remake.mjs and other doc-truth phases — this is the foundational P1 module the rest of the suite (P2-P5) builds on.
whatBreaks: Since remake.mjs and other phases import its claim-extraction functions directly, a bug here cascades through the whole doc-truth pipeline's accuracy — false claims could pass unnoticed or true docs could be wrongly flagged stale across the entire corpus.

role: doc-truth P2 restatement detector — proposes fact-collapse across docs
description: Hashes verifiable claim anchors (paths/commands/symbols + code invariants) per doc section, clusters sections that restate the same facts via Jaccard overlap, and emits propose-only collapse proposals with a lose-no-fact guarantee. Never edits docs; exports runWaterfall/factKeyForClaim/buildDag/defaultCorpus for query.mjs and highways.mjs to consume.
whatBreaks: Doc dedup proposals would be wrong or unsafe (could silently recommend losing a fact), degrading trust in the doc-truth pipeline's P2 stage and any tool built on its DAG (highways --topic).

role: gitignore for ergonomics outputs
description: Excludes the generated ergonomics-report.json from version control.
whatBreaks: Stale ergonomics data gets committed, causing the bloat/god-file rankings to be wrong for anyone who does not regenerate.

role: Refactor-worth scorer: bloat × churn × separability, plus a safety classifier
description: Computes per-file token/def counts and a refactorWorth score from bloat-excess, churn, and definition-count separability; also exports a pure, deterministic classifySafety (test/cli-tool/contract/prod) used to rank split candidates by risk without touching the score itself. Feeds ergonomics-report.json, which scoring.mjs reads as the 'tokens'/'defs'/'churn' composite roots.
whatBreaks: Wrong refactor-worth ranking or safety labels could steer split-recommendations toward a risky prod/contract module or hide a genuinely safe test-file split.

role: ergonomics analysis script
description: Reads file-signals.json and produces token-size distributions, bloat candidates (large files weighted by churn), fragmentation candidates (dirs with many tiny files), and high-responsibility-density modules. Console-only output used for agent-ergonomics decision-making.
whatBreaks: Bloat and fragmentation analyses produce misleading data, leading to wrong refactor priorities.

role: unit test for classifySafety() risk-labeling used by god-module split ranking
description: Pure, dependency-free assertions covering the four safety categories (contract/test/cli-tool/prod), the danger-boundary crux (a prod file must never read 'safe'), and the churn overlay note. Guards ergonomics.mjs's classifySafety from mislabeling and misguiding refactor risk.
whatBreaks: A regression in classifySafety (e.g. a prod module misclassified as 'safe') would go undetected, letting the ergonomics tool mis-rank a risky split as low-risk.

role: gitignore for generated signal files
description: Ignores the four large generated artifacts: file-signals.json, file-batches.json, the batches/ directory, and the results/ directory. Keeps the tooling directory clean of cached outputs.
whatBreaks: Generated signal files are accidentally committed, polluting git history and causing merge conflicts.

role: Computes objective per-file importance signals (fan-in, churn, seam, prior score)
description: Zero-token programmatic backbone: for every tracked file computes fan-in (via blast-radius index), git churn, seam membership (via blast-radius config), entrypoint/core-dir flags, a deterministic prior importance score, and an auto-description for non-code files; partitions code/test files into agent-scored batches (file-batches.json) and writes file-signals.json, which many downstream tools (ergonomics, scoring.mjs, cody) read as their churn/fanIn/seam source of truth.
whatBreaks: Every downstream importance/priority/refactor-worth score across the codebase-intelligence toolchain (scoring.mjs, ergonomics, cody preflight) would be silently wrong.

role: Criticality merger: agent verdicts + programmatic signals
description: Blends deterministic prior (45%) with agent criticality votes (55%) for code/test files; prior alone for data/docs. Ingests multi-vote results (flat results/ = 1 vote; results/vote-*/ = N independent votes). Consensus's votes (median + agreement); flags contested judgments where the panel disagreed. Emits importance-chart.{csv,html} with sortable, color-graded interface.
whatBreaks: File importance chart becomes unavailable. Agent verdicts (role, description, whatBreaks) are lost. Multi-vote consensus system breaks—no panel disagreement detection. Developers cannot find critical files by importance. The 45-55 blend law cannot be applied; scores revert to prior alone (lower signal quality).

role: build artifact exclusion for the fit calibration engine outputs
description: Standard .gitignore file excluding scoring-config.json, fit-report.html, and other derived outputs from the fit calibration process. These artifacts are regenerated on each fit.mjs run.
whatBreaks: Derived scoring configuration and HTML reports would pollute git history; not a functional issue, just hygiene. Re-running fit.mjs regenerates them.

role: append-only ledger of fit calibration runs and AUC metrics over time
description: JSONL file that records one line per fit.mjs calibration run, keyed by HEAD commit. Tracks AUC, posRate, confidence, and file counts over time. NOT gitignored — survives across runs as the standing loop ledger for monitoring model validity drift.
whatBreaks: Loss of historical AUC tracking means no visibility into whether the scoring model's predictive power degrades over time; the CI release cadence cannot monitor for regressed calibration; must rebuild history from scratch.

role: the calibration engine — learns scoring weights from codebase history via logistic regression
description: Pure programmatic (zero-token) fit system that learns importance scoring from git history. Assembles per-file signal matrix (reach, churn, loc, tokens, defs, defectDensity, testScore, ownership, consistency, importance), labels files as future-defect via git commits in recent window, fits logistic regression, and outputs scoring-config.json + fit-report.html. Core to the codebase-intelligence v2 pipeline.
whatBreaks: The entire file-importance scoring ledger becomes stale — importance scores are no longer calibrated against the codebase's own defect history. Batch verdicts and risk assessment lose their empirical grounding. The fit-report.html and scoring thresholds degrade in accuracy.

role: build artifact exclusion for the intentions batching and results
description: Standard .gitignore excluding batches/, results/, batch-count.txt, and taxonomy.json (derived) from the intentions layer. These are regenerated from the taxonomy derivation pipeline.
whatBreaks: Derived batches and results pollute git; not functional. Re-running intentions.mjs digest/batches regenerates.

role: Raw git log digest feeding the intentions/research pipeline
description: A flat text dump of ~600+ commit subject lines (oldest cutoff to HEAD) used as raw input for the codebase-quality/enrich tooling to mine intentions, epics, and wave history. Not consumed by the running app; it's a generated tooling artifact.
whatBreaks: If stale or corrupted, downstream intention-mining and research-coverage summaries would misattribute or miss recent epics/waves, degrading analysis quality but not breaking any runtime system.

role: second-edge-type layering — tags files by objective/intention instead of dependency
description: CLI that orchestrates the intentions pipeline: digest (extract file corpus), batches (partition for tagging), merge (aggregate results into intentions-report.json). Reads from barkpark-sync/nodes.json and orchestrates the 3-step workflow. Part of the codebase-intelligence suite.
whatBreaks: The intentions layer cannot be generated — files are not tagged by objective/intention. The intentions-report.json becomes stale. Graph visualization and intention-based filtering in Studio lose their data source.

role: Generated importance manifest for internal/cli files
description: A JSON list of 74 CLI source files with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling as a review batch for the internal/cli subsystem (the bp CLI's command implementations).
whatBreaks: Wrong or stale importance scores only mislead the tooling's own reporting/prioritization output; no runtime behavior depends on this file.

role: Generated importance manifest for api/lib/barkpark context files
description: A JSON list of 72 core Elixir context modules (access, accounts, content, media, tasks, tenancy, webhooks, etc.) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the accuracy of the tooling's importance/reach reporting for the API's core domain contexts; no production code path reads this file.

role: Generated importance manifest for API Phoenix controllers
description: A JSON list of 66 barkpark_web controller files (auth, media, tasks, webhooks, github, tickets, etc.) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the controller layer; no runtime dependency.

role: Generated importance manifest for api/lib/barkpark/content submodule
description: A JSON list of 40 files under the Content context (document schema, envelope, graph, scope, writer, codelists, etc.) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the content subsystem; no runtime dependency.

role: Generated importance manifest for api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs
description: A JSON list of 39 Phoenix plug files (auth, CORS, rate-limit, tenancy, share/grant gates) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the plug layer; no runtime dependency.

role: Generated importance manifest for cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud
description: A JSON list of 36 files under the control-plane Cloud app (accounts, azure, billing, github, registry, router, vercel) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the cloud control-plane; no runtime dependency.

role: Generated importance manifest for the paper-editor JS asset bundle
description: A JSON list of 35 files under api/assets/paper-editor/src (TipTap editor entrypoint, converters, slash-menu, and its test suite) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the paper editor; no runtime dependency.

role: Generated importance manifest for web/lib (Next.js)
description: A JSON list of 35 files under web/lib (Barkpark client, search, sheets, papers, graph helpers) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the Next.js web app's lib layer; no runtime dependency.

role: Generated importance manifest for internal/pdrender
description: A JSON list of 34 Go files implementing the terminal PortableDoc renderer (block renderers, mermaid/chart/heatmap, theme/token generation) with role/importance scores, produced by the codebase-quality tooling.
whatBreaks: Only affects the tooling's own analysis output for the pdrender subsystem; no runtime dependency.

role: generated subsystem-review input batch (tooling/, 33 files)
description: Auto-generated by review.mjs: lists every node in the 'tooling' subsystem with path/role/importance for an agent review pass; overwritten wholesale each pipeline run.
